# SOTA Agentic Harness Reference (November 2026)

This file collects state-of-the-art information for every major area of building an agentic harness: the scaffolding around an LLM that turns it into a working agent. That covers the loop, context, memory, tools, sandbox, permissions, orchestration, evals, operations and training co-design. It is meant to be complete rather than short. The companion document, [`SOTA agentic harness build plan.md`](./SOTA%20agentic%20harness%20build%20plan.md), turns this material into a phased plan for building one.

**How each section is organized.** Every area uses the same template so that sections can be compared directly:

| Subsection | What it contains |
|---|---|
| `N.1` Where the field is | Current consensus and recent shifts, with dates |
| `N.2` By lab | Anthropic, OpenAI, DeepSeek, and open source and other labs |
| `N.3` Techniques and patterns | Each technique: what it is, how it works (parameters, defaults), evidence, when to use it |
| `N.4` Key numbers | Measured results with source, date and confidence |
| `N.5` APIs, parameters and defaults | Tool names, beta headers, config keys, defaults |
| `N.6` Reference implementations | Repos and files to copy from |
| `N.7` Build checklist | Concrete implementation steps with recommended defaults |
| `N.8` Pitfalls and anti-patterns | What goes wrong |
| `N.9` Open questions and unverified claims | What is still uncertain |

(Section 12, on repositories, uses a repo-by-repo layout instead.)

**Confidence markers.** Claims taken directly from primary sources (lab engineering posts, official docs, or source code in `openai/codex`, `anthropics/*` and other repos cloned on 2026-11-03) have no marker. Claims seen only in search-engine summaries or secondary write-ups are marked *(secondary)*, *(reported)* or *(via search summary)*. Inferences are marked *(inference)*. Pre-2025 work is marked *(background)*. Defaults we propose ourselves, rather than taking from a vendor, are labeled as such.

**Source limitations.** This session's network policy blocked openai.com, developers.openai.com, platform.openai.com, arxiv.org, api-docs.deepseek.com, huggingface.co, tbench.ai, metr.org, modelcontextprotocol.io and several others. For OpenAI, the open-source Codex code was read directly instead, and the MCP spec was read from its GitHub repo. The OpenAI API details, DeepSeek details, arXiv numbers and leaderboard rows that remain should be confirmed against primary sources before you rely on them. Benchmark numbers change quickly, so every score carries a date.

**Research notes.** The raw notes behind this reference, with every source link, are in [`research_notes/SOTA agentic harness build plan/`](../research_notes/SOTA%20agentic%20harness%20build%20plan/).

## 1. Agent architecture

> **SOTA in one paragraph:** A production harness in November 2026 separates three parts: a durable, append-only session/event log, a stateless harness loop that calls the model and routes its tool calls, and a disposable sandbox reached through a narrow `execute(name, input) → string` interface. Anthropic made this split explicit for Managed Agents in April 2026, and OpenHands' event-sourced SDK and Cline's stateless-loop/stateful-core layering follow the same idea. The default control structure is one autonomous tool-use loop, with Anthropic's 2024 workflow patterns (prompt chaining, routing, parallelization, orchestrator-workers, evaluator-optimizer) layered on top as optional outer structure: plan-mode gates, Stop-hook or goal evaluators, subagents and script-driven workflows. Claude Code and Codex have converged on almost the same harness surface (identical hook event names, permission modes including a classifier-based auto mode, a read-only plan mode, SKILL.md skills, AGENTS.md, MCP, JSONL sessions with resume and fork, headless JSON streaming and an SDK), while client protocols still differ (Codex app-server JSON-RPC, Claude stream-JSON control protocol, ACP, A2A). With the model held fixed, harness choice moves agentic benchmark scores by roughly 3–14 points, yet a ~100-line bash-only agent scores above 74% on SWE-bench Verified, because frontier models are post-trained inside their vendors' own harnesses. The SOTA recipe is therefore a thin core that can be ablated, plus thick, feature-flagged control-plane middleware and per-model tool and prompt profiles, re-tested on every model release because scaffolds built for older models become "dead weight".

### 1.1 Where the field is (Nov 2026)

**Consensus positions**

- **Split session, harness and sandbox.** Anthropic's Managed Agents design (2026-04-08) defines three interfaces that can each be swapped independently:
  - **Session**: "an append-only event log".
  - **Harness**: "the loop that calls Claude and routes Claude's tool calls".
  - **Sandbox**: the execution environment.

  The first design kept all three in one container, so a container failure lost the session. Decoupling them made containers disposable ("pets vs. cattle"). The session log is kept *outside* the context window because compaction, the memory tool and trimming of old tool results or thinking blocks "are irreversible." ([Anthropic Engineering: Scaling Managed Agents](https://anthropic.com/engineering/managed-agents)) Open-source equivalents:
  - OpenHands Software Agent SDK: the conversation is "an append-only event log" with tombstone-style `Condensation` events and a `View` projection.
  - Cline SDK: the canonical transcript is kept at full fidelity, and compaction state lives in a separate, hash-validated `${sessionId}.compaction.json`.

  ([OpenHands condenser README](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/main/openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/context/condenser/README.md); [Cline sdk/ARCHITECTURE.md](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/main/sdk/ARCHITECTURE.md))
- **"Give your agents a computer."** On 2025-09-29 Anthropic renamed the Claude Code SDK to the Claude Agent SDK, because "the agent harness that powers Claude Code" now powers "almost all of [Anthropic's] major agent loops." The loop is "gather context -> take action -> verify work -> repeat". ([Claude blog: Building agents with the Claude Agent SDK](https://claude.com/blog/building-agents-with-the-claude-agent-sdk)) Every leading coding harness has converged on a small kernel:
  - a shell
  - file read and search
  - a structured edit primitive
  - a plan/todo tool
  - web search/fetch
  - subagent spawn
  - MCP passthrough

  Bash plus the filesystem became the universal tool because it gives composition, grep/head/tail context economy, persistence of state in files, reuse of pretraining on shell transcripts, and a single choke-point for sandboxing. (tools notes, from the [Claude Agent SDK post](https://claude.com/blog/building-agents-with-the-claude-agent-sdk) and the [Codex source](https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/main/codex-rs/tools))
- **One autonomous loop is the default; workflow patterns are composable outer structure.** Anthropic's taxonomy from 2024-12-19 is still the reference vocabulary. In it, workflows are "systems where LLMs and tools are orchestrated through predefined code paths" and agents "dynamically direct their own processes and tool usage". ([Building effective agents](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/building-effective-agents)) 2026 practice puts these patterns *inside* the harness rather than choosing between them:
  - planner/generator/evaluator agents (2026-03-24)
  - `/goal` evaluators
  - loops classified by trigger: turn, goal, time, proactive (2026-06-30)

  ([Harness design for long-running apps](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/harness-design-long-running-apps); [Loop engineering](https://claude.com/blog/getting-started-with-loops))
- **The feature surface has converged.** Claude Code and Codex use the same hook event names (`PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `Stop`, `SubagentStop`, `SessionStart`, `SessionEnd`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `PreCompact`, `PostCompact`, `PermissionRequest`). Both have:
  - permission modes, including a model-classifier "auto" mode
  - a read-only plan mode kept separate from the plan/todo tool
  - SKILL.md skills
  - AGENTS.md, stewarded by the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) since 2025-12-09
  - MCP as the tool bus
  - append-only JSONL sessions with resume and fork
  - headless JSON-streaming modes and SDKs

  ([Claude Code hooks](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks); [codex hooks](https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/main/codex-rs/hooks/src); [agents.md AboutSection](https://github.com/agentsmd/agents.md/blob/main/components/AboutSection.tsx))
- **Where harnesses still diverge** ([open-source repo survey](https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/main/codex-rs)):
  - Edit format: `apply_patch` envelope vs `str_replace` vs SEARCH/REPLACE vs bash-only.
  - Shell model: stateful PTY vs stateless subprocess.
  - Client protocol: Codex app-server JSON-RPC vs Claude stream-JSON control protocol vs ACP vs A2A.
  - Implementation language: Rust, TypeScript, Python, Go.
  - Where state and compaction live: client-side; provider-side `responses.compact`; Anthropic server-side compaction; Managed Agents.
- **The harness matters, and it is co-designed with the model.**
  - Same model, harness changes only: LangChain's Deep Agents went from 52.8% to 66.5% on Terminal-Bench 2.0 with GPT-5.2-Codex (secondary).
  - Minimal harness: mini-swe-agent (~100 lines, bash only) scores above 74% on SWE-bench Verified. On Vals.ai's 2026-09-01 board, the top three entries all ran on the mini-SWE-agent bash-only harness, led by Opus 5 at 97.00% (secondary).
  - Co-design: Codex ships per-model system prompts, Cursor Composer and Windsurf SWE-1.5 were RL-trained in their own harnesses, and DeepSeek V3.2 designs thinking retention around the tool role.

  Details are in §1.3 and §1.4.
- **Prune scaffolds as models improve.** "Every harness component encodes an assumption about what the model can't do alone," and those assumptions go stale. ([Harness design](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/harness-design-long-running-apps)) Examples:
  - Context resets added for Sonnet 4.5 "had become dead weight" on Opus 4.5. ([Managed Agents](https://anthropic.com/engineering/managed-agents))
  - Sprints were removed on Opus 4.6.
  - Todo tools are off by default on the newest Claude models. ([Track todos](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/todo-tracking))
- **Primitives standardize faster than harnesses.**
  - Roo Code shut down on 2026-05-15.
  - Kimi CLI was archived and replaced by Kimi Code CLI.
  - Swarm is superseded by the Agents SDK.
  - SWE-agent points users to mini-swe-agent.
  - Aider has had no tagged release since v0.86.x (~Aug 2025).

  Meanwhile AGENTS.md, MCP, Skills and ACP spread across almost every harness. ([open-source repo survey](https://github.com/RooCodeInc/Roo-Code); [kimi-cli README](https://github.com/MoonshotAI/kimi-cli/blob/main/README.md); [swarm README](https://github.com/openai/swarm/blob/main/README.md))
- **Code-driven orchestration is gaining ground for large fan-outs.**
  - The OpenAI Agents SDK says orchestrating via code "makes tasks more deterministic and predictable, in terms of speed, cost and performance."
  - Claude Code dynamic workflows (around 2026-05-28) move the plan into a JavaScript script, so "Claude's context holds only the final answer".

  ([OpenAI Agents SDK multi_agent.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/openai-agents-python/main/docs/multi_agent.md); [Claude Code workflows](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows))

### 1.2 By lab

#### Anthropic

**Claude Code (the product harness; closed source)**

- **Licence and status.** The repo's LICENSE.md reads "© Anthropic PBC. All rights reserved … Commercial Terms of Service". It has ~154.3k stars and is at tag `v2.1.317`. The repo holds issues, the changelog, examples, and plugin and "mod" sources. You cannot fork the harness; you can only use it via the SDK or replicate its open interfaces (hooks, skills, settings, plugins, AGENTS.md). — [claude-code LICENSE.md](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/main/LICENSE.md)
- **Loop description.** The loop is "gather context, take action, and verify results. These phases blend together." The harness is "the layer around the model that provides the tools and manages the context the model sees." — [How Claude Code works](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/how-claude-code-works)
- **Built-in tools.** `Bash`, `Read`, `Edit`, `Write`, `Glob`, `Grep`, `WebFetch`, `WebSearch`, `NotebookEdit`, `Agent` (formerly `Task`; `Task(...)` still aliases it) and `TodoWrite`. These exact strings are used in permission rules, subagent tool lists and hook matchers. — [tools reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference); [subagents](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents)
- **Sessions and checkpoints.** JSONL transcripts under `~/.claude/projects/`, with resume, fork and rewind. File checkpoints are taken before edits, are "separate from git", and are auto-cleaned after 30 days (mechanics in §1.3, "Session persistence"). — [How Claude Code works](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/how-claude-code-works); [file checkpointing](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/file-checkpointing)
- **Permission modes.** `Shift+Tab` cycles Auto, Manual, Accept edits and Plan. Since Claude Code v2.1.283, auto mode is "the built-in starting permission mode" for interactive terminal and VS Code sessions. — [How Claude Code works](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/how-claude-code-works)
- **Auto mode architecture** (engineering post, 2026-03-25):
  - Input layer: a server-side prompt-injection probe scans tool outputs.
  - Output layer: a two-stage transcript classifier on Sonnet 4.6 runs before each action. Stage 1 is a single-token yes/no filter that "err[s] on the side of blocking". Stage 2 is chain-of-thought re-evaluation, run only if stage 1 flags.
  - The classifier is "reasoning-blind by design": it sees user messages and tool calls only.
  - Three tiers: a fixed allowlist; in-project edits that skip the classifier; everything else goes to the classifier.
  - A denial returns as a tool result telling the agent not to route around it. Three consecutive or 20 total denials escalate to the human, and headless `claude -p` terminates.

  Measured: users approved 93% of prompts anyway; the classifier's FPR is 0.4% on n=10,000 real traffic and its FNR is 17% on n=52 real overeager actions. — [Anthropic auto mode](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/claude-code-auto-mode)
- **Extension surfaces.**
  - **Plugins**, now in `anthropics/claude-plugins-official`, bundle "custom slash commands, specialized agents, hooks, and MCP servers" and install via `/plugin` marketplaces.
  - **Mods** are plugins whose behaviour is a hooks module with `register(on, options)`, hooking engine events as `($, e, next)` middleware. Four built-in mods ship as source:
    - `sec-default`, which shields managed policy from user-installed plugins
    - `diff`
    - `telemetry`
    - `agents-md`, which loads AGENTS.md where no CLAUDE.md exists. Its default mode is `claude-md-or-agents-md`; the others are `claude-md-and-agents-md`, `managed-only` and `claude-md`.

  — [plugins/README.md](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/main/plugins/README.md); [mods/README.md](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/main/mods/README.md)
- **Example settings and changelog.** Example settings exist for strict, lax, bash-sandbox and HIPAA configurations (`settings-strict.json`, `settings-bash-sandbox.json`, `managed-mcp-hipaa.json`), plus `bash_command_validator_example.py`. The v2.1.317 changelog mentions Agent SDK hook callbacks `onFailure: "block"`, auto mode, agent teams, background agents, `/loop`, `/schedule`, compaction fixes and OTel attributes. — [examples/](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/tree/main/examples); [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)
- **Scheduling and orchestration tiers.**
  - `/loop` runs locally at an interval.
  - `/schedule` and "routines" run in the cloud on cron, API or GitHub events.
  - Subagents: nesting depth 3, 20 concurrent, background by default.
  - Experimental agent teams: shared task list with file-locked claiming, JSON mailboxes; interactive sessions only.
  - Dynamic workflows: a JavaScript orchestration script; 16 concurrent agents by default; up to 1,000 agents per run; deterministic and resumable.

  — [Loop engineering](https://claude.com/blog/getting-started-with-loops); [subagents](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents); [agent teams](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams); [workflows](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows)

**Claude Agent SDK (embedding the harness)**

- **Packaging and licences.** The Python SDK is MIT (~8.4k stars, `v0.2.177`). The TypeScript SDK is under Commercial Terms (`v0.3.317`). "The Claude Code CLI is automatically bundled with the package"; a custom `cli_path` is optional. There are two entry points: `query()` (one-shot) and `ClaudeSDKClient` (bidirectional; enables custom tools and hooks). — [README](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python/blob/main/README.md)
- **Transport and control protocol.** There is a single transport, `_internal/transport/subprocess_cli.py`, plus `_internal/query.py`. The SDK sends `control_request` JSON lines and handles inbound control requests with subtypes:
  - `initialize`
  - `can_use_tool` (permission callback)
  - `hook_callback`
  - `mcp_message` (routing to in-process SDK MCP servers)

  The model: "the harness is a subprocess; the SDK is a protocol client." — [_internal/query.py](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python/blob/main/src/claude_agent_sdk/_internal/query.py)
- **Custom tools.** Custom tools are in-process MCP servers built with `@tool` and `create_sdk_mcp_server()`, with "No subprocess management … No IPC overhead … Single Python process". `allowed_tools` pre-approves tools; it "does not control tool availability". — [README](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python/blob/main/README.md)
- **`ClaudeAgentOptions` fields:** `tools`, `allowed_tools`, `disallowed_tools`, `system_prompt`, `mcp_servers`, `permission_mode`, `can_use_tool`, `hooks`, `agents`, `setting_sources`, `skills`, `sandbox`, `plugins`, `max_turns`, `max_budget_usd`, `task_budget`, `fallback_model`, `thinking`, `effort`, `output_format`, `enable_file_checkpointing`, `session_store`, `fork_session`, `resume`, `include_partial_messages`. — [types.py](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python/blob/main/src/claude_agent_sdk/types.py)
- **Message stream.**
  - `SystemMessage` subtype `"init"` at start.
  - One `AssistantMessage` per content block.
  - A final `ResultMessage` with result text, usage, cost and `session_id`.
  - `SystemMessage` `subtype: "compact_boundary"` on compaction.
  - `StreamEvent` deltas when `include_partial_messages` is set.

  Slash commands such as `/compact` are sent "as a prompt string". A `session_store`/`sessionStore` adapter mirrors transcripts to your own backend so stateless hosts can resume them ("dual-write"). — [agent-loop docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/agent-loop)
- **Programmatic subagents and the Workflow tool.** Subagents are defined as `agents={name: AgentDefinition(...)}`, which requires `Agent` in `allowed_tools`. Subagent messages carry `parent_tool_use_id` (and `agent_id` in TS). The `Workflow` tool requires TS SDK v0.3.149+. — [Agent SDK subagents](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/subagents)
- **Over-delegation on Opus 5.** "Claude Opus 5 delegates to subagents more readily than earlier models." With the `claude_code` preset on Opus 5, Claude Code adds a system-prompt line telling Claude not to call the Agent tool unless asked. Custom prompts must add their own delegation instruction, and hard limits should be set regardless. — [Agent SDK subagents](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/subagents)

**Claude Managed Agents (hosted harness, 2026-04-08)**

- **Design.** A session/harness/sandbox split with interfaces `execute(name, input) → string`, `provision({resources})`, `wake(sessionId)`/`getSession(id)`, and `emitEvent(id, event)`/`getEvents()`. Sandbox death is returned to Claude as a tool error. Lazy provisioning cut p50 TTFT by about 60% and p95 by more than 90%. Mechanics are in §1.3. — [Managed Agents](https://anthropic.com/engineering/managed-agents)
- **API surface.** Session endpoints use beta header `managed-agents-2026-04-01`. Compaction is always on and emits an `agent.thread_context_compacted` event. — [Managed Agents memory](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/memory); [Threshold compaction](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/compaction-threshold)
- **Memory stores (beta, announced 2026-04-23).**
  - Header `agent-memory-2026-07-22`. Sending it together with `managed-agents-2026-04-01` returns a 400.
  - Stores are attached at session creation via `resources: [{type: "memory_store", …}]` and mounted at `/mnt/memory/<slug>/`.
  - Limits: 100 kB per memory, 10,000 memories per store, 8 stores per session.

  — [Managed Agents memory](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/memory)
- **Quickstart apps.** `anthropics/claude-quickstarts/managed-agents/` holds apps built on "agents Anthropic runs for you, with server-side sessions, sandboxed tools, and an event stream your app consumes". Examples include assistant-ui, Vercel Chat SDK, AG-UI/CopilotKit, Slack, Linear, Sentry autofix and self-hosted sandboxes. Bash is configurable as `always_ask`, with resumable approval gates. — [managed-agents/README.md](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-quickstarts/blob/main/managed-agents/README.md)

**Open-source scaffolding Anthropic does publish**

- `anthropic-experimental/sandbox-runtime` (`srt`, Apache-2.0, `v0.0.81`): an OS-level sandbox (Seatbelt or bubblewrap) plus a domain-allowlist proxy. — [README](https://github.com/anthropic-experimental/sandbox-runtime/blob/main/README.md)
- `anthropics/skills` (~186.8k stars): SKILL.md with YAML frontmatter `name` and `description`. The spec is now at agentskills.io. — [README](https://github.com/anthropics/skills/blob/main/README.md)
- `claude-quickstarts/autonomous-coding`: "a minimal harness demonstrating long-running autonomous coding with the Claude Agent SDK" (see §2). `claude-quickstarts/agents/`: "a minimal educational implementation … NOT an SDK". — [autonomous-coding](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-quickstarts/blob/main/autonomous-coding/README.md); [agents](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-quickstarts/blob/main/agents/README.md)
- `claude-cookbooks`:
  - `patterns/agents/`: workflows, orchestrator-workers, evaluator-optimizer, async multi-agent
  - `claude_agent_sdk/` notebooks 00–08: research, chief-of-staff, observability, SRE, migrating from the OpenAI Agents SDK, session browser, hosting, dynamic workflows

  — [patterns/agents](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-cookbooks/tree/main/patterns/agents); [claude_agent_sdk/](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-cookbooks/tree/main/claude_agent_sdk)
- `anthropics/claude-code-action` (`v1.0.267`): runs Claude Code on your runner. It responds to `@claude` mentions or uses unified `prompt`/`claude_args` inputs, auto-detects its mode, tracks progress with checkboxes, and supports structured JSON outputs. — [README](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action/blob/main/README.md)

**Design guidance posts** (detailed in §1.3 and §2.3)

- Building effective agents (2024-12-19)
- Effective harnesses for long-running agents (2025-11-26)
- Harness design for long-running apps (2026-03-24)
- Loop engineering (2026-06-30)
- C compiler with parallel Claudes (2026-02-05)
- Demystifying evals (2026-01-09)
- Quantifying infrastructure noise in agentic coding evals (2026-02-05; title only, not read)

#### OpenAI

**Codex (`openai/codex`, Apache-2.0; the most complete open-source production harness)**

- **Status.** ~132.9k stars, ~21.0k forks, latest stable tag `rust-v0.166.0`, HEAD `fbf5f0d` on 2026-11-03. It ships as a CLI, an IDE extension, a desktop app (`codex app`) and cloud "Codex Web". Install via standalone installer, npm `@openai/codex` or Homebrew. It works with a ChatGPT plan or an API key. — [README](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/README.md)
- **Workspace layout.** A roughly 150-crate Rust workspace. Crates include:
  - core and editing: `core`, `apply-patch`
  - protocol and execution: `app-server`, `app-server-protocol`, `exec`, `exec-server`, `execpolicy`
  - extensions: `hooks`, `skills`, `memories`
  - sandboxing: `linux-sandbox`, `bwrap`, `windows-sandbox-rs`, `network-proxy`, `sandboxing`
  - MCP and code mode: `rmcp-client`, `codex-mcp`, `code-mode`
  - state and UI: `rollout`, `thread-store`, `tui`, `otel`
  - multi-agent: `worktree`, `agent-roles`, `message-board`
  - `responses-api-proxy`

  `codex-core` "implements the business logic for Codex … used by the various Codex UIs written in Rust". — [codex-rs tree](https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/main/codex-rs); [core/README.md](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/core/README.md)
- **Core modules** (`core/src`):
  - `codex_thread.rs`, `thread_manager.rs`, `session/` (the turn loop lives in `session/turn.rs`), `tasks/`
  - `client.rs` (Responses API client), `responses_retry.rs`
  - `context_manager/`, `turn_diff_tracker.rs`, `rollout.rs`, `shell_snapshot.rs`, `exec_policy.rs`, `guardian_review.rs`
  - `mcp_tool_call.rs`, `skills.rs`, `agents_md.rs`, `compact*.rs`

  Tool plumbing lives under `core/src/tools/`: `registry.rs`, `router.rs`, `orchestrator.rs`, `parallel.rs`, `approvals.rs`, `sandboxing.rs`, `network_approval.rs`, `spec_plan.rs`. — [core/src](https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/main/codex-rs/core/src); [core/src/tools](https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/main/codex-rs/core/src/tools)
- **Per-model and per-mode prompts.** Model-specific base prompts ship as markdown in core: `gpt_5_codex_prompt.md`, `gpt-5.1-codex-max_prompt.md`, `gpt-5.2-codex_prompt.md`, `gpt_5_1_prompt.md`, `gpt_5_2_prompt.md`. There are prompt templates per sandbox mode (`read_only`, `workspace_write`, `danger_full_access`) and per approval policy (`never`, `on_request`, `unless_trusted`, plus `approved_prefixes.md`), and a "guardian" auto-review classifier prompt (`guardian/policy.md`, `classifier_instructions.md`). — [codex-rs/core](https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/main/codex-rs/core); [prompts/templates](https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/main/codex-rs/prompts/templates)
- **Approval policies.** `AskForApproval` variants:
  - `untrusted` (`UnlessTrusted`)
  - `on-request`, the default; `on-failure` is now a serde alias for it
  - `granular` (per-category booleans, where false means auto-reject)
  - `never`, which returns failures to the model

  `ApprovalsReviewer` is `user` (default) or `auto_review` (alias `guardian_subagent`). — [protocol.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/protocol/src/protocol.rs); [guardian](https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/main/codex-rs/core/src/guardian)
- **CLI subcommands.** `exec` (alias `e`), `review`, `mcp`, `plugin`, `app-server`, `remote-control`, `sandbox`, `execpolicy`, `apply`, `resume`, `fork`, `queue`, `cloud`, `exec-server`. Current `main` has no top-level `mcp-server` subcommand (it existed in 2025-era versions); this was checked only against the subcommand enum. — [cli/src/main.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/cli/src/main.rs)
- **Headless mode.** `codex exec --json` emits JSONL `ThreadEvent`s: `thread.started`, `turn.started`, `turn.completed`, `turn.failed`, `item.started`, `item.updated`, `item.completed`, `error`. — [exec_events.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/exec/src/exec_events.rs)
- **App-server protocol.** JSON-RPC over a thread/turn/item model that every OpenAI surface (TUI, IDE, desktop, SDK) is built on. Methods:
  - threads: `thread/start|resume|fork|read|list|search|compact/start|revert|archive`, `thread/goal/set|get|clear`, `thread/queue/*`, `thread/memory/read`
  - turns: `turn/start`, `turn/steer`, `turn/interrupt`
  - streamed items: `item/agentMessage/delta`, `item/commandExecution/requestApproval`, `item/fileChange/requestApproval`, `item/plan/delta`, `item/reasoning/summaryTextDelta`
  - other: `review/start`, `skills/list`, `mcpServer/elicitation/request`

  — [app-server-protocol](https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/main/codex-rs/app-server-protocol); [app-server/README.md](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/app-server/README.md)
- **SDKs.** The TypeScript `@openai/codex-sdk` "wraps the `codex` CLI … spawns the CLI and exchanges JSONL events over stdin/stdout" (`codex.startThread()` then `thread.run(...)`). A Python SDK lives in `sdk/python`. — [sdk/typescript/README.md](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/sdk/typescript/README.md)
- **Hooks, skills and MCP.** The hooks crate implements Claude Code's event names. The `skills` crate has bundled sample skills and `mcp_skill_dependencies`, showing that OpenAI adopted the SKILL.md model. The MCP client uses the official Rust SDK `rmcp`, pinned `=3.5.1`. — [hooks/src](https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/main/codex-rs/hooks/src); [skills](https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/main/codex-rs/skills); [Cargo.toml](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/Cargo.toml)
- **Plan Mode.** A "collaboration mode" that allows only non-mutating actions and ends in a `<proposed_plan>` that must be "decision complete". Calling `update_plan` in Plan Mode returns an error. — [plan.md](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/collaboration-mode-templates/templates/plan.md)
- **Harness posts.**
  - "Unrolling the Codex agent loop" (2026-01-23, Michael Bolin; first in a series): the prompt is a list of items (developer messages describing the sandbox, plus tool definitions for a shell tool, a plan tool and MCP tools), and inference goes over HTTP to the Responses API. (search snippet only; openai.com unreachable)
  - "Harness engineering" (2026-02-11), per secondary coverage: about 1M lines of agent-written code, a team that grew from 3 to 7 engineers over five months, and AGENTS.md (about 100 lines) used as a table of contents into a structured `docs/` directory. Coverage also quotes "Codex models are trained in the presence of the harness". (unverified)

  — [Unrolling the Codex agent loop](https://openai.com/index/unrolling-the-codex-agent-loop); [Harness engineering](https://openai.com/index/harness-engineering/); [36kr](https://eu.36kr.com/en/p/3715546375188870)
- **Reported open-sourcing.** OpenAI's 2026-08-20 open-sourcing of the "Codex harness" is reported only by secondary outlets and is unverified. — [OpenSourceForU](https://www.opensourceforu.com/2026/08/openai-open-sources-codex-harness-framework)
- **Codex app.** The macOS app (2026-02-02) is a "command center" for managing multiple coding agents in parallel. Codex also spawns parallel subagents and consolidates their results. — [IntuitionLabs](https://intuitionlabs.ai/articles/openai-codex-app-ai-coding-agents) (secondary)

**OpenAI Agents SDK (`openai-agents-python` / `-js`, MIT)**

- **Status.** Python: ~30.5k stars, `v0.24.0`, last commit 2026-10-30. JS: `v0.21.0`, last commit 2026-11-02; a monorepo of `agents`, `agents-core`, `agents-openai`, `agents-extensions` and `agents-realtime`; runs on Node 22+, Deno and Bun. — [openai-agents-python](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python); [openai-agents-js README](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-js/blob/main/README.md)
- **Scope.** "provider-agnostic, supporting the OpenAI Responses and Chat Completions APIs, as well as 100+ other LLMs". Concepts: Agents, Sandbox agents, Realtime agents, Voice, Agents-as-tools/Handoffs, Tools (function, MCP, hosted), Guardrails, Human in the loop, Sessions, Tracing. — [README](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/main/README.md)
- **Loop internals.** `src/agents/run_internal/` contains `run_loop.py`, `turn_preparation.py`, `turn_resolution.py`, `tool_planning.py`, `tool_execution.py`, `approvals.py`, `guardrails.py`, `session_persistence.py`, `prompt_cache_key.py`, `model_retry.py`, `streaming.py`. — [run_internal](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/tree/main/src/agents/run_internal)
- **Handoffs and guardrails.** Handoffs are exposed to the model as tools named `transfer_to_{agent.name}`. Guardrails are `InputGuardrail`/`OutputGuardrail` returning `GuardrailFunctionOutput(tripwire_triggered=…)`; tool-level guardrails live in `tool_guardrails.py`. — [handoffs/__init__.py](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/main/src/agents/handoffs/__init__.py); [guardrail.py](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/main/src/agents/guardrail.py)
- **Sessions.** Backends: `SQLiteSession`, `AsyncSQLiteSession`, `RedisSession`, `SQLAlchemySession`, `MongoDBSession`, `DaprSession`, `OpenAIConversationsSession`, `OpenAIResponsesCompactionSession` (which "triggers responses.compact when stored history grows"), `AdvancedSQLiteSession` (branching and analytics) and `EncryptedSession`. — [sessions docs](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/main/docs/sessions/index.md)
- **Tracing.** Built into `tracing/` and exported to the OpenAI Traces dashboard by default. — [src/agents/tracing](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/tree/main/src/agents/tracing)
- **`SandboxAgent` (new in 2026).** OpenAI's answer to "give the agent a computer". It takes:
  - a `Manifest` of workspace entries (`GitRepo`, `LocalDir`)
  - `capabilities` (`Capabilities.default()` plus `Skills(lazy_from=…)`)
  - `SandboxRunConfig(client=UnixLocalSandboxClient()|DockerSandboxClient|hosted)`

  It provides "file staging, filesystem tools, shell access, sandbox lifecycle, snapshots". Capability modules: `compaction.py`, `filesystem.py`, `memory.py`, `shell.py`, `skills.py`. Hosted extensions: `e2b`, `modal`, `daytona`, `cloudflare`, `vercel`, `blaxel`. Warning: UnixLocal "adds no OS-level confinement" on Linux. — [docs/sandbox_agents.md](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/main/docs/sandbox_agents.md); [src/agents/sandbox](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/tree/main/src/agents/sandbox)
- **Two orchestration modes.**
  - "Via LLM": an agent plans with instructions, tools and handoffs.
  - "Via code": structured-output routing, chaining, evaluator `while` loops, and `asyncio.gather`.

  `Agent.as_tool()` keeps the manager in charge, whereas a handoff makes the specialist the active agent. — [multi_agent.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/openai-agents-python/main/docs/multi_agent.md)
- **Durable execution.** The Temporal integration has been GA since 2026-03-23. Agents run inside a Temporal Workflow and every model invocation runs as an Activity (`OpenAIAgentsPlugin`; `activity_as_tool`). — [Temporal blog](https://temporal.io/blog/announcing-openai-agents-sdk-integration)

**Other OpenAI repos and products**

- **Swarm** (deprecated): "Swarm is now replaced by the OpenAI Agents SDK"; "experimental, educational", client-side and stateless. — [swarm README](https://github.com/openai/swarm/blob/main/README.md)
- **Harmony and gpt-oss.**
  - Harmony (`v0.0.8`) is the format gpt-oss was trained on: roles `system`/`developer`/`user`/`assistant`; channels `analysis`/`commentary`/`final`, with function calls going to `commentary`; TypeScript-like tool namespaces.
  - gpt-oss (`v0.0.9`) ships the reference tools it was trained on (`simple_browser`, `python_docker`, `apply_patch`) and states that the models "should only be used with this format".

  — [harmony README](https://github.com/openai/harmony/blob/main/README.md); [gpt-oss README](https://github.com/openai/gpt-oss/blob/main/README.md)
- **AgentKit / Agent Builder.** Visual canvas launched at DevDay in Oct 2025. Deprecation notices were reportedly sent 2026-06-03, with shutdown cited as 2026-11-30 (secondary; dates conflict). Agent RFT launched with AgentKit (Oct 2025): the policy calls *your* tool endpoints during RL rollouts. — [osher.com.au](https://osher.com.au/blog/openai-agentkit/); [Introducing AgentKit](https://openai.com/index/introducing-agentkit/)

#### DeepSeek

- **The research notes conflict on whether DeepSeek ships a harness.**
  - The open-source repo survey probed GitHub for `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4`, `DeepSeek-V4-Pro`, `DeepSeek-V3.1` and `DeepSeek-Agent`, found no public repo, and concluded that DeepSeek "does not publish an agent harness". It explicitly calls this "absence of evidence … not proof". — [git ls-remote probes](https://github.com/deepseek-ai)
  - The memory notes report a **"DeepSeek Harness"** open-source agent runtime (MIT): v0.1 around 2026-08-13 (Gigazine), or a public debut on 2026-07-31 per one source. The official repo [deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) exists, but its README "is tiny and only points agents to `AGENTS.md`". Secondary sources say persistent memory is planned, not shipped. Third-party memory plugins exist: Mem0, AgentScope ReMe (requires DSH ≥0.1.2-rc.1) and MemOS (2026-08-17). — [Gigazine](https://gigazine.net/gsc_news/en/20260814-deepseek-harness-v0-1/) (secondary); [teamorouter](https://teamorouter.com/blogs/deepseek-harness-agent-framework) (secondary); [MemOS README](https://github.com/MemTensor/MemOS)

  Treat DeepSeek Harness as real but immature and largely undocumented. Its architecture and loop are not described anywhere in the notes.
- **Strategy: be driven by third-party harnesses.**
  - The API exposes an Anthropic-format endpoint, `https://api.deepseek.com/anthropic`, used with Claude Code via `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` plus `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (community guides also use `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`).
  - `anthropic-beta` and `anthropic-version` headers are ignored.
  - The Chinese docs reportedly map `claude-opus*` → `deepseek-v4-pro`, and `claude-sonnet*`, `claude-haiku*` and unknown names → `deepseek-v4-flash`.
  - A third-party summary says MCP tool-use blocks are unsupported.
  - The API also exposes Responses-API-compatible endpoints.

  — [api-docs.deepseek.com anthropic_api](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/anthropic_api) (search summary); [developersdigest](https://www.developersdigest.tech/reference/api-compatibility/deepseek) (secondary)
- **V4 harness support (secondary).** Coverage says V4 shipped "with documented support for Claude Code, OpenClaw, OpenCode, and CodeBuddy", integrated by swapping the base URL, and that DeepSeek runs V4-Pro as its internal coding agent. — [handyai substack](https://handyai.substack.com/p/model-drop-deepseek-v4); [atlascloud](https://www.atlascloud.ai/blog/deepseek-v4-preview-launch)
- **V4 release (secondary only).** An open-weight preview on 2026-04-24: V4-Pro (~1.6T total / 49B active) and V4-Flash (~284B / 13B active), both with 1M context and MIT weights. Sources conflict on parameter counts, pricing, and SWE-bench Verified (80.6 "vendor-reported" vs ~91.2). Vals.ai lists DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813 at 96.40% on SWE-bench Verified using the mini-SWE-agent bash-only harness (search summary). — [letsdatascience](https://letsdatascience.com/news/deepseek-v4-preview-adds-open-weight-1m-context-models-4a8f21c6); [Vals.ai](https://www.vals.ai/benchmarks/swebench)
- **Reference encoders.** DeepSeek publishes Python "encoding" reference scripts on Hugging Face rather than agent code:
  - V3.2: `encode_messages`, `parse_message_from_completion_text`, `encode_config = dict(thinking_mode="thinking", drop_thinking=True, add_default_bos_token=True)`. A `developer` role exists "only for search-agent scenarios" and is not accepted by the official API. The parser "is designed to handle well-formatted strings only".
  - V4: `encoding_dsv4.py`.

  Builders running self-hosted weights should use these encoders and the vLLM/SGLang parsers built on them, not hand-rolled templates. — [HF mirror of DeepSeek-V3.2 card](https://huggingface.co/Deniss8686/DeepSeek-V3.2) (search-summarized; unverified)
- **Model-side co-design.** The V3.2 tech report designs thinking retention around agent-framework conventions: tool role vs user role. It warns that frameworks which simulate tool calls through user messages (it names Roo Code and Terminus) trigger reasoning discard. Loop details are in §2.2. — [DeepSeek-V3.2 report, arXiv 2512.02556](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.02556) (search snippet)
- **First-class provider elsewhere.** Aider added "DeepSeek Reasoner model and updated DeepSeek model metadata with costs and prompt caching". — [aider HISTORY.md](https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider/blob/main/HISTORY.md)

**Frameworks**

- **Microsoft Agent Framework 1.0** (around 2026-04-02 to 04-07; sources differ). Unifies Semantic Kernel and AutoGen. Stable surface: a single-agent abstraction, connectors, middleware hooks, memory/context providers, and graph-based workflows, for .NET and Python. Uses MCP for tools and A2A for interop (the A2A packages are still preview). — [Visual Studio Magazine](https://visualstudiomagazine.com/articles/2026/04/06/microsoft-ships-production-ready-agent-framework-1-0-for-net-and-python.aspx)
- **Google ADK** (community sources). `SequentialAgent`, `ParallelAgent` (shared `session.state` with distinct `output_key`s), `LoopAgent` (runs until `escalate=True` or `max_iterations`), `AgentTool`, and `transfer_to_agent`. — [community ADK guide](https://zack.onrender.com/docs/GEN%20AI%20DEV/Agents/Google%20ADK)

**Model–harness co-design outside the big three**

- **Cursor Composer 2** is evaluated "in the same Cursor harness that is used by the deployed model, with equivalent tools and structure". Its RL tasks "run in environments that emulate real Cursor sessions"; the base model is Kimi K2.5 (1.04T total / 32B active MoE). Composer 1 was RL-trained in a harness that simulated Cursor's production tools. — [Cursor Composer 2 report, arXiv 2603.24477](https://arxiv.org/html/2603.24477) (snippet)
- **Windsurf SWE-1.5** was RL-trained in its own Cascade harness. — [Simon Willison, 2025-10-29](https://simonwillison.net/2025/Oct/29/) (snippet)

**Manus** (2025-07-18; primary post blocked; via search extracts and a gist summary)

- "KV-cache hit rate is the single most important metric for a production-stage AI agent".
- Input:output ratio is about 100:1, and a typical task is about 50 tool calls.
- Rules: stable prefix, append-only context, deterministic serialization.
- "Mask, don't remove" tools, using logit masking with namespaced prefixes (`browser_*`, `shell_*`).
- `todo.md` recitation.
- "Keep the wrong stuff in".

— [Manus blog (via search)](https://manus.im/blog/Context-Engineering-for-AI-Agents-Lessons-from-Building-Manus); [gist summary](https://gist.github.com/cedrickchee/b9646b3007b4a15f528351abd331984f)

**Neutral benchmark harnesses**

- **Terminus 2** is the neutral reference harness for Terminal-Bench 2.0. vals.ai runs every model through Terminus 2 so that models can be compared with the harness held fixed. — [vals.ai TB2](https://www.vals.ai/benchmarks/terminal-bench-2)
- **Harbor** runs Terminus-2 in a separate process from the task container and doubles as an RL rollout generator (`collect_rollout_details` captures token IDs and logprobs). — [Harbor Terminus-2 docs](https://www.harborframework.com/docs/agents/terminus-2)
- **METR** mostly uses the Triframe and ReAct scaffolds. It has also measured time horizon using Claude Code and Codex as the harness (note dated 2026-02-13). — [METR TH1.1](https://metr.org/blog/2026-01-29-time-horizon-1-1/) (via search snippets)

### 1.3 Techniques and patterns

**Session / harness / sandbox decomposition (the "brain–hands–memory" split)**
- *What it is:* Three independently replaceable components:
  - a durable, append-only session event log (memory)
  - a stateless harness loop that samples the model and routes tool calls (brain)
  - a sandbox reached only through a tool-dispatch interface (hands)
- *Mechanics (Managed Agents):*
  - Tools are dispatched as `execute(name, input) → string`, and sandboxes are created with `provision({resources})`.
  - Events are written with `emitEvent(id, event)` and read in positional slices with `getEvents()`, which supports rewind and re-reading.
  - A crashed harness is replaced via `wake(sessionId)`, and `getSession(id)` resumes "from the last event".
  - A dead sandbox is surfaced to the model as a tool-call error, and the model "can choose to retry".
  - The harness may transform events on the way into context (for cache hit rate) without changing the log.
- *Evidence:*
  - Anthropic's first design co-located all three in one container, so a container failure lost the session. Decoupling made containers "cattle". — [Managed Agents](https://anthropic.com/engineering/managed-agents)
  - The log lives outside the context window because compaction, the memory tool and trimming of tool results or thinking "are irreversible." — [Managed Agents](https://anthropic.com/engineering/managed-agents)
- *When to use / when not:* Use it for any harness that must survive crashes, resume, fork or rewind, or run on stateless hosts. A single-process CLI can co-locate the components, but it should still keep the log append-only and separate from what it sends to the model.

```text
            ┌───────────────────────────── Session (append-only event log) ────────────────────────────┐
            │  user_msg · model_msg · tool_call · tool_result · compaction · hook_decision · checkpoint │
            └──────────────▲───────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────┘
                 emitEvent │                               │ getEvents(slice) → projection/View → prompt
            ┌──────────────┴───────────────┐       ┌───────▼───────────┐
            │ Harness (stateless loop)     │──────▶│ Model API         │  (Messages / Responses / DeepSeek)
            │ hooks · budgets · compaction │◀──────│                   │
            └──────────────┬───────────────┘       └───────────────────┘
                 execute(name, input) → string   (sandbox death ⇒ tool error ⇒ model may retry)
            ┌──────────────▼───────────────┐
            │ Sandbox (lazily provisioned) │  provision({resources}); disposable; OS sandbox or container
            └──────────────────────────────┘
```

**Append-only event log plus a projection ("View") for context**
- *What it is:* Never mutate history. Record condensation and compaction as new events, and compute what the LLM sees by projecting the log.
- *Mechanics:*
  - **OpenHands.** Condensation is recorded as `Condensation` events, "similar to tombstones in … Cassandra and Kafka", and a `View` applies them to produce the LLM-visible context. The default `LLMSummarizingCondenser` replaces "the first half of all events with a single summary event" (`max_size=240` events, `keep_first=2`, optional `max_tokens`). Condensation is "soft" (a resource limit; it can be skipped if it would break message-structure invariants) or "hard" (explicitly requested, for example after a context-window error).
  - **Cline.** Canonical history stays at full fidelity. Compaction state is stored in `${sessionId}.compaction.json` and is reused on resume only after validating a hash of the canonical prefix. Automatic compaction requires a known context window ("unknown custom-model limits do not trigger compaction").
  - **Claude Code and Codex** keep append-only JSONL. Codex rollouts contain `session_meta`, `turn_context`, `event_msg` and `response_item`.
- *Evidence:* OpenHands' README states that regular condensation keeps prompt-cache rebuild costs low. Anthropic recommends append-only history for cache stability and because irreversible edits lose information. — [OpenHands condenser README](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/main/openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/context/condenser/README.md); [Cline ARCHITECTURE.md](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/main/sdk/ARCHITECTURE.md); [codex read_path.md](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/ext/memories/templates/memories/read_path.md)
- *When to use / when not:* Always use it. The only cost is storage. Pair it with a projection cache so that you do not re-summarize on every resume.

**Stateless loop package vs stateful core**
- *What it is:* A layering in which the loop library (iteration, tool orchestration, events, hooks) holds no durable state. Sessions, persistence, compaction policy and RPC sit in a separate core package.
- *Mechanics:* Cline SDK: `@cline/shared` → `@cline/llms` → `@cline/agents` (stateless runtime loop) → `@cline/core` → host apps. The OpenAI Agents SDK has a similar internal split: `run_loop.py`, `turn_preparation.py`, `turn_resolution.py`, `tool_planning.py`, `tool_execution.py`, `session_persistence.py`, `model_retry.py`.
- *Evidence:* The open-source repo survey names Cline's layering as "the best pattern for resumable compaction without losing the original transcript". — [Cline ARCHITECTURE.md](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/main/sdk/ARCHITECTURE.md); [run_internal](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/tree/main/src/agents/run_internal)
- *When to use / when not:* Use it whenever the loop must be embedded in more than one host (CLI, IDE, server, CI).

**Harness-as-subprocess with a control protocol (Claude Agent SDK model)**
- *What it is:* The host process spawns the harness binary and speaks newline-delimited JSON to it. Callbacks flow back for permission, hook and tool decisions.
- *Mechanics:*
  - `subprocess_cli.py` transport.
  - Outbound `control_request` lines; inbound control requests of subtype `initialize`, `can_use_tool`, `hook_callback` and `mcp_message`.
  - Custom tools run as in-process SDK MCP servers.
  - The TypeScript Codex SDK uses the same shape: it spawns `codex` and exchanges JSONL events over stdin/stdout.
- *Evidence:* This cleanly separates the agent loop from host-supplied policy and tools. Both vendors chose it for their SDKs. — [_internal/query.py](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python/blob/main/src/claude_agent_sdk/_internal/query.py); [codex sdk/typescript](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/sdk/typescript/README.md)
- *When to use / when not:* Use it when you ship one harness binary and many language SDKs. In-process embedding is simpler if you only target one language.

**Thread/turn/item JSON-RPC client protocol (Codex app-server)**
- *What it is:* A UI-agnostic harness↔client boundary. A *thread* (durable conversation) contains *turns* (one user request through to the final answer), which contain *items* (message, command execution, file change, plan, reasoning).
- *Mechanics:*
  - Thread methods: `thread/start|resume|fork|read|list|search|compact/start|revert|archive`, `thread/goal/set|get|clear`, `thread/queue/*`, `thread/memory/read`.
  - Turn methods: `turn/start`, `turn/steer` (inject user input mid-turn) and `turn/interrupt`.
  - Item-level approval requests: `item/commandExecution/requestApproval`, `item/fileChange/requestApproval`.
  - Delta streams: `item/agentMessage/delta`, `item/plan/delta`, `item/reasoning/summaryTextDelta`.
- *Evidence:* Every OpenAI surface (TUI, IDE, desktop, SDK) is built on it. The open-source repo survey calls it "the most complete open spec for a UI-agnostic harness/client boundary". — [app-server-protocol](https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/main/codex-rs/app-server-protocol)
- *When to use / when not:* Adopt it, or mirror it, instead of inventing a client protocol. Also expose ACP if IDEs (Zed, JetBrains) or control centers (OpenHands Agent Canvas) should be able to drive the harness.

**Headless JSONL mode, SDK and ACP exposure**
- *What it is:* A non-interactive mode that streams typed events, so CI, other agents and control centers can drive the harness.
- *Mechanics:*
  - Claude: `claude -p "…"` with `--output-format stream-json --verbose`.
  - Codex: `codex exec --json`, emitting `thread.started`, `turn.started`, `turn.completed`, `turn.failed`, `item.started`, `item.updated`, `item.completed` and `error`.
  - ACP is spoken by Kimi Code (`kimi acp`, `acp-server`), Goose, deepagents (`libs/acp`) and Pi. OpenHands Agent Canvas uses it to run any of them.
- *Evidence:* Convergence across every surveyed harness. Cline ships a headless CLI for CI, and Pi offers print/JSON and RPC modes. — [/goal docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal); [exec_events.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/exec/src/exec_events.rs); [OpenHands README](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/blob/main/README.md)
- *When to use / when not:* Always ship both a JSONL headless mode and an SDK. Add ACP for IDE reach.

**Lazy sandbox provisioning**
- *What it is:* Do not create the execution container until the first tool call needs it.
- *Mechanics:* The harness starts sampling immediately and calls `provision()` on demand.
- *Evidence:* It cut p50 time-to-first-token by about 60% and p95 by more than 90%. Harness architecture affects latency independently of the model. — [Managed Agents](https://anthropic.com/engineering/managed-agents)
- *When to use / when not:* Use it in any hosted or multi-tenant harness. It does not matter for a local CLI, where the host machine is the sandbox. Pair it with pre-warmed pools when tool use is near-certain (latency lever from the production-operations notes).

**Durable execution, idempotent tools and rainbow deployments**
- *What it is:* Each model call and each side-effecting tool call becomes a persisted step, so a replay neither re-bills nor repeats side effects. Deployments never break in-flight agents.
- *Mechanics:*
  - Temporal + OpenAI Agents SDK (GA 2026-03-23): agents run inside a Workflow, each model invocation is an Activity, enabled with `OpenAIAgentsPlugin`; `activity_as_tool` exposes Activities as durable tools.
  - Alternatives (secondary vendor comparisons): Restate (keyed "Virtual Objects"), Inngest (event-driven steps), DBOS (Postgres-backed workflows).
  - Idempotency keys come from `(workflow_id, step_id)`. The notes' reference architecture uses `hash(session_id, step_idx, tool_call_id)`.
  - Anthropic's research agent "built systems that can resume from where the agent was when the errors occurred", uses checkpoints and retry logic, tells agents when a tool is failing, and uses **rainbow deployments** (traffic shifts gradually while both versions run).
- *Evidence:* "Minor failures" in long stateful runs compound. — [Anthropic multi-agent research system](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/multi-agent-research-system); [Temporal blog](https://temporal.io/blog/announcing-openai-agents-sdk-integration); [AppScale durable execution 2026](https://appscale.blog/en/blog/durable-execution-llm-agents-temporal-langgraph-checkpointing-2026) (secondary)
- *When to use / when not:* Use it for hosted, long-running or side-effecting agents. A local CLI can rely on its JSONL log plus resume. Never mutate a running workflow's prompt or tool set.

**Workflow patterns as composable outer structure** (Anthropic taxonomy, 2024-12-19)
- *What it is:* Five predefined-code-path patterns. The modern harness offers them as optional wrappers around the core loop rather than as alternatives to it.
- *Mechanics and when to use each:*
  - **Prompt chaining:** fixed subtask decomposition with programmatic gates between steps; "trade off latency for higher accuracy".
  - **Routing:** distinct input categories that can be classified accurately, for example sending easy queries to smaller models.
  - **Parallelization.** *Sectioning* runs independent subtasks, such as a guardrail call alongside the response call. *Voting* runs the same task several times when "multiple perspectives or attempts are needed".
  - **Orchestrator-workers:** when you "can't predict the subtasks needed", for example multi-file code changes.
  - **Evaluator-optimizer:** when criteria are clear and iteration "provides measurable value".
  - **Autonomous agents** are "typically just LLMs using tools based on environmental feedback in a loop". They need "ground truth from the environment" at each step, may pause at checkpoints for human feedback, and need stopping conditions such as "a maximum number of iterations".
  - Three principles: simplicity, transparency (show planning steps), and a carefully crafted agent-computer interface (ACI). Poka-yoke example: requiring absolute file paths eliminated a class of SWE-bench errors.
- *2026 mapping into the harness:*
  - router → model/effort routing per subagent
  - chaining → plan-mode gate, then implement
  - parallelization → read-only parallel tools and subagent fan-out
  - orchestrator-workers → subagents or dynamic workflows
  - evaluator-optimizer → Stop-hook / `/goal` evaluator, Codex goal completion audit, planner/generator/evaluator

  The OpenAI Agents SDK adds **handoffs** as a third output class of the core loop, next to final output and tool calls.
- *Evidence:* Evaluator-optimizer has become the most important pattern for long-horizon work. It appears as Anthropic's evaluator agent and `/goal` evaluator, Codex's completion audit, and LangChain's self-verification. "Find the simplest solution possible, and only increasing complexity when needed." There is no quantitative head-to-head comparison of the patterns. — [Building effective agents](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/building-effective-agents); [running_agents.md](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/main/docs/running_agents.md)
- *When to use / when not:* Default to the single loop. Add an outer pattern only when an eval shows it is load-bearing, and keep each pattern behind configuration so it can be removed when a newer model no longer needs it.

**Loop taxonomy by trigger** (Loop engineering, 2026-06-30)
- *What it is:* Classify loops by what starts and stops them.
  - **Turn-based:** user-prompted; stops when Claude judges the work done. Improve them with verification skills.
  - **Goal-based** (`/goal`): stops when "an evaluator model checks the condition each time Claude tries to stop", or at max turns. Best for verifiable exit criteria.
  - **Time-based** (`/loop`, `/schedule`): runs on an interval.
  - **Proactive:** event- or schedule-triggered with no human in real time. Route routine work to smaller models.
- *Mechanics:* Expose each trigger as a harness feature. In Claude Code: `/loop` (local interval), `/schedule` and "routines" (cloud; cron, API or GitHub events), and dynamic workflows (rerunnable scripts).
- *Evidence:* Recommendations from the post: "Start with the simplest solution", make verification quantitative, and "Use a separate reviewer agent with fresh context". — [Loop engineering](https://claude.com/blog/getting-started-with-loops)
- *When to use / when not:* Use goal loops only when the exit condition can be judged from the transcript (see §2.3). Proactive loops need hard budgets, because no human is watching.

**Hooks as the control plane**
- *What it is:* Lifecycle callbacks that can block a tool, rewrite its input, veto a stop, inject context or audit, without consuming model context ("don't consume context").
- *Mechanics (Claude Code):*
  - Events, in lifecycle order: `SessionStart`, `Setup`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `UserPromptExpansion`, `PreToolUse`, `PermissionRequest`, `PermissionDenied`, `PostToolUse`, `PostToolUseFailure`, `PostToolBatch`, `Notification`, `SubagentStart`/`SubagentStop`, `TaskCreated`/`TaskCompleted`, `Stop`, `StopFailure`, `TeammateIdle`, `InstructionsLoaded`, `ConfigChange`, `CwdChanged`, `FileChanged`, `WorktreeCreate`/`WorktreeRemove`, `PreCompact`/`PostCompact`, `PreModelSwitch`/`PostModelSwitch`, `Elicitation`/`ElicitationResult`, `SessionEnd`.
  - Hook types: `command`, `http`, `mcp_tool`, `prompt` (a single-turn LLM decision) and `agent` (a subagent with tools; experimental; up to 50 tool-use turns).
  - Default timeouts: 600 s for command, http and mcp_tool; 30 s for prompt; 60 s for agent.
  - Exit code `2` is a blocking error, and stderr becomes the reason.
  - `PreToolUse` returns `hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision` ∈ {`allow`, `deny`, `ask`, `defer`} plus `updatedInput`, which rewrites the arguments.
  - A Stop hook returns `{"decision":"block","reason":…}` to force continuation, or `{"continue": false, "stopReason": …}` to halt. Its input includes `last_assistant_message`.
  - Hook input includes `permission_mode`.
  - The Python SDK's `HookEvent` set: `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `PostToolUseFailure`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `Stop`, `SubagentStop`, `PreCompact`, `Notification`, `SubagentStart`, `PermissionRequest`.
- *Mechanics (Codex):*
  - Event names match Claude Code's. The architecture notes list `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `Stop`, `SessionStart`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `SubagentStop`, `SessionEnd`, `PreCompact`, `PostCompact` and `PermissionRequest`; the open-source repo survey's crate listing omits `SessionEnd` (unreconciled).
  - Stop hooks block with "continuation fragments" that are injected as a prompt message. A block without a prompt is ignored with the warning "Stop hook requested continuation without a prompt; ignoring the block."
- *Mechanics (Gemini CLI):* A different vocabulary that adds model-level hooks Claude and Codex lack: `BeforeModel`, `AfterModel`, `BeforeToolSelection`.
- *Evidence:* The two leading harnesses share near-identical names and semantics, so matching them gives free ecosystem compatibility. Hooks are also features of Kimi Code, Letta Code, the OpenHands SDK and Cline. — [Hooks reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks); [hooks guide](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide); [codex hooks](https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/main/codex-rs/hooks/src); [types.py](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python/blob/main/src/claude_agent_sdk/types.py); [Gemini hooks/types.ts](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/main/packages/core/src/hooks/types.ts)
- *When to use / when not:* Put enforcement (deny rules, test-file immutability, quality gates) in hooks rather than prompts. CLAUDE.md and auto memory are "context, not enforced configuration". Keep hooks fast, because the default command timeout of 600 s can stall the loop.

**Permission modes, and plan mode as a separate state from the plan tool**
- *What it is:* A small set of named permission states that the loop consults before each tool call. Plan mode is a read-only *mode* that ends in an approvable plan artifact. It is not the same thing as the todo/`update_plan` *tool*.
- *Mechanics:*
  - **Agent SDK `permission_mode`:**
    - `"default"`: a `canUseTool` callback; with no callback, deny.
    - `"acceptEdits"`: auto-runs reads, edits and common FS commands (mkdir/touch/mv/cp).
    - `"plan"`: no source edits; only reads and read-only shell.
    - `"dontAsk"`: never prompts; anything not pre-approved is denied; for headless use.
    - `"auto"`: a model classifier reviews actions.
    - `"bypassPermissions"`: isolated environments only. In TypeScript it also needs `allowDangerouslySkipPermissions: true`, and it cannot be used as root.

    Rules can be scoped, for example `"Bash(npm *)"`.
  - **Codex** has sandbox modes (`read_only`, `workspace_write`, `danger_full_access`) crossed with approval policies, plus a guardian auto-reviewer.
  - **Codex Plan Mode** ends in a `<proposed_plan>` that must be "decision complete" so another agent can implement it, and `update_plan` errors in this mode.
  - **OpenCode** has a `plan` agent (read-only, denies edits, asks before bash).
  - **Gemini CLI** has `enter-plan-mode`/`exit-plan-mode` tools plus a `plan.toml` policy.
  - In Claude Code, plan-mode content and skill loading *append* messages rather than editing the prompt prefix, which keeps the cache.
- *Evidence:* Claude Code and Codex both separate mode from tool. Auto mode data: users approved 93% of prompts; the classifier's FPR is 0.4% and its FNR is 17%. Sandboxing alone gave an 84% reduction in permission prompts ([Claude Code sandboxing](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/claude-code-sandboxing), 2025-10-20). — [agent-loop docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/agent-loop); [codex plan.md](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/collaboration-mode-templates/templates/plan.md); [Anthropic auto mode](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/claude-code-auto-mode); [Claude Code prompt caching](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/prompt-caching)
- *When to use / when not:* Plan mode pays off on ambiguous or multi-file tasks where the user wants to approve scope. Skip it for trivial edits. Pi deliberately omits plan mode, which is evidence that it can be an add-on rather than core.

**Skills, slash commands, plugins and mods as packaging**
- *What it is:* Procedures packaged as folders that are loaded on demand. User shortcuts are sent as plain prompts. Third-party extensions bundle commands, agents, hooks and MCP servers.
- *Mechanics:*
  - **Skills** use three-level progressive disclosure:
    - metadata (`name` up to 64 characters, plus `description`), always loaded, about 100 tokens per skill
    - the SKILL.md body (under 5k tokens; keep it under 500 lines), loaded when triggered
    - bundled resources (`scripts/`, `references/`, `assets/`), zero tokens until read
  - "Claude sees skill descriptions at session start, but the full content only loads when a skill is used". `disable-model-invocation: true` keeps a skill's description out of context.
  - After compaction, Claude Code re-injects invoked skill bodies, capped at 5,000 tokens per skill and 25,000 in total.
  - **Slash commands** in the SDK are sent "as a prompt string".
  - **Plugins** install via `/plugin` marketplaces (`/plugin marketplace add anthropics/skills`).
  - **Mods** are hook middleware (`register(on, options)`, `($, e, next)`).
- *Evidence:* Skills launched 2025-10-16 and became an open standard on 2025-12-18. They have been adopted by Codex (`skills` crate, `skills/list` RPC), the Agents SDK (`Skills(lazy_from=…)`), Gemini CLI (`activate-skill`), deepagents, Letta Code (`.agents/skills`), Pi, OpenHands SDK and Crush. Secondary sources report about 40–44 clients by mid-2026, and one analysis found 22% of 673 sampled skills failed structural validation. Single-agent-with-skills matched multi-agent accuracy (+0.7%) with 54% fewer tokens and 50% lower latency, but selection degrades beyond about 50–100 skills. — [How Claude Code works](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/how-claude-code-works); [Agent Skills overview](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/overview); [arXiv 2601.04748](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2601.04748) (snippet)
- *When to use / when not:* Put procedures in skills, always-true facts in CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, and actions in tools. Cap the size of the skill catalogue, or use search over it. Audit third-party skills, because malicious skills can exfiltrate data.

**Session persistence: resume, fork, checkpoints, rewind, external session stores**
- *What it is:* Durable transcripts plus file snapshots, so the user or host can continue, branch or undo.
- *Mechanics:*
  - **Claude Code:** JSONL under `~/.claude/projects/`; `--continue`/`--resume [name|path]`/`/resume`; `--fork-session` or `/branch`; Esc Esc → `/rewind` (code+conversation, conversation only, or code only); checkpoints auto-cleaned after 30 days.
  - **Agent SDK:** capture `ResultMessage.session_id`; use `resume`, `fork_session` and `session_store` (dual-write to your backend); `enable_file_checkpointing` tracks Write/Edit/NotebookEdit only.
  - **Codex:** `resume` and `fork` subcommands; `thread/fork`, `thread/revert`.
  - **Agents SDK:** conversation state is client-side (`to_input_list()`), an SDK `session`, a server `conversation_id`, or `previous_response_id` chaining. These are mutually exclusive. A paused run resumes from a `RunState`.
- *Evidence:* All major harnesses implement this. Checkpoints cannot undo remote side effects or Bash edits. — [How Claude Code works](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/how-claude-code-works); [agent-loop docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/agent-loop); [running_agents.md](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/main/docs/running_agents.md)
- *When to use / when not:* Always provide it. Add git-stash or worktree snapshots to cover Bash side effects.

**Choosing the multi-agent tier as an architectural decision** (details in the multi-agent section)
- *What it is:* Agent count is a compute and context-isolation knob. Each tier has a distinct coordination model.
- *Mechanics (Claude Code tiers):*
  - **Subagents:** "a few delegated tasks per turn". Own context; only the final report returns; depth 3 (`CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH`); 20 concurrent (`CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS`); background by default; forks inherit full history.
  - **Agent teams:** "a handful of long-running peers" (`CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1`).
  - **Dynamic workflows:** "dozens to hundreds of agents per run"; 16 concurrent by default (1–256); 4,096 items per `parallel()`/`pipeline()`; 1,000 agents per run; deterministic replay.
  - **Peer swarm** (C compiler): a bash `while true` relaunching `claude`, Docker per agent, a bare git upstream, and `current_tasks/` lock files.
- *Evidence:*
  - Multi-agent research beat single-agent Opus 4 by 90.2%, at about 15× chat tokens. Token usage explained 80% of BrowseComp variance.
  - Controlled scaling (arXiv 2512.08296; snippet): +81% on Finance-Agent, but −39% to −70% on sequential PlanCraft; independent agents amplified errors 17.2×; returns diminish once the single-agent baseline exceeds about 45%.

  — [Anthropic multi-agent research system](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/multi-agent-research-system); [workflows](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows); [building-c-compiler](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/building-c-compiler)
- *When to use / when not:* Default to one agent. Use fan-out only for parallelizable, read-heavy or independently verifiable work, and always end a fan-out in a verifier or merge step. Writes should stay single-threaded, or be strictly partitioned with an oracle.

**Thin core plus thick, optional control-plane middleware**
- *What it is:* Keep the loop minimal (linear history, a few general tools, bash/exec as the universal tool), and put the measured gains in pluggable middleware:
  - verification gates
  - loop and no-progress detection
  - time and token budget warnings
  - compaction
  - goal evaluators
- *Mechanics:*
  - mini-swe-agent is the ablation floor: a ~100-line agent class, bash only, "doesn't even need to use the tool-calling interface", "completely linear history … no difference between the trajectory and the messages", and `subprocess.run` per action, so sandboxing is a swap to `docker exec`.
  - deepagents implements the middleware stack (summarization, blob offload, message eviction, overflow clipping, prompt caching, subagents, skills, memory, permissions, `patch_tool_calls`).
- *Evidence:*
  - LangChain's +13.7 points on TB 2.0 came from middleware (time-budget warnings; loop detection that tracks edit counts per file) "without touching the underlying model" (secondary).
  - mini-swe-agent scores above 74% on SWE-bench Verified, and it is used by Meta, NVIDIA, Essential AI, IBM, Nebius, Anyscale, Princeton and Stanford.
  - Pi's high adoption with a 4-tool core is further evidence.

  — [mini-swe-agent README](https://github.com/SWE-agent/mini-swe-agent); [explainx.ai summary](https://www.explainx.ai/blog/agent-harness-engineering-terminal-bench-langchain-2026) (secondary)
- *When to use / when not:* Always build so the harness can be ablated down to the mini-swe-agent configuration as a control condition. Add each middleware behind a flag.

**Per-model prompt and tool profiles (match the training distribution)**
- *What it is:* Present each model with the system prompt, tool names, tool shapes and edit format it was post-trained on.
- *Mechanics:*
  - **OpenAI/Codex models:** the `apply_patch` envelope as a grammar-constrained freeform tool, plus `shell`/`exec_command`, `update_plan`, and model-specific prompt files. OpenAI says: "We strongly recommend using our exact apply_patch implementation as the model has been trained to excel at this diff format."
  - **Claude:** `Read`/`Edit`/`Bash`/`TodoWrite`-style tools with `str_replace` edits. This is inferred from the Claude Code SDK uplift, not from a confirmed Anthropic training disclosure.
  - **DeepSeek:** native tool role and reasoning replay.
  - Aider's per-model edit-format table is the template for selection.
- *Evidence:*
  - Codex repo per-model prompts (`gpt_5_codex_prompt.md`, …).
  - GPT-5.3-Codex tries to call a non-existent `apply_patch` in harnesses that lack it (secondary).
  - Claude-4.5-Opus gains 20.5% inside the Claude Code SDK compared with a generalist scaffold (AgencyBench).
  - Opus 4.5 on SWE-bench Pro scored 45.9% in Scale's SEAL scaffold vs 55.4% in Claude Code (secondary; unverified against Scale).
  - GPT-5.2-Codex scored 64.7% in Codex CLI vs 57.5% in Terminus-2 (secondary).

  — [codex-rs/core](https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/main/codex-rs/core); [OpenAI Codex Prompting Guide](https://developers.openai.com/cookbook/examples/gpt-5/codex_prompting_guide); [zenn.dev](https://zenn.dev/c_c/articles/188a9bef9f3290?locale=en); [AgencyBench arXiv 2601.11044](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2601.11044); [particula.tech](https://particula.tech/blog/agent-scaffolding-beats-model-upgrades-swe-bench)
- *When to use / when not:* Always use it for frontier vendor models. For self-hosted open weights, use the vendor's reference encoder (DeepSeek `encoding_dsv4.py`, Harmony for gpt-oss).

**Scaffold pruning by one-at-a-time ablation**
- *What it is:* Treat every harness component as a hypothesis about model weakness. Re-run evals with each component removed, one at a time, on every new model.
- *Mechanics:*
  - Anthropic removed components one at a time to find which were load-bearing. On Opus 4.6, sprints were removed and the evaluator moved to a single end-of-run pass; the planner was kept because without it the generator under-scoped.
  - Context resets were dropped once Opus 4.5 no longer showed "context anxiety".
  - Todo tools are off by default after Opus 4.7, Sonnet 4.6 and Haiku 4.5.
- *Evidence:* "The space of useful harness combinations shifts as models improve rather than shrinking." — [Harness design](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/harness-design-long-running-apps); [Track todos](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/todo-tracking)
- *When to use / when not:* Do this on every model upgrade. Keep the old configuration available for older or weaker models.

**Model-agnostic backends via an Anthropic-compatible endpoint plus model aliasing**
- *What it is:* Write the harness against the Anthropic Messages API (or a Responses-compatible API) with a configurable base URL and a model-alias map.
- *Mechanics:* DeepSeek's `https://api.deepseek.com/anthropic` with `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`. `anthropic-beta`/`anthropic-version` are ignored, and model names map `claude-opus*` → `deepseek-v4-pro`, others → `deepseek-v4-flash` (search summary).
- *Evidence:* Claude Code, OpenCode, OpenClaw and CodeBuddy reportedly drive DeepSeek V4 this way (secondary). — [api-docs.deepseek.com anthropic_api](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/anthropic_api)
- *When to use / when not:* It is the cheapest way to get multi-provider support. Beta features (compaction blocks, context editing, MCP tool-use blocks) silently degrade on compatible endpoints, so feature-detect them.

**Cache-aware layering of the prompt** (architecture constraint; details in the context-engineering section)
- *What it is:* Fix the serialization order so the prefix never changes mid-session.
- *Mechanics:*
  - The order is `[tools (stable; most deferred)] → [system (stable)] → [project instructions/skills index] → [append-only conversation]`.
  - Dynamic data (time, budgets, todo recitation, file-change notices) is appended as messages. Claude Code appends a `<system-reminder>` on file edits rather than rewriting earlier reads, and applies CLAUDE.md edits only after `/clear`, `/compact` or a restart.
  - On Claude 5.x, mid-conversation `{"role":"system"}` messages and turn-scoped system messages (beta `mid-conversation-system-clear-at-2026-08-21`, `clear_at: "next_user_message"`) add dynamic content without breaking the prefix. Tool changes go through `tool_addition`/`tool_removal` (beta `inline-tools-2026-09-15`).
- *Evidence:* Manus input:output is about 100:1. Cached Sonnet input costs $0.30/MTok vs $3/MTok uncached. Anthropic cache reads cost 0.1× base (0.05× on Opus/Sonnet 5.5; 0.025× on Fable/Mythos 5.1). — [Claude Code prompt caching](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/prompt-caching); [Mid-conversation system messages](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-system-messages); [Prompt caching](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching)
- *When to use / when not:* This is a hard architectural constraint for any harness that pays per input token.

**Self-improving harness loops** (optional)
- *What it is:* Use agents to optimize the harness itself: prompts, tool descriptions and harness code.
- *Mechanics:*
  - **Anthropic** (2025-09-11): prototype tools as a local MCP server → have Claude Code generate eval tasks → run → collect metrics → paste transcripts back to refactor the tools → validate on a held-out set.
  - **DGM:** an archive of agent variants, where a foundation model edits the agent's own harness code.
  - **GEPA/ACE:** reflective prompt evolution, or evolving playbooks.
- *Evidence:*
  - Claude-optimized Slack and Asana MCP servers beat human-written ones on held-out tests.
  - DGM: SWE-bench 20.0% → 50.0%; Polyglot 14.2% → 30.7%.
  - GEPA beats GRPO by about 6% on average with up to 35× fewer rollouts.

  — [Writing effective tools](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/writing-tools-for-agents); [Sakana DGM](https://sakana.ai/dgm/); [arXiv 2507.19457](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.19457)
- *When to use / when not:* Only once a solid eval suite exists. Gate code self-modification behind isolated sandboxes and hidden verifiers.
