### 1.7 Build checklist for our harness

1. **Event log first.** Persist every user message, model message (including reasoning items and signatures), tool call, tool result, hook decision, compaction and checkpoint as an append-only event keyed by `session_id`. Never mutate it. Build each prompt by projecting the log (an OpenHands-style `View`). Record compaction as a new event, and store derived projections separately with a hash of the canonical prefix they summarize (Cline pattern).
2. **Split the packages.** Use a stateless loop package (iteration, tool orchestration, events, hooks) and a stateful core (sessions, persistence, compaction policy, RPC). Host apps (CLI, IDE, server, CI) depend only on the core.
3. **Put the sandbox behind `execute(name, input) → string`.** Provision lazily on the first tool call (expect roughly −60% p50 TTFT in hosted mode) and keep a warm pool for hosted tenants. Convert sandbox death into a tool-error result so the model can retry. Never lose the session when a sandbox dies.
4. **Hook engine compatible with Claude Code and Codex.**
   - Events: at minimum `SessionStart`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `PreToolUse`, `PermissionRequest`, `PostToolUse`, `PostToolUseFailure`, `Stop`, `SubagentStop`, `PreCompact`, `PostCompact`, `SessionEnd`.
   - Semantics: exit code `2` = block with stderr as the reason; JSON `permissionDecision` (`allow`/`deny`/`ask`/`defer`) plus `updatedInput`; Stop `decision: "block"` plus `reason`, or `continue: false`.
   - Hook types: `command`, `http`, `prompt`, `agent`, with default timeouts of 600 / 600 / 30 / 60 s.
   - Optionally add Gemini-style `BeforeModel`/`AfterModel`.
5. **Permission modes.** Implement `default` (callback, else deny), `acceptEdits`, `plan` (read-only; ends in an approvable plan artifact), `dontAsk` (headless; deny anything not pre-approved), `auto` (classifier) and `bypass` (isolated environments only, never as root). Scoped rules use a `Tool(pattern)` syntax with deny precedence. Escalate after 3 consecutive or 20 total classifier denials, and terminate headless runs at that point. Keep plan *mode* separate from the plan/todo *tool*.
6. **Sessions UX.** Provide `--continue`, `--resume <id|name>`, fork/branch, rewind (code+conversation, conversation only, code only), file snapshots before every edit (retain 30 days), and git-stash or worktree snapshots for Bash side effects. Offer a session-store adapter so stateless hosts can dual-write transcripts.
7. **Client protocols.**
   - Expose a thread/turn/item JSON-RPC (mirror Codex `turn/start|steer|interrupt`, item approvals and delta events).
   - Provide a JSONL headless mode reusing Codex `exec --json` event names (`thread.started`, `turn.started`, `item.*`, `turn.completed|failed`, `error`).
   - Provide an SDK that spawns the binary and speaks NDJSON plus control requests (`can_use_tool`, `hook_callback`, `mcp_message`).
   - Provide an ACP server for IDEs and control centers.
8. **Instructions and skills.**
   - Load hierarchical AGENTS.md (root → cwd, `AGENTS.override.md`, a byte budget), and CLAUDE.md when present.
   - Support SKILL.md with three-level disclosure: ~100-token metadata always loaded; body loaded on trigger; resources loaded on read. Honour `disable-model-invocation`, and re-inject invoked skills after compaction, capped at 5k tokens each and 25k in total.
   - Treat slash commands as prompt strings. Plugins bundle commands, agents, hooks and MCP servers.
9. **Per-model profiles.** For each model family store:
   - system prompt file
   - tool set and names
   - edit format (`apply_patch` freeform grammar for OpenAI Codex-family models; `str_replace`-style for Claude)
   - reasoning-replay adapter (§2)
   - default effort
   - base URL and model-alias map (for DeepSeek's Anthropic-compatible endpoint)
10. **Multi-agent behind hard caps.** Default subagent depth is 3, concurrency 20, plus a session dollar budget. Subagents are background by default and return only condensed reports. Run large fan-outs through a deterministic, resumable script runtime with schema-validated outputs (up to 5 retries) and a final verify/merge stage. Add an explicit delegation-policy line for models that over-delegate (Opus 5).
11. **Hosted durability.** Make each model call and each side-effecting tool call a persisted step with idempotency key `hash(session_id, step_idx, tool_call_id)`; mark read-only tools retry-safe. Deploy with rainbow (gradual) traffic shifts, and never mutate a running session's prompt or tool set.
12. **Cache-stable layering.** Fix the order to tools → system → project instructions and skills index → append-only conversation. Append dynamic content as messages (turn-scoped system messages on Claude 5.x). Change tools via deferred loading or `tool_addition`, never by editing `tools`. Target a cache-read share of input tokens above 80–90%.
13. **Ablation configuration.** Ship a `--minimal` profile equivalent to mini-swe-agent (bash only, linear history, no hooks or middleware), and put every scaffold behind a flag. On each model release, re-run the eval suite removing one component at a time. Report harness version, model, effort, number of runs (at least 5 for TB2) and mean ± SE.
14. **Tracing.** Emit OTel-style `invoke_agent` → `chat` → `execute_tool` spans, plus custom spans for compaction, subagent spawn and approval waits. Tag every session with harness version, model, effort, and the git SHA of prompts and tools.

### 1.8 Pitfalls and anti-patterns

- **Co-locating session, harness and sandbox in one container.** A container failure loses the session. Anthropic's first Managed Agents design had exactly this problem.
- **Treating the compacted context as the source of truth.** Compaction, the memory tool and trimming are irreversible. Keep the raw log.
- **Mutating the prompt prefix mid-session.** This covers timestamps in the system prompt, editing CLAUDE.md and expecting it live, adding or removing tools or MCP servers, and switching model or effort on models where that busts the cache. Each causes full cache misses at 10× input price.
- **Hard-coding scaffolds that a newer model no longer needs** (context resets, sprints, todo lists). They become "dead weight" and cost tokens and latency.
- **Reading harness benchmark claims without controls.** Comparisons are only meaningful with a fixed model, the same benchmark version (TB 2.0 and 2.1 differ), multiple runs (2.2–6.0 pts of single-run noise) and controlled infrastructure noise. Watch for partial-credit vs strict scoring and for "fallback-assisted" counting.
- **Giving a vendor model an unfamiliar tool surface.** For example, GPT-5.3-Codex calls a non-existent `apply_patch` when the harness lacks it.
- **Simulating tool results as user messages.** DeepSeek V3.2 discards reasoning on user messages, and the report names Roo Code and Terminus as frameworks that do this.
- **Unbounded delegation.** Opus 5 delegates more readily. Without a prompt policy and hard depth, concurrency and budget caps, cost explodes.
- **Using multi-agent for sequential, tightly coupled work** (−39% to −70% on PlanCraft). Independent parallel agents without a central verifier amplify errors 17.2×.
- **Misreading `allowed_tools` as an availability filter.** It only pre-approves tools.
- **Trusting weak sandboxes.** The Agents SDK UnixLocal client adds "no OS-level confinement" on Linux, and smolagents' `LocalPythonExecutor` "is not a security sandbox". `bypassPermissions` belongs in isolated environments only.
- **Assuming checkpoints cover everything.** SDK checkpoints miss Bash side effects, and no checkpoint undoes remote side effects.
- **Tight coupling to one harness or vendor canvas.** Roo Code shut down, Kimi CLI was archived, and Agent Builder deprecation has been reported. Build on protocols (MCP, AGENTS.md, Skills, ACP) instead.
- **Planning to fork Claude Code or the TS SDK.** Both are under Commercial Terms; only their open interfaces can be replicated.
- **Letting the skill catalogue grow without bound.** Selection accuracy degrades beyond about 50–100 skills, and 22% of sampled public skills failed structural validation.
- **Assuming a compatible endpoint supports everything.** Anthropic beta headers are ignored by DeepSeek's endpoint, and MCP tool-use blocks are reportedly unsupported. Feature-detect.
- **Leaving unknown custom-model windows unconfigured.** Cline will not auto-compact, so set context windows explicitly for custom models.
- **Expecting CLAUDE.md or memory to enforce policy.** They are "context, not enforced configuration". Use hooks or managed settings for enforcement.

### 1.9 Open questions and unverified claims

- **OpenAI posts not read.** The full texts of "Unrolling the Codex agent loop" (2026-01-23) and its follow-ups, "Harness engineering" (2026-02-11) and "A practical guide to building agents" (Apr 2025) were unreachable. Their details here come from codex-rs source or search snippets.
- **The 2026-08-20 "Codex harness" open-sourcing** is reported only by secondary outlets and is unverified.
- **DeepSeek's harness status is contradictory.** One set of notes found no DeepSeek-authored harness; another reports `deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness` (MIT, v0.1 around 2026-08-13) with a near-empty README. Its loop, tools and architecture are undocumented in the notes.
- **Terminal-Bench harness deltas are secondary and partly inconsistent.** Claude Code + Fable is 83.1% in one source and 83.8% on Snorkel. Opus 4.6 is 58.0% in Claude Code vs 74.7% in Terminus-KIRA, the opposite direction. tbench.ai, snorkel.ai and blog.langchain.com were unreachable.
- **No controlled, peer-reviewed study isolates harness effects across many models.** The "agent harness survey" ([Preprints.org 202604.0428](https://preprints.org/manuscript/202604.0428)) was found but not read. There is no primary OpenAI or Anthropic statement quantifying harness-only deltas on SWE-bench.
- **Claude Code internals are closed**: system prompt, built-in tool schemas (Edit, TodoWrite, Agent) and compaction thresholds. There is no primary confirmation that Claude is RL-trained on Claude Code's exact toolset.
- **When auto mode became the default** is unclear: v2.1.283 per the docs, or 2026-08-14 for new Pro/Max/Team sessions per a search summary. The Mar 25, 2026 auto-mode post was read only via the tools notes.
- **Agent Builder dates conflict**: deprecation notices on 2026-06-03 and shutdown on 2026-11-30, per secondary sources.
- **Codex hook event list.** Whether it includes `SessionEnd` differs between the two note sets.
- **No quantitative comparisons** of the workflow patterns, or of agent teams vs subagents vs workflows, were found.
- **Protocol specs not read in depth.** The Codex app-server protocol, the ACP spec (agentclientprotocol.com) and the agentskills.io spec text were not fetched.
- **Durable-execution vendor APIs are unverified**: Restate, Inngest and DBOS agent APIs come from secondary vendor comparisons only.
- **Two Anthropic posts are title-only**: "Quantifying infrastructure noise in agentic coding evals" (2026-02-05) was not read, and its numbers are unknown.
- **DGM transfer is unknown.** There is no data on whether DGM-style evolved harnesses transfer across model versions.
- **Exact OTel attribute names** for cache tokens, and the current semantic-conventions release, are unverified.

## 2. The agent loop and long-horizon control

> **SOTA in one paragraph:** Every major harness runs the same inner loop (sample the model, execute any tool calls, append the results in the native tool-result role, sample again) and stops only when the last response has no tool calls, no user input is queued, and the Stop hooks or goal evaluator allow it. The differences lie in the control plane around that loop: layered budgets (max turns, dollars or tokens checked after each response, stream idle timeouts), a split between retryable and terminal errors (Codex defaults: 5 stream retries, 4 request retries, 300 s idle timeout), mid-turn steering and interrupts, scheduling that runs read-only tools in parallel and mutating tools serially, in-loop compaction at about 90% of the window with a thrash guard, and correct replay of reasoning state (Anthropic signed thinking blocks, OpenAI encrypted reasoning items with `store:false`, DeepSeek `reasoning_content`). Reasoning is now native, interleaved between tool calls, and set per session with an `effort` enum from `low` to `max` (Opus 5.5 defaults to `medium`), so separate think tools and written todo lists are optional, and Anthropic turns todo tools off by default on its newest models. In 2026 both labs added an outer loop that vetoes premature stops: Claude Code `/goal` (a prompt-based Stop hook judged by a small evaluator model) and Codex thread goals (token budgets, a no-progress check, a completion audit that must *prove* completion, and a blocked status allowed only after the same blocker repeats for three turns). These sit alongside the older Ralph loop and the initializer + progress-file + git multi-session harness. Multi-hour runs are now routine (Anthropic reports 4–6-hour app builds; OpenAI reports internal runs of more than 24 hours), but the labs also report that scaffolds such as context resets and sprints became dead weight on newer models, so every long-horizon mechanism should be feature-flagged and re-evaluated for each model.

### 2.1 Where the field is (Nov 2026)

**Consensus positions**

- **The core loop is the same everywhere.**
  - *Claude Agent SDK:* "runs the same execution loop that powers Claude Code" and repeats "until it produces a response with no tool calls".
  - *Codex:* after each inference the model either "(1) produces a final response … or (2) requests a tool call". "An agent could decide to make hundreds of tool calls in a single turn," so context management is the agent's responsibility.
  - *OpenAI Agents SDK:* final output ends the loop, a handoff switches agents, and tool calls cause a re-run.
  - *DeepSeek V3.2:* "Before outputting the final answer, the model can perform multiple turns of reasoning and tool calls."
  - Sources: [agent-loop docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/agent-loop); [Unrolling the Codex agent loop](https://openai.com/index/unrolling-the-codex-agent-loop) (snippet); [running_agents.md](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/main/docs/running_agents.md); [DeepSeek Thinking Mode](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/thinking_mode/) (snippet)
- **Termination is a conjunction of three conditions.** The loop stops when (1) the last response has no tool calls, (2) no user input is pending, and (3) the Stop hooks or goal evaluator allow it. Codex implements this as `needs_follow_up = model_needs_follow_up || has_pending_input`, followed by `run_turn_stop_hooks`. Claude Code uses queued messages plus Stop hooks. — [turn.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/core/src/session/turn.rs); [hooks reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks)
- **Budgets are enforced in layers by the harness, not only by the prompt.**
  - Per-run turns: `max_turns`/`maxTurns` defaults to "No limit".
  - Cumulative spend: `max_budget_usd` defaults to "No limit", but the docs say "Setting a budget is a good default for production agents". It is checked after each response, so a run can overshoot by one response.
  - Tokens: Codex goal token budgets; Anthropic task budgets (beta header `task-budgets-2026-03-13`).
  - Wall-clock and idle time: Codex's stream idle timeout is 300 s.
  - Sources: [agent-loop docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/agent-loop); [Task budgets](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/task-budgets); [model-provider-info](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/model-provider-info/src/lib.rs)
- **Errors are split into retryable and terminal.** Transient stream or network errors get about 4–5 retries with backoff. Context overflow after compaction has failed, authentication failures, exhausted credit or usage limits, and budget exhaustion are terminal (or *pause* conditions in goal loops). Both labs make this split.
- **Users can steer mid-turn.** In Claude Code, a message typed while Claude is working is read "as soon as those calls finish, within the same turn". Codex exposes `turn/steer` and treats pending input as a reason to continue. — [How Claude Code works](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/how-claude-code-works); [app-server-protocol](https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/main/codex-rs/app-server-protocol)
- **Read-only tools run in parallel; mutating tools run serially.** Read-only tools (`Read`, `Glob`, `Grep`, and MCP tools marked read-only) "can run concurrently". `Edit`, `Write` and `Bash` "run sequentially". — [agent-loop docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/agent-loop)
- **Reasoning is native and interleaved, and effort is the main control.**
  - On Claude 4.7 and later, manual `budget_tokens` thinking is rejected with a 400. The replacement is `thinking: {type: "adaptive"}`, which "interleaves automatically", plus `output_config: {effort: ...}`.
  - Opus 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 default to `"medium"` effort; other effort-capable models default to `"high"`.
  - OpenAI's GPT-6 guidance lists `reasoning.effort` values `low`, `medium` (the default), `high`, `xhigh` and `max`.
  - Sources: [Extended thinking](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/extended-thinking); [upgrading-to-gpt-6-astra.md](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/skills/src/assets/samples/openai-docs/references/upgrading-to-gpt-6-astra.md)
- **Explicit plan and todo tools are now optional.** On models newer than Opus 4.7, Sonnet 4.6 and Haiku 4.5, Claude Code makes `TodoWrite` and the Task* tools opt-in: "Newer models track multi-step work without a written todo list". Codex keeps `update_plan` but says "do not treat a plan update as a substitute for doing the work". A plan tool's main value now is user-facing progress display and state that survives compaction. — [Track todos](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/todo-tracking); [goal continuation.md](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/ext/goal/templates/goals/continuation.md)
- **Outer goal loops arrived in 2026.** Claude Code `/goal` is "a wrapper around a session-scoped prompt-based Stop hook". Codex thread goals live in `codex-rs/ext/goal` and are driven by the app-server methods `thread/goal/set|get|clear`. In both, a separate check decides whether the work is really done before the agent is allowed to stop. — [/goal docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal); [codex ext/goal](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/ext/goal/templates/goals/continuation.md)
- **Long-horizon continuity has converged on two families.**
  1. *External-state continuity:*
     - initializer session
     - JSON feature list
     - progress log
     - `init.sh`
     - git commit per unit of work
     - fresh-context sessions
     - Ralph loops as the extreme case
  2. *In-model and in-harness continuity:*
     - models trained across compaction boundaries (GPT-5.1-Codex-Max, 2025-11-19)
     - in-loop compaction at about 90% of the window
     - goal loops with independent audits
- **Run durations are measured in hours.**
  - Anthropic: 4–6 hours per app build. The browser DAW build ran for about 3 h 50 m, and "the builder ran coherently for over two hours without sprints".
  - OpenAI observed GPT-5.1-Codex-Max working on tasks for more than 24 hours in internal evaluations (snippet).
  - Opus 4.5's reported METR-style 50% horizon is about 4 h 49 m (secondary), and Opus 4.6's reported 50% horizon is 14.5 hours (secondary, unverified).
  - Claude Mythos Preview's 50% horizon is at least 16 h (95% CI 8.5–55 h); METR says measurements above 16 hours are unreliable with its current task suite.
- **Scaffolds become dead weight.**
  - Context resets were "essential" for Sonnet 4.5's "context anxiety" but unnecessary on Opus 4.5.
  - Sprints were removed on Opus 4.6.
  - Todo tools are off by default on the newest models.
  - Sources: [Harness design](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/harness-design-long-running-apps); [Managed Agents](https://anthropic.com/engineering/managed-agents)
- **Models trained for autonomy now need explicit persistence prompting.**
  - OpenAI's 2026 guidance says newer models are "more likely to ask the user a question… This can cause it to stop when the user may expect it to… persist". It recommends "persist until the user's intended goal is complete… Do not stop at acknowledging capability… proposing a plan, or offering to continue." — [prompting-guide.md](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/skills/src/assets/samples/openai-docs/references/prompting-guide.md)
  - The Codex base prompt says "keep going until the query is completely resolved… Only terminate your turn when you are sure that the problem is solved." — [default.md](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/protocol/src/prompts/base_instructions/default.md)
