### 2.2 By lab

#### Anthropic

**Claude Agent SDK / Claude Code turn loop** ([agent-loop docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/agent-loop))

- **The five steps of a run.**
  1. Receive the prompt plus the system prompt, tool definitions and history. The SDK yields `SystemMessage` subtype `"init"`.
  2. Claude "may respond with text, request one or more tool calls, or both". The SDK yields one `AssistantMessage` per content block.
  3. Execute tools. Hooks "intercept, modify, or block tool calls before they run".
  4. Repeat "until it produces a response with no tool calls".
  5. Yield a final `AssistantMessage`, then a `ResultMessage` with the final text, usage, cost and `session_id`.
- **What counts as a turn.** A turn is one pass of model output plus tool execution, with no control returned to the caller. `max_turns`/`maxTurns` counts "each turn with tool calls, plus one for the final text-only response".
- **Spend cap.** `max_budget_usd`/`maxBudgetUsd` caps estimated spend and is checked *after* each model response, so spend "can therefore pass the cap by up to the cost of that one response", plus whatever running subagents spend.
  - Subagent spend counts toward the cap.
  - Once the cap is reached, spawning a subagent fails with `Budget limit reached`, and background subagents are stopped (Claude Code v2.1.217+).
- **Termination enum.** `ResultMessage.subtype` takes these values:
  - `success`
  - `error_max_turns`
  - `error_max_budget_usd`
  - `error_during_execution` (a cancelled request or a crash)
  - `error_max_structured_output_retries`

  Every subtype carries `total_cost_usd`, `usage`, `num_turns` and `session_id`. `stop_reason` is `end_turn`, `max_tokens` or `refusal`, and `null` after a crash.
- **Error behaviour depends on the input mode.**
  - Single-shot `query()` raises after yielding an error result.
  - A streaming-input session "stays alive" after an error result.
  - With streaming input, a message still queued when a turn hits max turns starts a new turn and resets the turn count, but the budget keeps accumulating.
- **Tool execution.**
  - Read-only tools run concurrently; state-modifying tools run sequentially.
  - Custom tools are sequential unless they set `readOnlyHint`.
  - A denied tool call comes back to Claude "as the tool result".
- **Effort.** Levels are `"low"`, `"medium"`, `"high"`, `"xhigh"` and `"max"`. Effort can be set per session or per subagent (`AgentDefinition.effort`) and is independent of thinking display.
- **Compaction in the SDK.** The SDK compacts automatically near the limit and emits `SystemMessage` `subtype: "compact_boundary"`. A `PreCompact` hook (trigger `manual` or `auto`) can archive the transcript. Compaction instructions can live in CLAUDE.md, because "CLAUDE.md content is re-injected on every request" while early instructions in the prompt may be lost.

**Claude Code interactive control** ([How Claude Code works](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/how-claude-code-works); [Context window](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/context-window); [Model config](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/model-config))

- **Interrupts.** "Press `Esc` to stop Claude immediately. The running tool call is canceled."
- **Steering.** "Type a correction and press Enter without stopping Claude… If Claude is running tool calls, it reads the message as soon as those calls finish, within the same turn."
- **Compaction thrash guard.** "If a single file or tool output is so large that context refills immediately after each summary, Claude Code stops auto-compacting after a few attempts and shows an error instead of looping."
- **Auto-compact thresholds.**
  - Native-1M models (Fable, Sonnet 5+, Haiku 5.5, Opus 4.7+) compact at about 967K.
  - Sonnet 4.6 and Opus 4.6 without extended context compact at 200K.
  - Overrides: `/autocompact 500k`, `autoCompactWindow`, `--autocompact`, or `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW` (highest precedence). A per-subagent `autoCompactWindow` is allowed (100k–1M).
- **What survives compaction.** After compaction Claude Code re-injects:
  - CLAUDE.md and unscoped rules
  - auto memory
  - the plan-mode plan
  - a fresh git status
  - invoked skill bodies (5k tokens each, 25k total)
  - up to 5 recently touched files (files over 5,000 tokens come back as path only)

  Background commands and subagents keep running, with a reminder so they are not duplicated. Since v2.1.198 the summarization request inherits the session's thinking configuration.
- **Subagent turn cap.** A subagent with `maxTurns` set has its output marked partial and resumable when it hits the cap. — [subagents](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents)

**Thinking, effort and budgets in the Claude API** ([Extended thinking](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/extended-thinking); [Context windows](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/context-windows); [Task budgets](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/task-budgets))

- **Interleaved thinking.** It "lets Claude think between tool calls within a single assistant turn". On Opus 4.5, Sonnet 4.5 and earlier Claude 4 models it needs the `interleaved-thinking-2025-05-14` beta header. Adaptive thinking (`thinking: {type: "adaptive"}`) "interleaves automatically".
- **Manual thinking budgets are deprecated.** `type: "enabled"` with `budget_tokens`: "Claude 4.7 and later models… reject requests that use it, returning a 400 error". Migration: drop `budget_tokens`, set `adaptive`, and use `output_config: {effort: ...}`.
- **Thinking-block retention.** "Claude Opus 4.5 and models numbered 4.6 and higher keep prior turns' thinking blocks in context and bill them as input". The context-windows docs list Opus 4.5+, Sonnet 4.6+, Haiku 5.5 and Fable/Mythos. Sonnet 4.5, Haiku 4.5 and earlier strip them.
  - Thinking blocks paired with tool results must be returned unmodified, with their signature.
  - On Claude 5.1+ models, thinking blocks before a compaction block are not carried forward.
- **Thinking settings and the prompt cache.** Changing `budget_tokens` or switching thinking mode invalidates prompt-cache breakpoints, so "pick a budget and hold it stable for the life of a cached conversation". The docs show a full re-creation of a 1,370-token cache after a budget change.
  - Claude Code lists "changing effort" as cache-busting *except* on Opus/Sonnet/Haiku 5.5 and Fable 5.1. — [Claude Code prompt caching](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/prompt-caching)
- **Effort defaults.** Opus 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 default to `"medium"`; other effort-capable models default to `"high"`. Secondary sources say the API default dropped from "high" on Opus 5 to "medium" on Opus 5.5, and that this changes benchmark scores. — [Vellum](https://www.vellum.ai/blog/claude-opus-5-5-benchmarks-explained) (secondary)
- **Task budgets (beta `task-budgets-2026-03-13`).** Set with `output_config.task_budget = {type:"tokens", total, remaining?}`.
  - Scope: covers thinking, tool calls, tool results and output across one agentic turn (until a user message without tool results).
  - Countdown: the model sees a server-injected countdown, and the API returns no remaining field.
  - Limits and caveats: minimum `total` is 20,000; budgets that are too small can cause refusal-like early stopping; server compaction doesn't reset the budget; and it is advisory, unlike `max_tokens`.
- **Context-awareness tags.**
  - Sonnet 5, Sonnet 4.6, Sonnet 4.5 and Haiku 4.5 receive `<budget:token_budget>200000</budget:token_budget>` (or 1M) in the system prompt.
  - After each tool call they receive `<system_warning>Token usage: 35000/200000; 165000 remaining</system_warning>`.
  - Opus 4.7+, Sonnet 5.5, Fable and Haiku 5.5 do not receive these tags; use task budgets instead.
- **Context-window stop.** If input + `max_tokens` exceeds the window, generation stops with `stop_reason: "model_context_window_exceeded"` (Claude 4.5+). Max output is 128k tokens per request.
- **Server-side compaction in the loop** ([Threshold compaction](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/compaction-threshold)). Threshold compaction is `compact_20260112`.
  - With server tools, the trigger is checked at each sampling iteration, so one request can compact several times.
  - `pause_after_compaction: true` stops with `stop_reason: "compaction"`, so the client can re-insert content.
  - Combine `pause_after_compaction` with a compaction counter to enforce a total token budget across a long task.
- **Memory tool (`memory_20250818`).** The API auto-injects: "IMPORTANT: ALWAYS VIEW YOUR MEMORY DIRECTORY BEFORE DOING ANYTHING ELSE… ASSUME INTERRUPTION: Your context window might be reset at any moment, so you risk losing any progress that is not recorded in your memory directory." — [Memory tool](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/memory-tool)

**Todo tools** ([Track todos](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/todo-tracking))

- **Model gating.** `TodoWrite`, `TaskCreate`, `TaskGet`, `TaskUpdate` and `TaskList` are on by default "only on Claude Opus 4.7, Claude Sonnet 4.6, Claude Haiku 4.5, and earlier models". On newer models they are opt-in: set `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TODO_TOOLS=1`, or list them in `allowedTools`.
- **Lifecycle.** `pending` → `in_progress` → `completed`; `status: "deleted"` removes an item. Todos are used for tasks with "three or more distinct actions" (applies from v2.1.268).

**Outer loops: `/goal`, Ralph, Stop-hook caps**

- **`/goal`.** Detailed in §2.3. — [/goal docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal)
- **Ralph loop plugin.** Official plugin `ralph-loop` in `anthropics/claude-plugins-official`. — [plugins/ralph-loop](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-plugins-official/tree/main/plugins/ralph-loop)
- **Stop-hook safety cap.** "Claude Code overrides a Stop hook after it blocks eight times in a row with no tool call from Claude in between." Scripts should check `stop_hook_active` and exit early if it is true. — [hooks guide](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide)

**Long-running harness research** (engineering posts)

- **Initializer + coding agent** (2025-11-26, Justin Young, Opus 4.5 on the Agent SDK), with the open reference implementation `claude-quickstarts/autonomous-coding`.
- **Planner → generator → evaluator** (2026-03-24, Prithvi Rajasekaran).

Both are detailed in §2.3.

**Hosted loop durability (Managed Agents).** Crash-resume via `wake(sessionId)` → `getSession(id)` ("from the last event"); sandbox death returned as a retryable tool error; compaction always on, emitting `agent.thread_context_compacted` (§1.3). — [Managed Agents](https://anthropic.com/engineering/managed-agents)

**Auto-mode loop interaction.** A denial returns as a tool result telling the agent to find a safer path and not route around it. Three consecutive or 20 total denials escalate to the human, and headless `claude -p` terminates. — [Anthropic auto mode](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/claude-code-auto-mode)

**Workflow and agent-level fault handling** ([workflows](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows); [Agent SDK subagents](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/subagents); [agent teams](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams))

- **Stalls and failures.** A stalled workflow agent auto-restarts up to 5 times (`stallMs`, `CLAUDE_ASYNC_AGENT_STALL_TIMEOUT_MS`). `agent()` resolves to `null` on stop or unrecoverable error. Inside `parallel`/`pipeline`, a failure leaves `null` and the run continues.
- **Usage limits and output validation.** Usage-limit hits pause and auto-resume. Schema output is validated with up to 5 retries (`MAX_STRUCTURED_OUTPUT_RETRIES`).
- **Errors from subagents and teammates.** API errors are never delivered as a subagent's result. A teammate that ends on an API error notifies the lead with the error text.
- **Built-in convergence rules.** "keep fixing until the type check passes or two rounds in a row make no progress"; "stop once two rounds in a row find nothing new."

**Peer-swarm outer loop** (C compiler, 2026-02-05) ([building-c-compiler](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/building-c-compiler))

- **The loop.** A bash `while true` loop re-launches `claude` with a prompt file, one Docker container per agent.
- **Run hygiene.**
  - Agents maintain READMEs and progress files, because each one starts fresh.
  - Test output is kept to a few lines, with details sent to log files and errors tagged `ERROR`.
  - A `--fast` mode runs a deterministic per-agent 1% or 10% random sample to compensate for "time blindness".
- **Failure mode.** One agent ran `pkill -9 bash` and killed its own loop.

#### OpenAI

**Codex `run_turn`** (`codex-rs/core/src/session/turn.rs`, read from source at `fbf5f0d`)

- **Each iteration of the loop:**
  1. Clone history.
  2. Call `run_sampling_request`, a streamed Responses call that returns `SamplingRequestResult { needs_follow_up, last_agent_message }`.
  3. Compute `needs_follow_up = model_needs_follow_up || has_pending_input`.
  4. Read the context-window token status, and possibly start async compaction (phase `MidTurn` or `PostTurn`).
  5. Compact and continue if `auto_compaction_enabled && needs_follow_up && (model requested new context window || token_limit_reached || async-compaction candidate ready)`. This runs `run_auto_compact`, then `continue`s.
  6. If `!needs_follow_up`, run `run_turn_stop_hooks`.
  7. If a Stop hook blocks with a continuation prompt, record the prompt as a new message, set `stop_hook_active = true`, and continue. A block with no prompt is ignored, with the warning "Stop hook requested continuation without a prompt; ignoring the block."
  8. If `should_stop`, break.

  — [turn.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/core/src/session/turn.rs)
- **Retries and timeouts.**
  - Defaults: `DEFAULT_STREAM_MAX_RETRIES = 5`, `DEFAULT_REQUEST_MAX_RETRIES = 4`, `DEFAULT_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS = 300_000`.
  - `ContextWindowExceeded`, `UsageLimitReached`, `SessionBudgetExceeded` and `Fatal` are returned without retry.
  - Other stream errors go through `handle_response_stream_error` with backoff.
  - Cancellation surfaces as `CodexErr::TurnAborted`.

  — [model-provider-info/src/lib.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/model-provider-info/src/lib.rs); [turn.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/core/src/session/turn.rs)
- **Compaction thresholds and config.**
  - `auto_compact_token_limit()` returns `min(configured model_auto_compact_token_limit, context_window * 9 / 10)`, i.e. 90% of the window by default.
  - `effective_context_window_percent` defaults to 95%, reserving headroom.
  - `model_auto_compact_token_limit_scope` chooses between full context and tokens after the carried compaction prefix.
  - `model_post_turn_compact_threshold_percent` controls turn-end compaction; 0 disables it.
  - The `token_budget` feature has `reminder_threshold_tokens`, `auto_compact_fallback_prompt` (up to 2,000 bytes) and `auto_compact_fallback_buffer_tokens`.
  - Known bug: in codex-cli 0.117.0, changing `model_context_window` could make auto-compaction fail permanently after the first overflow (stale token count).

  — [openai_models.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/protocol/src/openai_models.rs); [config/mod.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/core/src/config/mod.rs); [issue #16068](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/16068)
- **Compaction prompt and history rebuild.**
  - The prompt reads "You are performing a CONTEXT CHECKPOINT COMPACTION. Create a handoff summary for another LLM that will resume the task". It asks for progress and decisions, constraints and preferences, remaining next steps, and critical data.
  - The summary is re-inserted with the prefix "Another language model started to solve this problem and produced a summary of its thinking process. You also have access to the state of the tools that were used by that language model. Use this to build on the work that has already been done and avoid duplicating work…"
  - Rebuilt history is the initial context, then prior real user messages (newest first, up to `COMPACT_USER_MESSAGE_MAX_TOKENS = 20_000`), then the summary.
  - `compact_prompt` in config overrides the prompt. Compaction can run inline (`run_inline_auto_compact_task`) or via the remote-v2 server path.

  — [compact/prompt.md](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/prompts/templates/compact/prompt.md); [summary_prefix.md](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/prompts/templates/compact/summary_prefix.md); [compact.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/core/src/compact.rs)
- **Stateless requests.** Codex sends `store: false` and `include: ["reasoning.encrypted_content"]`, so the API holds no state (zero data retention) and the client replays encrypted reasoning items itself. `parallel_tool_calls` is passed through. — [client.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/core/src/client.rs); [responses_websocket.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/codex-api/src/endpoint/responses_websocket.rs)
- **Loop-control tools the model can call.**
  - `new_context`: "Start a new context window. Does not clear, reset, or otherwise affect environment state." The open-source repo survey lists the handler as `new_context_window`; the name is unreconciled.
  - `get_context_remaining`: "Get the remaining tokens in the current context window."
  - `sleep`: "Pause execution… The sleep ends early when new input arrives for the active turn".
  - Other handlers: `update_plan`, `request_user_input`, `request_permissions`, `multi_agents`/`multi_agents_v2` (`spawn_agent`, `send_input`, `send_message`, `wait_agent`, `close_agent`, `resume_agent`, `interrupt_agent`, `list_agents`, `followup_task`), `tool_search`, `unified_exec` (`exec_command`, `write_stdin`), `apply_patch`, `view_image`, `send_message_to_user_async`.

  — [core/src/tools/handlers](https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/main/codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers)
- **Autonomy and preambles in the system prompt.**
  - "You are a coding agent. Please keep going until the query is completely resolved, before ending your turn and yielding back to the user. Only terminate your turn when you are sure that the problem is solved."
  - The model sends "a brief preamble to the user explaining what you're about to do" before tool calls, grouping related actions. The `models-manager/prompt.md` variant specifies 8–12 words.

  — [default.md](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/protocol/src/prompts/base_instructions/default.md); [models-manager/prompt.md](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/models-manager/prompt.md)
- **`update_plan`.**
  - Takes "a short list of 1‑sentence steps (no more than 5-7 words each) with a `status` for each step (`pending`, `in_progress`, or `completed`)".
  - "There should always be exactly one `in_progress` step until everything is done."
  - Mid-task changes are made by calling it again with an `explanation`.
  - "Do not repeat the full contents of the plan after an `update_plan` call — the harness already displays it."
  - In Plan Mode, calling `update_plan` returns an error.

  — [default.md](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/protocol/src/prompts/base_instructions/default.md); [plan.md](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/collaboration-mode-templates/templates/plan.md)
- **Thread goals and persistent mode.** Detailed in §2.3. — [ext/goal templates](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/ext/goal/templates/goals/continuation.md); [persistent_mode.md](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/prompts/templates/persistent_mode.md)

**OpenAI models and Responses API**

- **GPT-5.1-Codex-Max (2025-11-19).** OpenAI's first model "trained to run across several context windows via compaction". It can work "over millions of tokens on one task", and OpenAI observed it working on tasks for more than 24 hours internally. — [OpenAI](https://openai.com/index/gpt-5-1-codex-max/) (search snippet)
- **GPT-6 guidance** (a bundled snapshot of developers.openai.com; near-primary):
  - `reasoning.effort` ∈ `low`, `medium` (default), `high`, `xhigh`, `max`. GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol do not support `none`; Sol and Luna do.
  - To change effort mid-conversation without breaking the cache, add a `configuration_update` input item and "keep request-level `reasoning.effort` unchanged to preserve the prompt prefix for caching."
  - Tool calling with reasoning requires the Responses API.
  - Optional features: "persisted reasoning", "Programmatic Tool Calling", "compaction" and "pro mode".

  — [upgrading-to-gpt-6-astra.md](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/skills/src/assets/samples/openai-docs/references/upgrading-to-gpt-6-astra.md)
- **Responses compaction** (search extracts). `/responses/compact` is a stateless endpoint that returns an encrypted compaction item: "Do not prune /responses/compact output." `context_management.compact_threshold` on `POST /responses` compacts inline; the docs' examples use 200,000 with `store=false`. — [OpenAI Compaction guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/compaction)
- **Parallel tool calls.** `parallel_tool_calls: false` guarantees zero or one tool call per turn. Whether strict mode is incompatible with parallel calls is unverified; current reports say it applies only to fine-tuned models. — [function calling guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/function-calling) (search summary)

**OpenAI Agents SDK `Runner`** ([running_agents.md](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/main/docs/running_agents.md))

- **Turn logic.**
  1. Call the LLM.
  2. Classify the output. A **final output** ("text output with the desired type, and there are no tool calls") ends the loop. A **handoff** switches the agent and input and reruns. **Tool calls** run, their results are appended, and the loop reruns.
- **Turn cap and fallbacks.**
  - Exceeding `max_turns` raises `MaxTurnsExceeded`; `max_turns=None` disables the cap.
  - `error_handlers` keys `"max_turns"`, `"model_refusal"` and `"invalid_final_output"` can return fallback outputs instead of raising.
- **Tool lookup, concurrency and timeouts.**
  - `tool_not_found_behavior` raises `ModelBehaviorError` by default, or can be `"return_error_to_model"`.
  - `ToolExecutionConfig.max_function_tool_concurrency` caps concurrent function tools.
  - Timeouts are set with `ModelSettings.timeout`; a tool timeout raises `ToolTimeoutError`.
- **Reasoning replay.** `reasoning_item_id_policy` is `"preserve"` by default, or `"omit"`. `"omit"` is a mitigation for "Responses API 400 errors caused by a reasoning item that lacks its required following item."
- **Human approval.** Approval pauses the run, and `RunResult.interruptions` holds `ToolApprovalItem`s. The run resumes from a `RunState`. — [PR #4280](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/pull/4280/files) (secondary)
- **Evaluator loop.** For code orchestration, a task agent runs in a `while` loop with an evaluator agent until the criteria pass. — [multi_agent.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/openai-agents-python/main/docs/multi_agent.md)

**Agent RFT and the loop** ([InfoQ](https://www.infoq.com/presentations/rft-openai-model/); [ZenML](https://www.zenml.io/llmops-database/agent-reinforcement-fine-tuning-for-production-ai-agents))

- Each rollout has a unique ID attached to its tool calls.
- Tool calls were capped (example: 10).
- Training reduced turns, and models learned to issue more parallel calls.

#### DeepSeek

- **V3.2 thinking-context rule** (tech report, arXiv 2512.02556; search snippet). Historical reasoning content is discarded **only when a new user message arrives**. Appending tool outputs keeps it, and tool calls and results always stay in context.
  - Copying R1's approach of discarding at the second round "wasted" tokens.
  - Frameworks that simulate tool calls through user messages (the report names Roo Code and Terminus) will trigger the discard.
  - The [Cline blog](https://cline.bot/blog/deepseek-v3-2-and-v3-2-speciale-are-now-available-in-cline) is consistent with this.
- **API (search snippets and secondary sources).**
  - Thinking mode "supports tool calls. Before outputting the final answer, the model can perform multiple turns of reasoning and tool calls."
  - The official sample appends `content`, `reasoning_content` and `tool_calls` to history.
  - In tool loops `reasoning_content` must be passed back, "otherwise, the API returns 400". This comes from a third-party summary and the official guide via search.
  - Without `tools`, `reasoning_content` need not be passed back and is ignored if sent.
  - A secondary source says old reasoning should be cleared when a new user question begins (not DeepSeek's own wording).
  - Thinking is enabled via `extra_body={"thinking": {"type": "enabled"}}`.
  - The official API returns `None` when there are no tool calls; vLLM returns `[]`.
  - One extract references a `deepseek-flash` model ID, which suggests a post-V3.2 generation (unverified).

  — [DeepSeek Thinking Mode](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/thinking_mode/); [Tabbit summary](https://go.tabbit.ai/model/deepseek-v3-2/prompts/deepseek-official-thinking-tool-calls-multi-turn-state) (secondary); [CometAPI](https://www.cometapi.com/how-to-use-deepseek-v3-2-api/) (secondary); [vLLM recipe](https://docs.vllm.ai/projects/recipes/en/latest/DeepSeek/DeepSeek-V3_2.html)
- **Model variants.**
  - V3.2-Speciale (high-compute) does not support tool calling. — [SGLang cookbook](https://cookbook.sglang.io/autoregressive/DeepSeek/DeepSeek-V3_2)
  - Conflict: Vercel AI Gateway says the "V3.2 Thinking" variant doesn't support tool use, while DeepSeek's notes say thinking and tools are integrated. — [Vercel](https://vercel.com/ai-gateway/models/deepseek-v3.2-thinking)
- **V4 encoding** (search-summarized from the HF `encoding/README.md`; unverified).
  - Thinking mode emits reasoning before tool calls or answers; chat mode closes the thinking block immediately.
  - `drop_thinking` defaults to True but is **automatically disabled when tools are defined**, so tool-calling conversations keep the full reasoning.
  - Tool calls use a DSML `tool_calls` block with named invoke/parameter elements; `string="false"` marks JSON-typed parameters.
  - Tool results are wrapped in `tool_result` tags *inside user messages* in the template. This is the model's native serialization, which differs from a framework faking tool results as plain user text.
  - Three reasoning-effort levels are set as text prefixes. The reference file is `encoding_dsv4.py`.

  — [DeepSeek-V4 Encoding README](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-DSpark/raw/main/encoding/README.md)
- **Strict function calling (Beta).** Use `base_url="https://api.deepseek.com/beta"` with `strict: true` on every function. It works in both thinking and non-thinking modes and was introduced with V3.1 (Aug 2025). — [DeepSeek Tool Calls guide](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/tool_calls/)
- **Training for the loop.**
  - The V3.2 general-agent pipeline synthesized 1,827 task-oriented environments and about 85K complex prompts that are "hard to solve but easy to verify". The synthesis agent adds tools when the toolset is insufficient.
  - Recalled, unverified V3.2 figures: SWE-bench Verified ~73.1, Terminal Bench 2.0 ~46.4, BrowseComp ~51.4, rising to ~67.6 "with context-management strategies" (an in-loop harness effect), tau2 ~80.3.

  — [DeepSeek-V3.2 paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.02556) (via search summary)
- **DSA and the loop.** DeepSeek Sparse Attention attends to the top-2048 keys per query (`index_topk` default 2048). It lowers the cost of long trajectories on self-hosted DeepSeek, which makes less aggressive in-loop compaction viable there. The top-k overlap with exact attention averages about 60% on a 128K HELMET variant, so retrieval precision still matters. — [AMD article](https://www.amd.com/en/developer/resources/technical-articles/2025/amd-instinct-mi335x-gpu-supports-deepseek-v3-2-exp.html); [arXiv 2512.03494](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.03494) (via search)
- **DeepSeek Harness (v0.1, reported Aug 2026).** No loop details are available in the notes (see §1.2).

#### Open source and others

- **mini-swe-agent.** The loop is a linear message history with bash-only actions run via `subprocess.run`. It "doesn't even need to use the tool-calling interface", so each action is stateless and independent. — [README](https://github.com/SWE-agent/mini-swe-agent/blob/main/README.md)
- **OpenHands Software Agent SDK.**
  - A `StuckDetector` scans recent events for repetitive patterns (for example 4 repeats × 2 events per cycle).
  - The `conversation` package includes `goal` and `stuck_detector`, and the SDK has a `critic` module.
  - Condensation is "hard" when explicitly requested, for example after a context-window error.

  — [stuck_detector.py](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/main/openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/conversation/stuck_detector.py)
- **LangChain Deep Agents (secondary).** Its +13.7-point TB 2.0 gain included **time-budget warnings** (agents are "famously bad at time estimation") and **loop-detection middleware** that tracks edit counts per file and prompts the agent to reconsider after repeated edits. — [explainx.ai](https://www.explainx.ai/blog/agent-harness-engineering-terminal-bench-langchain-2026)
- **Gemini CLI.** Compression triggers at `DEFAULT_COMPRESSION_TOKEN_THRESHOLD = 0.5` of the window and keeps the latest 30% (`COMPRESSION_PRESERVE_THRESHOLD = 0.3`). It has explicit `complete-task`, `write-todos` and `enter-plan-mode`/`exit-plan-mode` tools. — [chatCompressionService.ts](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/main/packages/core/src/context/chatCompressionService.ts); [core/src/tools](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/tree/main/packages/core/src/tools)
- **Cline.** `@cline/agents` is the stateless loop. Automatic compaction requires a known context window. — [ARCHITECTURE.md](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/main/sdk/ARCHITECTURE.md)
- **Ralph (Geoffrey Huntley's original).** "Ralph is a Bash loop": a `while true` that re-feeds a prompt file. — [ralph-loop plugin README](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-plugins-official/tree/main/plugins/ralph-loop)
- **Google ADK.** `LoopAgent` runs until `escalate=True` or `max_iterations`. — [community ADK guide](https://zack.onrender.com/docs/GEN%20AI%20DEV/Agents/Google%20ADK)
- **Manus** (via search extracts and a gist).
  - `todo.md` recitation keeps the global plan at the end of context over loops of about 50 steps.
  - Secondary sources report that todo.md maintenance consumed about ⅓ of actions, so Manus later moved planning to a dedicated planner agent (unverified).
  - "Keep the wrong stuff in": failed actions and stack traces stay in context, because "error recovery is one of the clearest indicators of true agentic behavior."
  - A "pre-rot threshold" of about 128K–200K tokens triggers context reduction.

  — [gist summary](https://gist.github.com/cedrickchee/b9646b3007b4a15f528351abd331984f); [MarkTechPost](https://www.marktechpost.com/2025/07/22/context-engineering-for-ai-agents-key-lessons-from-manus/)
- **Cognition (2025).** Recommends single-threaded linear agents plus an LLM that compresses history for long tasks. — [jxnl.co summary](https://jxnl.co/writing/2025/09/11/why-cognition-does-not-use-multi-agent-systems/) (secondary)
- **METR.**
  - Most measurements use the **Triframe and ReAct** scaffolds. Results are "somewhat sensitive to scaffold (including prompting)".
  - TH1.1 (2026-01-29) grew the suite from 170 to 228 tasks (8h+ tasks from 14 to 31).
  - The post-2023 doubling time is 131 days under TH1.1 (vs 165 days under TH1), and the P50 doubling time is 88.6 days for 2024 onward.

  — [METR TH1.1](https://metr.org/blog/2026-01-29-time-horizon-1-1/) (via search snippets)
- **Research on learned in-loop context control** (via search; see the context-engineering section).
  - **AgentFold** (arXiv 2510.24699): proactive "folding" of history. Context grows from about 3.5k to 7k tokens over 100 turns.
  - **Context-Folding / FoldGRPO** (arXiv 2510.11967): `branch`/`return` actions open sub-trajectories and fold them on return. It matches baselines with a 32K active budget and up to 10 branches.
  - **ACON** (arXiv 2510.00615): optimized compression guidelines that cut peak tokens 26–54%.
- **Kimi K3** (2026) reportedly advertises long-horizon agentic RL with persistent sandbox state, so the trainer must checkpoint and resume environments. — [HF blog](https://huggingface.co/blog/sergiopaniego/rl-environments-2026) (secondary)

### 2.3 Techniques and patterns

**The canonical turn loop**
- *What it is:* The inner loop every harness shares. It samples, executes tool calls, appends the results, and repeats. Around that it adds compaction, steering, budgets and stop arbitration.
- *Mechanics:* The pseudocode below is synthesized from Codex `run_turn` (`turn.rs`) and the Claude Agent SDK's documented semantics. It is not a copy of either.

```python
def run(session, user_input, cfg):
    session.append(user_input)                     # append-only event log (§1.3)
    turns, spend, stop_hook_active = 0, 0.0, False
    while True:
        if session.cancelled():                    # Esc / turn/interrupt
            cancel_running_tools(); return result("error_during_execution")  # Codex: CodexErr::TurnAborted
        prompt = project(session)                  # stable prefix + append-only tail; reasoning items replayed (§2.3 replay)
        try:
            resp = sample_streaming(prompt,        # stream idle timeout 300 s (Codex); 5 stream / 4 request retries w/ backoff
                                    effort=cfg.effort, thinking={"type": "adaptive"})
        except (ContextWindowExceeded, UsageLimitReached, SessionBudgetExceeded, AuthError, Fatal) as e:
            return result("error_during_execution", error=e)   # terminal: no retry
        session.append(resp)                       # keep thinking blocks + signatures / encrypted reasoning verbatim
        turns += 1; spend += cost(resp)            # budget checked AFTER the response → may overshoot by one response
        if spend >= cfg.max_budget_usd: return result("error_max_budget_usd")
        if resp.tool_calls:
            results = execute(resp.tool_calls)     # PreToolUse/PostToolUse hooks; read-only parallel, mutating serial;
            session.append(results)                # denials & sandbox failures come back AS tool results, native tool role
        pending = session.drain_steering_queue()   # user typed mid-turn → read after current tool calls finish
        session.append(pending)
        needs_follow_up = bool(resp.tool_calls) or bool(pending)
        if needs_follow_up:
            if turns >= cfg.max_turns: return result("error_max_turns")
            if cfg.auto_compact and over_threshold(session, frac=0.90):   # or model called new_context
                compact(session)                   # handoff summary; thrash guard: give up after a few attempts
            continue
        verdict = run_stop_hooks(last_assistant_message=resp.text, stop_hook_active=stop_hook_active)
        if verdict.block and verdict.prompt:       # Codex ignores a block with no prompt
            session.append(continuation(verdict.prompt)); stop_hook_active = True; continue
        return result("success", stop_reason=resp.stop_reason)   # end_turn | max_tokens | refusal
```

- *Evidence:* This is the shipped shape in Codex (`needs_follow_up = model_needs_follow_up || has_pending_input`, followed by Stop hooks) and in Claude Code/SDK (queued messages, Stop hooks, the `ResultMessage` subtypes). — [turn.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/core/src/session/turn.rs); [agent-loop docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/agent-loop)
- *When to use / when not:* Always use this shape. Keep the loop itself stateless (§1.3), and implement each control (compaction, steering, Stop hooks) as a pluggable stage.

**Termination predicate and stop reasons**
- *What it is:* A single explicit rule: `stop ⇔ (no tool calls in last response) ∧ (no pending user input) ∧ (Stop hooks / goal evaluator allow stop)`. Hard caps take precedence over it.
- *Mechanics:* Distinguish *why* the run ended. The Claude SDK `ResultMessage.subtype` values are:
  - `success`
  - `error_max_turns`
  - `error_max_budget_usd`
  - `error_during_execution`
  - `error_max_structured_output_retries`

  The model's last stop is reported separately as `stop_reason` ∈ {`end_turn`, `max_tokens`, `refusal`}, or `null` after a crash. The Claude API adds `model_context_window_exceeded` and `compaction` (when `pause_after_compaction` is set). The OpenAI Agents SDK defines a final output as "text output with the desired type, and there are no tool calls". Exceeding `max_turns` raises `MaxTurnsExceeded`, and `error_handlers` can turn that, a refusal or an invalid final output into fallback output.
- *Evidence:* Both labs implement the same three-part predicate. — [agent-loop docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/agent-loop); [running_agents.md](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/main/docs/running_agents.md)
- *When to use / when not:* Always use it. Expose the termination reason to callers and to traces, because it is the primary signal for debugging early stops.

**Turn counting and max-turns semantics**
- *What it is:* A deterministic cap on loop iterations.
- *Mechanics:*
  - Claude SDK: `max_turns` counts "each turn with tool calls, plus one for the final text-only response". The default is "No limit".
  - With streaming input, a queued message after a max-turns stop starts a new turn and *resets* the turn count, but the budget keeps accumulating.
  - `/goal` resets its turn count and token baseline on `--continue`/`--resume`.
  - Agents SDK: `max_turns=None` disables the cap.
  - Subagent `maxTurns` marks the output partial and resumable.
- *Evidence:* Documented defaults. — [agent-loop docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/agent-loop); [subagents](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents)
- *When to use / when not:* Use turn caps for subagents and headless runs. For long autonomous goals, prefer token and dollar budgets, because turn counts are a poor proxy for work.

**Layered budgets: turns, dollars or tokens, and time**
- *What it is:* Several independent caps enforced by the harness, plus model-visible budget signals so the model can pace itself.
- *Mechanics:*
  - **Dollar cap:** `max_budget_usd`, checked after each response, so leave headroom of about one response plus in-flight subagents. When it trips, subagent spawns fail with `Budget limit reached` and background subagents stop.
  - **Token budget (Anthropic):** task budgets (`task-budgets-2026-03-13`; `output_config.task_budget`; minimum 20,000; advisory; not reset by compaction).
  - **Token budget (Codex goals):** "Tokens used / Token budget / Tokens remaining" in each continuation prompt, and `budget_limit.md` on exhaustion.
  - **Total token budget via compaction:** `pause_after_compaction` plus a compaction counter.
  - **Time:** Codex stream idle timeout of 300 s; the `/goal` background check-in cadence; LangChain time-budget warnings.
  - **Model-visible signals:** `<budget:token_budget>` and per-tool-call `<system_warning>` tags on some Claude models; Codex `get_context_remaining`; the Codex `token_budget` feature's `reminder_threshold_tokens`.
- *Evidence:*
  - "Setting a budget is a good default for production agents." — [agent-loop docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/agent-loop)
  - Time-budget warnings were part of LangChain's +13.7-point gain (secondary).
  - The C-compiler team added a deterministic `--fast` 1% or 10% test sample because agents have "time blindness".
  - Too-small task budgets can cause refusal-like early stopping. — [Task budgets](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/task-budgets)
  - No public data was found on how much the usage tags or task budgets improve completion.
- *When to use / when not:* Always set a dollar or token cap in production. Add a model-visible budget note on providers without native signals. Make it turn-scoped (§1.3, cache) so it does not accumulate.

**Retries, timeouts and the error taxonomy**
- *What it is:* Classify every failure as retryable, a pause condition, or terminal, and handle each class differently.
- *Mechanics:*
  - **Retryable:** transient stream or network errors, overloads, 429, 5xx and timeouts. Codex retries streams 5 times and requests 4 times, with backoff. LiteLLM-style routers use exponential backoff with jitter (about 0–2 s, 0–4 s, 0–8 s), honour `retry_after`, and fall back to another model group only after retries are exhausted (for example `num_retries=3`, then a cheaper model). A context-window error can fall back to a larger-context model group.
  - **Pause:** `/goal` pauses on rate or usage limits and resumes when the limit resets. Workflows pause and auto-resume on usage limits.
  - **Terminal:** `ContextWindowExceeded` after compaction has failed, `UsageLimitReached`, `SessionBudgetExceeded`, `Fatal`, authentication failure, exhausted credit, and an unavailable model. Never retry authentication or validation errors.
  - **Tool errors** go back to the model as results, so it can adapt. Anthropic tells agents when a tool is failing. The Agents SDK option `tool_not_found_behavior="return_error_to_model"` converts unknown tool names into feedback.
  - **Tool timeouts:** `ModelSettings.timeout` / `ToolTimeoutError` in the Agents SDK. Workflow stall restarts are capped at 5.
- *Evidence:* Codex source defaults; the `/goal` error policy; [LiteLLM retries](https://www.mintlify.com/BerriAI/litellm/features/retries) (mirror); [Anthropic multi-agent research](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/multi-agent-research-system).
- *When to use / when not:* Always use it. Count each retry against rate limits and latency, and log retry counts per `chat` span.

**Interrupts and mid-turn steering**
- *What it is:* The user can stop the agent, or redirect it without stopping it.
- *Mechanics:*
  - **Hard interrupt:** Esc in Claude Code cancels the running tool call. Codex has `turn/interrupt` and returns `TurnAborted`. The Codex multi-agent tool `interrupt_agent` interrupts a sub-agent.
  - **Soft steering:** queued input is read "as soon as those calls finish, within the same turn" (Claude Code). Codex has `turn/steer`, and `has_pending_input` forces follow-up. The Codex `sleep` tool "ends early when new input arrives for the active turn".
  - **Approval pauses:** Agents SDK `RunResult.interruptions` holds `ToolApprovalItem`s and resumes from `RunState`. Managed Agents uses resumable approval gates (`always_ask`). Codex sends item-level `requestApproval` events.
- *Evidence:* The documented behaviour in all three products.
- *When to use / when not:* Always implement both hard and soft interrupts. Apply steering messages between tool batches, never in the middle of a tool call, to keep tool-call/tool-result pairing intact.

**Parallel vs serial tool execution**
- *What it is:* Run independent read-only calls concurrently, and serialize anything that mutates state.
- *Mechanics:*
  - **Claude Agent SDK:** read-only tools (`Read`, `Glob`, `Grep`, and MCP tools marked read-only) run concurrently; `Edit`, `Write` and `Bash` run sequentially; custom tools are sequential unless they set `readOnlyHint`. Note that MCP `readOnlyHint` defaults to false and annotations are untrusted unless the server is trusted.
  - **OpenAI:** `parallel_tool_calls` is passed through; `false` guarantees zero or one call per turn. The Agents SDK caps concurrency with `ToolExecutionConfig.max_function_tool_concurrency`. Codex has `tools/parallel.rs`.
  - **Programmatic tool calling (Anthropic)** collapses many calls into one code block: "20+ calls in one code block save 19+ inference passes".
- *Evidence:*
  - Anthropic research subagents use 3+ tools in parallel; combined with 3–5 parallel subagents this cut research time by up to 90%.
  - OpenAI agent RFT taught models to issue more parallel calls and fewer turns.
  - PTC cut tokens by 37% (43,588 → 27,297) and raised GAIA from 46.5% to 51.2%.
  - Sources: [agent-loop docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/agent-loop); [Anthropic advanced tool use](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/advanced-tool-use); [InfoQ](https://www.infoq.com/presentations/rft-openai-model/)
- *When to use / when not:* Parallelize reads by default. Serialize writes and shell commands. Large parallel fan-outs can add 20 or more blocks between cache breakpoints, so add a mid-history breakpoint in that case.

**Interleaved and adaptive reasoning with effort control**
- *What it is:* The model thinks between tool calls within one assistant turn, giving a native ReAct pattern. Depth is set with an effort enum rather than a token budget.
- *Mechanics:*
  - **Anthropic:** `thinking: {type: "adaptive"}` plus `output_config: {effort}` with `low`/`medium`/`high`/`xhigh`/`max`, set per session or per subagent. `budget_tokens` returns a 400 on 4.7+. The `interleaved-thinking-2025-05-14` header applies only to Opus 4.5, Sonnet 4.5 and earlier Claude 4 models.
  - **OpenAI:** `reasoning.effort`; change it mid-conversation with a `configuration_update` input item while keeping the request-level effort unchanged.
  - **DeepSeek:** thinking mode via `extra_body`. V4 has three effort levels set as text prefixes.
  - Claude Code has an `ultracode` effort mode that lets Claude plan a workflow for every substantive task.
- *Evidence:*
  - Effort defaults: Opus 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 use `medium`, others `high`.
  - Opus 5.5's Terminal-Bench 4.0 score was self-reported at xhigh effort (66.4% ±2.6), versus 59.6% measured by Artificial Analysis and 65.15% by Vals.ai (secondary). Effort is a score-changing harness setting.
  - Anthropic's research system used "extended thinking for planning and interleaved thinking after tool results".
- *When to use / when not:* Treat effort and thinking mode as part of the cache key. Set them per session or per subagent, not per request. Route cheap work to lower effort or smaller models rather than toggling mid-conversation, except where the vendor explicitly supports cache-safe changes (OpenAI `configuration_update`; Claude 5.5-family models and Fable 5.1, where an effort change does not bust the cache per Claude Code docs).

**Reasoning-state replay per vendor**
- *What it is:* Returning prior reasoning to the API in the exact form the vendor requires, so that tool loops keep their chain of thought and do not error.
- *Mechanics:*

| Vendor | What must be replayed | How | Failure mode if wrong |
|---|---|---|---|
| Anthropic | Thinking blocks with their signatures, unmodified, especially those paired with tool results | Opus 4.5 and 4.6+ (plus Sonnet 4.6+, Haiku 5.5, Fable/Mythos) keep prior thinking in context, billed as input; Sonnet 4.5, Haiku 4.5 and earlier strip it. Clear server-side with `clear_thinking_20251015` (`keep: {type:"thinking_turns", value:N}` or `"all"`; must be listed first). On 5.1+ models thinking before a compaction block is not carried forward. | Editing earlier turns client-side breaks signatures and the prefix check. Changing thinking mode or budget invalidates the cache (the docs show a 1,370-token cache rebuilt). On older models, non-tool-result user content strips cached thinking. |
| OpenAI | Encrypted reasoning items | `store: false` + `include: ["reasoning.encrypted_content"]`; replay the items in input. Agents SDK `reasoning_item_id_policy="preserve"` (default) or `"omit"`. Tool calling with reasoning requires the Responses API. | A 400 for "a reasoning item that lacks its required following item" (mitigated by `"omit"`). Changing request-level `reasoning.effort` breaks the prefix; use `configuration_update`. |
| DeepSeek | `reasoning_content` together with `content` and `tool_calls` within a tool loop | Append the full assistant message. Reasoning is discarded only at a new user message. The V4 encoder disables `drop_thinking` when tools are defined. | A 400 if omitted in tool loops (secondary). Frameworks that send tool results as user messages trigger reasoning discard (Roo Code and Terminus are named). |

- *Evidence:* [Extended thinking](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/extended-thinking); [Context editing](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/context-editing); [codex client.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/core/src/client.rs); [running_agents.md](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/main/docs/running_agents.md); [DeepSeek-V3.2 report](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.02556) (snippet)
- *When to use / when not:* This is mandatory in any multi-provider harness. Implement it as a per-provider adapter behind the event log, and store reasoning items verbatim in the log.

**The "think" tool (legacy)**
- *What it is:* A no-op tool whose argument is free-form reasoning, giving the model a place to reflect between tool calls.
- *Mechanics:* Define a `think` tool and add an optimized prompt telling the model when to use it.
- *Evidence:*
  - τ-bench airline pass^1 rose from 0.370 to 0.570 with an optimized prompt (+54% relative); retail rose from 0.783 to 0.812. A similar tool contributed to Claude 3.7 Sonnet's 0.623 on SWE-bench. — [Anthropic, 2025-03-20](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/claude-think-tool) (figures via snippet)
  - A secondary source says Anthropic now recommends extended or adaptive thinking over a separate think tool in most cases. — [agentpatterns.ai](https://agentpatterns.ai/patterns/agent-design/think-tool/) (secondary, unverified)
- *When to use / when not:* Use it only for models without native interleaved thinking, or for a self-hosted model with thinking disabled.

**Preambles (user-visible intent before tool calls)**
- *What it is:* A short message to the user before a group of tool calls, for transparency.
- *Mechanics:* Codex asks for "a brief preamble to the user explaining what you're about to do", grouping related actions. The `models-manager/prompt.md` variant specifies 8–12 words.
- *Evidence:* It is in the shipped Codex prompts, and it matches Anthropic's transparency principle ("show planning steps").
- *When to use / when not:* Use it in interactive UIs. Suppress it in headless runs to save tokens.

**Todo and plan tools vs plan mode, and recitation**
- *What it is:* A structured, model-maintained checklist (the *tool*). It is distinct from plan *mode*, a read-only permission state that ends in an approvable plan. Recitation means rewriting the plan into recent context to fight goal drift.
- *Mechanics:*
  - **Codex `update_plan`:** 5–7-word steps; exactly one `in_progress`; an `explanation` when the plan changes; do not repeat the plan after calling it, because the harness renders it.
  - **Claude:** `TodoWrite`/`TaskCreate`/`TaskUpdate`/`TaskGet`/`TaskList` with `pending` → `in_progress` → `completed`/`deleted`, for tasks with "three or more distinct actions". Off by default on newer models; `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TODO_TOOLS=1` turns it on.
  - **Gemini CLI** `write-todos`, **OpenCode** `todowrite`, **OpenHands** `task_tracker`.
  - **Manus** rewrites `todo.md` so the global plan sits at the end of context.
  - Claude Code re-injects the plan-mode plan after compaction.
- *Evidence:*
  - Anthropic: "Newer models track multi-step work without a written todo list."
  - Codex: "do not treat a plan update as a substitute for doing the work."
  - Manus todo.md maintenance reportedly took about ⅓ of actions (secondary, unverified).
- *When to use / when not:* Make the plan tool a model-gated option. Enable it for older or weaker models, for UI progress rendering, and for work that must survive compaction. Keep recitation out of the cache prefix by appending it as a turn-scoped message.

**In-loop compaction, the thrash guard, and model-callable context tools**
- *What it is:* Summarize history inside the loop before overflow, guard against compaction loops, and optionally let the model request a fresh window itself.
- *Mechanics:*
  - **Codex:** the trigger is `min(configured, 90% of the window)`; phases `MidTurn` and `PostTurn`; async compaction candidates; a handoff-summary prompt; up to 20k tokens of recent user messages kept; initial context re-inserted.
  - **Codex tools:** `new_context` (or `new_context_window`) starts a new window without touching environment state; `get_context_remaining` reports remaining tokens.
  - **Claude Code** stops auto-compacting "after a few attempts" if context refills immediately. Its threshold defaults to about 967K on native-1M models (overridable). It re-injects durable state after compaction.
  - **Anthropic API:** threshold compaction (`compact_20260112`; default trigger 150k input tokens, minimum 50k) is checked at each server-tool sampling iteration. On-demand compaction (`compact-2026-09-04`) can run in the background, replacing exactly the first N messages when the block arrives.
  - **Summary prompts must forbid tool calls.** With tools defined, the model sometimes calls a tool instead of summarizing, which yields `content: null`. Fix with "Do not call any tools while writing this summary; respond with text only."
- *Evidence:*
  - The Anthropic long-running post says "compaction isn't sufficient" because it "doesn't always pass perfectly clear instructions to the next agent".
  - GPT-5.1-Codex-Max is trained to work across compactions.
  - Sources: [Effective harnesses](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/effective-harnesses-for-long-running-agents); [Threshold compaction](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/compaction-threshold); [Compaction in the background](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/compaction-background)
- *When to use / when not:* Always use it for long sessions. For multi-session work, pair it with external state files (below). Compact at natural task breaks where possible, because compaction busts the conversation cache layer. Full compaction mechanics are in the context-engineering section.

**Stop hooks as a veto on termination**
- *What it is:* A hook that runs when the model tries to stop. It can block the stop and inject a continuation prompt, which is the building block of every outer loop.
- *Mechanics:*
  - **Claude Code:** return `{"decision":"block","reason":…}` to continue, or `{"continue": false, "stopReason": …}` to halt. Input includes `last_assistant_message` and `stop_hook_active`. Prompt-type hooks (single-turn LLM decision, 30 s default timeout) and agent-type hooks (up to 50 tool turns, 60 s) can judge completion.
  - **Codex:** blocks must carry continuation fragments; an empty block is ignored. `stop_hook_active = true` is set after a block.
- *Evidence:* Safety cap: "Claude Code overrides a Stop hook after it blocks eight times in a row with no tool call from Claude in between". — [hooks guide](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide); [turn.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/core/src/session/turn.rs)
- *When to use / when not:* Use Stop hooks for verifiable gates (tests pass, lint clean, feature flag flipped). Always check `stop_hook_active`, and rely on the consecutive-block cap. Never block without a reason or prompt.

Illustrative Stop-hook gate (Claude Code semantics) that blocks the stop until tests pass:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
input=$(cat)
if [ "$(echo "$input" | jq -r '.stop_hook_active')" = "true" ]; then exit 0; fi   # avoid runaway re-blocking
if ! npm test --silent >/tmp/test.log 2>&1; then
  jq -n --arg r "Tests are failing; see /tmp/test.log (last lines: $(tail -5 /tmp/test.log | tr '\n' ' ')). Fix before stopping." \
     '{decision:"block", reason:$r}'
  exit 0
fi
exit 0
```

**Goal loop: Claude Code `/goal`**
- *What it is:* A session-scoped outer loop. A small, fast evaluator model judges a natural-language exit condition every time Claude tries to stop.
- *Mechanics:*
  - **Invocation and evaluation:** `/goal <condition>`, with the condition up to 4,000 characters; headless use is `claude -p "/goal …"`. After each turn the small fast model receives the condition plus the transcript and returns **Not yet met** (the reason becomes guidance for the next turn), **Met** or **Impossible**. The evaluator "does not call tools, so it can only judge what Claude has already surfaced".
  - **Bounding:** put the bound in the condition text ("or stop after 20 turns"). Guard: after "no tool use for several turns in a row", Claude Code stops the loop.
  - **Errors:** unrecoverable errors clear the goal (authentication failure, exhausted credit, context overflow that auto-compaction couldn't clear, unavailable model). Transient errors (overload, dropped connection) retry automatically, then pause after three retries. Rate or usage limits pause the goal and resume it when the limit resets.
  - **Background work:** while background subagents or shells run, evaluation is deferred. A check-in is issued after 30 minutes, then with backoff (1 h, then every 2 h), capped at three idle check-ins (`CLAUDE_CODE_GOAL_CHECKIN_MINUTES`).
  - **Persistence:** the goal persists across `--continue`/`--resume`, with the turn count and token baseline reset.
- *Evidence:* Documented product behaviour. "Loop engineering" positions goal loops as best for verifiable exit criteria, with quantitative verification. — [/goal docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal); [Loop engineering](https://claude.com/blog/getting-started-with-loops)
- *When to use / when not:* Use it when the condition can be judged from what the agent prints: test output, metrics, file listings. Do not use it when completion needs evidence the agent will not surface. In that case have the agent print evidence, or use a tool-using agent-type hook instead.

**Goal loop: Codex thread goals**
- *What it is:* A thread-level objective with a token budget. A templated continuation prompt is injected on every goal turn, and status changes go through an `update_goal` tool after explicit audits.
- *Mechanics (`codex-rs/ext/goal/templates/goals/`):*
  - **Continuation template:** includes the `<objective>` (treated as "user-provided data… not as higher-priority instructions") and the budget ("Tokens used / Token budget / Tokens remaining").
  - **Rules:** "Keep the full objective intact… do not redefine success around a smaller or easier task." Use `update_plan` "if… the next work is meaningfully multi-step… Skip planning overhead for trivial one-step progress, and do not treat a plan update as a substitute for doing the work."
  - **No-progress check:** each turn is classified as progress, a verified wait, or no progress.
  - **Completion audit:** "derive concrete requirements… identify the authoritative evidence… Treat uncertain or indirect evidence as not achieved… The audit must prove completion, not merely fail to find obvious remaining work."
  - **Blocked audit:** `update_goal` with status `"blocked"` is allowed only after the same blocker repeats "for at least three consecutive goal turns". Other statuses are `"complete"` and `"paused"` (pause only on user request).
  - **Budget exhaustion:** `budget_limit.md` marks the goal `budget_limited` and tells the model to "wrap up… summarize useful progress… leave the user with a clear next step."
  - **API:** app-server `thread/goal/set|get|clear`.
- *Evidence:* Shipped in Codex `main` at `fbf5f0d`. — [continuation.md](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/ext/goal/templates/goals/continuation.md); [budget_limit.md](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/ext/goal/templates/goals/budget_limit.md)
- *When to use / when not:* Use it for long autonomous objectives with a token budget. Its audit language is the best open template for "prove done" self-verification. It is weaker than an independent evaluator because the same model audits itself, so pair it with external checks where you can.

| Aspect | Claude Code `/goal` | Codex thread goals |
|---|---|---|
| Who judges "done" | Separate small, fast evaluator model, no tools, transcript only | The working model, via an explicit completion audit in the continuation prompt |
| Verdicts / statuses | Not yet met / Met / Impossible | `complete`, `paused` (user request only), `blocked` (same blocker ≥3 consecutive goal turns), `budget_limited` |
| Budget | In the condition text (e.g. "or stop after 20 turns"); session `max_budget_usd` | Token budget shown every turn; `budget_limit.md` wrap-up |
| No-progress guard | Stops after "no tool use for several turns in a row" | Each turn classified as progress, verified wait, or no progress |
| Error policy | Unrecoverable → clear; transient → retry, pause after 3; rate limit → pause, then resume | Not documented in the notes |
| Long background work | Evaluation deferred; check-ins at 30 min, 1 h, then every 2 h; max 3 idle | Persistent mode: short waits "often 1–3 minutes" |
| Prompt-injection stance | — | Objective is "user-provided data", not higher-priority instructions |
| Persistence | Survives `--continue`/`--resume` (turn count and token baseline reset) | Thread-scoped via app-server |

**Persistent mode and proactive follow-ups (Codex)**
- *What it is:* A prompt mode for keeping a task alive after the final answer: monitoring, waiting on CI, polling.
- *Mechanics:*
  - Before starting a follow-up, the model identifies "its scope, the outcome you want to establish, the evidence needed, and a stopping condition".
  - It polls with "short, proportionate waits, often 1–3 minutes".
  - It keeps "the target, last known state, stopping condition, and next check in the available task/checkpoint state so the follow-up survives sleep and context resets."
  - "Persistence does not broaden that scope."
  - It is paired with the `sleep` tool, which ends early on new input, and `send_message_to_user_async`.
- *Evidence:* [persistent_mode.md](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/prompts/templates/persistent_mode.md)
- *When to use / when not:* Use it for event-driven or proactive loops. Always require an explicit stopping condition and store state outside context.

**Ralph Wiggum loop**
- *What it is:* An outer loop that re-feeds the *same* prompt until a completion promise appears. All progress persists in files and git, not in context.
- *Mechanics:*
  - **Original (Huntley):** "Ralph is a Bash loop", a `while true` that re-feeds a prompt file.
  - **Anthropic's official `ralph-loop` plugin:** runs inside a session with a **Stop hook** that blocks exit and feeds the same prompt back, so "Claude's previous work persists in files" and git.
  - **Usage:** `/ralph-loop "<prompt>" --max-iterations <n> --completion-promise "<text>"`; cancel with `/cancel-ralph`.
  - **State:** `.claude/ralph-loop.local.md`, with frontmatter `max_iterations`, `completion_promise` and `session_id`.
  - **Completion check:** the hook reads the last assistant text block from `transcript_path` and looks for `<promise>…</promise>`.
- *Evidence:* The C-compiler swarm used the same bash `while true` pattern at scale (16 agents, about 2,000 sessions). One agent killed its own loop with `pkill -9 bash`. — [plugins/ralph-loop](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-plugins-official/tree/main/plugins/ralph-loop); [building-c-compiler](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/building-c-compiler)
- *When to use / when not:* Use it for tasks with a mechanical completion signal and a strong external verifier (tests or a compiler). Always set `--max-iterations`. Do not use it without a verifier: it will loop indefinitely or declare a false promise.

Illustrative `.claude/ralph-loop.local.md` (field names from the plugin; values are examples):

```markdown
---
max_iterations: 30
completion_promise: "ALL TESTS PASS"
session_id: "..."
---
(the same prompt text is re-fed every iteration; the model must print the completion
 promise wrapped in promise tags only when it is literally true)
```

**Initializer + incremental coding agent with progress file and git (multi-session harness)**
- *What it is:* A two-prompt pattern on one harness. The first session builds machine-checkable task state, and every later fresh-context session does exactly one verified unit of work.
- *Mechanics (Anthropic, 2025-11-26; Opus 4.5 on the Claude Agent SDK):*
  1. **Initializer session** creates `init.sh` (starts the dev server), `claude-progress.txt`, an initial git commit, and a JSON feature list. The claude.ai-clone experiment had more than 200 features, all starting as failing, each with `category`, `description`, `steps` and `passes`. Later agents may change only `passes`. The prompt says: "It is unacceptable to remove or edit tests because this could lead to missing or buggy functionality." JSON was chosen because the model is less likely to inappropriately rewrite it than Markdown.
  2. **Coding sessions** follow a start ritual: `pwd` → read git logs and progress files → read the feature list and pick the highest-priority failing feature → run `init.sh` → run a basic end-to-end test before any new work.
  3. **One feature per session.** Verify end to end "as a human user would" (Puppeteer MCP), then commit with a descriptive message and update the progress log, leaving code "clean" enough to merge.
  4. The initializer and coding agents differ **only in the initial user prompt**; the system prompt, tools and harness are identical.
  5. The open reference implementation is `claude-quickstarts/autonomous-coding`:
     - `feature_list.json` (200 test cases), `init.sh` and a git repo
     - coding sessions that resume from `feature_list.json`, `claude-progress.txt` and git, and auto-continue
     - defence in depth: an OS sandbox, a filesystem restricted to the project dir, and a bash allowlist enforced by a security hook (`security.py`)
- *Evidence:* The failure modes it fixed:
  - declaring the project done too early → fixed by the feature list
  - leaving bugs or undocumented state → fixed by git, progress notes and a smoke test at start
  - marking features done prematurely → fixed by end-to-end tests
  - wasting time on startup → fixed by `init.sh`

  The memory tool's documented "multisession software development pattern" codifies the same flow. No quantitative ablation (with vs without progress files) was published, so the evidence is qualitative. — [Effective harnesses](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/effective-harnesses-for-long-running-agents); [autonomous-coding](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-quickstarts/blob/main/autonomous-coding/README.md); [Memory tool](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/memory-tool)
- *When to use / when not:* Use it for any task larger than one context window, or that must survive crashes and model swaps. It is cheap and model-agnostic. Enforce the "flip `passes` only" invariant in a hook, not just the prompt. It is overkill for single-session tasks.

```jsonc
// feature_list.json — illustrative shape (fields from the Anthropic post)
[
  { "category": "functional",
    "description": "User can start a new chat and see the assistant's streamed reply",
    "steps": ["Open the app", "Click 'New chat'", "Type a message and submit", "Verify streamed reply renders"],
    "passes": false }
]
```

Coding-session prompt skeleton (illustrative; steps from the Anthropic post):

```text
1. Run `pwd`. Read `claude-progress.txt` and `git log --oneline -20`.
2. Read feature_list.json; choose the highest-priority feature with "passes": false.
3. Run ./init.sh; run the basic end-to-end smoke test. If it fails, fix that first.
4. Implement ONLY the chosen feature. Verify end to end as a human user would (browser automation).
5. Set "passes": true for that feature only. Never delete or edit tests/features.
6. git commit -m "<descriptive message>"; append a dated entry to claude-progress.txt
   (what was done, what was verified, known issues, next feature).
```

**Planner → generator → evaluator harness with sprint contracts**
- *What it is:* A GAN-inspired three-agent harness for multi-hour builds. "Separating the agent doing the work from the agent judging it proves to be a strong lever."
- *Mechanics (Anthropic, 2026-03-24):*
  - **Planner:** expands a 1–4 sentence prompt into a product spec, kept high level so spec errors do not cascade.
  - **Generator:** builds in sprints with git.
  - **Evaluator:** drives the running app with Playwright MCP, checking UI, API and database state against per-criterion **hard thresholds**. Failing any criterion fails the sprint.
  - **Sprint contracts:** before coding, generator and evaluator agree on what "done" means and how it will be verified. Sprint 3 alone had 27 criteria.
  - Agents communicate **through files**.
  - **Frontend-design variant:** four criteria (design quality, originality, craft, functionality), a few-shot-calibrated evaluator, Playwright MCP screenshots, 5–15 iterations, runs of up to 4 hours.
- *Evidence:*
  - RetroForge on Opus 4.5: the solo run took 20 min and $9 and was broken; the full harness took 6 hr and $200, delivered 16 features across 10 sprints, and was playable.
  - On Opus 4.6 the sprints were **removed** (the model "built coherently without decomposition"). The planner was kept (without it the generator under-scoped), and the evaluator moved to a single end-of-run pass.
  - Browser DAW total: about 3 h 50 m and $124.70. Planner 4.7 min / $0.46; build round 1 2 h 7 m / $71.08; QA 8.8 min / $3.24; build round 2 1 h 2 m / $36.89; plus two more short rounds. QA still caught stubbed features.
  - Self-evaluation bias: "tuning a standalone evaluator to be skeptical" was easier than making the generator self-critical. Even so, out of the box the evaluator "talked itself out of real issues" and needed several tuning rounds against logs plus few-shot calibration. "Claude out of the box is a poor QA agent."
  - Source: [Harness design](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/harness-design-long-running-apps)
- *When to use / when not:* Use it for multi-hour builds where quality is judged against an interactive end state. Re-ablate it per model: the planner and a final evaluator pass seem durable, but sprints were not needed on Opus 4.6. It costs more than 20× a solo run.

**Context resets vs compaction ("context anxiety")**
- *What it is:* A context reset starts a fresh agent with a structured handoff artifact instead of summarizing in place.
- *Mechanics:* At a threshold or phase boundary, write the handoff file (state, decisions, next steps), end the session, and start a new agent that reads it. Codex's `new_context` tool lets the *model* trigger this.
- *Evidence:*
  - Sonnet 4.5 wrapped up early as it approached its perceived context limit, so resets were "essential".
  - Opus 4.5 "largely removed" the behaviour, so resets were dropped in favour of automatic compaction.
  - Managed Agents calls the resets "dead weight" on Opus 4.5.
  - The Anthropic research lead also spawned fresh subagents with clean contexts as limits approached, and saved its plan to memory because context beyond 200,000 tokens is truncated.
  - Sources: [Harness design](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/harness-design-long-running-apps); [Managed Agents](https://anthropic.com/engineering/managed-agents); [Multi-agent research](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/multi-agent-research-system)
- *When to use / when not:* Keep resets as a per-model flag. Turn them on for models that show early wrap-up near the limit, and off for models trained across compaction.

**Loop, stuck and no-progress detection**
- *What it is:* Harness middleware that notices repetition or stagnation and intervenes.
- *Mechanics:*
  - OpenHands `StuckDetector`: repetitive event patterns, for example 4 repeats × 2 events per cycle.
  - LangChain: edit counts per file, with a "reconsider" prompt after repeated edits.
  - `/goal`: stops after several turns with no tool use.
  - Codex goals: per-turn progress / verified-wait / no-progress classification, and a blocked status only after 3 consecutive repeats.
  - Claude Code workflows: "two rounds in a row make no progress" / "find nothing new".
  - Auto mode: 3 consecutive or 20 total denials escalate.
  - Stop-hook cap: 8 consecutive blocks with no tool call.
  - Claude Code compaction thrash guard.
- *Evidence:* Loop detection was part of LangChain's +13.7-point gain (secondary). — [stuck_detector.py](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/main/openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/conversation/stuck_detector.py)
- *When to use / when not:* Always run it in autonomous and goal loops. Tune thresholds on transcripts to avoid false positives on legitimate polling ("verified wait").

**End-to-end verification inside the loop**
- *What it is:* The agent checks its work against ground truth from the environment before claiming done.
- *Mechanics:*
  - Puppeteer or Playwright MCP to drive the app "as a human user would".
  - A start-of-session smoke test.
  - Rules and linting (TypeScript gives more feedback than JS).
  - Visual feedback.
  - LLM-as-judge only as a fallback ("generally not a very robust method").
  - A separate reviewer with fresh context.
  - Keep test output to a few lines, with details in log files and `ERROR`-tagged lines.
- *Evidence:*
  - Autonomous agents need "ground truth from the environment" at each step.
  - The C-compiler verifier "must be nearly perfect, or agents solve the wrong problem".
  - Devin Review (fresh context) catches about 2 bugs per PR (secondary).
  - Sources: [Building effective agents](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/building-effective-agents); [Claude Agent SDK post](https://claude.com/blog/building-agents-with-the-claude-agent-sdk); [building-c-compiler](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/building-c-compiler)
- *When to use / when not:* Always use it. Make verification quantitative and part of the stop gate.

**Error retention ("keep the wrong stuff in")**
- *What it is:* Leave failed actions and error traces in context so the model updates its beliefs rather than repeating the mistake.
- *Mechanics:*
  - Tool errors, denials and sandbox failures are returned as tool results.
  - After an error is resolved, keep the error message and the corrective decision, and clear the verbose traces (context-engineering inference).
  - Codex memories over-index on user corrections, redo requests and interruptions.
- *Evidence:* Manus: "error recovery is one of the clearest indicators of true agentic behavior" (gist summary). Anthropic tells agents when a tool is failing.
- *When to use / when not:* This is the default. Prune verbose traces once the error is resolved.

**Crash-resume and resume-not-restart**
- *What it is:* After a harness or infrastructure failure, continue from the last durable event instead of restarting the task.
- *Mechanics:*
  - **Managed Agents:** `wake(sessionId)` → `getSession(id)` → continue "from the last event".
  - **Claude SDK:** `resume` with `session_id`. A streaming session "stays alive" after an error result.
  - **Agents SDK:** a `RunState` resumes paused runs, and Sessions support "resuming interrupted runs with the same session".
  - **Workflows:** deterministic replay returns cached results until the first changed `agent()` prompt.
  - **Durable steps:** idempotency keys for side-effecting tools.
- *Evidence:* Anthropic: in long stateful runs "minor failures" compound, so it "built systems that can resume from where the agent was when the errors occurred". — [Multi-agent research](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/multi-agent-research-system); [Managed Agents](https://anthropic.com/engineering/managed-agents)
- *When to use / when not:* Always use it for runs longer than a few minutes.
