### 2.7 Build checklist for our harness

1. **Implement the canonical loop (§2.3) with an explicit termination predicate.** `stop ⇔ no tool calls ∧ no pending input ∧ stop hooks allow`. Emit a typed result (`success`, `error_max_turns`, `error_max_budget_usd`, `error_during_execution`, `error_max_structured_output_retries`) and carry the model `stop_reason`, cost, usage, turn count and `session_id`.
2. **Layered budgets.**
   - Require a per-deployment `max_budget_usd`; never ship "no limit" to production. Leave headroom of one response plus in-flight subagents.
   - Set `max_turns` on every subagent and headless run.
   - Offer a token budget (native task budgets where available, otherwise harness-counted).
   - Inject a turn-scoped "tokens used / remaining / next compaction at N" note.
   - When a budget trips: refuse new subagent spawns, stop background subagents, and run a Codex-style wrap-up turn (summarize progress, give a next step).
3. **Retry policy.** Use 5 stream retries and 4 request retries with exponential backoff and jitter, honour `retry_after`, and set a 300 s stream idle timeout.
   - Terminal: context-window-exceeded after compaction failed, authentication failure, exhausted credit or usage, budget exceeded, fatal.
   - Pause and resume: rate limits.
   - Fallback model only after retries are exhausted.
   - Count retries in the `chat` span.
4. **Interrupts.** Provide a hard cancel that kills the running tool and records an aborted turn, and a soft steering queue drained only between tool batches. Add a `sleep` tool that wakes on new input. Approval waits are durable pauses resumable from a serialized run state.
5. **Tool scheduler.**
   - Run tools concurrently only when trusted metadata marks them read-only. Treat untrusted MCP `readOnlyHint` as false, which is MCP's default anyway. Serialize writes and shell commands, and cap concurrency.
   - Return denials, timeouts, sandbox failures and unknown-tool errors to the model as tool results.
   - Preserve call/result pairing exactly.
6. **Reasoning adapters.** One adapter per provider:
   - Anthropic signed thinking blocks
   - OpenAI encrypted reasoning items with `store:false` + `include`, plus the `preserve`/`omit` ID policy
   - DeepSeek `reasoning_content`

   Store reasoning verbatim in the event log. Never edit prior turns client-side. Set effort per session or per subagent from the model profile (Opus 5.5: `medium` by default; raise to `high`/`xhigh` for hard agentic work after eval). Never change effort or thinking mid-session except through cache-safe vendor mechanisms (`configuration_update`; 5.5-family Claude models).
7. **In-loop compaction.**
   - Trigger at `min(config, 90% of the window)`, or the provider's server-side threshold. Check it both mid-turn and post-turn.
   - Run a handoff-summary prompt that says "do not call tools", and keep recent user messages (≤20k tokens) or the last 1–2 turns verbatim. Re-inject instruction files, the plan or todo, recently touched files and active skills.
   - Fire a `PreCompact` hook to archive.
   - Thrash guard: stop auto-compacting after a few consecutive attempts that fail to free space, and surface an error.
   - Use async or background compaction where supported.
8. **Plan and todo tools.** Make them model-gated: on for older or weaker models and for UI progress rendering, off by default on the newest models. Enforce exactly one `in_progress` and short steps. Keep plan *mode* (read-only, ends in an approvable plan) separate. Recite the plan as a turn-scoped message, never in the prefix.
9. **Stop hooks.** Support `decision:block` with a reason, and `continue:false` to halt. Pass `stop_hook_active` and `last_assistant_message`. Override a hook after 8 consecutive blocks with no tool call, and ignore blocks without a prompt.
10. **Goal mode.** Implement `/goal`-style outer loops:
    - a separate small evaluator model returning Met / Not yet met (with a reason that becomes guidance) / Impossible
    - a no-tool-use-for-N-turns guard
    - the error policy: clear on unrecoverable, retry 3 then pause on transient, pause and resume on rate limits
    - a background-work deferral with check-ins at 30 min → 1 h → every 2 h (max 3)
    - persistence across resume

    Add the Codex audit template to the continuation prompt: keep the objective intact, prove completion with authoritative evidence, mark blocked only after 3 consecutive identical blockers, wrap up on budget exhaustion. Treat the objective as data, not instructions.
11. **Long-running templates.** Ship `init` and `continue` prompt templates for the initializer + coding-agent pattern:
    - `feature_list.json` (`category`, `description`, `steps`, `passes`)
    - `claude-progress.txt` (or equivalent)
    - `init.sh`
    - a start-of-session ritual (`pwd`, git log, progress, pick a failing feature, `init.sh`, smoke test)
    - one feature per session with end-to-end verification
    - a git commit plus progress entry per feature

    Enforce "only `passes` may change; tests are immutable" with a `PreToolUse` hook.
12. **Ralph mode.** `--max-iterations` (required) plus `--completion-promise`, with a state file. Use it only with an executable verifier. Protect the supervisor process from the agent (it must not be able to `pkill` its own loop).
13. **Planner/generator/evaluator profile (optional, flagged).** Include:
    - a planner that writes a high-level spec
    - a generator
    - a skeptical evaluator with hard per-criterion thresholds, few-shot calibration and browser automation
    - sprint contracts in files

    Ablate per model: drop sprints, and keep the planner and a final evaluator pass if evals agree.
14. **Stuck and no-progress middleware.** Detect repeated event patterns (e.g. 4 × 2), track per-file edit counts with a "reconsider" nudge, count no-progress turns, and count denials. Feed signals to the goal loop, and allow "verified wait" for legitimate polling.
15. **Per-model long-horizon flags.** Context resets on or off (on for models with early wrap-up near the limit). Offer a `new_context` tool. Add persistence prompting for models that stop to ask questions ("persist until the user's intended goal is complete…").
16. **Telemetry.** Per turn, record termination reason, retries, cache-read and cache-write tokens, compaction events and budget remaining. Track turns, tool calls, tokens, cost and wall-clock per task as eval outputs alongside pass rate. Fewer turns and more parallel calls are wins (OpenAI RFT; Anthropic eval YAML).

### 2.8 Pitfalls and anti-patterns

- **Wrong reasoning replay.**
  - Dropping DeepSeek `reasoning_content` in tool loops gives a 400 (secondary).
  - Replaying an OpenAI reasoning item without its following item gives a 400 (use `"omit"`).
  - Editing Anthropic thinking blocks breaks signatures and the cache.
- **Sending tool results as user messages.** DeepSeek discards reasoning, and other models lose the tool-result pairing they were trained on.
- **Changing effort or thinking mode mid-conversation** on models where it invalidates the cache. Using `budget_tokens` on Claude 4.7+ returns a 400.
- **Treating `max_budget_usd` as exact.** It is checked after each response, so spend can overshoot by one response plus subagents.
- **Treating `max_turns` as a total cap in streaming sessions.** Queued messages reset the turn count while the budget keeps accumulating.
- **Getting retries wrong in either direction.** Retrying terminal errors (authentication, budget, overflow after compaction) wastes money. Failing to retry transient errors kills long runs.
- **Compaction failures.**
  - Compaction thrash on a single oversized tool output. Cap and paginate tool output at ingestion.
  - Summaries that call tools (`content: null`). Say "do not call tools".
  - Compacting *after* overflow; you must compact before overflow because the summarization prompt must still fit.
  - On-demand compaction: leaving summarized messages after the block re-sends them, and omitting the block loses the summary.
  - Losing images and documents, mid-range system instructions and per-message effort in compaction.
  - Codex 0.117.0: changing `model_context_window` made auto-compaction fail permanently (stale token count).
- **Runaway Stop hooks.** Not checking `stop_hook_active` loops forever, and Codex ignores a block with no prompt.
- **Trusting an evaluator that cannot see evidence.** The `/goal` evaluator only judges what the transcript surfaced. Make the agent print proof.
- **Self-audits that "fail to find obvious remaining work".** That is not proof of completion. Codex's audit explicitly requires *proving* completion.
- **Goal shrinking.** The agent redefines success around "a smaller or easier task". Restate the full objective every turn.
- **Treating the goal objective as higher-priority instructions.** That makes it a prompt-injection vector. Treat it as user data.
- **Premature victory and one-shotting.** Agents declare done early or mark features passing without end-to-end tests. Use the feature list, one feature per session, and E2E verification.
- **Letting agents edit tests or the feature list.** Enforce immutability in hooks. Markdown task lists get rewritten more easily than JSON.
- **Keeping obsolete scaffolds.** Context resets, sprints and todo lists on models that no longer need them add cost and latency ("dead weight").
- **Plan-tool overhead.** Manus's todo.md reportedly consumed about ⅓ of actions (secondary). Codex warns against treating plan updates as work.
- **Parallelizing mutating tools,** or trusting MCP `readOnlyHint` from untrusted servers.
- **Autonomous runs stalling on questions.** Newer OpenAI models stop to ask questions or offer to continue. Add persistence prompting for autonomous runs.
- **Agents killing their own loop** (`pkill -9 bash` in the C-compiler run). Run the supervisor outside the agent's sandbox.
- **Verbose tool output and time blindness.** Keep test output to a few lines with logs in files, and give time-budget warnings and fast sampled test modes.
- **Task budgets set too small.** They cause refusal-like early stopping.
- **Ralph loops without a verifier or a max-iterations cap.**

### 2.9 Open questions and unverified claims

- **OpenAI primary texts were unreachable.** The full "Unrolling the Codex agent loop" post and its follow-ups, and the Responses "persisted reasoning" docs (`#preserve-reasoning-across-calls`), could not be read. Loop details come from codex-rs source.
- **DeepSeek specifics are mostly secondary.**
  - The 400-without-`reasoning_content` rule comes from secondary summaries and search extracts.
  - V4 encoding details (DSML syntax, effort prefixes, tool results inside user messages) are search-summarized.
  - There is no primary source on a 2026 DeepSeek agent-loop change.
  - The `deepseek-flash` model ID is unverified.
  - Any DeepSeek Harness loop design is undocumented.
- **No published quantification** of the gain from interleaved or adaptive thinking on agentic benchmarks. The claim that Anthropic now prefers adaptive thinking over the think tool is secondary only.
- **No public data on budget signals.** Nothing shows how much `<budget:token_budget>`/`<system_warning>` tags or task budgets improve task completion.
- **Run-duration claims for 2026 models** (Opus 4.8, Opus 5, GPT-5.5, GPT-6) have no primary source.
  - Opus 4.6's 14.5 h horizon is secondary.
  - Sonnet 4.5's "30+ hours" (Sep 2025) was not re-verified.
  - METR says horizons above 16 h are unreliable with its suite.
- **Codex compaction defaults per model.** Per-model `auto_compact_token_limit` values are unconfirmed (third-party posts conflict: 64k vs ~200k), as is whether OpenAI-hosted sessions default to remote compaction. The exact OpenAI default compaction prompt is unverified.
- **Tool naming.** Codex's context tool is `new_context` in one note set and `new_context_window` in the other.
- **Codex goals error policy.** Retry and pause semantics for errors during goal turns are not documented in the notes.
- **Unspecified counts.** Claude Code's "a few attempts" (thrash guard) and `/goal`'s "several turns" (no-tool-use guard) are not given numerically in the docs.
- **No quantitative ablation** of progress files or feature lists, and no head-to-head comparison of `/goal`, Codex goals and Ralph loops.
- **Effort default history.** Whether Opus 5's API default effort was "high" before Opus 5.5's "medium" is secondary (Vellum). The docs confirm only the current defaults.
- **OpenAI parallel calls.** The current interaction between `strict` mode and `parallel_tool_calls` is unverified from the primary page.
- **Agents SDK HITL** (`RunResult.interruptions`, sticky hosted-MCP decisions) is secondary for some details.
- **Manus figures.** The figure that todo.md maintenance consumed ~⅓ of actions, and the move to a planner agent, are secondary.
- **Async research agents.** Asynchronous lead/subagent execution in Anthropic's research product was "planned", and no follow-up confirms it shipped.



---

## 3. Context engineering

> **SOTA in one paragraph:** Context engineering is curating "the smallest set of high-signal tokens that maximizes the likelihood of the desired outcome" ([Anthropic, Sep 29, 2025](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/effective-context-engineering-for-ai-agents)). Every token costs money, latency and attention, and quality degrades ("context rot") long before the hard limit, even on 1M-token models. A Nov 2026 production harness keeps a fixed, deterministic, cache-stable prefix (tools → system → project instructions) with append-only history, and adds all dynamic content as appended or turn-scoped messages rather than prefix edits. It defers most tools behind a tool search, runs data-heavy chains as code (programmatic tool calling or code-mode MCP), packages procedures as progressively disclosed skills, and loads data just in time with grep/glob/read-with-range instead of RAG pre-loading. When the window fills, it works down a ladder from cheap, reversible steps (output caps, offload to files, tool-result clearing) to irreversible ones (server-side or handoff-style compaction plus re-injection of durable state), and finally to fresh contexts rebuilt from progress files. Both Anthropic and OpenAI now ship compaction as an API primitive, and the research frontier (ACE, ACON, AgentFold, Context-Folding, RLMs) tries to learn or optimize these operations instead of hand-tuning them.

### 3.1 Where the field is (Nov 2026) — consensus and recent shifts, with dates

**Consensus positions (all labs plus the main open-source harnesses)**

- **Tokens in the window are a cost to minimize, not free space to fill.**
  - Anthropic: n tokens create n² pairwise attention relationships, every token draws down a finite "attention budget", and the decline is "a gradient, not a cliff" that bigger windows are not expected to remove ([Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/effective-context-engineering-for-ai-agents)).
  - The Claude docs define context rot as accuracy and recall degrading as token count grows. Cached prefixes still occupy the window; caching changes price, not size ([Claude docs: Context windows](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/context-windows)).
- **The KV/prompt-cache hit rate is the top production metric.** Manus calls it "the single most important metric for a production-stage AI agent", with an average input:output ratio of about 100:1 ([Manus (secondary, via search extract)](https://manus.im/blog/Context-Engineering-for-AI-Agents-Lessons-from-Building-Manus)). Manus, Codex and Anthropic all treat cache-hit rate as a top-line metric alongside cost, latency and tool error rate.
- **Agentic search beats wholesale pre-loading for code and file-heavy work.** Grep/glob/head/tail plus lightweight identifiers is the default. Claude Code pre-loads only CLAUDE.md and fetches everything else just in time ([Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/effective-context-engineering-for-ai-agents)). The Agent SDK guidance is to use agentic search first, "only adding semantic search if you need faster results" ([Claude blog, Sep 29, 2025](https://claude.com/blog/building-agents-with-the-claude-agent-sdk)).
- **Compaction is a first-class API primitive** at Anthropic (threshold `compact_20260112` and on-demand `compact-2026-09-04`) and OpenAI (`/responses/compact`, `context_management.compact_threshold`). Every major open-source harness also ships LLM-summary compaction. They diverge on how much they retain and where the summary lives (client-side vs provider-side) ([Codex compact.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/core/src/compact.rs); [Gemini CLI chatCompressionService.ts](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/main/packages/core/src/context/chatCompressionService.ts)).
- **Tool definitions are context.** Defer most of them, and keep 3–5 hot tools plus a search tool loaded ([Claude docs: Tool search tool](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/tool-search-tool)).
- **Procedures go in skills, always-true facts in instruction files, and long-horizon state in files and git** rather than in chat ([Claude Code: Memory](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory); [Anthropic: Effective harnesses](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/effective-harnesses-for-long-running-agents)).
- **Sub-agents are primarily a context-isolation tool.** They explore with tens of thousands of tokens and return condensed results, "often 1,000–2,000 tokens" ([Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/effective-context-engineering-for-ai-agents)).
- **The taxonomies are settled.** Breunig's four failure modes (poisoning, distraction, confusion, clash) and LangChain's four operations (write, select, compress, isolate) are the common vocabulary ([Breunig (secondary)](https://www.dbreunig.com/2025/06/22/how-contexts-fail-and-how-to-fix-them.html); [LangChain (via search extract)](https://www.langchain.com/blog/context-engineering-for-agents)).

**What changed in practice**

- **Scaffolds are being removed as models internalize behavior.**
  - Context resets were essential for Sonnet 4.5 ("context anxiety": wrapping up early near its perceived limit). Opus 4.5 "largely removed" the behavior, so resets were replaced by compaction ([Anthropic: Harness design](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/harness-design-long-running-apps)).
  - Claude Code's todo tools are off by default on its newest models: "Newer models track multi-step work without a written todo list" ([Claude Code: Track todos](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/todo-tracking)).
  - "Every harness component encodes an assumption about what the model can't do alone," and those assumptions go stale ([Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/harness-design-long-running-apps)).
- **Models are trained with their harness's context management.** GPT-5.1-Codex-Max was trained across compaction boundaries. The DeepSeek V3.2 report designs reasoning retention around tool-role conventions and warns that frameworks putting tool results in user messages (it names Roo Code and Terminus) trigger reasoning discard ([arXiv 2512.02556 (via search)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.02556)).
- **Cache-preserving dynamic content became an API feature.** On Claude, mid-conversation system messages, turn-scoped system messages and inline tool add/remove mean a harness no longer has to choose between Manus-style recitation and prefix stability.
- **No controlled 2026 study quantifies context-rot curves for current 1M-token frontier models.** Vendors assert degradation qualitatively, but no public numbers were found.

### 3.2 By lab

#### Anthropic

The most complete public stack. Numbers in parentheses point to the techniques in 3.3 where the mechanics are spelled out.

- **Guidance.**
  - Effective context engineering (Sep 29, 2025): right altitude, minimal tools, canonical examples, just-in-time retrieval, hybrid pre-load, compaction, notes, sub-agents. "Do the simplest thing that works" ([Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/effective-context-engineering-for-ai-agents)).
  - Writing tools for agents (Sep 11, 2025) ([Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/writing-tools-for-agents)).
  - Code execution with MCP (Nov 4, 2025) ([Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/code-execution-with-mcp)) and Advanced tool use (Nov 24, 2025) ([Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/advanced-tool-use)).
  - Effective harnesses for long-running agents (Nov 26, 2025): compaction "isn't sufficient" because it "doesn't always pass perfectly clear instructions to the next agent" ([Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/effective-harnesses-for-long-running-agents)).
  - Rollout order for tool context: cache tool definitions from day one (the 25% write markup pays back on the second hit), add tool search past ~20 tools, then context editing for long runs, then programmatic tool calling for chains ([Manage tool context](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/manage-tool-context)).
- **API primitives (Nov 2026).**
  - Threshold compaction `compact_20260112` (#16) and on-demand compaction `compact-2026-09-04`, which Anthropic recommends "wherever it is available" (#17).
  - Context editing `clear_tool_uses_20250919` and `clear_thinking_20251015` (#14, #15).
  - Prompt caching with automatic or ≤4 breakpoints, 5-minute/1-hour TTLs and a 20-block lookback (#7).
  - Mid-conversation, turn-scoped and inline-tool messages (#6).
  - Tool search with `defer_loading` (#8); programmatic tool calling (#9); `input_examples` (#11); Agent Skills (#12).
  - Memory tool `memory_20250818` (#22), designed to pair with clearing and compaction: "compaction keeps the active context small … memory preserves the information that must survive summarization" ([Memory tool](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/memory-tool)).
  - Context-awareness tags and task budgets (#25).
  - 1M windows as the default on Fable 5/5.1, Mythos 5/5.1/Preview, Opus 5.5/5/4.8/4.7/4.6, Sonnet 5.5/5/4.6 and Haiku 5.5: no beta header, standard pricing except Haiku 5.5 above 100k, 128k max output, up to 600 images or PDF pages (100 on 200k models), and `stop_reason: "model_context_window_exceeded"` when input + `max_tokens` exceeds the window (Claude 4.5+) ([Context windows](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/context-windows)).
- **Claude Code** is the reference cache-aware harness.
  - Layering is system + tools → project context → conversation, with appended `<system-reminder>`s (#5, #6).
  - Auto-compact at ~967K on native-1M models, with re-injection of durable state (#19, #20) and a thrash guard ([How Claude Code works](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/how-claude-code-works)).
  - A 25,000-token tool-output cap, and MCP tools deferred by default (#8, #10).
  - `/context` and `/usage` cache visibility (#2).
  - Hierarchical CLAUDE.md with path rules and AGENTS.md fallback (#13).
  - Subagents with their own cache vs forks sharing the parent's (#24), and workflows where "Claude's context holds only the final answer" ([Workflows](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows)).
  - Changelog v2.1.317: "Fixed very long conversations losing their earlier summary when compaction had to shorten its own request" ([CHANGELOG](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)).
- **Claude Agent SDK.**
  - Emits `SystemMessage` `subtype: "compact_boundary"`. A `PreCompact` hook (trigger `manual` or `auto`) can archive the transcript.
  - Compaction instructions can live in CLAUDE.md because "CLAUDE.md content is re-injected on every request".
  - `ClaudeAgentOptions.task_budget` and per-subagent `autoCompactWindow`.
  - [agent-loop docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/agent-loop); [types.py](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python/blob/main/src/claude_agent_sdk/types.py)
- **Managed Agents (Apr 8, 2026).**
  - The session is "an append-only event log" kept outside the window because compaction, the memory tool and trimming "are irreversible" (#27). Compaction is always on (`agent.thread_context_compacted`).
  - Memory stores (beta `agent-memory-2026-07-22`) mount at `/mnt/memory/<slug>/` with a note auto-added to the system prompt: 100 kB per memory (~25k tokens), ≤8 stores per session, `instructions` ≤4,096 chars. "Structure memory as many small focused files, not a few large ones."
  - [Managed Agents](https://anthropic.com/engineering/managed-agents); [memory docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/memory)

#### OpenAI

developers.openai.com was blocked, so Responses API facts come from search extracts. Codex facts come from source on `main` at commit `fbf5f0d` (2026-11-03).

- **Responses API compaction.** The stateless `/responses/compact` endpoint and inline `context_management.compact_threshold` both return an opaque, encrypted compaction item (#18). LiteLLM and the Vercel AI Gateway expose `/v1/responses/compact` ([LiteLLM](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/response_api_compact.md); [Vercel](https://vercel.com/docs/ai-gateway/sdks-and-apis/responses/compaction.md)).
- **Prompt caching** ([Prompt caching (via search)](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompt-caching); [Azure Foundry](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-ca/Azure/foundry/openai/how-to/prompt-caching)):
  - Automatic for prompts ≥1,024 tokens: up to −90% input cost and −80% latency; `cached_tokens` is always present.
  - `prompt_cache_key`: keep each prefix+key under ~15 requests/minute.
  - `prompt_cache_retention` is `in_memory` or `24h` at the same price. 24h stores KV tensors on GPU-local storage and is not ZDR-eligible. Defaults reportedly vary by org; Azure says `in_memory` for gpt-5.4 and older.
  - GPT-5.6+: `prompt_cache_key` is required for "more reliable matching", retention is a minimum of ≥30 minutes, and explicit breakpoints plus `prompt_cache_options` are introduced (older models reject them).
  - Secondary summaries of "Unrolling the Codex agent loop" (Jan 23, 2026): the old prompt must be an exact prefix of the new one, dynamic MCP tool lists can break the prefix, and compaction invalidates it ([all-ai.de](https://www.all-ai.de/news/beitrage2026/codex-agent-loop); [danielvaughan](https://codex.danielvaughan.com/2026/04/21/codex-cli-prompt-caching-maximise-cache-hits-cost-reduction/)).
- **Cache-safe controls.**
  - `allowed_tools` restricts callable tools per turn without changing `tools` (third-party description). `tool_search` is available on gpt-5.4+ ([Function calling (search summary)](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/function-calling)).
  - To change effort mid-conversation, add a `configuration_update` input item and "keep request-level `reasoning.effort` unchanged to preserve the prompt prefix for caching". This comes from a GPT-6 migration guide bundled in the Codex repo (near-primary) ([upgrading-to-gpt-6-astra.md](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/skills/src/assets/samples/openai-docs/references/upgrading-to-gpt-6-astra.md)).
  - Encrypted reasoning replay via `include: ["reasoning.encrypted_content"]` + `store: false` (#15).
- **Codex CLI.**
  - Handoff-summary compaction with a local streamed path (`run_inline_auto_compact_task`, or manual) and a "remote v2" path (`compact_remote_v2*.rs`) that retains selected tool outputs, budgets images, falls back to another model and runs Pre/PostCompact hooks. Thresholds are min(config, 90%) with a 95% effective window (#19).
  - The turn loop can start async compaction mid-turn or post-turn (phases `MidTurn`/`PostTurn`). If `auto_compaction_enabled && needs_follow_up && (model requested new context window || token_limit_reached || async-compaction candidate ready)`, it runs `run_auto_compact` and continues. `ContextWindowExceeded` is returned without retry ([turn.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/core/src/session/turn.rs)).
  - Model-callable `new_context` ("Start a new context window. Does not clear, reset, or otherwise affect environment state."; listed elsewhere as `new_context_window`), `get_context_remaining` and `tool_search` ([handlers](https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/main/codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers)).
  - Code-mode crates (#9) and hierarchical AGENTS.md (#13).
  - Per-model system prompts (`gpt_5_codex_prompt.md`, `gpt-5.1-codex-max_prompt.md`, `gpt-5.2-codex_prompt.md`, `gpt_5_1_prompt.md`, `gpt_5_2_prompt.md`) ([codex-rs/core](https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/main/codex-rs/core)).
  - Goal continuation injects "Tokens used / Token budget / Tokens remaining", and `budget_limit.md` says "wrap up… summarize useful progress" ([continuation.md](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/ext/goal/templates/goals/continuation.md)).
  - Memories: `memory_summary.md` is injected into the developer prompt between `MEMORY_SUMMARY BEGINS/ENDS`, followed by a "quick memory pass" of "ideally <= 4-6 search steps". `disable_on_external_context` marks `memory_mode = "polluted"` ([read_path.md](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/ext/memories/templates/memories/read_path.md)).
  - Known bug in 0.117.0: changing `model_context_window` could permanently break auto-compaction after the first overflow because of a stale token count ([issue #16068](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/16068)).
- **Agents SDK.**
  - `OpenAIResponsesCompactionSession` "triggers responses.compact when stored history grows" (`should_trigger_compaction`).
  - `run_internal/prompt_cache_key.py`.
  - `reasoning_item_id_policy` (`"preserve"` default; `"omit"` avoids orphan-reasoning 400s).
  - `SandboxAgent` capabilities `compaction.py` and `Skills(lazy_from=…)`.
  - [compaction session](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/main/src/agents/memory/openai_responses_compaction_session.py); [running_agents.md](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/main/docs/running_agents.md); [sandbox_agents.md](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/main/docs/sandbox_agents.md)
- **Model–harness co-design.** GPT-5.1-Codex-Max (Nov 19, 2025) was "trained to run across several context windows via compaction" and worked >24 hours on tasks internally ([OpenAI (snippet)](https://openai.com/index/gpt-5-1-codex-max/)).
- **Instruction files.** OpenAI donated AGENTS.md to AAIF (Dec 9, 2025) ([OpenAI](https://openai.com/index/agentic-ai-foundation/)). "Harness engineering" (Feb 11, 2026) reportedly used a ~100-line AGENTS.md as a table of contents into `docs/` (unverified) ([36kr](https://eu.36kr.com/en/p/3715546375188870)).

#### DeepSeek

(api-docs.deepseek.com, arXiv and Hugging Face were blocked; findings come from search extracts and secondary sources.)
- **Reasoning retention in tool loops (V3.2).**
  - Historical reasoning is discarded **only when a new user message arrives**. Appending tool outputs keeps it, and tool calls and results always stay in context.
  - Copying R1's approach of discarding at the second round "wasted" tokens.
  - Frameworks that simulate tool calls through user messages (Roo Code, Terminus) trigger the discard.
  - [arXiv 2512.02556 (via search)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.02556); consistent with [Cline blog](https://cline.bot/blog/deepseek-v3-2-and-v3-2-speciale-are-now-available-in-cline)
- **API rule.** In thinking mode with tool calls, the assistant message's `reasoning_content` must be passed back with `content` and `tool_calls`, or the API returns 400. Without `tools`, it is not needed and is ignored if sent. The official sample appends the full assistant message.
  - Thinking is enabled via `extra_body={"thinking": {"type": "enabled"}}`. One extract references `deepseek-flash`.
  - A secondary source says old reasoning should be cleared when a new user question begins (not DeepSeek's wording).
  - [Thinking Mode guide (via search)](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/thinking_mode); [CometAPI](https://www.cometapi.com/how-to-use-deepseek-v3-2-api/)
- **Chat-template encoders.**
  - V3.2: `encode_config = dict(thinking_mode="thinking", drop_thinking=True, add_default_bos_token=True)`.
  - V4: `drop_thinking` defaults to True but is automatically disabled when tools are defined, so tool-calling conversations keep full reasoning. Tool results are wrapped in `tool_result` tags inside user messages; three reasoning-effort levels are set as text prefixes; the reference encoder is `encoding_dsv4.py`.
  - [HF mirror](https://huggingface.co/Deniss8686/DeepSeek-V3.2); [V4 encoding README](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-DSpark/raw/main/encoding/README.md) (search-summarized; unverified)
- **Context caching.**
  - Automatic and disk-based (launched Aug 2, 2024 at $0.014/MTok for hits). Usage reports hit and miss tokens separately, and a hit requires the prefix to already be persisted to disk.
  - Later pricing (secondary): V4 Flash $0.0028/MTok hit vs $0.14 miss; V4 Pro $0.003625 hit vs $0.435 miss.
  - [DeepSeek news](https://deepseek.com/en/news/context-caching/); [KV cache guide (via search)](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/kv_cache); [benchlm.ai](https://www.benchlm.ai/deepseek/api-pricing)
- **DeepSeek Sparse Attention (V3.2).**
  - A "lightning indexer" selects the top-2048 KV entries per query (`index_topk` default 2048). Core attention is O(L·k); the indexer stays O(N²) with a small coefficient.
  - Training: a 2.1B-token dense indexer warm-up, then 943.7B tokens of sparse training.
  - The indexer's top-k overlap with exact attention averages ~60% on a 128K HELMET variant, while end-to-end quality stays strong.
  - DSA is the only architectural change in V3.2. A 2025-11-17 disclosure notes the indexer RoPE must be non-interleaved, while MLA RoPE is interleaved.
  - [arXiv 2512.02556 (via search)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.02556); [AMD](https://www.amd.com/en/developer/resources/technical-articles/2025/amd-instinct-mi335x-gpu-supports-deepseek-v3-2-exp.html); [Raschka](https://www.sebastianraschka.com/llm-architecture-gallery/deepseek-sparse-attention/); [arXiv 2512.03494 (via search)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.03494); [V3.2-Exp README](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp/blob/main/README.md)
- **Context-management effect (recalled, unverified).** V3.2's BrowseComp is reported as ~51.4, rising to ~67.6 "with context-management strategies" ([paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.02556); evals notes).
- **Anthropic-compatible endpoint**: `https://api.deepseek.com/anthropic`, where `anthropic-beta` and `anthropic-version` headers are ignored. Inference: Anthropic beta-gated context features (compaction, context editing, inline tools) should not be assumed to work there ([anthropic_api (via search)](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/anthropic_api)).
- **DeepSeek Harness** (reported v0.1, ~Aug 2026): the official README is tiny and only points agents to `AGENTS.md` ([deepseek-harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)).
- **Gaps**: no first-party server-side compaction or context-editing feature was found, and the V4 architecture and context-management features were not researched.

- **LangChain**:
  - The write / select / compress / isolate taxonomy and the `langchain-ai/context_engineering` repo ([README](https://github.com/langchain-ai/context_engineering)).
