### 3.3 Techniques and patterns

Each technique below follows the same layout: *What*, *Mechanics*, *Evidence*, *Use / avoid*.

_Group A: System prompt and baseline context_

**1. Right-altitude system prompts**
- *What:* Write the system prompt at the level between brittle hard-coded if/else logic and vague high-level guidance.
- *Mechanics:*
  - Organize sections with XML tags or Markdown headers.
  - Aim for "the minimal information that fully specifies behavior"; minimal does not have to mean short.
  - Start with a minimal prompt on the best model, then add instructions only in response to observed failures.
  - Use a small, diverse set of canonical examples rather than long lists of edge-case rules.
  - Keep the prompt static: no timestamps, IDs or environment state (see technique 5).
  - Ship per-model prompt variants where the vendor does. Codex ships separate files for each GPT-5.x variant, and vendor models are post-trained inside their harnesses, so matching vendor conventions matters.
- *Evidence:* Qualitative vendor guidance ([Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/effective-context-engineering-for-ai-agents)). Codex's per-model prompts are in [codex-rs/core](https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/main/codex-rs/core).
- *Use / avoid:* Use always. Avoid accreting rules for every past incident; route procedures to skills and area rules to path-scoped files instead.

**2. Per-category token budgets and visibility**
- *What:* Treat the window as a budget broken down by category: tools, system, project instructions, skills index, history, tool results.
- *Mechanics:*
  - Report usage per category, as Claude Code's `/context` does, and give each category a budget.
  - Surface concrete trims, e.g. `/usage` recommends "Trim ~/code/api/CLAUDE.md · 49k tokens per request".
  - On Anthropic, total input = `cache_read_input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens + input_tokens`, where `input_tokens` counts only tokens after the last breakpoint.
  - With compaction, true cost must be summed over `usage.iterations`.
- *Evidence:* [Claude Code: Costs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs); [Prompt caching](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching); [Threshold compaction](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/compaction-threshold).
- *Use / avoid:* Use from day one. The per-category view is what catches a 49k-token instruction file or a 55k-token MCP tool set.

_Group B: Retrieval strategy_

**3. Just-in-time retrieval and agentic search (vs RAG pre-loading)**
- *What:* Keep lightweight identifiers (file paths, stored queries, URLs, line ranges) in context and load data at runtime with tools (grep, glob, read-with-range, `head`/`tail`, queries), instead of pre-loading documents or RAG chunks.
- *Mechanics:*
  - Claude Code analyzes large data by writing queries and using `head`/`tail` without loading full objects.
  - Metadata is signal. Folder hierarchy, naming and timestamps carry meaning (`test_utils.py` under `tests/` vs `src/core_logic/`). File sizes suggest complexity, names suggest purpose, timestamps proxy relevance. This is progressive disclosure.
  - *Hybrid:* pre-load small, stable context (CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, memory index) and fetch everything else. A hybrid may suit less dynamic domains such as legal or finance.
  - Embedding search and RAG become an optional select tool for large, unstructured corpora, not wholesale pre-loading.
  - For code, a ranked symbol map under a token budget is a cheap pre-load (Aider `map_tokens=1024`).
- *Evidence:*
  - Anthropic guidance and practice ([Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/effective-context-engineering-for-ai-agents)). The Agent SDK advice is agentic search first, "only adding semantic search if you need faster results" ([Claude blog](https://claude.com/blog/building-agents-with-the-claude-agent-sdk)).
  - From the memory literature (secondary): a GPT-4o-mini agent with only file tools (`grep`, semantic `search_files`) scored 74.0% on LoCoMo vs Mem0-graph's 68.5% ([Letta blog](https://www.letta.com/blog/benchmarking-ai-agent-memory)).
  - MemoryAgentBench found "RAG is not a silver bullet". BM25 hits 100% vs GPT-4o-mini long context at 22.8% on NIAH-MQ, but RAG fails on global and long-range tasks. Under compute matching, RAG wins at low budgets and long context at higher budgets ([arXiv 2507.05257](https://arxiv.org/html/2507.05257v2)).
- *Use / avoid:*
  - Default for code and file-heavy work.
  - Runtime exploration is slower than pre-computed retrieval and wastes context without good tools and heuristics. Invest in tool quality first.
  - Prefer precision: Chroma's distractor findings mean "semantically near but wrong" content is especially harmful.

**4. Context-rot-aware placement and thresholds**
- *What:* Assume quality degrades with length well inside the advertised window, and design thresholds, placement and pruning for quality, not just to avoid overflow.
- *Mechanics:*
  - Compact or clear at quality thresholds, e.g. Anthropic's 150k default and Manus's 128K–200K "pre-rot threshold".
  - Recite goals near the end of context (technique 22).
  - Put critical instructions at the start or end ("Lost in the Middle").
  - Prune stale and near-duplicate results.
- *Evidence:*
  - **Chroma "Context Rot"** (Jul 14, 2025; Hong, Troynikov, Huber). Primary unreachable; via search extracts and secondary sources.
    - 18 LLMs including GPT-4.1, Claude 4, Gemini 2.5 and Qwen3. Performance "grows increasingly unreliable as input length grows" even on trivial tasks.
    - ~194,480 LLM calls (8 input lengths × 11 needle positions per condition).
    - LongMemEval experiment: 306 prompts, "focused" inputs of ~300 tokens (Hamel Husain's notes say ~100, a conflict) vs full ~113k-token histories with the same answer. Focused inputs scored better across models.
    - Secondary findings:
      - Lower question–needle semantic similarity makes performance fall faster with length.
      - Plausible distractors cut accuracy, and different distractors hurt to different degrees.
      - Shuffled haystacks beat logically coherent ones.
      - On repeated-word copy tasks, long outputs degrade into hallucination, refusal or random tokens.
      - Claude Opus 4 tends to abstain, GPT-4.1 to hallucinate.
      - Thinking mode helps, but the focused-vs-full gap remains.
    - [Chroma (via search extract)](https://research.trychroma.com/context-rot); [ZenML](https://www.zenml.io/llmops-database/context-rot-evaluating-llm-performance-degradation-with-increasing-input-tokens); [hamel.dev](https://hamel.dev/notes/llm/rag/p6-context_rot.html); [gist](https://gist.github.com/cedrickchee/b9646b3007b4a15f528351abd331984f)
  - **Lost in the Middle** (2023, background): accuracy highest when relevant info is at the start or end ([arXiv 2307.03172](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.03172)).
  - **Lab statements**: the Claude docs say "curating what is in context matters as much as available space" ([Context windows](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/context-windows)). Tran and Kiela (Apr 2026, secondary snippet) found that at a fixed thinking-token budget single agents match or beat multi-agent systems, which pull ahead only when the single agent's context use is already degraded ([alphaXiv 2604.02460](https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2604.02460v1)).
- *Use / avoid:* Use for every threshold decision. Do not assume a 1M window means 1M usable tokens at full quality. No public quality-vs-threshold curve exists for current models.

_Group C: Cache-aware layout_

**5. Cache-stable prefix: stable, append-only, deterministic**
- *What:* Order the request so the expensive, stable parts form a byte-identical prefix across every turn, and only ever append to the end.
- *Mechanics:*
  - **Fixed order:** `tools` → `system` → project context (instruction files, skills index, memory index) → append-only `messages`. Anthropic's cache prefix order is `tools` → `system` → `messages`.
  - **Single-token sensitivity:** one changed token invalidates the cache from that point on (Manus). OpenAI: the old prompt must be an exact prefix of the new one (secondary summaries of the Codex loop post).
  - **Determinism:**
    - Serialize JSON keys and tool lists in a fixed order.
    - Request deterministic `tools/list` from MCP servers (MCP 2026-07-28) and cache it by `ttlMs`.
    - Never put a timestamp at the start of the system prompt.
    - Claude Code workflow scripts make `Date.now()`, `Math.random()` and `new Date()` throw so replays are identical ([Workflows](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows)).
  - **Things that bust the cache (avoid mid-session):**
    - Claude Code list: switching model (each model has its own cache), changing effort (except on Opus/Sonnet/Haiku 5.5 and Fable 5.1), connecting or removing an MCP server, denying an entire tool, compaction, and removing batches of old images.
    - Anthropic API invalidation matrix: tool definition changes invalidate everything. Web-search/citations toggles and the speed setting invalidate system + messages. `tool_choice`, images, thinking parameters and effort invalidate messages; thinking and effort can also invalidate tools and system on some models. On older models, non-tool-result user content strips cached thinking.
    - Changing the thinking `budget_tokens` or mode invalidates breakpoints; the docs demonstrate a full re-creation of a 1,370-token cache.
  - **Model routing:** each model has its own cache. Route side tasks (compaction, titles) to forks or subagents that share or have their own prefix, rather than switching the main model. On OpenAI, change effort via a `configuration_update` input item instead of request-level `reasoning.effort`.
- *Evidence:*
  - Manus economics (secondary): ~100:1 input:output, ~50 tool calls per typical task, Claude Sonnet cached $0.30/MTok vs $3 uncached (10×) ([Manus (via search)](https://manus.im/blog/Context-Engineering-for-AI-Agents-Lessons-from-Building-Manus)).
  - Anthropic reads cost 0.1× base (0.05× on Opus/Sonnet 5.5; 0.025× on Fable/Mythos 5.1) ([Prompt caching](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching)).
  - OpenAI caching gives up to 90% lower input cost and 80% lower latency ([OpenAI (via search)](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompt-caching)).
  - One article reportedly calls cache misses "production incidents" ([implicator.ai](https://www.implicator.ai/anthropic-says-cache-misses-are-production-incidents-reveals-caching-shaped-claude-code/), secondary, not verified).
- *Use / avoid:* Always. The only deliberate breaks should be "expected rebuilds" (compaction, clearing) that are logged as such.

**6. Cache-safe dynamic content (appended, not edited)**
- *What:* Put time, environment state, file-change notices, budgets, todo recitation and per-turn reminders after the cached prefix, as appended messages, never in `system`.
- *Mechanics:*
  - **Claude mid-conversation system messages:** append `{"role":"system", ...}` to `messages` instead of editing top-level `system`. No beta header on supported 5.x models.
  - **Turn-scoped system messages** (beta `mid-conversation-system-clear-at-2026-08-21`):
    - Set `clear_at: "next_user_message"`. The message renders only until the next user or `tool_result` message, then costs 0 tokens.
    - Designed for per-turn reminders in tool loops that never pile up.
    - Resend cleared messages verbatim.
  - **Claude Code pattern:**
    - File edits produce an appended `<system-reminder>` instead of rewriting earlier reads.
    - Plan mode and skill loading append messages.
    - CLAUDE.md edits take effect only after `/clear`, `/compact` or a restart.
  - **Mid-conversation tool changes** (beta `inline-tools-2026-09-15`):
    - `tool_addition`/`tool_removal` blocks add, change or withdraw tools (including defining a new tool by value) while the `tools` array and earlier messages stay byte-identical.
    - Keep at least one non-deferred tool in `tools`, or the first by-value definition costs a full cache miss.
  - **OpenAI:** `allowed_tools` restricts callable tools per turn without changing `tools` (third-party description). `configuration_update` changes effort in-band.
  - **Self-hosted models:** Manus-style logit/prefill masking with namespaced tool prefixes (`browser_*`, `shell_*`) constrains action groups without changing definitions.
- *Evidence:* [Mid-conversation system messages](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-system-messages); [Claude Code: Prompt caching](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/prompt-caching); [Manus gist](https://gist.github.com/cedrickchee/b9646b3007b4a15f528351abd331984f).
- *Use / avoid:*
  - Use turn-scoped messages for anything that is only true "right now" (budget, time, git status).
  - Use persistent appended messages for facts that must stay (a newly loaded nested instruction file).
  - Never edit earlier turns client-side. On Claude 5.1+ that breaks thinking signatures and the prefix check.

**7. Breakpoint placement and TTL management (Anthropic)**
- *What:* Choose where cache writes happen and how long entries live.
- *Mechanics:*
  - **Modes:** automatic caching (one top-level `cache_control` moves the breakpoint to the last cacheable block each turn) or up to 4 explicit breakpoints; the automatic one uses a slot.
  - **Lookback:** writes occur only at breakpoints. Reads walk back at most 20 blocks (a run of consecutive `tool_use`/`tool_result` blocks counts as one position). A turn that adds 20 or more blocks between writes misses unless there is a second breakpoint.
  - **TTL:**
    - Default 5 minutes, refreshed free on each hit; 1-hour TTL costs 2× on write.
    - Lifetime is measured from the start of the request, so a 4-minute streamed response leaves ~1 minute to send the follow-up.
    - An entry is available only once the first response starts, so parallel fan-out should wait for the first response.
  - **Minimum cacheable length** (shorter prompts silently don't cache):
    - 512 tokens: Opus 5.5/5, Sonnet 5.5, Fable 5/5.1, Haiku 5.5
    - 1,024: Sonnet 4.6, Sonnet 5, Opus 4.8
    - 2,048: Opus 4.7
    - 4,096: Opus 4.6/4.5, Haiku 4.5
  - **Classic mistake:** a breakpoint on a block containing a timestamp means a write every request and never a read.
  - **Compaction:** put `cache_control` on the compaction block and a separate breakpoint at the end of the system prompt, so the system-prompt cache survives and only the summary is re-written.
  - **Claude Code TTL policy:**
    - Main conversation: 1 h on a subscription within plan usage; 5 min on API key or credits.
    - Subagents, compaction, forks and titles: 5 min. `subagentPromptCacheTtl: 1h` extends subagents at a higher write cost.
    - Workflow fan-outs hold all but the first agent for up to 5 s so they read its prefix.
    - With the 1 h TTL, Claude Code can idle-compact (`idleCompaction`).
- *Evidence:* [Prompt caching](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching); [Claude Code: Prompt caching](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/prompt-caching); [Workflows](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows). Pricing examples are in 3.4.
- *Use / avoid:*
  - Use 1 h TTL for interactive sessions with human think time.
  - Use 5 min for tight tool loops and subagents.
  - Add the mid-history breakpoint only when a turn can add 20+ blocks (large parallel fan-outs).

_Group D: Tools as context_

**8. Deferred tool loading plus tool search**
- *What:* Exclude most tool definitions from the prompt and let the model discover them through a search tool.
- *Mechanics:*
  - **Deferral:** mark tools `defer_loading: true`; keep the 3–5 most-used tools non-deferred, and never defer the search tool itself. For MCP, use `mcp_toolset` with `default_config: {"defer_loading": true}` plus per-tool `configs`.
  - **Variants:** `tool_search_tool_regex_20251119` takes Python `re.search` patterns ≤200 chars. `tool_search_tool_bm25_20251119` takes natural-language queries ≤500 chars. Both search names, descriptions, argument names and argument descriptions.
  - **Limits:** returns up to 5 `tool_reference` blocks by default (`limit` 1–10,000); up to 10,000 deferred tools per request.
  - **Custom search:** return `tool_reference` blocks from your own tool (e.g. embeddings; a cookbook `tool_search_with_embeddings.ipynb` exists).
  - **Caching:** deferred tools are excluded from the system-prompt prefix, and a discovered tool is appended inline as a `tool_reference`, so the prefix and cache are untouched. A deferred tool cannot carry `cache_control`.
  - **Claude Code:** MCP tools are deferred by default; only names and server instructions are in context until used.
  - **OpenAI:** `tool_search` on gpt-5.4+. **Codex:** registers a `tool_search` handler.
  - **Manus alternative:** keep definitions fixed and mask logits. Manus explicitly avoided RAG-selecting tools for cache reasons.
- *Evidence:*
  - Typical 5-server setup (GitHub, Slack, Sentry, Grafana, Splunk): 58 tools ≈ 55K tokens (Jira alone ≈ 17K). Definitions of 134K were seen before optimization.
  - Traditional loading ≈ 77K tokens before work (50+ tools ≈ 72K) vs ≈ 8.7K with tool search (≈500 upfront + ~3K discovered), an 85%+ reduction.
  - MCP-eval accuracy: Opus 4 49% → 74%; Opus 4.5 79.5% → 88.1%.
  - Claude's selection accuracy "degrades once you exceed 30–50 available tools".
  - The post also cites 191,300 vs 122,800 tokens preserved, which it doesn't reconcile with the other figures.
  - Secondary: a quantized Llama 3.1 8B failed with 46 tools and succeeded with 19 (Breunig, unverified).
  - [Tool search tool](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/tool-search-tool); [Advanced tool use](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/advanced-tool-use); [Breunig](https://www.dbreunig.com/2025/06/26/how-to-fix-your-context.html)
- *Use / avoid:*
  - Use when definitions exceed 10K tokens, with 10+ tools, multiple MCP servers, or observed selection errors. The docs' rollout order says past ~20 tools.
  - Not worth it for <10 tools or compact definitions.
  - Use embedding search only for catalogs of thousands of tools.

**9. Programmatic tool calling (PTC) and code-mode**
- *What:* The model writes code that calls tools as functions inside a sandbox; intermediate results stay in the sandbox and only the final output enters context.
- *Mechanics:*
  - **Claude PTC:**
    - Mark tools `allowed_callers: ["code_execution_20260120"]`; the current docs require code execution `code_execution_20260120`+. The Nov 2025 launch used `{"type":"code_execution_20250825","name":"code_execution"}` with `allowed_callers: ["code_execution_20250825"]`.
    - Claude writes Python that calls tools as async functions (parallel via `asyncio.gather`). Each call pauses execution and returns a `tool_use` with a `caller` field. The model's code invocation appears as `server_tool_use` and output as `code_execution_tool_result`.
    - Not on Haiku 4.5. Not ZDR-eligible (data kept up to 30 days). `allowed_callers` is guidance, not a security boundary.
  - **Code execution with MCP:**
    - Present each server as a folder (`./servers/google-drive/getDocument.ts`, one typed TS file per tool wrapping `callMCPTool('google_drive__get_document', …)`).
    - The agent lists directories and reads only what it needs, or calls `search_tools` with detail levels: name only, name + description, or full schema.
    - PII can be tokenized by the MCP client (`[EMAIL_1]`) and untokenized between tools. State persists in workspace files, and working code can be saved as a `SKILL.md` skill.
  - **Codex code-mode:** `code-mode`, `code-mode-runtime` and `code-mode-host` crates; `augment_tool_spec_for_code_mode` adds exec samples to descriptions. OpenCode has a `codemode` package; smolagents `CodeAgent` writes actions as Python.
  - **Claude Code workflows:** code-driven fan-out where "Claude's context holds only the final answer".
- *Evidence:*
  - PTC: average tokens 43,588 → 27,297 (−37%) on complex research tasks. Internal knowledge retrieval 25.6% → 28.5%; GAIA 46.5% → 51.2% (benchmark label conflict noted in 3.9).
  - 20+ calls in one code block save 19+ inference passes. A budget/expense example: 2,000+ line items (200KB+) reduced to ~1KB in context. Claude for Excel uses PTC.
  - Code-mode MCP: 150,000 → 2,000 tokens (98.7%). A 10,000-row spreadsheet filtered to 5 rows before reaching the model; a 2-hour meeting transcript (~50,000 tokens) need not pass through context twice.
  - [PTC docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/programmatic-tool-calling); [Advanced tool use](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/advanced-tool-use); [Code execution with MCP](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/code-execution-with-mcp); [code_mode.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/tools/src/code_mode.rs)
- *Use / avoid:*
  - Use for 3+ dependent calls, large data, filtering, parallel fan-out, and bulk data tools (mark them code-only callers).
  - It requires a secure sandbox with resource limits and monitoring, and tool calls now originate from model-written code. Keep destructive tools direct-call and approval-gated.
  - Avoid on ZDR-required workloads (Claude PTC).

**10. Tool output hygiene (bounded, paginated, semantic, offloaded)**
- *What:* Every tool returns small, high-signal output by default.
- *Mechanics:*
  - **Size limits:** paginate, select ranges, filter and truncate with sensible defaults. "Claude Code restricts tool responses to 25,000 tokens by default." Truncation messages should steer the agent toward narrower, targeted searches.
  - **Verbosity modes:** add a `response_format` enum (`concise`/`detailed`).
  - **Semantic fields:** return `name`, `image_url`, `file_type` rather than `uuid`, `256px_image_url`, `mime_type`. Resolving IDs to natural-language names or 0-indexed IDs reduced hallucinations.
  - **Consolidation:** e.g. `schedule_event` replaces `list_users` + `list_events` + `create_event`; `search_logs` with context lines; `get_customer_context`.
  - **Namespacing:** by service or resource; whether a prefix or suffix works better depends on the model.
  - **Errors:** make them actionable, ideally with a correct-input example. Return validation errors as tool results (MCP SEP-1303).
  - **Offload large outputs to files** and return a path plus preview (Manus restorable compression; deepagents `_blob_offload.py`). A related open-source mechanism is Gemini CLI's `toolOutputMaskingService`.
  - **Test output for agents:** keep it to a few lines, send details to log files, and tag errors `ERROR` so they are grep-able. Precompute summary stats and offer a deterministic `--fast` 1%/10% sample ([Anthropic C compiler](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/building-c-compiler)).
  - **File views:** `text_editor_20250728` added `max_characters` for truncating large file views. The memory tool's `view` truncates text over 16,000 characters.
- *Evidence:* one example used 206 tokens detailed vs 72 concise; a Slack example was ~1/3 the tokens when concise ([Writing tools](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/writing-tools-for-agents)).
- *Use / avoid:* Use on every tool, which makes this the first rung of the compaction ladder. Don't truncate silently: say what was cut and how to get more.

**11. Tool-use examples and description quality**
- *What:* Attach realistic `input_examples` to complex tools and write descriptions "as if onboarding a new hire".
- *Mechanics:* use 1–5 realistic examples (minimal/partial/full) showing format conventions (`YYYY-MM-DD`, `USR-XXXXX`), nesting, and correlated optional parameters. Use unambiguous parameter names (`user_id`, not `user`).
- *Evidence:*
  - Complex-parameter accuracy rose from 72% to 90% ([Advanced tool use](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/advanced-tool-use)).
  - Claude-optimized Slack and Asana MCP servers beat human-written ones on held-out tests. A fix found this way: Claude was appending "2025" to search queries, corrected via the tool description ([Writing tools](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/writing-tools-for-agents)).
- *Use / avoid:* Use for complex schemas. They are not needed for simple tools or for formats JSON Schema already enforces, and examples add tokens to non-deferred definitions.

**12. Skills with progressive disclosure**
- *What:* Package procedures as folders with a `SKILL.md` that load in stages.
- *Mechanics:*
  - **Level 1:** metadata (`name` + `description` from YAML frontmatter), always loaded, about 100 tokens per skill.
  - **Level 2:** the SKILL.md body, loaded when triggered, under 5k tokens.
  - **Level 3+:** bundled `scripts/`, `references/`, `assets/` cost zero tokens until read. Scripts run via bash and only their output enters context.
  - **Authoring rules:**
    - `name` ≤64 chars; the `description` says what the skill does and when to use it.
    - Body under 500 lines.
    - References one level deep from SKILL.md, with a table of contents on reference files over 100 lines.
    - Organize by domain so irrelevant schemas aren't loaded.
    - Ask "does this paragraph justify its token cost?"
  - **Claude Code:** `disable-model-invocation: true` keeps a skill's description out of context. After compaction, invoked skill bodies are re-injected (5k tokens each, 25k total, oldest dropped first, truncated from the end), so put critical instructions at the top of SKILL.md.
- *Evidence:*
  - SkillsBench (NeurIPS 2026, secondary): curated skills +16.2pp on average (+4.5pp SWE to +51.9pp healthcare; 16/84 tasks regress). Self-generated skills give no benefit on average (NeurIPS version −1.3pp; curated +16.4pp) ([arXiv 2602.12670](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.12670v1)).
  - [Skills overview](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/overview); [Best practices](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/best-practices); [Claude Code: Context window](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/context-window)
- *Use / avoid:*
  - Use for multi-step procedures and domain knowledge. Build skills from evaluation-observed gaps and watch triggering (name and description drive it).
  - Curate or verify before promotion; don't auto-install self-authored skills.
  - Audit third-party skills, which can exfiltrate data.

_Group E: Instruction files_

**13. Hierarchical instruction files (CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md) and path-scoped rules**
- *What:* Pre-loaded project context that is paid on every request, so it holds only always-true facts: build and test commands, conventions, layout, "always do X".
- *Mechanics:*
  - **Size and content (Claude Code):**
    - Under 200 lines per CLAUDE.md; "Longer files consume more context and reduce adherence."
    - Move multi-step procedures to skills and area rules to `.claude/rules/*.md` with `paths:` globs, which load only when matching files are touched.
    - `@path` imports organize but don't reduce cost; they recurse up to 4 hops, and external imports need one-time approval.
    - Block-level HTML comments are stripped before injection.
    - Files over 4 MiB are skipped.
    - Contradictions cause arbitrary choices; `/doctor prompt-audit` audits them.
    - Instructions are context, not enforcement; use PreToolUse hooks to block actions.
  - **Hierarchy (Claude Code):**
    - Managed policy (`/etc/claude-code/CLAUDE.md` etc.) → user (`~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`) → project (`./CLAUDE.md` or `./.claude/CLAUDE.md`) → local. Files from root to cwd are concatenated root-first; `CLAUDE.local.md` is appended after `CLAUDE.md` at each level.
    - Subdirectory CLAUDE.md files load lazily when Claude reads, writes or edits a file in that subtree. `claudeMdExcludes` skips other teams' files in monorepos.
    - Auto memory loads the first 200 lines or 25KB of `MEMORY.md`.
  - **AGENTS.md in Claude Code:** read when no CLAUDE.md exists. If both exist, only CLAUDE.md is read unless it imports `@AGENTS.md`. The `agents-md` mod modes are `claude-md-or-agents-md` (default), `claude-md-and-agents-md`, `managed-only` and `claude-md`.
  - **AGENTS.md in Codex:** root-to-cwd discovery, `AGENTS.override.md`, `--- project-doc ---` joiner, a `project_doc_max_bytes` budget, deeper files win, and direct instructions beat AGENTS.md.
  - **Compaction interaction:** the project-root CLAUDE.md is re-read and re-injected after `/compact`. Nested files and path-scoped rules are summarized away and reload when a matching file is touched again. Instructions given only in conversation are lost unless written to CLAUDE.md.
- *Evidence:*
  - AGENTS.md is "a README for agents"; its canonical sections are dev environment tips, testing instructions and PR instructions ([agents.md README](https://github.com/agentsmd/agents.md)).
  - Stewarded by the AAIF since Dec 9, 2025; one report cites ~40,000 open-source projects ([InfoQ](https://infoq.com/news/2025/12/agentic-ai-foundation/)).
  - OpenAI "Harness engineering" reportedly used a ~100-line AGENTS.md as a table of contents into `docs/` (unverified).
  - [Claude Code: Memory](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory); [Codex agents_md.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/core/src/agents_md.rs); [mods README](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/main/mods/README.md)
- *Use / avoid:* Use for always-true facts. Keep multi-step procedures (skills) and area-specific rules (path-scoped files) out of root files. Treat imports that resolve outside the repo as untrusted.

_Group F: Shrinking history: clearing and compaction_

**14. Tool-result clearing (Anthropic context editing)**
- *What:* Server-side replacement of old tool results (and optionally their inputs) with placeholder text once the prompt grows past a trigger. It is the lightest and most reversible form of compaction, because the client keeps the full history.
- *Mechanics:*
  - **`clear_tool_uses_20250919`** (beta `context-management-2025-06-27`):
    - `trigger` defaults to 100,000 input tokens (can also be expressed in `tool_uses`); `keep` defaults to the last 3 tool use/result pairs.
    - `clear_at_least` sets a minimum number of tokens to clear, otherwise the edit is skipped. It exists to justify breaking the cache.
    - `exclude_tools` lists tools whose results are never cleared; `clear_tool_inputs` (default false) also clears call parameters.
  - **Cache cost:** clearing invalidates the cached prefix from the cleared point, so you pay a cache write each time.
  - **Telemetry:** the response carries `context_management.applied_edits` with `cleared_input_tokens`; `count_tokens` returns `input_tokens` and `original_input_tokens`.
  - **Memory pairing:** with the memory tool, Claude gets an automatic warning near the clearing threshold so it can save important results to memory files before they are cleared.
  - **Open-source analogues:** Gemini CLI `toolOutputMaskingService`/`toolDistillationService`; deepagents `_message_eviction.py`; Codex remote-v2 `compact_retained_tool_outputs.rs` (retain selected outputs).
- *Evidence:*
  - Internal agentic-search eval (Sep 29, 2025): memory tool + context editing +39% over baseline; context editing alone +29%.
  - 100-turn web-search eval: context editing let runs complete that otherwise exhausted context, and cut token consumption 84%.
  - [Context editing](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/context-editing); [Claude blog](https://claude.com/blog/context-management)
- *Use / avoid:*
  - Use for long tool loops where old observations are stale; keep ≈3–5 recent results.
  - Set `clear_at_least` large enough to amortize the cache write.
  - Exclude memory, todo and plan tools.
  - Avoid when old tool results are the evidence the task depends on. Offload them to files first.

**15. Reasoning-state management across turns (thinking blocks, encrypted reasoning, `reasoning_content`)**
- *What:* Replay each provider's reasoning artifacts exactly as required, so tool loops stay valid and cache-stable.
- *Mechanics:*
  - **Anthropic:**
    - Opus 4.5+, Sonnet 4.6+, Haiku 5.5 and Fable/Mythos keep previous thinking blocks by default and bill them as input; older models strip them.
    - Thinking blocks paired with tool results must be returned unmodified with their signature.
    - `clear_thinking_20251015`: `keep` = `{type:"thinking_turns", value:N}` or `"all"`. The default keeps all prior thinking on Opus 4.5+, Sonnet 4.6+ and Haiku 5.5+, and only the last turn on older models. It must be listed first when combined with tool clearing. Keeping thinking preserves the cache.
    - On Claude 5.1+, thinking before a compaction block is not carried forward.
    - Manual `thinking.type: "enabled"` with `budget_tokens` is rejected (400) on Claude 4.7+; use `thinking: {type: "adaptive"}` and `output_config.effort` ([Extended thinking](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/extended-thinking)).
  - **OpenAI:** `include: ["reasoning.encrypted_content"]` with `store: false` (Codex). The Agents SDK's `reasoning_item_id_policy: "omit"` avoids 400s from orphaned reasoning items.
  - **DeepSeek:**
    - Pass `reasoning_content` back with `content` and `tool_calls` inside tool loops, or get a 400.
    - Reasoning is dropped only at a new user message, so do not simulate tool results as user messages.
    - For self-hosted weights, use the official `encoding_dsv32.py`/`encoding_dsv4.py` encoders. `drop_thinking` is auto-disabled when tools are defined in V4.
- *Evidence:* [Context windows](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/context-windows); [Context editing](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/context-editing); [client.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/core/src/client.rs); [DeepSeek Thinking Mode (via search)](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/thinking_mode); [arXiv 2512.02556 (via search)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.02556).
- *Use / avoid:* Always implement per provider. Never edit or reorder reasoning items client-side; use server-side edits (`clear_thinking`) when you must reduce them.

**16. Threshold server-side compaction (Anthropic `compact_20260112`)**
- *What:* The API summarizes the conversation automatically once input crosses a trigger, then continues in the same request.
- *Mechanics:*
  - **Enable:** add `{"type":"compact_20260112"}` to `context_management.edits` with beta header `compact-2026-01-12`.
  - **`trigger`:** defaults to `{"type":"input_tokens","value":150000}`. `input_tokens` is the only type, and the value must be ≥50,000.
  - **`pause_after_compaction`** (default false): when true, the API stops with `stop_reason: "compaction"` so you can re-insert content. Combined with a compaction counter, it can enforce a total token budget.
  - **`instructions`** fully replaces the default summarization prompt.
  - **Flow:**
    - The API writes a summary into a `compaction` block at the start of the assistant response and continues. On later requests everything before the block is dropped.
    - Streamed compaction blocks arrive as a single delta.
    - With server tools, the trigger is checked at each sampling iteration, so one request can compact several times.
    - `count_tokens` applies existing blocks but never triggers new ones.
  - **Default prompt (one variant):** "You have written a partial transcript for the initial task above. Please write a summary of the transcript. The purpose of this summary is to provide continuity so you can continue to make progress towards solving the task in a future context, where the raw history above may not be accessible and will be replaced with this summary. Write down anything that would be helpful, including the state, next steps, learnings etc. You must wrap your summary in a `<summary></summary>` block."
  - **Billing:** compaction adds a sampling iteration. Top-level `usage.input_tokens`/`output_tokens` exclude it, so sum over `usage.iterations`.
  - **Caching:** put `cache_control` on the compaction block, plus a separate breakpoint at the end of the system prompt.
- *Evidence / limitations:*
  - The summary is written by the request's own model; you cannot pick a cheaper summarizer.
  - With tools defined, the model sometimes calls a tool instead of summarizing (`content: null`). Fix with instructions such as "Do not call any tools while writing this summary; respond with text only."
  - On Claude 5.1+ the summary must hold everything needed, because earlier thinking is dropped.
  - Managed Agents always has compaction on and emits `agent.thread_context_compacted`.
  - [Threshold compaction](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/compaction-threshold)
- *Use / avoid:* Use when you want zero-client-logic compaction. Prefer on-demand compaction (17) where available, because it gives control over timing, kept tail and background execution.

**17. On-demand, keep-tail and background compaction (Anthropic `compact-2026-09-04`)**
- *What:* The client asks for a signed summary block whenever it chooses, decides which recent turns stay verbatim, and can compute the summary in the background.
- *Mechanics:*
  - **Request:**
    - Send the conversation with `"compaction": {"type":"summarize"}`. The response is a single signed `compaction` block with `stop_reason: "compaction"` and no reply.
    - Send the same `system` and `tools` as the conversation. The summarizer reads tool definitions but never runs a tool.
    - `max_tokens` caps summary plus thinking, so allow several thousand.
    - Cannot be combined with `context_management` on the same request.
    - `instructions` takes up to 16,384 characters and replaces the default prompt.
  - **Swap rules:**
    - The block goes first in `messages` and replaces the summarized messages. Send exactly one block, unmodified (with its signature), on every later request.
    - Errors: `compaction_block_misplaced`, `compaction_signature_invalid`, `compaction_nothing_to_summarize`.
    - Silent failures: leaving summarized messages after the block re-sends them; omitting the block means no summary.
    - "Compact again" summarizes the old summary plus everything after it.
  - **When to compact:** estimate the next request as `input_tokens + cache_read_input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens + output_tokens` from the last `usage`, and compare it to a limit you choose below the window. The Python and TypeScript SDK tool runners expose `compact_before_next_turn()` (cookbook `automatic-context-compaction.ipynb`).
  - **Failure handling:** a summary is produced only when the call ends normally with text. Otherwise you get HTTP 200 with empty content and `stop_reason` of `max_tokens`, `model_context_window_exceeded`, `tool_use`, `refusal` or `end_turn`. Compact before overflow, because the conversation plus summarization prompt must still fit.
  - **What is lost:** images, documents, `container_upload` blocks and fetched URLs in summarized messages. Mid-conversation `role:"system"` instructions in the summarized range stop applying, and per-message effort is not carried over.
  - **Keep-tail:**
    - There is no parameter; the client picks a cut point, sends only the older turns to compaction, then sends block + kept turns verbatim (thinking included).
    - The cut must not split a tool call from its result.
    - The reference loop keeps the last 2 turns (cut 4 messages from the end).
  - **Background ("async"):**
    - Fire the compaction request with the history as it stands, record the message count, and keep working on the full history.
    - When the block arrives, replace exactly the first N messages with it and keep turns appended since.
    - Do not edit history or start a second compaction while one is pending.
    - Start early enough that the window can absorb the turns that arrive meanwhile.
  - **Cookbook:** `misc/session_memory_compaction.ipynb` builds background session memory for "instant compaction" with threading plus prompt caching (claimed ~80% cost reduction for the background updates).
- *Evidence:* [Compaction on demand](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/compaction-on-demand); [Keep recent turns](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/compaction-keep-recent-turns); [Compaction in the background](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/compaction-background); [cookbooks](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-cookbooks/blob/main/misc/session_memory_compaction.ipynb).
- *Use / avoid:* The default on Claude where supported. Background compaction removes the user-visible pause but requires append-only history semantics.

**18. OpenAI Responses compaction (`/responses/compact`, `compact_threshold`)**
- *What:* Provider-side compaction that returns an opaque, encrypted compaction item.
- *Mechanics:*
  - **Standalone endpoint:** `/responses/compact` is stateless and ZDR-friendly. Pass the returned window unchanged to the next `/responses` call ("Do not prune /responses/compact output").
  - **Inline:** `context_management.compact_threshold` on `POST /responses` (doc examples use 200,000 with `store=false`). The server compacts when the rendered token count crosses the threshold and streams the item.
  - **Pruning:** with `previous_response_id`, do not prune manually. With an input array, items before the latest compaction item may be dropped.
  - **Integrations:** Agents SDK `OpenAIResponsesCompactionSession`; Codex remote-v2 path; LiteLLM and Vercel gateways.
- *Evidence:* [Compaction guide (via search)](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/compaction); [Context management (via search)](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/context-management). GPT-5.1-Codex-Max was trained across compaction boundaries and can work "over millions of tokens on one task"; OpenAI observed >24-hour tasks internally ([OpenAI (snippet)](https://openai.com/index/gpt-5-1-codex-max/)).
- *Use / avoid:* Use with OpenAI models, especially Codex models trained with it. The summary cannot be inspected or edited, so keep your own readable state (todo, notes, progress) alongside it. The default prompt, item contents and any minimum or default threshold were unverifiable.

**19. Client-side handoff-summary compaction (Codex recipe and open-source variants)**
- *What:* The harness asks the model for a structured handoff summary and rebuilds history around it.
- *Mechanics:*
  - **Codex prompt** (`codex-rs/prompts/templates/compact/prompt.md`): "You are performing a CONTEXT CHECKPOINT COMPACTION. Create a handoff summary for another LLM that will resume the task. Include: Current progress and key decisions made; Important context, constraints, or user preferences; What remains to be done (clear next steps); Any critical data, examples, or references needed to continue. Be concise, structured, and focused on helping the next LLM seamlessly continue the work."
  - **Codex summary prefix:** "Another language model started to solve this problem and produced a summary of its thinking process. You also have access to the state of the tools that were used by that language model. Use this to build on the work that has already been done and avoid duplicating work…"
  - **Codex history rebuild:**
    - New history = initial context + the user's own prior messages (newest-first, up to `COMPACT_USER_MESSAGE_MAX_TOKENS = 20_000`, over-budget messages truncated, images and audio dropped) + the summary.
    - The initial context is inserted before the last real user message or summary.
    - `compact_prompt` in config overrides the prompt. Compaction runs inline when the limit is hit (`run_inline_auto_compact_task`) or manually.
  - **Codex thresholds:**
    - `auto_compact_token_limit()` = min(`model_auto_compact_token_limit`, 90% of window); without config, 90%.
    - `effective_context_window_percent` = 95% (headroom for system prompt, tools, output).
    - `model_auto_compact_token_limit_scope` (full context vs tokens after the carried compaction prefix).
    - `model_post_turn_compact_threshold_percent` (turn-end compaction; 0 disables).
    - The `token_budget` feature has `reminder_threshold_tokens`, `auto_compact_fallback_prompt` (≤2,000 bytes) and `auto_compact_fallback_buffer_tokens`.
  - **Deprecated Anthropic SDK `compaction_control`:** default `context_token_threshold` 100,000; ~100k histories shrank to "~2–3k tokens". The prompt had 5 sections: Task Overview; Current State (files modified, artifacts); Important Discoveries (constraints, decisions, errors resolved, failed approaches); Next Steps (blockers, priorities); Context to Preserve (user preferences, commitments). Removed in Python SDK v1.0.
  - **Other recipes:**
    - Gemini CLI compresses at 50% of window and keeps the latest 30%.
    - OpenHands summarizes the first half of events (`keep_first=2`, `max_size=240`).
    - Cline keeps a hash-validated `${sessionId}.compaction.json` projection beside the canonical transcript.
    - deepagents uses a summarization middleware plus filesystem offload.
  - **Claude Code:** compaction preserves "architectural decisions, unresolved bugs, and implementation details" and discards redundant tool outputs. User controls are `/compact <focus instructions>`, `/rewind` → "Summarize from here / up to here", and custom compaction instructions in CLAUDE.md. Since v2.1.198 the summarization request inherits the session's thinking configuration.
- *Evidence:* [compact.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/core/src/compact.rs); [prompt.md](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/prompts/templates/compact/prompt.md); [summary_prefix.md](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/prompts/templates/compact/summary_prefix.md); [openai_models.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/protocol/src/openai_models.rs); [config/mod.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/core/src/config/mod.rs); [Context editing](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/context-editing); [Claude Code: Context window](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/context-window). There is no head-to-head benchmark of Anthropic server compaction vs OpenAI compaction vs the Codex prompt.
- *Use / avoid:*
  - Use as the provider-neutral fallback (DeepSeek, self-hosted, unknown providers), and as the template for `instructions` on Anthropic.
  - The recommended summary schema merges the Anthropic SDK and Codex prompts: task and constraints, current state and files touched, decisions and rationale, errors and failed approaches, next steps, user preferences, and always "do not call tools".
  - Avoid compacting mid-subtask. Compact at natural task breaks, and prefer `/rewind`-style truncation to an already-cached prefix when abandoning a path ([Claude Code: Prompt caching](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/prompt-caching)).

**20. Post-compaction re-injection of durable state**
- *What:* After any summary, re-load from disk the things a summary must not be trusted to carry.
- *Mechanics (Claude Code list):*
  - The system prompt and output style still apply.
  - Re-injected from disk: project-root CLAUDE.md and unscoped rules, auto memory, the plan-mode plan, and a fresh git status snapshot.
  - Skill descriptions are rebuilt; invoked skill bodies come back at ≤5,000 tokens per skill and ≤25,000 total, oldest dropped first, truncated from the end.
  - Path-scoped rules and nested CLAUDE.md files reload on demand.
  - Up to 5 most recently modified read or edited files are re-read; files over 5,000 tokens come back as a path-only "Referenced file".
  - Background commands and subagents keep running, with a reminder so they are not duplicated.
  - Hook-added context is summarized, and SessionStart hooks matching `compact` run again.
  - Codex re-inserts initial context plus ≤20k tokens of user messages. On Anthropic, `pause_after_compaction` gives the client a hook point to re-insert content.
- *Evidence:* [Claude Code: Context window](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/context-window); [Threshold compaction](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/compaction-threshold).
- *Use / avoid:* Always pair compaction with re-injection, and hook "reload task state" into post-compaction events. Instructions that exist only in conversation are lost, so persist them to files.

**21. Restorable compression and the file system as context**
- *What:* Drop bulky content from the window but keep a pointer (path, URL, query) so it can be re-fetched. Only summarize irreversibly when that no longer frees enough space.
- *Mechanics:*
  - Manus: the file system is "the ultimate context" (unlimited, persistent, directly operable). Compaction strips content that also exists in the environment or file system and keeps a path; summarization is the irreversible fallback.
  - Sub-agents write outputs to external storage and return lightweight references to avoid a "game of telephone".
  - Claude Code returns >5k-token files after compaction as path-only "Referenced file".
  - deepagents `_blob_offload.py`.
- *Evidence:* [Manus gist](https://gist.github.com/cedrickchee/b9646b3007b4a15f528351abd331984f); [ZenML webinar summary](https://www.zenml.io/llmops-database/context-engineering-for-production-ai-agents-at-scale) (secondary); [Anthropic multi-agent](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/multi-agent-research-system).
- *Use / avoid:* Use as rung 2 of the ladder, before any summarization. It requires a persistent workspace.

_Group G: State outside the window_

**22. Recitation and structured note-taking (todo.md, NOTES.md, memory tool)**
- *What:* The agent writes its plan, progress and findings to files and re-reads or rewrites them, which pushes goals into recent attention and survives resets.
- *Mechanics:*
  - **Manus:** rewrites `todo.md` step by step so the global plan sits at the end of context, against lost-in-the-middle and goal drift over ~50-step loops.
  - **Anthropic:** agent-written notes (to-do lists, NOTES.md). Claude playing Pokémon kept tallies such as "for the last 1,234 steps" of training, and maintained maps and strategy notes across resets.
  - **Memory tool `memory_20250818`:**
    - Client-side `/memories` operations: `view`, `create`, `str_replace`, `insert`, `delete`, `rename`. `view` truncates text over 16,000 characters.
    - The API auto-injects: "IMPORTANT: ALWAYS VIEW YOUR MEMORY DIRECTORY BEFORE DOING ANYTHING ELSE… ASSUME INTERRUPTION: Your context window might be reset at any moment, so you risk losing any progress that is not recorded in your memory directory."
    - The handler must block path traversal.
  - **Plan tools:** Codex `update_plan` ("Do not repeat the full contents of the plan after an `update_plan` call — the harness already displays it"); Claude Code `TodoWrite`/`Task*`, opt-in on newest models via `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TODO_TOOLS=1`.
  - **Recitation on Claude without breaking the cache:** use turn-scoped system messages.
- *Evidence:*
  - Memory + context editing +39% (technique 14).
  - Secondary: todo.md maintenance reportedly consumed ~⅓ of Manus's actions, and planning moved to a dedicated planner agent (unverified) ([tianpan.co](https://tianpan.co/blog/2026-03-02-context-engineering-lessons-from-manus)).
  - [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/effective-context-engineering-for-ai-agents); [Memory tool](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/memory-tool); [Track todos](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/todo-tracking)
- *Use / avoid:*
  - Use for long loops.
  - On frontier models that track work internally, make plan tools optional and model-gated. Their main value is UX and persistence across compaction.
  - Use delta-style updates (technique 28) rather than full rewrites.

**23. Fresh-context restarts from progress files (multi-window harness)**
- *What:* Instead of (or in addition to) compacting, end the session and start a new context that re-hydrates from structured files.
- *Mechanics:*
  - An initializer agent writes `init.sh`, `claude-progress.txt`, a JSON feature list (200+ features, all initially failing, each with `category`, `description`, `steps[]`, `passes: false`; agents may only flip `passes`) and an initial git commit.
  - JSON was chosen because models are less likely to overwrite it than Markdown.
  - Each later session: `pwd` → read progress and git log → pick the highest-priority failing feature → `init.sh` → basic end-to-end test → implement one feature → verify (Puppeteer MCP) → commit + progress update.
  - Codex offers the model a `new_context` tool, and Anthropic's research lead spawns fresh subagents with clean contexts as limits approach, after summarizing completed phases into external memory.
- *Evidence:* Opus 4.5 looping across windows with compaction alone still fell short of a production web app. The pattern counters "one-shotting" and premature victory (qualitative; no ablation published) ([Effective harnesses](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/effective-harnesses-for-long-running-agents); [quickstart](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-quickstarts/blob/main/autonomous-coding/README.md)).
- *Use / avoid:* Use for multi-hour or multi-session builds. For models with "context anxiety" (e.g. Sonnet 4.5), resets beat compaction. In Anthropic's later harness-design post, Opus 4.5 "largely removed" that behavior, so resets were dropped in favor of compaction within a run; the progress-file pattern still carries state across sessions.

**24. Sub-agent isolation (context quarantine) and forks**
- *What:* Push large reads and exploration into a separate context window and return only a condensed result or artifact reference.
- *Mechanics:*
  - **Return size:** sub-agents return summaries "often 1,000–2,000 tokens".
  - **Claude Code fresh subagent:** gets its own system prompt, the task message, CLAUDE.md (except Explore/Plan or `omitClaudeMd`), git status, preloaded skills and a sibling roster. It does not inherit history, files read or invoked skills, and has its own cache.
  - **Forks:** inherit the full conversation and tool pool and read the parent's cache.
  - **Delegation:** "include any file paths, error messages, or decisions the subagent needs directly in that prompt".
  - **Results:** schema-validated JSON (workflows retry up to 5 times) or an artifact path. Subagent reports are scanned, labeled, and carry no user authority.
  - **Limits:** depth 3 (`CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH`), 20 concurrent (`CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS`).
- *Evidence:*
  - Multi-agent (Opus 4 lead + Sonnet 4 subagents) beat single-agent Opus 4 by 90.2%.
  - Token usage explains 80% of BrowseComp variance (95% with tool-call count and model).
  - Agents use ~4× chat tokens; multi-agent ~15×.
  - The lead saves its plan to memory because contexts over 200,000 tokens get truncated.
  - [Anthropic multi-agent](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/multi-agent-research-system); [Claude Code: Subagents](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents); [Agent SDK subagents](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/subagents)
- *Use / avoid:*
  - Use when exploration is large relative to the result: breadth-first research, log processing, docs fetch, test runs, large reads.
  - Avoid for small edits, tightly coupled sequential work, and "most coding tasks" where all agents need the same context.
  - Cap return length (e.g. ≤2k tokens) and "mind the result volume".

**25. Budget-awareness signals**
- *What:* Tell the model how much context or task budget remains, so it can pace work and wrap up cleanly.
- *Mechanics:*
  - **Claude context awareness (automatic):**
    - Sonnet 5, Sonnet 4.6, Sonnet 4.5 and Haiku 4.5 get `<budget:token_budget>200000</budget:token_budget>` (or 1M) in the system prompt, and after each tool call `<system_warning>Token usage: 35000/200000; 165000 remaining</system_warning>`. Image tokens are included.
    - Opus 4.7+, Sonnet 5.5, Fable and Haiku 5.5 do not get these tags.
  - **Claude task budgets** (beta `task-budgets-2026-03-13`):
    - `output_config.task_budget = {type:"tokens", total, remaining?}` covers thinking, tool calls, tool results and output across one agentic turn (until a user message without tool results).
    - The model sees a server-injected countdown; the API returns no remaining field. Minimum `total` is 20,000.
    - Too-small budgets can cause refusal-like early stopping. Server compaction doesn't reset the budget, and it is advisory, unlike `max_tokens`.
    - Agent SDK `ClaudeAgentOptions.task_budget`.
  - **Codex:** a `get_context_remaining` tool; goal continuation injects "Tokens used / Token budget / Tokens remaining"; `token_budget.reminder_threshold_tokens`.
  - **Harness-injected note** (inference): a short appended "tokens used / remaining / next compaction at N", turn-scoped on Claude.
  - **LangChain:** time-budget warnings (agents are "famously bad at time estimation"), secondary.
- *Evidence:* [Context windows](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/context-windows); [Task budgets](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/task-budgets); [Codex handlers](https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/main/codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers). No public data was found on how much these signals improve task completion.
- *Use / avoid:* Use native signals where they exist, plus a harness note on every provider. Avoid small task budgets (<20k is rejected; small ones cause early stopping).

**26. Keep errors in, vary structure (anti-few-shot)**
- *What:* Leave failed actions and error traces in context so the model updates its beliefs, and introduce structured variation so uniform history doesn't make the agent imitative.
- *Mechanics:*
  - Retain error messages and the corrective decision; clear verbose traces after resolution (inference).
  - Vary serialization templates, phrasing and order in a controlled way.
  - Codex quick memory pass: "redo the pass on repeated errors".
- *Evidence:* Manus: "error recovery is one of the clearest indicators of true agentic behavior"; "Don't get few-shotted" (secondary, [gist](https://gist.github.com/cedrickchee/b9646b3007b4a15f528351abd331984f)). OpenHands `StuckDetector` flags repetitive patterns (e.g. 4 repeats × 2 events per cycle) ([stuck_detector.py](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/main/openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/conversation/stuck_detector.py)).
- *Use / avoid:* Use always. The tension with poisoning (technique 33) is resolved by keeping the verified error message, not unverified conclusions drawn from it. Any variation must be decided once and kept deterministic, or it breaks the cache.

**27. Durable event log separate from the context window**
- *What:* Persist the full, append-only session log outside the window and treat the LLM-visible context as a projection of it.
- *Mechanics:*
  - **Managed Agents:** `emitEvent`/`getEvents()` positional slices. The harness transforms events before they enter context, for example for cache hit rate.
  - **OpenHands:** `Condensation` tombstone events plus a `View`.
  - **Cline:** a canonical full-fidelity history plus a hash-validated compaction projection.
  - **Codex:** rollouts are append-only jsonl (`session_meta`, `turn_context`, `event_msg`, `response_item`).
  - **Claude Code:** `.jsonl` transcripts; the `PreCompact` hook can archive the transcript.
- *Evidence:* [Managed Agents](https://anthropic.com/engineering/managed-agents); [OpenHands condenser](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/main/openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/context/condenser/README.md); [Cline ARCHITECTURE.md](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/main/sdk/ARCHITECTURE.md).
- *Use / avoid:* Always. This is what makes compaction non-destructive and enables rewind, fork, crash-resume and post-hoc audits.

_Group H: Learned and optimized context management (research, 2025–2026)_

**28. ACE — Agentic Context Engineering** (arXiv 2510.04618; ICLR 2026 per listings; repo Nov 2025)
- *What:* Context is an evolving "playbook" curated by three roles: Generator (runs tasks), Reflector (extracts lessons from successes and failures) and Curator (merges lessons).
- *Mechanics:*
  - Incremental delta updates of itemized bullets, each with an ID and helpful/harmful counters, plus deterministic merge, de-duplication and pruning.
  - This avoids "brevity bias" and "context collapse" (iterative rewriting eroding detail). It builds on Dynamic Cheatsheet.
- *Evidence:*
  - +10.6% on AppWorld (matching the top GPT-4.1-based production agent, IBM CUGA, on average with a smaller open model, DeepSeek-V3.1 per coverage, and beating it on the harder split) and +8.6% on finance (FiNER + XBRL Formula).
  - −86.9% adaptation latency on average. Offline AppWorld: −82.3% latency and −75.1% rollouts vs GEPA. Online FiNER: −91.5% latency and −83.6% token cost vs Dynamic Cheatsheet.
  - [ace-agent/ace](https://github.com/ace-agent/ace); [arXiv 2510.04618](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.04618); [ICLR listing](https://iclr.cc/virtual/2026/10018667)
  - Follow-up: Meta Context Engineering via Agentic Skill Evolution ([arXiv 2601.21557](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2601.21557)).
- *Use / avoid:* Use the delta-update discipline for any persistent playbook, notes or memory file that is updated across many compactions. Avoid "rewrite the whole file" consolidation.

**29. ACON — optimized compression guidelines** (Microsoft/KAIST; arXiv 2510.00615; ICML 2026)
- *What:* Learns natural-language compression guidelines for history and observations.
- *Mechanics:* contrasts paired trajectories where full context succeeds and compressed context fails, refines the guideline, and distills it into smaller compressors.
- *Evidence:* peak tokens −26–54% on AppWorld, OfficeBench and multi-objective QA while largely preserving accuracy. Distilled compressors keep >95% of accuracy, and smaller LMs as agents improve by up to 46% ([arXiv (via search)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.00615); [microsoft/acon](https://github.com/microsoft/acon); [ICML 2026](https://icml.cc/virtual/2026/poster/66270)).
- *Use / avoid:* A method for tuning your compaction `instructions` offline against your own failure pairs. It needs an eval set with paired runs.

**30. AgentFold — proactive context folding** (arXiv 2510.24699; ICLR 2026)
- *What:* The agent proactively "folds" its history as it goes, instead of ReAct context saturation or "fixed full-history summarization" that risks irreversible detail loss.
- *Evidence:* the 30B-A3B model scores 36.2% on BrowseComp vs DeepSeek-V3.1-671B's 30.0%, and 62.1% on WideSearch. Context grows from about 3.5k to 7k tokens over 100 turns ([arXiv (via search)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.24699)).
- *Use / avoid:* Mostly a model-training approach. For a harness, the takeaway is to fold incrementally at sub-task boundaries rather than with one big summary at the threshold.

**31. Context-Folding / FoldGRPO** (arXiv 2510.11967; ICML 2026)
- *What:* `branch`/`return` actions open sub-trajectories and fold them on return, trained with RL and token-level process rewards.
- *Evidence:* matches baselines with up to 10× smaller active context (32K active budget, ≤10 branches). Seed-OSS-36B scores 62.0% on BrowseComp-Plus and 58.0% on SWE-Bench Verified ([arXiv (via search)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.11967); [PMLR](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v306/sun26x.html)).
- *Use / avoid:* The harness analogue is in-context sub-task scoping: a "branch" opens a scratch region that is replaced by its result on return, like a sub-agent but in one window. It requires models trained for it to be reliable.

**32. Recursive Language Models (RLMs)** (Zhang, Kraska, Khattab; arXiv 2512.24601)
- *What:* The prompt is held as a variable in a Python REPL. The model inspects and chunks it with code and recursively calls sub-models, so the full input never enters one window.
- *Evidence (secondary summaries):* reported to handle 10M+ tokens. On BrowseComp-Plus (1,000 docs, 6–11M tokens), RLM(GPT-5) scores 91.3 vs 70.5 for a compaction agent and 51.0 for CodeAct+BM25 ([arXiv (via search)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.24601)).
- *Use / avoid:* Use for corpus-scale inputs far beyond any window, where it pairs naturally with PTC/code-mode. Overkill for normal coding sessions.

_Group I: Failure-mode taxonomy and mitigation mapping_

**33. Failure-mode-driven guard design**
- *What:* Map each known long-context failure mode to concrete harness guards.
- *Mechanics:*

| Failure mode | Definition (source) | Harness guard (vendor feature where one exists) |
|---|---|---|
| Context poisoning | A hallucination or error gets into context and is repeatedly referenced (Breunig) | Verify (tests, schema checks) before facts enter durable notes; versioned, correctable notes; cite tool outputs over model restatements. Codex `memory_mode="polluted"` when external context is used; Managed Agents `read_only` stores |
| Context distraction | Context grows so long the model over-focuses on it and neglects what it learned in training; beware the "distraction ceiling" (Breunig) | Quality-oriented compaction thresholds, tool-result clearing, sub-agent quarantine for large reads |
| Context confusion | Superfluous content, e.g. MCP tool overload, is used to produce a low-quality response (Breunig) | Tool search with few hot tools, path-scoped instructions, skills instead of monolithic prompts |
| Context clash | New information and tools conflict with other information in context (Breunig) | Instruction-file linting (`/doctor prompt-audit`), a single source of truth for task state (JSON feature list or todo), explicit supersession notes when plans change |
| Lost in the middle / goal drift | Mid-context info under-attended over long loops (Liu et al.; Manus) | `todo.md` recitation, turn-scoped reminders, critical instructions at top or bottom |
| Few-shot rut | Repetitive action-observation patterns induce drift (Manus) | Structured variation; stuck or loop detectors (OpenHands `StuckDetector`; LangChain per-file edit counts) |
| Brevity bias / context collapse | Iterative rewriting erodes detail (ACE) | Delta updates with counters, no whole-file rewrites |
| Context anxiety | Model wraps up early near its perceived limit, seen in Sonnet 4.5 (Anthropic) | Context resets with a structured handoff; on Opus 4.5+, compaction |

  - Breunig's fixes: RAG; Tool Loadout; Context Quarantine (dedicated threads); Context Pruning; Context Summarization; Context Offloading (a "think"/scratchpad tool). He cites Anthropic's finding of up to 54% improvement from the think tool with a domain prompt on a specialized-agent benchmark (τ-bench airline pass^1 0.370 → 0.570).
  - LangChain's operations: **Write** (scratchpads, memories) → memory tool and notes. **Select** (retrieval, few-shot, tools) → tool search and JIT retrieval. **Compress** (summarization, trimming) → compaction and clearing. **Isolate** (sub-agents, state fields, sandboxes) → sub-agents and PTC.
  - The prompt-injection design pattern "Context-Minimization" (drop unneeded content, including the user prompt, after use) doubles as a context-hygiene rule ([arXiv 2506.08837](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2506.08837), via search summaries).
- *Evidence:* [Breunig (via gist)](https://www.dbreunig.com/2025/06/22/how-contexts-fail-and-how-to-fix-them.html); [LangChain (via search)](https://www.langchain.com/blog/context-engineering-for-agents); [Anthropic think tool (search snippet)](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/claude-think-tool). A NeurIPS 2026 listing "Uniform Decay, Heterogeneous Causes: Long-Horizon Failure in Long-Context Agents" exists (title only, not reviewed) ([NeurIPS](https://neurips.cc/virtual/2026/173812)). Breunig's quantitative citations (Gemini 2.5 Pokémon ">100k tokens", Databricks long-context RAG degradation points, Berkeley Function-Calling Leaderboard tool counts) are unverified.
- *Use / avoid:* Use the table as a review checklist for every new context feature. No standardized benchmark measures each failure mode or mitigation separately.
