## 5. Tools and protocols

> **SOTA in one paragraph:** Tools are now designed as an agent-facing UX rather than API wrappers: a few consolidated, namespaced, task-shaped tools with strict schemas, token-bounded semantic outputs (pagination, truncation, a `response_format` verbosity switch, a ~25k-token cap), and validation errors returned as tool results so the model can self-correct. Every leading harness converged on the same small kernel (a shell, read/search, one structured edit primitive, an optional plan/todo tool, web access, subagent spawn and MCP passthrough), because "bash + filesystem" gives an unbounded action space, cheap context primitives and a single sandbox choke-point. Pi ships only four tools and mini-swe-agent only bash (>74% SWE-bench Verified). Edit formats are still the main divergence: OpenAI models are trained on the context-anchored `apply_patch` (V4A) envelope exposed as a grammar-constrained freeform tool, while Claude-style harnesses use `str_replace`/`old_string→new_string`, so a harness should present each model the tool shapes it was post-trained on. Tool definitions are treated as a context cost: deferred loading plus tool search (−85% definition tokens), programmatic/code-mode tool calling (−37% tokens) and `input_examples` (72%→90% on complex parameters) are the advanced-tool-use stack. On the protocol side, MCP 2026-07-28 (stateless core, `server/discover`, `input_required` round-trips, cacheable deterministic lists, tasks as an extension) under the Linux Foundation's AAIF is the tool bus, with A2A v1.0 for agent↔agent, ACP for editor↔agent, and Agent Skills (`SKILL.md`), AGENTS.md and Claude/Codex hook names as the de facto packaging and extension standards.

### 5.1 Where the field is (Nov 2026) — consensus and recent shifts, with dates

Source-access caveat that applies to this whole section: modelcontextprotocol.io, developers.openai.com, api-docs.deepseek.com, arxiv.org and simonwillison.net could not be fetched by the research sessions. The MCP spec was read from the GitHub spec repo (`modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol` @ `a40e90c`, 2026-11-02) and Codex from source (`openai/codex` @ `fbf5f0d`, 2026-11-03). OpenAI and DeepSeek documentation claims come from search-engine summaries and are marked as such.

**Consensus positions**

- **Tools are an agent-computer interface (ACI), not an API surface.** This line runs from Anthropic's "Building effective agents" ACI appendix (Dec 19, 2024) to "Writing effective tools for AI agents — with agents" (Sep 11, 2025). The settled advice: consolidate and namespace tools, return high-signal bounded output, make errors actionable, poka-yoke arguments (absolute paths), use strict schemas, and iterate descriptions against evals, because small description edits produce large measured gains — [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/writing-tools-for-agents); [Anthropic ACI appendix](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/building-effective-agents).
- **A small, universal kernel.** Claude Code, Codex CLI and Gemini CLI each ship a shell, file read/search (grep/glob), a structured edit primitive, a plan/todo tool, web search/fetch, subagents and MCP passthrough. OpenCode, OpenHands and Crush ship most of that set. Pi deliberately ships only `read`/`bash`/`edit`/`write` and leaves subagents and plan mode to extensions. Anthropic's framing is "give your agents a computer, allowing them to work like humans do" (Claude Agent SDK post, Sep 29, 2025) — [Claude blog](https://claude.com/blog/building-agents-with-the-claude-agent-sdk). The minimal end is Pi (`read`, `bash`, `edit`, `write`) and mini-swe-agent (bash only, no tool-calling interface, ">74%" on SWE-bench Verified) — [pi tools/index.ts](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/blob/main/packages/coding-agent/src/core/tools/index.ts); [mini-swe-agent README](https://github.com/SWE-agent/mini-swe-agent/blob/main/README.md).
- **Why bash + filesystem became universal** (inference in the notes, consistent across sources): (a) an unbounded action space via composition; (b) the context-economy primitives grep/head/tail/jq ("agentic search" before semantic search); (c) state persists across turns in files ("the folder and file structure of an agent becomes a form of context engineering"); (d) direct reuse of pretraining on shell transcripts; and (e) one OS sandbox covers every subprocess, so the security story becomes "sandbox the shell" rather than "secure each tool" (see §6).
- **Edit formats remain the main divergence.** The `apply_patch` envelope (Codex Lark grammar) is spreading as a cross-vendor format: OpenCode `patch`, OpenAI Agents SDK sandbox `apply_patch.py`, gpt-oss `apply_patch`, OpenHands `apply_patch` and Aider `patch_coder.py`. The `str_replace`/`old_string→new_string` family covers Gemini CLI `edit`, Crush `edit`/`multiedit`, Pi `edit`, SWE-agent `edit_anthropic` and OpenHands `file_editor`. Aider keeps SEARCH/REPLACE, udiff and whole-file; mini-swe-agent is bash-only — [codex parser.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/apply-patch/src/parser.rs); [opencode patch.txt](https://github.com/sst/opencode/blob/dev/packages/core/src/tool/patch.txt); [gemini edit.ts](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/main/packages/core/src/tools/edit.ts); [aider edit-formats.md](https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider/blob/main/aider/website/docs/more/edit-formats.md).
- **Models are trained inside their vendor's harness, so tool shapes must match.** OpenAI: "We strongly recommend using our exact apply_patch implementation as the model has been trained to excel at this diff format" — [OpenAI Codex Prompting Guide](https://developers.openai.com/cookbook/examples/gpt-5/codex_prompting_guide) (search summary). Claude-4.5-Opus scores 20.5% higher inside the Claude Code SDK than in a generalist scaffold — [AgencyBench arXiv 2601.11044](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2601.11044). Harness choice alone moves agentic scores by roughly 3–14 points (7–20+ in another compilation) with the model fixed.
- **Tool definitions are a context budget item.** Five MCP servers ≈ 55K tokens, and up to 134K has been observed. Claude's tool-selection accuracy "degrades once you exceed 30–50 available tools" — [Claude docs: Tool search tool](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/tool-search-tool). The answer is deferred loading behind a search tool: Anthropic (Nov 24, 2025), Claude Code (MCP tools deferred by default), OpenAI `tool_search` (gpt-5.4+, search summary) and Codex `tool_search`.
- **Code as the orchestration layer.** The model writes code that calls tools, so intermediate data never enters context. Examples: Anthropic "Code execution with MCP" (Nov 4, 2025; 150K→2K tokens), Anthropic Programmatic Tool Calling (Nov 24, 2025), Codex `code-mode` crates, OpenCode `codemode`, smolagents `CodeAgent`. OpenAI's bundled GPT-6 guidance lists "Programmatic Tool Calling" as an optional feature — [codex upgrading-to-gpt-6-astra.md](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/skills/src/assets/samples/openai-docs/references/upgrading-to-gpt-6-astra.md).
- **Strict schemas everywhere they exist.** OpenAI recommends always enabling `strict` (search summary). DeepSeek has had strict function calling (Beta) since V3.1 (Aug 2025). MCP made JSON Schema 2020-12 the default dialect (2025-11-25, SEP-1613) and allows any 2020-12 keywords with `$ref` and composition bounds (2026-07-28, SEP-2106). The provider subsets differ, so schemas must be compiled per provider.
- **Cache stability is a tool-design constraint.** Tool definitions sit at the front of the prompt, so any change invalidates everything after it. MCP 2026-07-28 says servers SHOULD return `tools/list` in deterministic order "to enable client-side caching and improve LLM prompt cache hit rates". The mitigations: Manus masks logits instead of removing tools; OpenAI `allowed_tools` restricts the callable set without editing `tools`; Anthropic `tool_addition`/`tool_removal` (beta `inline-tools-2026-09-15`) changes tools mid-conversation without touching the `tools` array.
- **Protocol stack settled by layer.**
  - MCP is the tool bus. It has been under the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF, Linux Foundation) since Dec 9, 2025, and the current revision is **2026-07-28**.
  - A2A v1.0 (2026) handles cross-organization agent↔agent calls.
  - ACP (Agent Client Protocol) handles editor/control-center↔agent.
  - Agent Skills (`SKILL.md`; open standard Dec 18, 2025) packages procedures, and AGENTS.md (AAIF) carries instructions.
  - Claude-Code-compatible hook names were adopted by Codex; Gemini CLI diverges.
  - "Primitives are standardizing faster than harnesses": Roo Code shut down (2026-05-15) and Kimi CLI was archived, while AGENTS.md, MCP, Skills and ACP spread.

### 5.2 By lab

#### Anthropic

**Tool-design guidance (primary)**
- **"Writing effective tools for AI agents — with agents" (Sep 11, 2025)** — [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/writing-tools-for-agents):
  - *Prototype.* Wrap tools in a local MCP server or Desktop extension (DXT) and connect them with `claude mcp add <name> <command> [args...]`. Feed Claude Code the SDK docs (e.g. `llms.txt`).
  - *Evaluate.* Generate dozens of realistic prompt/response tasks grounded in real services; strong tasks may need dozens of tool calls. Pair each with a verifier (exact match or LLM judge) that doesn't over-penalize formatting. Run a simple `while`-loop agent and have it emit reasoning/feedback blocks before tool calls (or use interleaved thinking). Collect accuracy, per-call and per-task runtime, total tool calls, total tokens and tool errors.
  - *Diagnose.* Many redundant calls mean pagination or token-limit params need adjusting. Many invalid-parameter errors mean descriptions need clarification or examples. Read raw transcripts. Example: Claude kept appending "2025" to the web-search `query`, and a description fix resolved it.
  - *Improve with agents.* Paste transcripts into Claude Code to refactor the tools, then validate on held-out tests. Claude-optimized Slack and Asana MCP servers beat human-written ones on held-out tests; no exact percentages are given in the text. Use held-out sets to avoid overfitting.
  - *Design rules:* consolidate, namespace, return semantic fields, `response_format`, the 25k-token cap with coaching truncation, actionable errors, unambiguous params, strict data models, and MCP annotations to flag open-world or destructive tools. Each is detailed with its evidence in §5.3 A.
  - Claude Sonnet 3.5 reached SOTA on SWE-bench Verified after precise tool-description refinements (no delta given).
- **ACI appendix (Dec 19, 2024)** — [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/building-effective-agents): give the model enough tokens to "think" before it writes itself into a corner; keep formats close to naturally occurring internet text; avoid line counting, hunk headers and code-in-JSON; "poka-yoke your tools" (§5.3 A).
- **Multi-agent research system (Jun 13, 2025):** a tool-testing agent rewrote a flawed MCP tool description and cut task completion time by 40% for later agents — [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/multi-agent-research-system).

**Claude Code / Claude Agent SDK tool set**
- **Built-in tool names.** `Bash`, `Read`, `Edit`, `Write`, `Glob`, `Grep`, `WebFetch`, `WebSearch`, `NotebookEdit`, Task/Agent (subagents) and `TodoWrite`. These exact strings are used in permission rules (e.g. `"Bash(npm *)"`), subagent tool lists and hook matchers. The tools reference has a "Permission required" column; the full table was not retrieved — [Claude Code tools reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference).
- **Approval classes.** Read-only tools (file reads, LS, Grep, Glob) need no approval. Bash and file edit/write need approval. File-modification approval lasts until session end, while Bash approvals can be persisted — [Claude Code IAM](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/iam).
- **Concurrency.** "Read-only tools (like `Read`, `Glob`, `Grep`, and MCP tools marked as read-only) can run concurrently. Tools that modify state (like `Edit`, `Write`, and `Bash`) run sequentially." Custom tools default to sequential unless they set `readOnlyHint`. A denied tool call comes back to Claude "as the tool result" — [agent-loop docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/agent-loop).
- **Todo tools are model-gated.** `TodoWrite`, `TaskCreate`, `TaskGet`, `TaskUpdate` and `TaskList` are on by default "only on Claude Opus 4.7, Claude Sonnet 4.6, Claude Haiku 4.5, and earlier models". On newer models they are opt-in (`CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TODO_TOOLS=1` or `allowedTools`): "Newer models track multi-step work without a written todo list." Lifecycle is `pending` → `in_progress` → `completed` (plus `status: "deleted"`). Use them for tasks with "three or more distinct actions" (from v2.1.268) — [Track todos](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/todo-tracking).
- **MCP in Claude Code.** MCP tool definitions are deferred by default; only tool names and server instructions enter context until a tool is used — [Claude Code: Costs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs). Connecting or removing an MCP server, or denying an entire tool, busts the prompt cache — [Claude Code: Prompt caching](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/prompt-caching).
- **Agent SDK custom tools are in-process MCP servers** (`@tool` + `create_sdk_mcp_server()`): "No subprocess management … No IPC overhead … Single Python process". `allowed_tools` pre-approves tools and "does not control tool availability". `ClaudeAgentOptions` includes `tools`, `allowed_tools`, `disallowed_tools`, `mcp_servers`, `can_use_tool`, `hooks`, `agents`, `skills`, `plugins`, `sandbox` and `output_format`. The control protocol routes `can_use_tool`, `hook_callback` and `mcp_message` requests into the host — [claude-agent-sdk-python README](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python/blob/main/README.md); [types.py](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python/blob/main/src/claude_agent_sdk/types.py); [_internal/query.py](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python/blob/main/src/claude_agent_sdk/_internal/query.py).
- **Subagent/workflow tools.** `AgentDefinition(description, prompt, tools, disallowedTools, model, skills, memory, mcpServers, …)` requires `Agent` in `allowed_tools`. The `Workflow` tool exists from TS SDK v0.3.149+ — [Agent SDK subagents](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/subagents).
- **Managed Agents.** Tools are dispatched through `execute(name, input) → string`. A dead sandbox is returned to Claude as a tool-call error "which can choose to retry". Bash is configurable as `always_ask` with resumable approval gates — [Anthropic: Managed Agents](https://anthropic.com/engineering/managed-agents); [managed-agents README](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-quickstarts/blob/main/managed-agents/README.md).

**Claude API tools (versioned type strings)**
- **Client tools.**
  - `text_editor_20250728` fixed earlier issues and added `max_characters` for truncating large file views. On May 1, 2025, bash and text-editor were decoupled from the computer-use system prompt — [release notes](https://docs.claude.com/en/release-notes/api).
  - `memory_20250818` is configured as `{"type": "memory_20250818", "name": "memory"}`. It has no input schema and needs no beta header per the primary docs; a third-party source claimed `context-management-2025-06-27`, which is unverified. Commands:
    - `view` (`path`, `view_range`, with `-1` = EOF). A directory listing goes 2 levels deep and excludes dotfiles and `node_modules`. A file view is line-numbered with a 6-char right-aligned number plus tab, truncates past 16,000 chars, and errors on files over 999,999 lines.
    - `create` (`path`, `file_text`).
    - `str_replace` (`path`, `old_str`, optional `new_str`; errors on not-found or on multiple occurrences).
    - `insert` (`insert_line`, `insert_text`).
    - `delete` and `rename`, both of which must reject the root.

    The handler must block path traversal (`../`, `..\\`, `%2e%2e%2f`) — [Memory tool docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/memory-tool).
  - The computer-use tool's current version string was not retrieved.
- **Server tools.**
  - `code_execution_20250825` runs bash + file ops in an Anthropic-hosted sandbox and is the substrate for PTC. Current docs require `code_execution_20260120`+ for PTC (see below).
  - Web fetch (beta) retrieves full web pages and PDFs; web search also exists.
  - Tool search comes as `tool_search_tool_regex_20251119` / `tool_search_tool_bm25_20251119`, plus `mcp_toolset` — [advanced tool use](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/advanced-tool-use); [Tool search tool](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/tool-search-tool).
- **Advanced tool use (Nov 24, 2025; beta header `advanced-tool-use-2025-11-20`; the Claude docs now describe tool search as stable).**
  - Tool Search (`defer_loading`): −85% definition tokens; Opus 4.5 MCP-eval 79.5%→88.1%.
  - Programmatic Tool Calling (`allowed_callers`): −37% tokens; GAIA 46.5%→51.2%.
  - `input_examples`: 72%→90% on complex parameters.

  Details in §5.3.
- **Cache-preserving tool changes.** Deferred tools stay out of the prefix (discovery appends `tool_reference` inline, no `cache_control` on deferred tools). `tool_addition`/`tool_removal` blocks (beta `inline-tools-2026-09-15`) add, change or withdraw tools, including defining one by value, without touching `tools` — [Tool use with prompt caching](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/tool-use-with-prompt-caching); [Mid-conversation system messages](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-system-messages). Mechanics in §5.3 B.
- **Tool-result lifecycle (context editing, beta `context-management-2025-06-27`).** `clear_tool_uses_20250919` replaces the oldest tool results with placeholders past `trigger` (default 100,000 input tokens), with `keep` (default last 3 pairs), `clear_at_least`, `exclude_tools` (never cleared) and `clear_tool_inputs` (default false). This matters for tool design because results you want to survive must be excluded or written to files — [Context editing](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/context-editing).
- **Rollout order recommended by Claude docs.** Cache tool definitions from day one, add tool search past about 20 tools, then context editing for long runs, then PTC for chains — [Manage tool context](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/manage-tool-context).

**Protocols, packaging and extension (Anthropic-originated)**
- Anthropic donated MCP to AAIF on Dec 9, 2025. Anthropic announced adoption of MCP 2026-07-28 in Claude; only the title was seen — [Claude blog](https://claude.com/blog/bringing-mcp-2026-07-28-to-claude).
- **Agent Skills.**
  - `anthropics/skills` (~186.8k stars) says "The spec is now located at https://agentskills.io/specification".
  - Many skills are Apache-2.0; the document skills are source-available.
  - The repo installs as a plugin marketplace (`/plugin marketplace add anthropics/skills`) — [anthropics/skills](https://github.com/anthropics/skills/blob/main/README.md).
  - Claude Code shows skill descriptions at session start and loads full content on use. `disable-model-invocation: true` keeps a description out of context — [How Claude Code works](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/how-claude-code-works).
- **Plugins and mods.**
  - Plugins bundle "custom slash commands, specialized agents, hooks, and MCP servers", are installed via `/plugin` marketplaces, and the official ones live in `anthropics/claude-plugins-official`.
  - "Mods" are plugins whose behaviour is a hooks module (`register(on, options)`, `($, e, next)` middleware). Four built-in mods ship as source: `sec-default`, `diff`, `telemetry` and `agents-md`. The `agents-md` mod loads AGENTS.md where no CLAUDE.md exists (default `claude-md-or-agents-md`), beside it (`claude-md-and-agents-md`), `managed-only` or `claude-md` only — [plugins/README.md](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/main/plugins/README.md); [mods/README.md](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/main/mods/README.md).
- **Hooks.**
  - Events: `SessionStart`, `Setup`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `UserPromptExpansion`, `PreToolUse`, `PermissionRequest`, `PermissionDenied`, `PostToolUse`, `PostToolUseFailure`, `PostToolBatch`, `Notification`, `SubagentStart`/`SubagentStop`, `TaskCreated`/`TaskCompleted`, `Stop`, `StopFailure`, `TeammateIdle`, `InstructionsLoaded`, `ConfigChange`, `CwdChanged`, `FileChanged`, `WorktreeCreate`/`WorktreeRemove`, `PreCompact`/`PostCompact`, `PreModelSwitch`/`PostModelSwitch`, `Elicitation`/`ElicitationResult` and `SessionEnd`.
  - Hook types: `command`, `http`, `mcp_tool`, `prompt` and `agent` (experimental, up to 50 tool-use turns). Timeouts are 600 s for command/http/mcp_tool, 30 s for prompt and 60 s for agent.
  - `PreToolUse` returns `hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision` ∈ {`allow`,`deny`,`ask`,`defer`} plus `updatedInput`. Exit code `2` blocks, with stderr as the reason — [Hooks reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks).

#### OpenAI

**Function-calling practice (search summaries; developers.openai.com not directly fetchable)**
- **`strict` mode.** "Always enable" it, so calls adhere to the schema rather than best-effort. Requirements: `additionalProperties: false` on every object, and every property listed in `required`; optional fields are expressed as nullable unions — [OpenAI function calling guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/function-calling) (search summary).
- **Parallel calls.** `parallel_tool_calls: false` guarantees zero or one tool call per turn. Older docs said strict was incompatible with parallel calls. Current reports say this applies only to fine-tuned models, where strict is disabled when multiple functions are called in one turn — [community thread](https://community.openai.com/t/parallel-tool-use-documentation-for-api-models/1304519). Unverified on the primary page.
- **Tool subsetting and search.** `allowed_tools` restricts the callable subset per turn without changing `tools`, which keeps the cache prefix stable (third-party description). `tool_search` defers rarely used tools and is supported only on gpt-5.4+ models per the guide. No public numbers were found.
- No primary-source OpenAI numeric tool-count limit (e.g. "fewer than 20 tools") could be verified.

**Responses API built-in tools (search summaries)**
- The `shell` tool supports local (client-run) and hosted execution in OpenAI-managed containers. Hosted shell has no interactive TTY and no sudo, and containers can be created and reused across Responses calls. `apply_patch` is a built-in tool alongside `shell` — [OpenAI shell guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-shell); [Microsoft Foundry shell docs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/openai/how-to/shells); [ruby_llm-responses_api](https://github.com/9elements/ruby_llm-responses_api). It is unverified whether hosted `apply_patch` executes server-side.
- `apply_patch` is offered "as a first-class Responses API tool or as a freeform tool with a context-free grammar". Codex models since GPT-5 use `apply_patch` for diff-based edits and file creation, plus a shell tool for search and navigation — [Codex Prompting Guide](https://developers.openai.com/cookbook/examples/gpt-5/codex_prompting_guide); [Kundel talk summary](https://daily.dev/posts/codex-behind-the-harness-dominik-kundel-openai-aheps4agd).
- Bundled GPT-6 guidance (near-primary snapshot in the Codex repo): "Tool calling with reasoning requires the Responses API". Optional features include "persisted reasoning", "Programmatic Tool Calling", "compaction" and "pro mode" — [upgrading-to-gpt-6-astra.md](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/skills/src/assets/samples/openai-docs/references/upgrading-to-gpt-6-astra.md).

**Codex CLI tool set (source @ `fbf5f0d`)**
- **Tools registered for the model:**
  - shell: `exec_command` + `write_stdin` ("unified exec": PTY sessions keyed by `session_id`) and legacy `shell`/`shell_command`
  - editing, planning and interaction: `apply_patch`, `update_plan`, `view_image`, `web_search`, `tool_search`, `request_user_input`, `request_permissions`
  - MCP resources: `list_mcp_resources`, `list_mcp_resource_templates`, `read_mcp_resource`
  - multi-agent: `spawn_agent`, `send_input`, `send_message`, `wait_agent`, `close_agent`, `resume_agent`, `interrupt_agent`, `list_agents`, `followup_task` (`multi_agents`/`multi_agents_v2` handlers)
  - context and plugins: `get_context_remaining`, `new_context` / `new_context_window` (both names appear in different source listings), `sleep`, `send_message_to_user_async`, `request_plugin_install`
  - a code-mode `exec`

  [codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers](https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/main/codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers); [codex-rs/tools](https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/main/codex-rs/tools)
- **Loop-control tool descriptions:** `new_context` "Start a new context window. Does not clear, reset, or otherwise affect environment state."; `get_context_remaining` "Get the remaining tokens in the current context window."; `sleep` "Pause execution… The sleep ends early when new input arrives for the active turn."
- **Tool plumbing.** `core/src/tools/`: `registry.rs`, `router.rs`, `orchestrator.rs`, `parallel.rs`, `approvals.rs`, `sandboxing.rs`, `network_approval.rs`, `spec_plan.rs`. Requests pass `parallel_tool_calls` through and use `store: false` + `include: ["reasoning.encrypted_content"]` — [core/src/tools](https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/main/codex-rs/core/src/tools); [client.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/core/src/client.rs).
- **`apply_patch`.** An official Lark grammar (`assets/tools/apply_patch.lark`) exposed as a FREEFORM grammar-constrained tool, with a lenient parser and `seek_sequence` matcher, a `streaming_parser.rs`, a standalone `apply_patch` executable and `prompt_with_apply_patch_instructions.md`. The full marker set, grammar sketch and matching rules are in §5.3 C — [parser.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/apply-patch/src/parser.rs); [apply_patch_spec.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/apply_patch_spec.rs).
- **`update_plan`.** "A short list of 1‑sentence steps (no more than 5-7 words each) with a `status` for each step (`pending`, `in_progress`, or `completed`)", and "exactly one `in_progress` step until everything is done". The model calls it with an `explanation` when the plan changes, and should not repeat the plan after calling it ("the harness already displays it"). In Plan Mode `update_plan` returns an error. The system prompt asks for brief preambles (8–12 words) before grouped tool calls — [base_instructions/default.md](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/protocol/src/prompts/base_instructions/default.md); [plan.md](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/collaboration-mode-templates/templates/plan.md); [models-manager/prompt.md](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/models-manager/prompt.md).
- **Code mode.** Crates `code-mode`, `code-mode-runtime` and `code-mode-host`. `augment_tool_spec_for_code_mode` augments tool descriptions "with code-mode-specific exec samples". The runtime engine (JS/V8?) is unconfirmed — [code_mode.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/tools/src/code_mode.rs).
- **MCP.**
  - The client uses the official Rust SDK `rmcp` pinned `=3.5.1`.
  - `codex-mcp` "manages Codex's MCP connections, tool calls, and their captured authority". Servers can opt into an experimental `codex/sandbox-state` capability to receive the sandbox policy in `_meta`.
  - CLI `codex mcp` supports list/get/add/remove/login/logout. There is no top-level `mcp-server` subcommand on main (it existed in 2025-era versions); app-server and the SDK are the embedding paths.

  [Cargo.toml](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/Cargo.toml); [codex-mcp/README.md](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/codex-mcp/README.md); [cli/src/main.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/cli/src/main.rs)
- **Skills, AGENTS.md and hooks.**
  - Skills: the `skills` crate with bundled samples, a `skills/list` app-server RPC, `mcp_skill_dependencies` and `docs/skills.md`.
  - AGENTS.md: every `AGENTS.md` from project root to cwd is collected. `AGENTS.override.md` is the preferred local override, docs are joined with `--- project-doc ---`, and the byte budget is `project_doc_max_bytes`. Scope is the directory tree rooted at the file, deeper files win, and direct system/developer/user instructions beat AGENTS.md.
  - Hooks: `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `SessionStart`, `SessionEnd`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `Stop`, `PreCompact`, `PostCompact`, `SubagentStop`, `PermissionRequest`. These are the Claude Code names.

  [codex-rs/skills](https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/main/codex-rs/skills); [agents_md.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/core/src/agents_md.rs); [hooks/src](https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/main/codex-rs/hooks/src)

**OpenAI Agents SDK (Python `v0.24.0`, JS `v0.21.0`)**
- **Tool kinds and agents as tools.** Tools are function, MCP and hosted. Handoffs are exposed as tools named `transfer_to_{agent.name}`; `Agent.as_tool()` turns an agent into a tool.
- **Tool-call behaviour.** `tool_not_found_behavior` defaults to raising `ModelBehaviorError` and may be set to `"return_error_to_model"`. Concurrency is capped with `ToolExecutionConfig.max_function_tool_concurrency`; timeouts use `ModelSettings.timeout` / `ToolTimeoutError`. Tool-level guardrails live in `tool_guardrails.py`.
- **HITL.** An approval pauses the run with `RunResult.interruptions` (`ToolApprovalItem`). Hosted-MCP sticky decisions are keyed by `server_label` + tool name.
- **`SandboxAgent`.** Capabilities include `filesystem.py`, `shell.py`, `skills.py` (`Skills(lazy_from=…)`), `memory.py` and `compaction.py`, plus `apply_patch.py`. Hosted sandbox clients: E2B, Modal, Daytona, Cloudflare, Vercel, Blaxel.

Sources: [handoffs](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/main/src/agents/handoffs/__init__.py); [running_agents.md](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/main/docs/running_agents.md); [src/agents/sandbox](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/tree/main/src/agents/sandbox); [PR #4280](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/pull/4280/files).

**gpt-oss / harmony**
- In Harmony, tools are declared TypeScript-like as `namespace functions { type f = (_: {...}) => any; }`, and function calls go to the `commentary` channel.
- gpt-oss ships the reference tools it was trained on: `simple_browser`, `python_docker` (stateless) and `apply_patch.py`/`apply_patch.md`. The models "should only be used with this format" — [harmony README](https://github.com/openai/harmony/blob/main/README.md); [gpt-oss README](https://github.com/openai/gpt-oss/blob/main/README.md).

**Training signals**
- Agent RFT (AgentKit, Oct 2025): the policy calls *your* tool endpoints during RL rollouts. Each rollout carries a unique ID on its tool calls, tool calls were capped (example: 10), and models learned to issue more parallel calls and fewer turns — [InfoQ](https://www.infoq.com/presentations/rft-openai-model/).
- Mismatch failure: GPT-5.3-Codex tries to call a non-existent `apply_patch` in harnesses that lack it — [zenn.dev](https://zenn.dev/c_c/articles/188a9bef9f3290?locale=en). A third-party claim (unverified) says GPT-5.5 and its Codex siblings are trained on the Codex CLI loop and `apply_patch`, so third-party harnesses must emulate V4A — [danielvaughan, 2026-04-28](https://codex.danielvaughan.com/2026/04/28/codex-models-third-party-harnesses-apply-patch-v4a-portable-agent/).
- AGENTS.md was donated by OpenAI to AAIF. OpenAI's "Harness engineering" post (Feb 11, 2026) reportedly uses an AGENTS.md of about 100 lines as a table of contents into a structured `docs/` directory (secondary, unverified).

#### DeepSeek

- **Strict function calling (Beta)** — [DeepSeek Tool Calls guide](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/tool_calls/) (search snippets; the page was not fetched directly):
  - Enable it with `base_url="https://api.deepseek.com/beta"` and `strict: true` on every function. It works in thinking and non-thinking modes.
  - The server validates the schema and errors on unsupported types. All properties must be `required`, with `additionalProperties: false`.
  - Strings support `pattern` and the formats `email`/`hostname`/`ipv4`/`ipv6`/`uuid`, but not `minLength`/`maxLength`. Numbers support `minimum`/`maximum`/`multipleOf`. Arrays do not support `minItems`/`maxItems`. `$ref`/`$def` are supported.
  - Introduced with V3.1 (Aug 2025) — [V3.1 release](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/news/news250821/).
- **Thinking with tools.**
  - V3.2 (Dec 1, 2025) is "our first model to integrate thinking directly into tool-use", with tool use in thinking and non-thinking modes — [V3.2 release](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/news/news251201).
  - Thinking is enabled with `extra_body={"thinking": {"type": "enabled"}}`, and reasoning is returned in `reasoning_content`. In a tool loop, append `content`, `reasoning_content` and `tool_calls` together; per a third-party summary, omitting `reasoning_content` returns HTTP 400.
  - The official API returns `None` when there are no tool calls; vLLM returns `[]`.
  - Sources: [Thinking Mode guide](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/thinking_mode/) (snippet); [vLLM recipe](https://docs.vllm.ai/projects/recipes/en/latest/DeepSeek/DeepSeek-V3_2.html); [Tabbit](https://go.tabbit.ai/model/deepseek-v3-2/prompts/deepseek-official-thinking-tool-calls-multi-turn-state) (secondary).
  - One extract references a `deepseek-flash` model ID with the same `extra_body`, which suggests a post-V3.2 generation. Unverified.
- **Reasoning retention rule (V3.2 report, via search snippet).** Historical reasoning is discarded only when a new user message arrives; tool outputs keep it. Frameworks that simulate tool calls through user messages (Roo Code and Terminus are named) trigger the discard — [arXiv 2512.02556](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.02556).
- **Conflict.** Vercel AI Gateway says "V3.2 Thinking" doesn't support tool use; the official notes say thinking and tools are integrated — [Vercel](https://vercel.com/ai-gateway/models/deepseek-v3.2-thinking). V3.2-Speciale does not support tool calling — [SGLang cookbook](https://cookbook.sglang.io/autoregressive/DeepSeek/DeepSeek-V3_2).
- **Chat templates (search-summarized HF cards; unverified).**
  - V3.2 introduced "a revised format for tool calling and … 'thinking with tools'". Its `encoding/` scripts (`encode_messages`, `parse_message_from_completion_text`; `encode_config = dict(thinking_mode="thinking", drop_thinking=True, add_default_bos_token=True)`) handle "well-formatted strings only". A `developer` role exists only for search-agent scenarios and is not accepted by the API.
  - In V4, tool calls use a DSML `tool_calls` block with named invoke/parameter elements, where `string="false"` marks JSON-typed params. Tool results are wrapped in `tool_result` tags inside user messages. `drop_thinking` defaults to True but is auto-disabled when tools are defined. The reference encoder is `encoding_dsv4.py`.
  - Sources: [HF V3.2 mirror](https://huggingface.co/Deniss8686/DeepSeek-V3.2); [V4 encoding README](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-DSpark/raw/main/encoding/README.md).
- **Agentic training (V3.2 report, via search summary).** A synthesis agent built 1,827 task-oriented environments and 85,000+ complex prompts that are "hard to solve but easy to verify". It iteratively raised difficulty and augmented toolsets when they were insufficient. It also built tens of thousands of reproducible issue-resolution environments from GitHub issue/PR pairs. Recalled and unverified per-agent counts: search ~50K, code ~24.7K, code interpreter ~5.9K, general ~4.4K.
- **Harness compatibility instead of a harness.**
  - DeepSeek exposes Anthropic-API (`https://api.deepseek.com/anthropic`) and Responses-API compatible endpoints.
  - With Claude Code, it is used via `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` + `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. `anthropic-beta` and `anthropic-version` headers are ignored. The reported mapping is `claude-opus*` → `deepseek-v4-pro` and `claude-sonnet*`/`claude-haiku*`/unknown → `deepseek-v4-flash`.
  - A third-party summary says MCP tool-use blocks are unsupported.
  - V4 reportedly shipped "with documented support for Claude Code, OpenClaw, OpenCode, and CodeBuddy" (secondary).
  - Sources: [anthropic_api](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/anthropic_api) (snippet); [developersdigest](https://www.developersdigest.tech/reference/api-compatibility/deepseek); [handyai](https://handyai.substack.com/p/model-drop-deepseek-v4).
- **DeepSeek Harness.** An MIT agent runtime reported as v0.1 around Aug 13, 2026 (secondary). The official repo README is tiny and only points agents to `AGENTS.md` — [deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness); [Gigazine](https://gigazine.net/gsc_news/en/20260814-deepseek-harness-v0-1/).
- **Agentic scores, V3.1-Terminus → V3.2-Exp.** BrowseComp 38.5→40.1, SWE Verified 68.4→67.8, Terminal-bench 36.7→37.7, Aider-Polyglot 76.1→74.5 — [V3.2-Exp README](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp/blob/main/README.md).
- No public information in the research notes on a DeepSeek-specific edit format, tool-search or code-mode feature.

#### Open source and others

- **Google Gemini CLI** (Apache-2.0, `v0.66.0`):
  - *Tools:* `read-file`, `read-many-files`, `write-file`, `edit` (`old_string`/`new_string`), `glob`, `grep`/`ripGrep`, `ls`, `shell` + `shellBackgroundTools`, `web-fetch`, `web-search`, `memoryTool` (`GEMINI.md`), `write-todos`, `trackerTools`, `enter-plan-mode`/`exit-plan-mode`, `activate-skill`, `ask-user`, `complete-task` and MCP resource tools.
  - *Hooks:* `BeforeTool`, `AfterTool`, `BeforeAgent`, `AfterAgent`, `BeforeModel`, `AfterModel`, `BeforeToolSelection`, `PreCompress`, `SessionStart`, `SessionEnd`, `Notification`. This is a different vocabulary from Claude/Codex.
  - *Policy and agents:* a TOML policy engine (`read-only`, `write`, `plan`, `yolo`, `sandbox-default`, `non-interactive`, `agents`, `conseca`) and remote subagents over A2A (`a2a-client-manager.ts`, `a2a-server` package).
  - *Tool output:* `toolOutputMaskingService` and `toolDistillationService`.

  Sources: [core/src/tools](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/tree/main/packages/core/src/tools); [hooks/types.ts](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/main/packages/core/src/hooks/types.ts); [policies](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/tree/main/packages/core/src/policy/policies).
- **Pi** (MIT, ~119.6k stars): the default coding toolset is exactly `read`, `bash`, `edit`, `write`; the read-only set is `read`, `grep`, `find`, `ls`. It "skips features like sub-agents and plan mode" and is extended via extensions, skills, prompt templates and packages. It is also runnable as an ACP agent from OpenHands Agent Canvas — [tools/index.ts](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/blob/main/packages/coding-agent/src/core/tools/index.ts); [README](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/blob/main/packages/coding-agent/README.md).
- **OpenCode** (MIT, ~224.1k stars): the `patch` tool uses the Codex envelope verbatim. It also has `todowrite`, `persistent-pty`, `lsp` handling and `codemode`, `plugin` and `protocol` packages. Its agents are `build` (full access) and `plan` (read-only, denies edits, asks before bash) — [patch.txt](https://github.com/sst/opencode/blob/dev/packages/core/src/tool/patch.txt).
- **OpenHands Software Agent SDK** (MIT, `v1.59.0`): tools `terminal`, `file_editor`, `apply_patch`, `glob`, `grep`, `browser_use`, `task_tracker`, `delegate`, `task`, `child_conversation`, `planning_file_editor`, `ask_oracle`, `tom_consult`. Its SDK modules include `mcp`, `skills`, `plugin`, `marketplace` and `security` (shell AST parser) — [openhands-tools](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/tree/main/openhands-tools/openhands/tools).
- **Crush** (Charm, FSL-1.1, Go): tools `bash`, `edit`, `multiedit`, `glob`, `grep`, `ls`, `fetch`, `download`, `diagnostics`, `job_output`/`job_kill`, `question`, plus LSP tools (`lsp_definition`, `lsp_rename`, `lsp_replace_symbol`, `lsp_symbols`, `lsp_call_hierarchy`). Tool descriptions are `.md`/`.md.tpl` templates next to the Go code — [internal/agent/tools](https://github.com/charmbracelet/crush/tree/main/internal/agent/tools).
- **Aider** (Apache-2.0; no release since v0.86.x, ~Aug 2025): edit formats `whole`, `diff` (SEARCH/REPLACE), `diff-fenced`, `udiff`, `editor-diff`/`editor-whole` (architect/editor split) and `patch_coder.py`. It has no tool calling, a per-model edit-format table and a tree-sitter repo map (`map_tokens=1024` default) — [edit-formats doc](https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider/blob/main/aider/website/docs/more/edit-formats.md).
- **mini-swe-agent / SWE-agent.**
  - mini-swe-agent: "Does not have any tools other than bash — it doesn't even need to use the tool-calling interface". Actions run via `subprocess.run` (stateless), and it powers the SWE-bench "bash only" leaderboard.
  - SWE-agent's ACI bundles: `windowed`, `windowed_edit_linting`, `windowed_edit_replace`, `windowed_edit_rewrite`, `edit_anthropic`, `search`, `filemap`, `submit`, `review_on_submit_m`, `diff_state`, `web_browser`.

  Sources: [mini README](https://github.com/SWE-agent/mini-swe-agent/blob/main/README.md); [SWE-agent tools](https://github.com/SWE-agent/SWE-agent/tree/main/tools).
- **Goose** (Block → AAIF): "70+ extensions via MCP" and ACP providers that let it use "Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini subscriptions" (`goose-acp-macros`). **Kimi Code CLI** (MIT): `acp-server` and `kap-server` packages, `kimi acp` for Zed/JetBrains, a plugin marketplace with trust levels, and `tree-sitter-bash`. **Qwen Code**: a Gemini CLI fork, multi-protocol (OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini/Qwen APIs). **deepagents**: middleware such as `patch_tool_calls.py`, `_overflow_clip.py`, `_blob_offload.py` (tool output offload to disk) and `skills.py`, plus `libs/acp`. **smolagents**: `CodeAgent` "writes its actions in code"; "`LocalPythonExecutor` is not a security sandbox" — [goose](https://github.com/block/goose/blob/main/README.md); [kimi-code](https://github.com/MoonshotAI/kimi-code/blob/main/README.md); [deepagents middleware](https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/tree/main/libs/deepagents/deepagents/middleware); [smolagents](https://github.com/huggingface/smolagents/blob/main/README.md).
- **Manus** (primary blocked; search extracts and gist):
  - "Mask, don't remove": keep tool definitions fixed and use logit masking during decoding. Action names share prefixes (`browser_*`, `shell_*`) so whole groups can be constrained.
  - The file system is "the ultimate context", and compression should be restorable (keep a path or URL).
  - Keep failed actions and error traces in context.
  - A typical task makes ~50 tool calls, with a ~100:1 input:output ratio.

  [gist](https://gist.github.com/cedrickchee/b9646b3007b4a15f528351abd331984f).
- **Training in the harness's own tools.**
  - Cursor Composer 2 is evaluated "in the same Cursor harness that is used by the deployed model, with equivalent tools and structure" — [arXiv 2603.24477](https://arxiv.org/html/2603.24477) (snippet).
  - Windsurf SWE-1.5 was RL-trained in Cascade.
  - Kimi K2 evolved hundreds of domains with thousands of tools (real MCP + synthetic); the commonly cited ~3,000 real MCP and ~20,000 synthetic tools are unconfirmed — [Kimi K2 blog](https://www.kimi.com/blog/kimi-k2.html).
- **Frameworks.** Microsoft Agent Framework 1.0 (Apr 2026) uses MCP for tools and A2A for interop; the A2A packages are still preview. Google ADK has built-in MCP and A2A plus `AgentTool` (community sources).
- **Tool overload (secondary).** A quantized Llama 3.1 8B reportedly failed with 46 tools and succeeded with 19 — [Breunig](https://www.dbreunig.com/2025/06/26/how-to-fix-your-context.html) (not verified).

### 5.3 Techniques and patterns

Format: **Name** — *What*; *Mechanics*; *Evidence*; *Use / avoid*.

#### A. Designing the tool surface

**Consolidated, task-shaped tools (don't wrap endpoints)**
- *What:* Expose the few operations an agent actually needs as single tools, each matching a unit of user intent, instead of a 1:1 mirror of a REST API.
- *Mechanics:*
  - Replace `list_*` enumerators with search and action tools (`search_contacts`/`message_contact` instead of `list_contacts`).
  - Fold chains into one call: `schedule_event` replaces `list_users` + `list_events` + `create_event`; `get_customer_context` replaces three getters; `search_logs` (returning context lines) replaces `read_logs`.
  - Remove overlapping tools so selection is unambiguous.
- *Evidence:* Anthropic's Slack and Asana tools rebuilt this way (by Claude Code, from eval transcripts) beat the human-written versions on held-out tests (no percentages given) — [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/writing-tools-for-agents). In Anthropic's research system, a rewritten MCP tool description cut task completion time 40% — [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/multi-agent-research-system).
- *Use / avoid:* Use for every domain (non-shell) tool. Don't apply it to the shell: there, composability is the point.

**Namespacing and tool naming**
- *What:* Prefix or suffix tool names by service and resource so related tools group together and names don't collide across MCP servers.
- *Mechanics:*
  - Use `asana_search`, `jira_search`, `asana_projects_search`.
  - MCP 2025-11-25 added tool-name guidance (SEP-986).
  - Manus uses shared prefixes (`browser_*`, `shell_*`) so whole groups can be logit-masked.
  - Anthropic's code-execution-with-MCP example calls `callMCPTool('google_drive__get_document', …)`, using a `server__tool` double-underscore namespace.
- *Evidence:* "Prefix vs suffix naming has non-trivial effects" on Anthropic's evals, so choose empirically per model — [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/writing-tools-for-agents); [MCP 2025-11-25 changelog](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/blob/main/docs/specification/2025-11-25/changelog.mdx).
- *Use / avoid:* Always namespace MCP-sourced tools per server; it is also a tool-poisoning hygiene step (§7). Keep the vendor-native names (`Bash`, `Read`, `apply_patch`) un-namespaced for core tools, because models are trained on them.

**Semantic, high-signal returns**
- *What:* Return fields a model can reason with, not internal identifiers.
- *Mechanics:*
  - Return `name`, `image_url`, `file_type` rather than `uuid`, `256px_image_url`, `mime_type`.
  - Resolve UUIDs to natural-language names or 0-indexed IDs.
  - Keep the IDs needed for follow-up calls in the detailed mode.
  - MCP 2025-06-18 added structured output (`structuredContent` + `outputSchema`) and resource links in tool results.
- *Evidence:* Resolving UUIDs "reduced hallucination and improved retrieval precision". Response structure (XML/JSON/Markdown) also affects performance — [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/writing-tools-for-agents).
- *Use / avoid:* Use always. Keep opaque handles only where the protocol needs them, e.g. MCP 2026-07-28 server-minted handles, which the model threads between calls.

**`response_format` verbosity switch**
- *What:* An enum parameter that lets the model choose a concise or a detailed payload.
- *Mechanics:* `response_format: "concise" | "detailed"` (Anthropic's example enum `DETAILED = "detailed"`, `CONCISE = "concise"`). Concise drops IDs and metadata; detailed carries the IDs needed for follow-up calls.
- *Evidence:* In the Slack example, detailed was 206 tokens vs 72 for concise (~1/3) — [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/writing-tools-for-agents).
- *Use / avoid:* Use on any tool that can return large payloads (search, list, fetch, log, DB). It is unnecessary for tools with tiny fixed outputs.

**Token-bounded outputs: pagination, truncation, caps and offload**
- *What:* Every tool result has a bounded size, with defaults and a coaching message when truncated.
- *Mechanics:*
  - Paginate, select ranges, filter and truncate with sensible defaults.
  - Use a global per-result cap (Claude Code: 25,000 tokens by default).
  - Truncation messages should "steer toward many small, targeted searches".
  - Anthropic's `text_editor_20250728` has `max_characters`. The memory tool truncates `view` past 16,000 chars. Claude Code compaction re-reads files over 5,000 tokens only as a path-only "Referenced file".
  - Offload big results to files and return a path plus a preview (Manus restorable compression; deepagents `_blob_offload.py`/`_overflow_clip.py`; Gemini CLI `toolOutputMaskingService`/`toolDistillationService`).
- *Evidence:* "Claude Code restricts tool responses to 25,000 tokens by default." In Anthropic's 100-turn web-search eval, context editing (clearing old tool results) cut token use 84% — [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/writing-tools-for-agents); [Claude blog](https://claude.com/blog/context-management).
- *Use / avoid:* Use always, and log a `truncated` flag and result size per call (see the observability section's `execute_tool` span). Don't silently truncate; tell the model how to narrow the query.

**Actionable errors returned as tool results**
- *What:* Validation and execution failures come back to the model as an ordinary tool result with a fix hint, not as a protocol or transport error.
- *Mechanics:*
  - Make errors specific and include a correct-input example, not opaque codes or tracebacks.
  - MCP 2025-11-25 SEP-1303: input-validation errors MUST be Tool Execution Errors (`isError` results), "to enable model self-correction".
  - OpenAI Agents SDK `tool_not_found_behavior: "return_error_to_model"`.
  - The Claude Agent SDK returns denied calls "as the tool result". Claude Code auto-mode denials tell the agent to find a safer path and not route around the block.
  - `srt` sandbox violations are surfaced to the model in a `<sandbox_violations>` block.
  - Managed Agents returns a dead sandbox as a tool error the model can retry.
- *Evidence:* The design rationale is stated in SEP-1303 and the Anthropic guide. Manus: "error recovery is one of the clearest indicators of true agentic behavior", and keeping failed actions in context lets the model update its beliefs (gist, secondary).
- *Use / avoid:* Use always. Count repeated failures and denials and escalate after N (auto mode: 3 consecutive or 20 total) to prevent grinding.

**Poka-yoke arguments**
- *What:* Change argument shapes so mistakes are hard to make.
- *Mechanics:*
  - Require absolute paths in file tools.
  - Use unambiguous names (`user_id`, not `user`) and enums instead of free strings.
  - Avoid formats that need counting (line numbers in diff headers) or escaping (code inside JSON). That is why `apply_patch` is a freeform grammar tool and why `str_replace` matches text rather than line numbers.
- *Evidence:* Anthropic's SWE-bench agent erred with relative paths after `cd`. Requiring absolute paths fixed it, and the team "spent more time optimizing our tools than the overall prompt" — [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/building-effective-agents).
- *Use / avoid:* Use always for file and path arguments. Exception (inference): for models trained on a different convention, check the native tool's own conventions first.

**Strict schemas with per-provider compilation**
- *What:* Constrained decoding against the JSON Schema, so arguments always parse and validate.
- *Mechanics:*
  - **OpenAI:** `strict: true`; `additionalProperties: false` on every object; every property in `required`; optional fields as nullable unions.
  - **DeepSeek (Beta):** `base_url="https://api.deepseek.com/beta"` with `strict: true` on every function and the same `required`/`additionalProperties` rules, but no `minLength`/`maxLength` or `minItems`/`maxItems`. The full keyword list is in §5.2 DeepSeek.
  - **MCP:** JSON Schema 2020-12 is the default (SEP-1613). `inputSchema`/`outputSchema` may use any 2020-12 keywords with `$ref` resolution and composition bounds (SEP-2106). `EnumSchema` covers single/multi-select (SEP-1330).
  - **Anthropic:** "Enforce inputs and outputs with strict data models." No strict-mode parameter name for Claude appears in the notes.
- *Evidence:* Recommended by OpenAI ("always enable", search summary) and Anthropic. No numeric delta in the notes.
- *Use / avoid:* Use on every provider that supports it. Because the subsets differ, write one canonical schema and compile and lint it per provider (drop unsupported keywords, make optional fields nullable-required). On fine-tuned OpenAI models with parallel calls, strict may be disabled (reported).

```jsonc
// Canonical strict-compatible parameters schema (OpenAI/DeepSeek rules from the notes).
// The wrapper ("type":"function", "name", "strict": true, ...) varies by provider API.
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "path":    { "type": "string", "description": "Absolute path to the file" },
    "query":   { "type": "string", "description": "Regex to search for" },
    "max_results": { "type": ["integer", "null"], "description": "Optional; null = default 50" },
    "response_format": { "type": "string", "enum": ["concise", "detailed"] }
  },
  "required": ["path", "query", "max_results", "response_format"],   // every property required
  "additionalProperties": false                                       // on every object
}
// DeepSeek strict: also avoid minLength/maxLength and minItems/maxItems (unsupported).
```

**Tool-description engineering with an eval loop ("tools written with agents")**
- *What:* Treat descriptions as code under test, and let an agent refactor tools from eval transcripts.
- *Mechanics:*
  1. Prototype as a local MCP server (`claude mcp add …`).
  2. Have Claude Code generate dozens of realistic multi-call tasks with verifiers.
  3. Run a `while`-loop agent that emits reasoning before tool calls.
  4. Collect accuracy, runtime, call counts, tokens and errors.
  5. Paste transcripts into Claude Code to refactor the tools.
  6. Validate on a held-out set.

  Write descriptions "as if onboarding a new hire".
- *Evidence:* Claude-optimized Slack/Asana MCP servers beat human-written ones (held-out). The "2025"-appended query bug was fixed by a description change. Sonnet 3.5's SWE-bench Verified SOTA followed "precise tool-description refinements". A Claude agent rewrote a flawed MCP tool description and cut later agents' completion time by 40% — [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/writing-tools-for-agents); [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/multi-agent-research-system).
- *Use / avoid:* Use for every non-trivial tool, and gate acceptance on a held-out suite so descriptions don't overfit (the same discipline as GEPA/ACE-style harness optimization in the evals section).

**Tool use examples (`input_examples`)**
- *What:* 1–5 concrete example invocations attached to a tool definition.
- *Mechanics:* Add an `input_examples` array to the tool definition (Anthropic advanced tool use, beta `advanced-tool-use-2025-11-20`). Show minimal, partial and full examples, format conventions (`YYYY-MM-DD`, `USR-XXXXX`), nesting, and correlated optional params.
- *Evidence:* Accuracy on complex parameters went from 72% to 90% — [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/advanced-tool-use).
- *Use / avoid:* Use for tools with nested objects, ID formats or interdependent optional fields. It is not needed for simple tools or for formats JSON Schema already enforces. Examples cost tokens, which is another reason to defer rarely used tools.

```jsonc
// Illustrative tool definition with input_examples (field name from the notes; tool is hypothetical).
{
  "name": "support_create_ticket",
  "description": "Create a support ticket. Use when the user reports a bug ...",
  "input_schema": {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
      "title": { "type": "string" },
      "reporter_id": { "type": "string", "description": "Format USR-XXXXX" },
      "due_date": { "type": "string", "description": "YYYY-MM-DD" },
      "escalation": { "type": "object", "properties": { "level": {"type": "integer"}, "notify": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}} } }
    },
    "required": ["title", "reporter_id"]
  },
  "input_examples": [
    { "title": "Login page 500", "reporter_id": "USR-12345" },
    { "title": "Checkout broken", "reporter_id": "USR-54321", "due_date": "2026-11-10",
      "escalation": { "level": 2, "notify": ["oncall"] } }
  ]
}
```

#### B. Managing tools as context

**Tool search / deferred loading (`defer_loading`)**
- *What:* Most tool definitions stay out of the prompt. A search tool returns references to the relevant ones on demand.
- *Mechanics (Anthropic):*
  1. Mark tools `"defer_loading": true` and keep the 3–5 most-used tools non-deferred. Never defer the search tool itself, and keep at least one non-deferred tool.
  2. Add a search tool: `tool_search_tool_regex_20251119` (Python `re.search` patterns, ≤200 chars) or `tool_search_tool_bm25_20251119` (natural-language queries, ≤500 chars). Both search names, descriptions, argument names and argument descriptions.
  3. Results come back as up to 5 `tool_reference` blocks by default (`limit` 1–10,000), with up to 10,000 deferred tools per request.
  4. For custom search (e.g. embeddings), return `tool_reference` blocks from your own tool.
  5. For MCP, use `mcp_toolset` with `default_config: {"defer_loading": true}` plus per-tool `configs`.

  Deferred tools are excluded from the prefix, so the cache is preserved. Discovered tools are appended inline as `tool_reference`, and deferred tools cannot carry `cache_control`. Claude Code defers MCP tools by default (names and server instructions only).
- *Mechanics (others):*
  - OpenAI `tool_search` defers rarely used functions on gpt-5.4+ only (search summary).
  - Codex registers a `tool_search` tool.
  - The Anthropic code-execution-with-MCP variant uses a `search_tools` tool with detail levels (name only / name + description / full schema).
  - For self-hosted models, the equivalent is logit or prefill masking over namespaced prefixes (inference).
- *Evidence:*
  - 50+ MCP tools ≈ 72K tokens (~77K consumed before any work) traditionally, vs ~500 upfront + ~3K for 3–5 discovered tools (~8.7K total): an "85% reduction".
  - 5 servers / 58 tools ≈ 55K; Jira alone ≈ 17K; 134K has been observed.
  - MCP-eval accuracy: Opus 4 49%→74%, Opus 4.5 79.5%→88.1%.
  - The post also cites 191,300 vs 122,800 tokens preserved, which it doesn't reconcile with the other figures.

  Claude's tool-selection accuracy "degrades once you exceed 30–50 available tools" — [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/advanced-tool-use); [Tool search tool docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/tool-search-tool).
- *Use / avoid:* Use when definitions exceed 10K tokens, with 10+ tools, multiple MCP servers, or observed selection errors. The Claude docs' rollout guide says "past about 20 tools". It is not worth it for fewer than 10 tools or compact definitions. No BM25 vs regex vs embedding accuracy comparison exists in the notes.

```jsonc
// Illustrative Anthropic request fragment (type strings and fields from the notes; other fields elided).
// Header: anthropic-beta: advanced-tool-use-2025-11-20  (Nov 2025 launch; docs now call tool search stable)
"tools": [
  { "type": "tool_search_tool_regex_20251119", "name": "..." },          // never deferred
  { "name": "Read",  "input_schema": { ... } },                          // hot (3-5 hot tools)
  { "name": "jira_search", "input_schema": { ... }, "defer_loading": true },
  { "type": "mcp_toolset", "...": "server reference (not in notes)",
    "default_config": { "defer_loading": true },
    "configs": { "github_create_pr": { "defer_loading": false } } }
]
```

**Programmatic Tool Calling (PTC) / code-mode**
- *What:* The model writes code that calls your tools as functions inside a sandbox. Only the final printed or returned result enters context.
- *Mechanics (Anthropic):*
  1. Add `{"type": "code_execution_20250825", "name": "code_execution"}`. The Nov 2025 post uses this version; current Claude docs require `code_execution_20260120`+ and show `allowed_callers: ["code_execution_20260120"]`.
  2. Set `"allowed_callers": [...]` on opted-in tools.
  3. Claude writes Python that calls them as async functions, in parallel via `asyncio.gather`.
  4. Each call pauses execution and returns a `tool_use` with a `caller` field. The model's code invocation appears as `server_tool_use` and its output as `code_execution_tool_result`.

  PTC is not available on Haiku 4.5, is not ZDR-eligible (data kept up to 30 days), and `allowed_callers` "is guidance, not a security boundary".
- *Mechanics (OpenAI):* Codex code-mode crates (`code-mode`, `code-mode-runtime`, `code-mode-host`) expose a code-mode `exec` tool. `augment_tool_spec_for_code_mode` adds "code-mode-specific exec samples" to tool descriptions. OpenAI's GPT-6 guidance lists "Programmatic Tool Calling" as an optional feature. OpenCode has a `codemode` package; smolagents `CodeAgent` is the open code-as-action reference.
- *Evidence:*
  - Complex research tasks: 43,588 → 27,297 average tokens (−37%).
  - Internal knowledge retrieval: 25.6% → 28.5%. GAIA: 46.5% → 51.2% (one source summary renders this as "GIA"; GAIA is meant).
  - 20+ calls in one code block save 19+ inference passes.
  - Budget/expense example: 2,000+ line items (~200KB) reduced to ~1KB in context.
  - Claude for Excel uses PTC.

  [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/advanced-tool-use); [Claude docs: PTC](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/programmatic-tool-calling).
- *Use / avoid:* Use for large data, 3+ dependent calls, filtering and aggregation, and parallel fan-out. Document return formats, and prefer idempotent, parallel-safe tools for code callers. Avoid it for destructive tools: keep them direct-call and approval-gated, because tool calls now originate from model-written code (§6–7). Mark bulk-data tools as code-only callers so raw results never reach the transcript.

```jsonc
// Illustrative PTC fragment (Anthropic; versions per the notes).
"tools": [
  { "type": "code_execution_20260120", "name": "code_execution" },        // Nov 2025 post: code_execution_20250825
  { "name": "expenses_list_line_items", "input_schema": { ... },
    "allowed_callers": ["code_execution_20260120"] }                      // callable from code; guidance, not a boundary
]
// Response: server_tool_use (model's code) -> tool_use blocks with "caller" -> code_execution_tool_result
```

**Code execution with MCP (tools as a filesystem code API)**
- *What:* Present each MCP server as a directory of typed code files. The agent explores them and writes scripts that chain calls.
- *Mechanics:*
  - Use `servers/<server>/` with one typed TS file per tool (e.g. `./servers/google-drive/getDocument.ts`), each wrapping `callMCPTool('google_drive__get_document', …)`.
  - The agent lists directories and reads only what it needs, or calls `search_tools` with a detail level.
  - Scripts keep intermediate data in the sandbox: loops and conditionals run in code, and state persists in workspace files.
  - The MCP client can tokenize PII (`[EMAIL_1]`) and untokenize it between tools.
  - Reusable code can be saved as `SKILL.md` skills.
- *Evidence:* "150,000 tokens to 2,000 tokens" (98.7%). A 10,000-row sheet is filtered to 5 rows before reaching the model, and a 2-hour transcript (~50K tokens) need not pass through context twice — [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/code-execution-with-mcp).
- *Use / avoid:* Use for data-heavy agents with many MCP servers. The cost is a secure sandbox with resource limits and monitoring. Don't adopt it without a hardened code sandbox (§6).

**Cache-stable tool lists**
- *What:* The tool array is part of the cached prefix. Never mutate it mid-session; gate tools in ways that don't change the bytes.
- *Mechanics:*
  - Fixed serialization order: tools (stable, most deferred), then system, then project instructions and skills index, then the append-only conversation.
  - MCP 2026-07-28: servers SHOULD return `tools/list` in deterministic order, and list results are `CacheableResult` with required `ttlMs` and `cacheScope` (`public`/`private`) (SEP-2549).
  - Restrict the callable set without changing definitions: OpenAI `allowed_tools`; Manus logit masking over prefixes.
  - Anthropic `tool_addition`/`tool_removal` (beta `inline-tools-2026-09-15`) adds or withdraws tools in-band.
- *Evidence:*
  - Anthropic: tool definition changes invalidate the entire cache.
  - Claude Code lists connecting or removing an MCP server, or denying an entire tool, as cache-busting actions.
  - Secondary summaries of OpenAI's Codex loop post: "dynamic tool lists (MCP) can break the prefix".
  - Manus calls KV-cache hit rate "the single most important metric".

  [Claude docs: prompt caching](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching); [MCP 2026-07-28 changelog](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/blob/main/docs/specification/2026-07-28/changelog.mdx).
- *Use / avoid:* Always. Treat unexpected cache misses after a tool change as regressions.

**Parallel tool calls and concurrency classes**
- *What:* Let the model emit several calls per turn. Run safe ones concurrently and mutating ones sequentially.
- *Mechanics:*
  - Claude Agent SDK: read-only tools (`Read`, `Glob`, `Grep`, read-only MCP tools) run concurrently, while `Edit`/`Write`/`Bash` run sequentially. Custom tools are sequential unless `readOnlyHint` is set.
  - OpenAI `parallel_tool_calls` (`false` = zero or one call per turn); Codex passes it through and has `core/src/tools/parallel.rs`.
  - Agents SDK `ToolExecutionConfig.max_function_tool_concurrency`.
  - In Anthropic's research system, each subagent used 3+ tools in parallel.
- *Evidence:* The parallel lead plus subagents with parallel tools cut research time by up to 90% — [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/multi-agent-research-system). OpenAI agent RFT models learned to issue more parallel calls.
- *Use / avoid:* Default to parallel for read-only and idempotent tools. Use `readOnlyHint`/annotations as the classifier (untrusted from unvetted servers). On Anthropic, add a mid-history cache breakpoint when a turn can add 20+ blocks.

#### C. Edit formats

Comparison first, details below.

| Format | Who uses it | Shape | Strengths | Weaknesses / notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `apply_patch` envelope (V4A) | Codex (Lark grammar, freeform), OpenAI Responses built-in, gpt-oss, OpenCode `patch`, Agents SDK sandbox `apply_patch.py`, OpenHands `apply_patch`, Aider `patch_coder.py` | Multi-file add/delete/update/move in one call; context-anchored hunks, no line numbers | OpenAI models trained on it; atomic multi-file; streamable; grammar-constrained (no JSON escaping) | Needs a tolerant matcher; non-OpenAI models may be less fluent (no data in the notes) |
| `str_replace` / `old_string→new_string` | Claude Code `Edit` (SDK-visible behaviour only; internal schema closed), Anthropic memory tool `str_replace`, Gemini CLI `edit`, Crush `edit`/`multiedit`, Pi `edit`, SWE-agent `edit_anthropic`, OpenHands `file_editor` | One exact snippet replaced per call (multi-edit variants batch) | Simple; uniqueness check gives a clear error; no line numbers | One file per call; must quote the old text exactly |
| SEARCH/REPLACE blocks, `diff-fenced`, `udiff`, `whole` | Aider (no tool calling); `editor-diff`/`editor-whole` for architect/editor split | Plain-text blocks in the assistant message | Works without tool calling; per-model table | Parsing free text; whole-file is token-expensive |
| Bash-only (`sed`, heredocs) | mini-swe-agent | Shell commands | Zero extra tools; trivially sandboxed; strong baseline (>74% SWE-bench Verified) | No edit validation; quoting errors |
| Code-as-action | smolagents `CodeAgent`; Codex/OpenCode code-mode | Program that edits files | Composes with data processing | Needs a hardened sandbox |

**`apply_patch` envelope (V4A) as a freeform grammar tool**
- *What:* A line-number-free, context-anchored patch language covering add, delete, update and move across many files in one call. It is sent as raw text constrained by a grammar rather than as a JSON argument.
- *Mechanics:*
  - The official Lark grammar's start rule is `start: begin_patch environment_id? hunk+ end_patch`.
  - Markers: `*** Begin Patch`; `*** Add File: <path>`; `*** Delete File: <path>`; `*** Update File: <path>` with optional `*** Move to: <path>`; `@@` or `@@ <context>` anchors; lines prefixed `+` / `-` / space; optional `*** End of File`; `*** End Patch`. A new optional `*** Environment ID:` header supports multi-environment threads.
  - Codex registers it as a FREEFORM tool with `format: {type: "grammar", syntax: "lark"}`, loaded from `assets/tools/apply_patch.lark`, with the description "This is a FREEFORM tool, so do not wrap the patch in JSON". OpenAI also offers it "as a first-class Responses API tool".
  - The parser tolerates surrounding whitespace. A streaming parser applies patches as they stream, and a standalone `apply_patch` executable exists. Model instructions are in `codex-rs/core/prompt_with_apply_patch_instructions.md`.
- *Evidence:* "We strongly recommend using our exact apply_patch implementation as the model has been trained to excel at this diff format." The format follows the ACI advice to avoid line counts and code-in-JSON. GPT-5.3-Codex tries to call `apply_patch` even when absent — [OpenAI Codex Prompting Guide](https://developers.openai.com/cookbook/examples/gpt-5/codex_prompting_guide) (search summary); [parser.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/apply-patch/src/parser.rs); [apply_patch_spec.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/apply_patch_spec.rs).
- *Use / avoid:* Mandatory for OpenAI Codex-family models and gpt-oss ("should only be used with this format"). Ship OpenAI's exact implementation or a byte-compatible port. Optional for other models; OpenCode ships the same envelope verbatim as its `patch` tool.

```lark
// Sketch reconstructed from the markers in the notes. Only the `start` rule is quoted verbatim;
// the authoritative grammar is codex-rs assets/tools/apply_patch.lark (loaded by apply_patch_spec.rs).
start: begin_patch environment_id? hunk+ end_patch
begin_patch: "*** Begin Patch" LF
environment_id: "*** Environment ID: " /(.+)/ LF          // new, optional
hunk: add_hunk | delete_hunk | update_hunk
add_hunk: "*** Add File: " filename LF ("+" /(.*)/ LF)+
delete_hunk: "*** Delete File: " filename LF
update_hunk: "*** Update File: " filename LF ("*** Move to: " filename LF)? change+
change: ("@@" | "@@ " /(.+)/) LF change_line+ ("*** End of File" LF)?
change_line: ("+" | "-" | " ") /(.*)/ LF
end_patch: "*** End Patch" LF?
```

```text
*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: docs/NOTES.md
+# Notes
+First line.
*** Update File: src/app.py
*** Move to: src/main.py
@@ def main():
-    run_old()
+    run_new()
*** Delete File: legacy/old_util.py
*** End Patch
```

**Tolerant patch matching and atomic application**
- *What:* Locate hunk context robustly and apply all-or-nothing.
- *Mechanics:* Codex `seek_sequence` tries exact match, then trim-end, then trim, then Unicode-normalised match. The parser is "deliberately lenient"; code comments say only gpt-4.1 "knowingly requires lenient parsing". Validate the whole patch before writing any file (inference in the notes: "validate edits atomically").
- *Evidence:* The Codex source design — [seek_sequence.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/apply-patch/src/seek_sequence.rs).
- *Use / avoid:* Always pair a patch format with fuzzy-but-safe matching. Return a precise error naming the failing hunk rather than partially applying.

**`str_replace` / `old_string→new_string`**
- *What:* Replace one exact, unique snippet in a file, with create/insert/view companions.
- *Mechanics:*
  - The documented reference semantics are the Anthropic memory tool's `str_replace` (`path`, `old_str`, optional `new_str`). It errors when the text is not found and when there are multiple occurrences.
  - Companions: `create` (`path`, `file_text`), `insert` (`insert_line`, `insert_text`; 0 = beginning) and `view`, which line-numbers output with a 6-char right-aligned number plus tab and accepts a `view_range` where `-1` = EOF.
  - Gemini CLI `edit` uses `old_string`/`new_string`, and Crush adds `multiedit` for batched edits.
  - The Claude Code `Edit` internal schema is closed; only SDK-visible behaviour is known. The SDK's file checkpointing tracks `Write`/`Edit`/`NotebookEdit` changes but not Bash side effects.
- *Evidence:* Recommended for Claude-style models by the open-source survey. It is inferred from the Claude Code SDK uplift (AgencyBench +20.5% inside the Claude Code SDK), not from a confirmed Anthropic training disclosure.
- *Use / avoid:* The default for Claude, Gemini and most non-OpenAI models. Pair it with `Write` for new files and full rewrites.

```jsonc
// Illustrative str_replace-style edit tool (semantics from the Anthropic memory tool / Gemini CLI edit).
{
  "name": "edit",
  "description": "Replace exactly one occurrence of old_string in the file at absolute path `path`. Fails if old_string is not found or is not unique; include more surrounding lines to disambiguate.",
  "input_schema": {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
      "path": { "type": "string", "description": "Absolute path" },
      "old_string": { "type": "string" },
      "new_string": { "type": "string" }
    },
    "required": ["path", "old_string", "new_string"],
    "additionalProperties": false
  }
}
```

**SEARCH/REPLACE, udiff and whole-file (Aider)**
- *What:* Edit formats emitted as plain text in the assistant message, for models or endpoints without tool calling.
- *Mechanics:* `whole`, `diff` (SEARCH/REPLACE blocks), `diff-fenced`, `udiff`, and `editor-diff`/`editor-whole` for the architect/editor two-model split, all selected through a per-model edit-format table.
- *Evidence:* Aider's leaderboard is the closest thing to an edit-format × model matrix, but its data was not extracted in the notes. DGM's self-modified agent surpassed hand-built Aider on Polyglot (14.2%→30.7%).
- *Use / avoid:* Use for weak, local or no-tool-calling models and as a fallback profile. Whole-file only for small files.

**Bash-only editing**
- *What:* No edit tool at all; the model edits with `sed`, heredocs and scripts.
- *Mechanics:* mini-swe-agent runs each action with `subprocess.run` and keeps a completely linear history. It "doesn't even need to use the tool-calling interface".
- *Evidence:* ">74%" SWE-bench Verified (PyPI attributes this to Gemini 3 Pro; the July 2025 version scored 65%). It powers the SWE-bench "bash only" leaderboard.
- *Use / avoid:* Use as the ablation and control condition for any harness. For production, add a validated edit tool for safer, checkpointable edits.

**Native toolset matching (per-model tool profiles)**
- *What:* Present each model the tool names, schemas, edit format and system prompt it was post-trained with.
- *Mechanics:*
  - OpenAI: `apply_patch` (V4A) + `shell`/`exec_command` + `update_plan`, per-model base prompts (`gpt_5_codex_prompt.md`, `gpt-5.1-codex-max_prompt.md`, `gpt-5.2-codex_prompt.md`, `gpt_5_1_prompt.md`, `gpt_5_2_prompt.md`).
  - Anthropic: `Read`/`Edit`/`Write`/`Bash`/`Glob`/`Grep`/`TodoWrite`-style tools.
  - gpt-oss: harmony plus its reference tools.
  - DeepSeek: whatever harness it is documented with (Claude Code via the Anthropic endpoint, or OpenCode).
- *Evidence:* AgencyBench: Claude-4.5-Opus is 20.5% higher in the Claude Code SDK than in a generalist scaffold. LangChain went from 52.8% to 66.5% on Terminal-Bench 2.0 with GPT-5.2-Codex from harness changes only (secondary). Codex CLI + GPT-5.5 scored 83.4% vs Terminus 2 + GPT-5.5 at 78.2% on TB 2.1 (secondary). Cursor, Windsurf and Kimi all train in their own tool harnesses.
- *Use / avoid:* Always. Make tool formats pluggable per model. Expect several benchmark points from this alone (inference).

#### D. Shell, kernel and auxiliary tools

**Shell model: PTY sessions vs stateless subprocess**
- *What:* Choose between a persistent interactive shell and independent per-command processes.
- *Mechanics:*
  - Codex uses `exec_command` + `write_stdin` (PTY sessions keyed by `session_id`) and keeps legacy `shell`. OpenCode has `persistent-pty`, Crush has `job_output`/`job_kill`, and Gemini CLI has `shellBackgroundTools`.
  - mini-swe-agent uses stateless `subprocess.run` ("a big deal" for sandboxing and scaling), where sandboxing is just swapping in `docker exec`.
  - OpenAI hosted shell has no TTY and no sudo, with containers reusable across calls.
- *Evidence:* Design statements from source and READMEs; no comparative numbers.
- *Use / avoid:* Use PTY sessions for interactive programs, dev servers and REPLs, with write-stdin and background-job tools. Use stateless execution for evals and RL rollouts, and for simple sandboxes.

**Plan/todo tool, model-gated**
- *What:* A tool that records a short step list with statuses and renders it to the user.
- *Mechanics:*
  - Codex `update_plan` takes 1-sentence steps of 5–7 words, statuses `pending`/`in_progress`/`completed`, exactly one `in_progress` at a time, and an `explanation` on change. It errors in Plan Mode.
  - Claude `TodoWrite`/`Task*` tools are opt-in on newer models (`CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TODO_TOOLS=1`) and are meant for tasks with 3+ distinct actions.
  - Others: OpenCode `todowrite`, Gemini `write-todos` + `trackerTools`, OpenHands `task_tracker`. Pi omits it.
  - Manus uses `todo.md` recitation to keep goals in recent attention.
- *Evidence:* "Newer models track multi-step work without a written todo list" (Anthropic). Codex guidance: "do not treat a plan update as a substitute for doing the work."
- *Use / avoid:* Enable per model (on for older or weaker models and for UI progress rendering). Keep plan *mode* (a read-only permission state) separate from the plan *tool*.

**Loop-control and context tools**
- *What:* Tools that let the model observe or manage its own context and time.
- *Mechanics:* Codex `get_context_remaining`, `new_context` ("Does not clear, reset, or otherwise affect environment state") and `sleep` (ends early on new input), plus `request_user_input`/`request_permissions`. Claude models receive an automatic token-budget signal instead (on some models), and Anthropic exposes the client-side `memory_20250818` tool.
- *Evidence:* Shipped in the Codex source. No measured gains in the notes.
- *Use / avoid:* Useful for long-horizon agents and models with "context anxiety". Keep them optional.

**LSP-as-tools**
- *What:* Expose language-server operations as tools.
- *Mechanics:* Crush `lsp_definition`, `lsp_rename`, `lsp_replace_symbol`, `lsp_symbols`, `lsp_call_hierarchy` and `diagnostics`. OpenCode has `lsp` handling.
- *Evidence:* Design only.
- *Use / avoid:* Worth copying for refactor-heavy work. Optional and deferred.

#### E. Protocols and packaging
