**MCP 2026-07-28 client (stateless core)**
- *What:* Implement the current MCP revision, with fallbacks for older servers.
- *Mechanics (from the changelog):*
  - **No sessions or handshake (SEP-2567, SEP-2575).** No `Mcp-Session-Id` and no `initialize`/`notifications/initialized`. Every request carries `_meta` `io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion` and `io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities` (and SHOULD carry `clientInfo`); results carry `serverInfo`; a mismatch returns `UnsupportedProtocolVersionError`.
  - **Handles.** Cross-call state uses "explicit, server-minted handles passed as ordinary tool arguments" ("the model can see the handle and thread it between tools").
  - **Discovery and subscriptions.** `server/discover` is new and MUST be implemented. `subscriptions/listen` replaces the GET stream and `resources/subscribe`.
  - **Removed.** `ping`, `logging/setLevel` (log level is set per request via `io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel`), `notifications/roots/list_changed`, and SSE resumability (`Last-Event-ID`), so a broken stream means re-issuing the request with a new ID.
  - **Multi Round-Trip Requests (SEP-2322).** The server returns `InputRequiredResult` (`resultType: "input_required"`, `inputRequests`), and the client retries the original request with `inputResponses`. This replaces server-initiated `roots/list`, `sampling/createMessage` and `elicitation/create`. All results carry `resultType` (`"complete"`/`"input_required"`). `elicitationId` and `notifications/elicitation/complete` are removed in favour of `requestState`.
  - **Tasks** become the extension `io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks` (SEP-2663): poll with `tasks/get`, send client→server input with the new `tasks/update`, `tasks/list` is removed, and servers may return task handles unsolicited.
  - **Headers, caching and errors.** `Mcp-Method`/`Mcp-Name` headers are required, plus `x-mcp-header` for custom headers from tool params (SEP-2243). `CacheableResult` carries `ttlMs` and `cacheScope` (SEP-2549). OTel `traceparent`/`tracestate`/`baggage` go in `_meta` (SEP-414). Capabilities gain an `extensions` field. Resource-not-found becomes `-32602`, and `-32020..-32099` is reserved.
  - **Auth.** RFC 9207 `iss` validation (SEP-2468), `application_type` in DCR (SEP-837), credentials bound to issuer (SEP-2352).
  - **Deprecated.** Roots, Sampling and Logging (SEP-2577; migrate to tool params/URIs, direct LLM APIs, stderr/OTel), HTTP+SSE transport, `includeContext` `thisServer`/`allServers`, and DCR in favour of CIMD (PR #2858). The lifecycle policy sets a ≥12-month deprecation window (SEP-2596).
- *Earlier revisions still relevant:*
  - 2025-06-18: `structuredContent`/`outputSchema`, resource links, elicitation, OAuth Resource Server + RFC 8707 Resource Indicators, `MCP-Protocol-Version` header, batching removed.
  - 2025-11-25: OIDC discovery (#797), icons (SEP-973), incremental scope consent via `WWW-Authenticate` (SEP-835), tool names (SEP-986), `EnumSchema` (SEP-1330), URL-mode elicitation (SEP-1036), tool calling inside sampling via `tools`/`toolChoice` (SEP-1577), CIMD (SEP-991), experimental tasks (SEP-1686), validation errors as tool errors (SEP-1303), polling SSE (SEP-1699), RFC 9728 (SEP-985), JSON Schema 2020-12 (SEP-1613), governance/WGs/SDK tiering (SEP-932/994/1302/1730), and 403 on an invalid `Origin` for Streamable HTTP.
- *Evidence of adoption:* At GA there were "close to half-a-billion downloads a month" across Tier 1 SDKs; TS and Python each crossed 1B total downloads; TS, Python, Go and C# SDKs were updated; extensions are Tasks, MCP Apps and Enterprise Managed Authorization (EMA). At the AAIF donation (Dec 2025): "97 million monthly SDK downloads, 10,000 active servers", with clients ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor, Gemini, Copilot and VS Code. The MCP Registry preview is at `registry.modelcontextprotocol.io` (Sep 8, 2025); MCPB bundles were announced Nov 20, 2025 — [MCP blog](https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2026-07-28/); [AAIF post](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/blob/main/blog/content/posts/2025-12-09-mcp-joins-agentic-ai-foundation.md).
- *Use / avoid:*
  - Implement stateless requests, `server/discover` with fallback to `initialize` for older servers, `input_required` handling (surface elicitation to the user and retry), `tools/list` caching by `ttlMs`, and CIMD-first OAuth with `iss` checks and resource indicators.
  - Use the tasks extension for long-running tools instead of holding streams open.
  - Don't build new features on Sampling, Roots, Logging or sessions.
  - Use an official SDK (Codex pins `rmcp =3.5.1`).

```jsonc
// Illustrative 2026-07-28 exchange (names from the changelog; shapes simplified).
// HTTP headers: Mcp-Method: tools/call   Mcp-Name: <tool name>
{ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 7, "method": "tools/call",
  "params": { "name": "deploy_preview", "arguments": { "branch": "feat-x" },
    "_meta": { "io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion": "2026-07-28",
               "io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities": { "...": "..." } } } }
// Server needs user input -> InputRequiredResult instead of a server->client request:
{ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 7, "result": { "resultType": "input_required",
  "inputRequests": [ { "...": "elicitation request" } ], "requestState": "opaque..." } }
// Client retries the ORIGINAL request with inputResponses (new id), carrying requestState back.
```

**MCP tool annotations as policy input (and tool-poisoning hygiene)**
- *What:* Server-declared hints about tool behaviour that feed the host's approval and concurrency policy.
- *Mechanics:* `ToolAnnotations {title, readOnlyHint (default false), destructiveHint (default true), idempotentHint (default false), openWorldHint (default true)}`. All are hints and untrusted unless the server is trusted. Pending SEPs: #1913 trust/sensitivity (GitHub + OpenAI), #1984 governance, #1561 `unsafeOutputHint`, #1560 `secretHint`, #1487 `trustedHint`. A `seesUntrustedData`-style hint could let hosts taint sessions.
- *Evidence:* ~17% of GitHub MCP users run its read-only mode. As of Mar 16, 2026, "no client yet filters by annotations or shows them in approval prompts" — [MCP blog](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/blob/main/blog/content/posts/2026-03-16-tool-annotations.md).
- *Use / avoid:* Use `readOnlyHint` for concurrency and auto-approval only from vetted servers. Tool poisoning and rug pulls (hidden instructions in descriptions; descriptions changed after approval) mean you should hash and pin approved descriptions and diff on change. See §7.

**Agent Skills (`SKILL.md`) with progressive disclosure**
- *What:* Procedures packaged as folders that load in stages.
- *Mechanics:*
  - A skill is a folder with a required `SKILL.md` (YAML frontmatter `name` + `description`, then markdown) plus optional `scripts/`, `references/` and `assets/`.
  - Level 1 is metadata (~100 tokens per skill), always loaded. Level 2 is the SKILL.md body (under 5k tokens), loaded when triggered. Level 3+ is bundled resources at zero tokens until read; scripts run via bash and only their output enters context.
  - Authoring rules: `name` ≤64 chars; the `description` says what the skill does and when to use it; body under 500 lines; references one level deep; a TOC for reference files over 100 lines. `disable-model-invocation: true` hides the description.
  - Claude Code re-injects invoked skill bodies after compaction (≤5,000 tokens each, 25,000 total).
  - The spec lives at agentskills.io/specification.
  - Adopters: Codex (`skills` crate, `skills/list`), OpenAI Agents SDK `Skills(lazy_from=…)`, Gemini CLI `activate-skill`, deepagents, Letta Code (`.agents/skills`), Pi, OpenHands SDK, Crush, plus reportedly GitHub Copilot, VS Code and Cursor. About 40–44 clients were listed on agentskills.io by mid-2026 (secondary).
- *Evidence:*
  - SkillsBench (arXiv 2602.12670): curated skills +16.2pp average (+16.4pp NeurIPS version; 16/84 tasks regress), while self-generated skills gave no benefit (−1.3pp).
  - Single-agent-with-skills matched multi-agent accuracy (+0.7%) with 54% fewer tokens and 50% lower latency, but selection degrades sharply beyond ~50–100 skills (arXiv 2601.04748, snippet).
  - 22% of 673 sampled skills failed structural validation (secondary).

  [Claude docs: Agent Skills](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/overview); [best practices](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/best-practices); [aictrl.dev](https://aictrl.dev/blog/skill-md-adoption-trajectory).
- *Use / avoid:* Put procedures in skills, facts in AGENTS.md and actions in tools. Validate skills structurally, audit third-party skills (they can exfiltrate), and gate self-authored skills on verification.

**AGENTS.md (and CLAUDE.md) instruction files**
- *What:* A cross-vendor "README for agents", stewarded by AAIF.
- *Mechanics:*
  - Codex collects every AGENTS.md from root to cwd, with `AGENTS.override.md`, the `--- project-doc ---` joiner and a `project_doc_max_bytes` budget. Deeper files win, and direct instructions beat AGENTS.md.
  - Claude Code reads AGENTS.md when no CLAUDE.md exists (the `agents-md` mod modes), or via an `@AGENTS.md` import.
  - Instruction files by harness: OpenCode and Kimi Code use AGENTS.md; Pi AGENTS.md + CLAUDE.md; Cline AGENTS.md + `.clinerules`; Goose AGENTS.md + CLAUDE.md + `.goosehints`; Crush AGENTS.md + CLAUDE.md + CRUSH.md + GEMINI.md; Qwen Code AGENTS.md + QWEN.md + CLAUDE.md + GEMINI.md; Gemini CLI GEMINI.md (configurable).
- *Evidence:* One report cites use across ~40,000 open-source projects. The spec's nested precedence rule is unverified from a primary source.
- *Use / avoid:* Support hierarchical discovery with a byte budget. Context loading details belong to the context-engineering section.

**Hooks with Claude/Codex-compatible names**
- *What:* Deterministic interception points around tool calls and the loop.
- *Mechanics:*
  - **Shared vocabulary (Claude Code / Agent SDK / Codex):** `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `SessionStart`, `SessionEnd`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `Stop`, `SubagentStop`, `PreCompact`, `PostCompact`, `PermissionRequest`. The Agent SDK `HookEvent` also has `PostToolUseFailure`, `Notification` and `SubagentStart`.
  - **Gemini CLI uses different names:** `BeforeTool`/`AfterTool`/`BeforeModel`/`AfterModel`/`BeforeToolSelection`/`PreCompress`.
  - **Pre-tool outputs:** `permissionDecision` ∈ {allow, deny, ask, defer} + `updatedInput`; exit code 2 blocks.
  - **Stop hooks:** block with a reason (Codex ignores a block without a prompt). Claude Code overrides a Stop hook after 8 consecutive blocks with no tool call.
- *Evidence:* Codex adopted the same names, so a matching contract gets ecosystem compatibility. Hooks are also present in Kimi Code, Letta Code, OpenHands SDK and Cline.
- *Use / avoid:* Implement this vocabulary. Optionally add Gemini-style model-level hooks (`BeforeModel`, `AfterModel`, `BeforeToolSelection`), which Claude and Codex lack.

**Agent↔client and agent↔agent protocols (ACP, A2A, app-server, plugins)**
- *What:* Protocols for driving the harness from editors and control centers, and for calling remote agents.
- *Mechanics:*
  - **ACP (Agent Client Protocol)** is spoken by Kimi Code (`acp-server`, `kimi acp` for Zed/JetBrains), Goose, deepagents (`libs/acp`) and Pi. OpenHands Agent Canvas runs "OpenHands, Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Pi, OpenCode, or any ACP-compatible agent". The spec text (agentclientprotocol.com) was not fetched.
  - **A2A v1.0.0** adds multi-protocol bindings (JSON-RPC 2.0/HTTPS, gRPC, HTTP+JSON/REST) with version negotiation, multi-tenancy, signed Agent Cards at `/.well-known/agent-card.json` (name, skills, interfaces, capabilities, security schemes) and the AP2 payments extension. It launched under the Linux Foundation on Jun 23, 2025 and joined AAIF (reported Aug 2026). The v1.0 date conflicts (March 2026 GA vs "RC"; Mar–Apr per other sources; v1.0.1 ~May 2026). Some docs still show `A2A-Version: 0.3` headers. Gemini CLI uses A2A for remote subagents; Microsoft Agent Framework's A2A packages are still preview.
  - **Codex app-server** is JSON-RPC over thread/turn/item. **Claude** uses stream-JSON plus `control_request`.
  - **Plugins** bundle commands, agents, hooks and MCP servers: Claude `/plugin` marketplaces, Codex `plugin` subcommand and `request_plugin_install` tool, Kimi Code marketplace with trust levels, OpenHands `plugin`/`marketplace` modules, OpenCode `plugin` package.
- *Evidence:* Adoption is from source and READMEs; A2A details are secondary — [A2A spec](https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/specification/) (search summary); [letsdatascience](https://letsdatascience.com/news/a2a-solidifies-cross-vendor-agent-interoperability-53400ea4).
- *Use / avoid:* Expose an ACP server and a JSONL headless mode for embedding. Use A2A only across trust or organization boundaries; inside one harness, function calls, files and git are simpler.

### 5.7 Build checklist for our harness

**Recommended core tool kernel (always loaded, ≤5–10 tools)**

| Tool | Shape | Recommended defaults | Precedent |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bash` / `exec_command` (+ `write_stdin`) | PTY session tool with session ID; stateless mode for evals/RL | Runs inside the OS sandbox; per-call timeout; output capped and truncated with a "narrow your command" hint | Codex unified exec; Claude `Bash`; mini-swe-agent `subprocess.run` |
| `read` | `path` (absolute), `offset`/`limit` or `view_range`, image support | Line-numbered output (6-char right-aligned + tab); `max_characters`-style truncation | Claude `Read`, `text_editor_20250728`, memory `view` |
| `grep` / `glob` (or `ls`/`find`) | Read-only search | Parallel-safe (`readOnlyHint: true`); bounded result counts with pagination | Claude `Grep`/`Glob`; Pi read-only set |
| `edit` **and/or** `apply_patch` | Per model profile (table below) | Unique-match `str_replace` with not-found/multiple-match errors; or V4A envelope via freeform grammar with `seek_sequence`-style matching; atomic application | Claude `Edit`; Codex `apply_patch` |
| `write` | Create/overwrite whole file | Absolute path; checkpoint before write | Claude `Write`, Pi `write` |
| `tool_search` | Regex and/or BM25 over deferred tools | Returns 5 references; never deferred | Anthropic tool search; Codex/OpenAI `tool_search` |
| `todo` / `update_plan` | Step list with `pending`/`in_progress`/`completed` | Model-gated: on for older/weaker models and UI; off by default on newest Claude | Codex `update_plan`; Claude `TodoWrite` |
| `spawn_agent` / `Task` | Subagent with tool allowlist | Return ≤~2k-token summaries (see multi-agent section) | Codex `spawn_agent`; Claude Agent tool |
| Deferred (searchable) | `web_fetch`, `web_search`, `view_image`, `request_user_input`, LSP tools, `get_context_remaining`/`new_context`, all MCP tools | `defer_loading: true`; namespaced `server__tool` | Claude Code defers MCP by default |

**Edit format per model family**

| Model family | Primary edit tool | Companion tools | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| OpenAI Codex-family (GPT-5-Codex, GPT-5.1-Codex-Max, GPT-5.2/5.3-Codex, GPT-5.5 Codex siblings) | `apply_patch` (V4A), freeform Lark grammar, OpenAI's exact implementation | `shell`/`exec_command`+`write_stdin`, `update_plan` | OpenAI prompting guide ("trained to excel at this diff format"); GPT-5.3-Codex calls `apply_patch` even when absent |
| OpenAI GPT-5.x / GPT-6 general models (Responses API) | `apply_patch` (Responses built-in or freeform) | Responses `shell` | Inference: `apply_patch` is a first-class Responses tool; "tool calling with reasoning requires the Responses API" for GPT-6; verify per model |
| gpt-4.1 | `apply_patch` with lenient parsing | shell | Codex parser comment: only gpt-4.1 "knowingly requires lenient parsing" |
| gpt-oss | `apply_patch.py` as shipped, harmony format | `python_docker`, `simple_browser` | gpt-oss README: "should only be used with this format" |
| Claude (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku/Fable/Mythos) | `str_replace`-style `Edit` (`old_string`/`new_string`, unique match) + `Write` | `Read`/`Glob`/`Grep`/`Bash`, `TodoWrite` on older models | Inferred from the Claude Code SDK uplift (AgencyBench +20.5%), not a confirmed training disclosure |
| Gemini (via Gemini CLI conventions) | `edit` (`old_string`/`new_string`) | `read-file`, `shell`, `write-todos` | Inference from Gemini CLI's shipped tools |
| DeepSeek V3.2 / V4 | Match the documented host harness: `str_replace`-style when driven through the Anthropic endpoint (Claude Code), or the patch envelope via OpenCode | Same as host; keep `reasoning_content` across tool calls | No public DeepSeek edit-format disclosure in the notes; V4 documented with Claude Code/OpenCode (secondary) |
| Qwen (Qwen Code) | `edit` (`old_string`/`new_string`) | Gemini-CLI-derived tools | Inference: Qwen Code is a Gemini CLI fork |
| Weak/local or no-tool-calling models | Aider-style SEARCH/REPLACE (`diff`) or `whole` for small files | Repo map | Aider per-model edit-format table |
| Any (ablation baseline) | Bash-only (`sed`/heredoc) | — | mini-swe-agent (>74% SWE-bench Verified) |

**Implementation steps**

1. **Per-model tool profiles.** Build a tool registry where each model profile chooses tool names, schemas, edit format, plan-tool on/off and base prompt. Ship profiles `openai-codex` (`apply_patch` + `exec_command`/`write_stdin` + `update_plan`), `anthropic` (`Read`/`Edit`/`Write`/`Bash`/`Glob`/`Grep`, todo tools model-gated) and `generic` (str_replace + bash). Evaluate every profile with the model fixed.
2. **Ship `apply_patch` exactly.** Port or vendor Codex's `apply-patch` crate, including `seek_sequence` fallbacks, the streaming parser and the optional `*** Environment ID:` header. Register it as a freeform tool with `format: {type: "grammar", syntax: "lark"}` where the provider supports custom grammar tools, and otherwise as a single-string-argument tool. Apply atomically, and on failure return the failing hunk and nearest context.
3. **Ship `str_replace` with strict uniqueness.** Error on zero or multiple matches with an actionable message ("add more surrounding lines"). Require absolute paths. Line-number `read` output so the model can quote exact text.
4. **Shell.** Default to a PTY session tool (`exec_command` + `write_stdin`, session IDs, background jobs) for interactive work, and provide a stateless `subprocess.run` mode for evals and RL. Sandbox the whole process tree (§6) and log each call's exit code, duration and output size.
5. **Output budgets on every tool.** Use a global 25,000-token per-result cap (Claude Code default), per-tool pagination (`limit`/`offset`/`cursor`) and a `response_format: "concise" | "detailed"` enum on large-payload tools. Truncation messages must tell the model how to narrow the query. Offload oversize results to a workspace file and return path + preview + size.
6. **Errors as tool results.** Convert schema-validation failures, not-found tools, permission denials, sandbox violations and dead sandboxes into tool results with a corrected-input example. Never raise them as transport errors (MCP SEP-1303; Agents SDK `"return_error_to_model"`). Count consecutive failures and denials, and escalate after 3 consecutive or 20 total (auto-mode precedent).
7. **Strict schemas via a per-provider compiler.** Author one canonical JSON Schema 2020-12 per tool. Compile it to OpenAI strict (all `required`, nullable optionals, `additionalProperties: false`), DeepSeek strict (also strip `minLength`/`maxLength`/`minItems`/`maxItems`; beta base URL) and Anthropic (`input_schema`). Lint in CI for unsupported keywords.
8. **Description hygiene.** Namespace (`service_resource_verb` or `server__tool`), and use unambiguous params (`user_id`), enums for modes and "onboarding a new hire" descriptions. Add `input_examples` (1–5) for tools with nested or ID-formatted params. Keep descriptions as versioned files next to the code (Crush `.md.tpl` pattern) and record their git SHA in traces.
9. **Tool-eval loop.** Build an eval set of dozens of realistic multi-call tasks with verifiers. Track accuracy, calls, tokens, runtime and tool-error rate per tool. Let an agent refactor descriptions from transcripts, and accept changes only if a held-out set improves.
10. **Tiered loading.** Keep 3–5 hot tools plus `tool_search`, and defer everything else, all MCP tools included (`defer_loading: true`, or `mcp_toolset` `default_config`). Switch on tool search automatically when definitions exceed 10K tokens or there are 10+ tools. Use regex/BM25 server-side on Anthropic, `tool_search` on gpt-5.4+, and a client-side embedding search returning references for others. Never defer the search tool, keep at least one non-deferred tool, and don't put `cache_control` on deferred tools.
11. **Cache-stable tool array.** Serialize tools in deterministic order (sorted, as MCP 2026-07-28 recommends for `tools/list`), never mutate mid-session, and gate with `allowed_tools` (OpenAI), `tool_addition`/`tool_removal` (Anthropic beta `inline-tools-2026-09-15`) or logit masking over namespaced prefixes (self-hosted). Defer new MCP servers rather than injecting their definitions mid-session. Alert on unexpected cache misses.
12. **Concurrency classes.** Run read-only tools in parallel and mutating tools sequentially (Claude Agent SDK rule), and expose `parallel_tool_calls` passthrough. Derive "read-only" from first-party metadata or annotations from vetted servers only, cap concurrency (`max_function_tool_concurrency`-style), and add a mid-history cache breakpoint on Anthropic when a turn adds 20+ blocks.
13. **Code-mode / PTC (phase 2).** Offer a sandboxed code tool that can call registered tools as functions (Anthropic `allowed_callers` with `code_execution_20260120`; otherwise a Codex-style code-mode host). Only printed or returned values reach the model. Opt in bulk-data and idempotent tools, keep destructive tools direct-call and approval-gated, and treat `allowed_callers` as guidance, not a security boundary.
14. **MCP client on 2026-07-28.** Use an official SDK and make requests stateless with `_meta` version/capabilities. Call `server/discover`, falling back to `initialize` for older servers. Handle `resultType: "input_required"` by surfacing elicitation to the user and retrying with `inputResponses` + `requestState`. Use `Mcp-Method`/`Mcp-Name` headers, cache `tools/list` by `ttlMs`/`cacheScope`, and use the tasks extension (`tasks/get`, `tasks/update`) for long jobs. OAuth is CIMD-first with RFC 9207 `iss` and RFC 8707 resource indicators. Propagate OTel `traceparent` in `_meta`. Don't build on Sampling, Roots, Logging, HTTP+SSE or DCR.
15. **MCP server hygiene (tool design side).** Namespace tools per server. Pin server versions, and hash approved tool descriptions so you can diff and alert on change. Show descriptions to users, treat annotations from unvetted servers as untrusted, and run local servers under `srt`. Full threat model in §7.
16. **MCP for your own tools.** Expose custom tools as in-process MCP servers (Claude Agent SDK pattern) so the same definitions serve the harness, other clients and the eval loop. Return structured output (`structuredContent` + `outputSchema`) and use server-minted handles for cross-call state.
17. **Skills.** Implement SKILL.md discovery with three-level disclosure: ~100-token metadata always loaded, body ≤5k tokens on trigger, resources on read. Support `disable-model-invocation`, structural validation at install (22% of sampled skills fail), a soft cap of ~50 active skills (selection degrades beyond ~50–100), post-compaction re-injection (≤5k per skill / 25k total) and a review gate for agent-authored skills.
18. **AGENTS.md.** Discover root→cwd with an override file and a byte budget (Codex `project_doc_max_bytes` pattern), and also honour CLAUDE.md/GEMINI.md per the harness tables. Loading policy is detailed in the context-engineering section.
19. **Hooks.** Implement the Claude/Codex event names (`PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `PermissionRequest`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `Stop`, `SubagentStop`, `PreCompact`, `PostCompact`, `SessionStart`, `SessionEnd`), with `permissionDecision` ∈ {allow, deny, ask, defer}, `updatedInput`, exit code 2 = block, and command/http/mcp_tool/prompt/agent hook types (timeouts 600/600/600/30/60 s). Cap Stop-hook blocks at 8 consecutive with no tool call. Optionally add `BeforeModel`/`AfterModel`/`BeforeToolSelection`.
20. **Plugins.** Package commands, subagents, hooks, MCP servers and skills as a plugin manifest installable from a marketplace (Claude `/plugin` pattern), with trust levels (Kimi Code pattern).
21. **Embedding and interop.** Expose a JSONL headless event stream and an ACP server for editors and control centers (Zed, JetBrains, OpenHands Agent Canvas). Add an A2A client only for cross-org remote agents, and don't use A2A inside the harness.
22. **DeepSeek specifics.** Support a configurable base URL plus model-alias mapping (Anthropic-compatible endpoint). In thinking mode, keep `reasoning_content` + `content` + `tool_calls` together across tool calls and drop reasoning only at a new user message. Never simulate tool results as user messages, normalize `tool_calls` `None` vs `[]`, and use DeepSeek's reference encoders when self-hosting.
23. **Optional auxiliaries behind flags.** LSP tools (Crush), loop-control tools (`get_context_remaining`, `new_context`, `sleep`), `view_image` and `request_user_input`. Evaluate each per model, since labs keep removing scaffolds new models don't need.
24. **Telemetry per tool call.** Record tool name, call ID, args hash, result size in tokens, truncated flag, error class, duration, idempotency key and sandbox ID, so the tool-eval loop and cost dashboards have data.

### 5.8 Pitfalls and anti-patterns

**Tool surface**
- **Wrapping raw endpoints 1:1.** `list_users` + `list_events` + `create_event` instead of `schedule_event`, and `list_contacts` instead of `search_contacts`. This multiplies calls and context, and overlapping tools confuse selection.
- **Returning internal identifiers.** `uuid`, `mime_type` and `256px_image_url` where `name`/`file_type`/`image_url` would do. Opaque IDs increase hallucination.
- **Unbounded or silently truncated outputs.** No pagination, no cap, or truncation without a "narrow your query" hint. A single log or search result can blow the window (Claude Code caps at 25,000 tokens for a reason).
- **Opaque errors.** Status codes or raw tracebacks instead of a specific message with a corrected example. Returning validation failures as protocol errors instead of `isError` tool results (MCP SEP-1303) prevents self-correction.
- **Relative paths and ambiguous params** (`user` vs `user_id`). The classic SWE-bench failure was relative paths after `cd`.
- **Formats that need counting or escaping.** Line-numbered diff headers, accurate line counts over long files, and code wrapped in JSON strings (the ACI appendix). Wrapping an `apply_patch` body in JSON is explicitly discouraged by Codex ("do not wrap the patch in JSON").
- **Ambiguous `allowed_tools` semantics.** In the Claude Agent SDK, `allowed_tools` pre-approves and "does not control tool availability", so use `tools`/`disallowed_tools` to restrict.
- **Folk "<20 tools" rule.** It was not verifiable for OpenAI. The evidence-based triggers are >10K definition tokens, 10+ tools, multiple servers, and Claude's 30–50-tool degradation point.

**Context and cache**
- **Loading every MCP tool upfront.** 55K–134K tokens of definitions before any work, with accuracy loss.
- **Mutating the tool array mid-session.** Adding or removing tools, reordering, non-deterministic serialization, connecting a new MCP server, or denying an entire tool all invalidate the cache from the tools onward. Use deferral, `allowed_tools`, `tool_addition`/`tool_removal` or masking instead.
- **Tool-search misconfiguration.** Deferring the search tool itself, deferring every tool (the first by-value definition then costs a full cache miss), or putting `cache_control` on deferred tools.
- **Assuming tool results persist.** With context editing, old results are replaced by placeholders past the trigger. Results that must survive need `exclude_tools` or must be written to files or memory.

**Edit formats**
- **Wrong edit format for the model.** GPT-5.3-Codex calls a non-existent `apply_patch` in harnesses that lack it. Codex-family models are "trained to excel" at OpenAI's exact implementation, so a "close enough" re-implementation risks regressions.
- **Strict patch parsing.** Rejecting near-miss context instead of using `seek_sequence`-style fallbacks, or applying hunks partially instead of atomically.
- **Non-unique `str_replace`.** Silently replacing the first occurrence instead of erroring on multiple matches, or failing without telling the model to add surrounding context.
- **Edit loops.** Repeated edits to the same file are a known failure. LangChain's harness gains came partly from loop-detection middleware that counts edits per file and prompts reconsideration (secondary).
- **Bash edits bypass checkpoints.** The Claude Agent SDK's file checkpointing tracks only `Write`/`Edit`/`NotebookEdit`. Shell-based edits (`sed`, heredocs) need git or worktree snapshots.

**Code-mode / PTC**
- **Treating `allowed_callers` as a security boundary.** The docs say it is "guidance". Model-written code originating tool calls means destructive tools must stay direct-call and approval-gated, with a hardened sandbox (§6).
- **Running code-mode without a real sandbox.** "`LocalPythonExecutor` is not a security sandbox" (smolagents), and Agents SDK UnixLocal "adds no OS-level confinement" on Linux.
- **ZDR assumptions.** PTC is not ZDR-eligible (data kept up to 30 days).

**Provider-specific**
- **One schema for all providers.** DeepSeek strict rejects `minLength`/`maxLength` and `minItems`/`maxItems`. OpenAI strict requires every property in `required` with nullable optionals. Strict may be disabled with parallel calls on fine-tuned OpenAI models (reported).
- **DeepSeek reasoning state.** Not passing `reasoning_content` back in tool loops returns 400 (secondary). Simulating tool results as user messages triggers reasoning discard (V3.2 report names Roo Code and Terminus). Don't assume V3.2-Speciale supports tools (it doesn't), and note the Vercel/DeepSeek conflict on "V3.2 Thinking" tool support.
- **DeepSeek Anthropic endpoint.** It ignores `anthropic-beta` headers, so Anthropic beta features (tool search, PTC, inline tools) won't work, and MCP tool-use blocks are reportedly unsupported.
- **Plan tools where the model doesn't need them.** Anthropic turned todo tools off by default on its newest models. Calling `update_plan` in Codex Plan Mode returns an error by design.

**Protocols and packaging**
- **Building on deprecated MCP features.** Sampling, Roots, Logging (SEP-2577), HTTP+SSE transport, `includeContext` `thisServer`/`allServers`, DCR, protocol sessions/`Mcp-Session-Id`, and SSE resumability (`Last-Event-ID`) are all gone or deprecated in 2026-07-28. Deprecations carry a ≥12-month window (SEP-2596).
- **Trusting annotations from unvetted servers.** `readOnlyHint` and friends are hints. Tool poisoning (hidden instructions in descriptions, cross-server redirection as in the WhatsApp demo) and rug pulls (descriptions changed after approval) are real; see §7.
- **Too many or unvetted skills.** Selection degrades beyond ~50–100 skills, self-generated skills average ~0 benefit (SkillsBench), 22% of sampled skills fail structural validation, and malicious skills can exfiltrate.
- **Hook-name drift.** Gemini CLI uses `BeforeTool`/`AfterTool` etc. Pick the Claude/Codex vocabulary for ecosystem compatibility, and add aliases rather than inventing names.
- **A2A version confusion.** Some docs still show `A2A-Version: 0.3` headers while the current release is 1.0.0. Microsoft Agent Framework's A2A packages are still preview.
- **Overfitting descriptions.** Tool-description tuning without a held-out set (Anthropic's warning) and harness claims without the model held fixed (TB 2.0 vs 2.1 differ; infrastructure noise).

### 5.9 Open questions and unverified claims

**OpenAI**
- The current OpenAI function-calling details are unverified from the primary page (developers.openai.com was unreachable): strict + parallel compatibility, `allowed_tools` semantics, `tool_search` (gpt-5.4+ only) behaviour and numbers, and any numeric tool-count guidance.
- Whether OpenAI's hosted `apply_patch` executes server-side in the container or only client-side is unverified.
- No public numbers were found for OpenAI `tool_search` or Codex code-mode, and the code-mode runtime engine (JS/V8?) was not confirmed from source.
- Codex tool naming: research listings show both `new_context` and `new_context_window` for the context-reset tool; check the handler source.
- There is no primary confirmation of *how* GPT-5-Codex and later were RL-trained in the Codex harness; only "trained to excel at this diff format" is primary. The GPT-5.5 training claim is third-party.
- OpenAI's Aug 20, 2026 open-sourcing of the "Codex harness" is reported only by secondary outlets.

**Anthropic**
- Current GA status (Nov 2026) of `advanced-tool-use-2025-11-20` features is unconfirmed. The Claude docs call tool search stable; PTC and `input_examples` status was not checked.
- PTC version drift: the Nov 2025 post shows `code_execution_20250825`, while current docs require `code_execution_20260120`+. Confirm which `allowed_callers` values are accepted.
- The PTC GAIA figure appears as "GIA" in one source summary; GAIA is assumed. The 191,300 vs 122,800 token figure in the advanced-tool-use post is unreconciled.
- Not retrieved: the Claude Code internal tool schemas (Edit/MultiEdit/TodoWrite/Task are closed source), the full "Permission required" table, the current computer-use tool version string, and the web fetch/web search type strings.
- Whether Claude is trained on Claude Code's exact toolset has no primary source; the str_replace recommendation for Claude is inferred.
- The `memory_20250818` beta-header requirement conflicts: the primary docs say none, a third-party source says `context-management-2025-06-27`.
- Claude's specific MCP 2026-07-28 adoption details were not read (title only).

**Cross-vendor**
- No comparison of BM25 vs regex vs embedding tool-search accuracy was found.
- No provider-neutral "max tools before degradation" number exists for GPT-5.x or DeepSeek; 30–50 is Claude's.
- No head-to-head 2026 benchmark of edit formats (apply_patch vs str_replace vs SEARCH/REPLACE) across models was found. Aider's leaderboard data was not extracted.
- The held-out Slack/Asana tool-optimization graphs give no exact percentages.

**DeepSeek**
- All DeepSeek tool-calling details come from search snippets, because api-docs.deepseek.com and huggingface.co were blocked. This covers strict-mode keyword support, the 400-on-missing-`reasoning_content` rule, the DSML syntax, the Anthropic-endpoint MCP limitation and model-name mapping, and the `deepseek-flash` model ID.
- The V3.2 per-agent task counts are recalled, not verified. The V4 parameter counts and SWE-bench figures conflict across sources.
- DeepSeek Harness (v0.1, ~Aug 2026) tool set and edit format: no public information in the research notes beyond a README pointing to AGENTS.md.

**Protocols**
- The A2A v1.0 exact GA date conflicts (March 2026 GA vs "RC"; Mar–Apr per other sources), and its AAIF membership is reported via search summary only. The official a2a-protocol.org spec text was not fetched.
- The agentskills.io spec text and the ACP spec (agentclientprotocol.com) were not fetched. Skill-adoption counts (~40–44 clients, 22% invalid) are secondary.
- AGENTS.md's nested-precedence rule in the spec itself ("closest file wins") was not verified; only Codex's implementation was.
- Pending MCP SEPs (#1913, #1984, #1561, #1560, #1487) may change annotation semantics, and no client filtered by annotations as of Mar 2026.
- MCP poisoning prevalence (5.5%) and unrestricted network access (33%) trace to an unnamed arXiv analysis via a secondary citation and are unverified.

**Other**
- Kimi K2 tool counts (~3,000 real MCP / ~20,000 synthetic) are unconfirmed.
- Breunig's 46-vs-19-tools Llama result is secondary.
- The think-tool deprecation in favour of native interleaved thinking is a secondary claim.

## 6. Execution environment and sandboxing

> **SOTA in one paragraph:** The state of the art is to sandbox the agent's whole process tree at the OS level and to send all egress through a proxy that enforces a domain allowlist, because filesystem and network isolation are both required and either alone can be bypassed through the other. Locally, that means Seatbelt (`sandbox-exec`) on macOS, bubblewrap plus seccomp on Linux (Codex moved its Linux default from Landlock to bubblewrap and keeps Landlock only as legacy), and a dedicated sandbox user or restricted token with WFP egress filters on Windows, with Anthropic's Apache-2.0 `sandbox-runtime` (`srt`) and Codex's sandbox crates as the reusable open implementations. In the cloud, every session gets its own disposable VM or container (Firecracker microVMs for untrusted code, gVisor for lighter isolation, plain Docker in many research and CI setups) with no long-lived credentials inside; a proxy outside the sandbox injects the real credential only after validating the operation. Anthropic's Managed Agents (Apr 8, 2026) split session, harness and sandbox into independently replaceable interfaces and provision sandboxes lazily, cutting p50 time-to-first-token by about 60% and p95 by more than 90%. Parallel writers get their own git worktree or container. Anthropic also measured an 84% drop in permission prompts once in-boundary actions could be auto-allowed, so the boundary pays for itself in UX as well as security.

### 6.1 Where the field is (Nov 2026)

**Consensus**

- **Sandbox the shell, not each tool.** Every leading coding harness converged on bash plus a filesystem as the universal tool ("give your agents a computer", [Claude Agent SDK post, Sep 29, 2025](https://claude.com/blog/building-agents-with-the-claude-agent-sdk)). That gives a single choke-point: one OS sandbox around the shell covers every subprocess the agent can spawn, so the security model is "sandbox the shell" rather than "secure each tool" (inference in the tools notes).
- **Both layers are mandatory.** Anthropic: "Both layers are required". Without network isolation, a compromised agent can exfiltrate SSH keys. Without filesystem isolation, it can escape the sandbox and regain network access — [Anthropic, Claude Code sandboxing, Oct 20, 2025](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/claude-code-sandboxing).
- **The threat model is prompt injection, not a malicious user.** The goal is that "a successful prompt injection is fully isolated" and the agent "can't steal your SSH keys, or phone home" — [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/claude-code-sandboxing).
- **OS mechanisms by platform** (convergent across Codex and `srt`):
  - macOS: Seatbelt via `/usr/bin/sandbox-exec` with generated profiles.
  - Linux: bubblewrap (`bwrap`) for filesystem and namespace isolation, plus seccomp for syscall filtering. In `srt` the network namespace is removed entirely and traffic goes through host proxies on bind-mounted Unix sockets.
  - Windows: a dedicated sandbox user or restricted token, plus a WFP (Windows Filtering Platform) egress filter (`srt` alpha). Codex ships an elevated Windows sandbox with split filesystem policies.
- **Egress through a proxy with a domain allowlist and deny-by-default.** Both `srt` and `codex-network-proxy` run HTTP and SOCKS5 proxies outside the sandbox. Codex additionally blocks private/LAN destinations even when an allowlisted hostname resolves to them.
- **Cloud: per-session disposable VMs or containers, with secrets outside.** Claude Code on the web runs each session in an isolated cloud sandbox. Git credentials and signing keys never enter it; a custom git proxy validates operations and attaches the real token — [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/claude-code-sandboxing).
- **Sandboxes are cattle, not pets.** Managed Agents decouples session, harness and sandbox. A dead sandbox becomes a tool-call error the model can retry, and containers are provisioned lazily — [Anthropic, Scaling Managed Agents, Apr 8, 2026](https://anthropic.com/engineering/managed-agents).
- **Sandboxing is the UX enabler for permissions.** "Sandboxing safely reduces permission prompts by 84%" in Anthropic's internal usage, because in-boundary actions can be auto-allowed and only boundary crossings need a prompt — [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/claude-code-sandboxing). The permission side is in §7.
- **Parallel writers are isolated by git worktree or container.** Claude Code subagents support `isolation: worktree` (a temporary git worktree). Anthropic's C-compiler swarm gave each agent its own Docker container cloned from a bare "upstream" repo. Codex and OpenCode both ship worktree modules — [Claude Code subagents docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents); [Anthropic C compiler](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/building-c-compiler).
