### 9.7 Build checklist for our harness

1. **Adopt the vocabulary and data model.** Store `task`, `trial`, `grader`, `transcript` and `outcome` as first-class records. A trial's record must include harness version, git SHA of prompts and tools, model, effort/thinking setting, benchmark/suite version, seed or run index, sandbox image digest, and grader versions.
2. **Use a Harbor-compatible task format** (container image, instruction, verifier script, reference solution) so the same artifact serves CI evals, public-benchmark comparisons and later RL. Harbor's exact file names were not captured in the notes, so the layout below is illustrative.

   ```text
   tasks/fix-timezone-parse-001/
     task.yaml            # metadata + graders (below)
     instruction.md       # what the agent sees
     environment/         # Dockerfile or image ref; pinned digest
     tests/               # hidden from the agent; mounted read-only at grade time
     solution/            # reference solution (proves solvability)
   ```

   ```yaml
   # Illustrative. Grader kinds and tracked metrics follow the Anthropic coding-agent example
   # (unit tests, llm_rubric, static analysis, state_check, tool_calls; turns/tool calls/tokens/latency).
   id: fix-timezone-parse-001
   origin: support-queue#4821        # real failure (bug tracker / support queue / pre-release check)
   suite: capability                 # capability | regression  (graduates at ~100%)
   polarity: positive                # keep positive and negative cases balanced
   isolation:
     fresh_sandbox_per_trial: true   # no git history, memory, caches from other trials
     tests_visible_to_agent: false
     tests_writable_by_agent: false
   graders:
     - kind: unit_tests              # deterministic first
       fail_to_pass: [tests/test_tz.py::test_dst_boundary]
       pass_to_pass: [tests/]
     - kind: static_analysis
       tools: [ruff, mypy, bandit]
     - kind: state_check             # verify outcome, not what the agent said
       check: "git diff --stat touches only src/tz/*"
     - kind: tool_calls
       forbid: ["rm -rf", "edit tests/"]
     - kind: llm_rubric              # one isolated judge per dimension, with UNKNOWN
       dimension: code_quality
       rubric: rubrics/code_quality.md
   scoring: binary                   # binary (release gate) | weighted (threshold) | hybrid
   partial_credit_reported: true     # always report strict alongside
   trials: 5
   metrics: [turns, tool_calls, input_tokens, cache_read_tokens, output_tokens, cost_usd, wall_clock_s]
   ```

   Conversational variant, with field values taken from Anthropic's examples:

   ```yaml
   id: refund-policy-007
   user_simulator: {model: <pinned>, persona: "frustrated, has order id", settings: <pinned>}
   graders:
     - kind: state_check     # refund row exists with correct order id
     - kind: transcript
       max_turns: 10
     - kind: tool_calls
       refund: {amount: "<=100"}
     - kind: llm_rubric
       dimension: tone_and_grounding
   report: [pass@1_mean, pass^k]   # k = 3-8 for customer-facing agents
   ```
3. **Seed with 20-50 tasks from real failures.**
   - Source them from manual pre-release checks, bug trackers and support queues.
   - Write a reference solution for each, and apply the two-experts-would-agree test.
   - Balance positive and negative cases, e.g. a tool that should fire vs one that should not.
   - Let non-engineers contribute tasks as PRs.
   - Treat any task at 0% pass@100 as broken until proven otherwise.
4. **Isolate every trial.**
   - Fresh container per trial: no git history from earlier trials, no shared memory or cache directories, independent resource limits.
   - Pool pre-warmed sandboxes for throughput. Recycle a sandbox only with a verified reset.
5. **Grade outcomes deterministically first.**
   - Use state checks and tests run from *outside* the agent's sandbox.
   - Hide tests and make them read-only.
   - Detect `sys.exit(0)`-style hacks.
   - Make graders tolerant of legitimate format variation, e.g. numeric tolerance (avoid the CORE-Bench "96.12" vs "96.124991…" bug).
6. **Add LLM-judge rubrics only for what code cannot check.**
   - Default: one isolated judge per dimension, with an "Unknown" option, outputting 0.0-1.0 plus pass/fail and quoted evidence.
   - Pin the judge model and prompt version.
   - Calibrate on a human-labelled sample before relying on a judge. Track judge-human agreement against human-human agreement; GDPval's 66% vs 71% is the reference gap for open-ended work.
   - Re-calibrate whenever the judge model changes.
   - A/B the alternative (one call scoring all dimensions, which Anthropic's research system found most consistent) on your own labels.
7. **Run enough trials.**
   - Default: 5 trials per task for capability and public suites, matching TB2.
   - Minimum: 3 trials for PR-level regression.
   - Report the mean pass@1 ± SE, and state whether the SE is across runs or across tasks.
   - Never base a decision on a single run; the noise band is 2.2-6.0 points.
   - On an ~89-task suite, treat deltas under ~5 points as noise unless you add repeats or tasks.
8. **Report the right reliability metric.**
   - For user-facing or transactional agents, report pass^k with k = 3-8 next to pass@1.
   - Use pass@k only where a verifier or human picks from several attempts, and label it as such.
   - Never compare pass@k or parallel-compute numbers against pass@1.
9. **Make efficiency first-class.**
   - Per trial, record turns, tool calls, input, cache-read, cache-write and output tokens, cost, wall-clock time, tool errors by tool, and compaction events.
   - Gate on cost per successful task and on p50/p95 latency as well as pass rate.
   - When comparing multi-agent or "heavy" modes, compare at matched token budgets.
10. **Split the suites into tiers** (evals-notes stack):
    - **Tier 0:** per-tool unit evals for schema adherence, error messages and token budget (the response cap; Claude Code's default is 25,000 tokens).
    - **Tier 1:** a ~50-task capability suite, run nightly and before releases.
    - **Tier 2:** a regression suite of graduated tasks, run on every PR and every model, effort or harness bump.
    - **Tier 3:** public suites for periodic external calibration: TB 2.1 via Harbor (5 runs), SWE-bench Pro (noting the broken-task dispute), tau2 airline/retail with pass^k. Keep SWE-bench Verified and tau2 telecom as smoke tests only.
    - **Tier 4:** online trace grading on sampled production traffic. Plumbing is in sections 10–11.
11. **Run the harness A/B protocol for every harness change.**
    - Hold model, effort and suite version fixed. Run baseline and candidate on the same tasks with the same trial count.
    - Always include the mini-swe-agent-style control and the vendor-native profile: `apply_patch` + shell for OpenAI Codex-family models; Claude Code-style read/edit/bash for Claude.
    - Accept a change only if it improves the capability suite, does not regress the regression suite, and stays inside cost and latency budgets.
12. **Ablate per model.** On every model upgrade, re-run the capability suite with each scaffold flag off in turn: todo tool, think tool, sprints/resets, planner, evaluator gate, compaction thresholds. Remove the components that are no longer load-bearing.
13. **Review transcripts weekly.**
    - Sample passes as well as failures and confirm that "failures should seem fair".
    - Cluster failures. MAST's specification / inter-agent / verification split is a starting taxonomy for multi-agent runs.
    - Convert each new failure class into a task.
14. **Run grader QA as a standing job.**
    - Audit a sample of failed trials every cycle for task or grader defects.
    - Track the broken-task rate. Public suites show 30-60% among audited failures.
    - Re-verify tasks with multiple reviewers, following TB2's specificity/solvability/integrity protocol.
    - Consider adversarially strengthening tests (SWE-ABS).
15. **Monitor saturation.**
    - Graduate tasks at ~100% into regression.
    - Retire saturated capability evals and replace them with harder tasks drawn from fresh failures.
    - Do the same for safety evals: Anthropic retired an injection eval that saturated at 0% ASR.
16. **Guard against contamination and overfitting.**
    - Keep a held-out split that no optimizer has seen, whether that is GEPA/ACE-style prompt evolution, Claude Code tool refactoring or DGM-style code edits.
    - Rotate it periodically.
    - Check public-benchmark tasks for gold-patch reproduction.
17. **Pin reporting conditions** in every report:
    - harness version and model;
    - effort (note Opus 5.5 defaults to `medium`);
    - benchmark version;
    - runs and SE;
    - partial vs strict;
    - fallback counting;
    - safeguards on or off;
    - user simulator and judge models.

    ```yaml
    # eval report header (one per run set)
    suite: capability-v14            # task-set hash
    harness: our-harness@1.8.2 (prompts sha 3f2a..., tools sha 9b1c...)
    model: <id>   effort: high   thinking: adaptive
    trials_per_task: 5   tasks: 52
    pass@1: 0.61 ± 0.03 (SE across tasks)   pass^3: 0.38   strict: 0.55   partial: 0.68
    fallback_assisted_counted_as: failure
    judge: <model>@<prompt v7>  judge_human_agreement: 0.68 (n=120)
    cost_per_success_usd: 1.42   p50_wall_s: 212   p95_wall_s: 640   cache_read_share: 0.87
    baseline: mini-control@same-model  delta_vs_baseline: +7.9
    ```
    (The values are placeholders that show the format, not results.)
18. **Evaluate the safety layers separately.** For permission classifiers and injection defenses:
    - Report FPR on real traffic and FNR on *real* failure cases, separately from synthetic ones.
    - Measure ASR against an adaptive attacker with a fixed attempt budget (e.g., 100 per environment).
19. **Pick a framework quickly.** Braintrust, LangSmith, Langfuse, Phoenix or Harbor's runner are all acceptable. Spend the effort on tasks and graders.

### 9.8 Pitfalls and anti-patterns

- **Reading a leaderboard number as a model property.** Scores are scaffold-conditional point estimates: GAIA, the up to 0.267 swing from a tau-bench scaffold flag, the +20.5% AgencyBench harness effect. Without harness, effort, runs and scoring rule, the number cannot be interpreted.
- **Comparing standardized-scaffold scores with vendor-reported ones.** On SWE-bench Pro, Scale's top standardized score is ~61% and vendor-reported scores reach ~90%. Different models lead each board.
- **Mixing benchmark versions:** TB 2.0 vs 2.1 vs a reported 4.0, or SWE-bench Pro vs Fireworks' "V2" (Opus 5 at 99.38%). TB 2.1 exists because 2.0 needed environment and instruction fixes.
- **Headlining partial credit.** OSWorld 2.0 is 81.8% with partial credit and 48.7% strict.
- **Ignoring fallback-assisted counting.** TB 4.0 on Vals.ai is 65.15% vs 53.54% depending on the rule.
- **Not pinning effort.** Opus 5.5's API default is `"medium"` and other effort-capable models default to `"high"`. Anthropic's TB 4.0 figure was run at xhigh. Changing thinking mode or budget mid-run also invalidates prompt-cache breakpoints, which changes eval cost and latency.
- **Single-run decisions.** Given a 2.2-6.0-point noise band, and LangChain's 44.9% vs 40.4% on one TB2 configuration, single-run deltas below ~5 points are not evidence.
- **Unreported ± semantics.** The notes do not say whether the published ± values (±0.76, ±2.1, ±2.6) are computed across runs or across tasks. State yours.
- **Trusting failures without audits.** Graders fail too: CORE-Bench 42% vs 95%, 59.4% of audited SWE-bench Verified failures flawed, ~30% of SWE-bench Pro reportedly broken.
- **Brittle exact-match graders.** "96.12" rejected against "96.124991…". Over-penalizing format punishes correct answers.
- **Rigid step-by-step trajectory grading.** Anthropic calls it "overly brittle". Grade the outcome and constrain the path only where policy requires it.
- **Grading what the agent *said* instead of the state it produced.** Check whether the reservation exists in the DB, not whether the agent claimed to book it.
- **Non-isolated trials.** Claude read git history left by previous trials. Shared memory or resource limits make trials non-independent and inflate pass rates.
- **Hackable graders:** tests visible or writable by the agent, or exit-code-only checks. In RL these produce emergent misalignment, not just bad scores.
- **Uncalibrated or self-assessing judges.** Generators rate their own work leniently, and even a separate evaluator "talked itself out of real issues" before tuning. Judges also depend on prompt and backbone ("Anatomy of Agentic Memory").
- **Unpinned simulator and judge configuration** for conversational evals. tau2 results depend on the simulator tier and the judge model.
- **Merging capability and regression suites** into one pass rate, which hides both progress and regressions.
- **Keeping a saturated eval as a capability signal.** "An eval at 100% tracks regressions but provides no signal for improvement." The same holds for SWE-bench Verified at ~97% and tau2 telecom at ~99%.
- **Contamination blindness.** Public repos and gold patches leak into training: every frontier model OpenAI tested could reproduce some SWE-bench Verified gold patches. Any suite an optimizer iterated on has the same problem.
- **Optimizing against the test set.** Tool or prompt refactors that Claude Code (or GEPA/ACE) made using transcripts from the same tasks used for acceptance. Use a held-out split.
- **Evaluating a model outside its native tool format** and blaming the model. Codex models are trained on `apply_patch`, and DeepSeek V3.2 loses its reasoning in harnesses that pass tool results as user messages (it names Terminus and Roo Code).
- **Ignoring cost and tokens.** Token usage explains ~80% of BrowseComp variance, and multi-agent uses ~15x chat tokens. A pass-rate gain bought with tokens has to be reported with its cost.
- **Over-reading conversational-memory benchmark scores.** LoCoMo and LongMemEval near 90%+ are poorly predictive of agentic usefulness, and Supermemory's "97%" is Recall@20, not QA accuracy.
- **Hard-coding scaffolds without per-model ablation.** Components such as sprints, context resets and todo tools went from load-bearing to dead weight within one model generation.
- **Over-trusting hub environment counts** (e.g., 2,500+ environments). Counts say nothing about verifier robustness.
- **Over-trusting time horizons beyond the suite's range.** METR says horizons above 16 hours are unreliable with its current task suite.
- **Reporting the stage-1 or synthetic-only safety number.** Anthropic's auto-mode FNR on real overeager actions was 17% for the full pipeline, against 5.7% on synthetic exfiltration.

No controlled, peer-reviewed 2025-2026 study isolating harness effects across many models was found, and the Preprints.org agent-harness survey was not read.

The only same-model pair on Pro in the notes is Opus 4.5 at 45.9% vs 55.4% (secondary).
- **Self-improvement loops:** no 2026 production case study quantifies GEPA or ACE gains in deployed commercial agents. There is no data on how DGM-evolved harnesses transfer across model versions.

## 10. Observability and production operations

> **SOTA in one paragraph:** In November 2026 a production agent harness records every run as an OpenTelemetry GenAI span tree (an `invoke_agent` root, one `chat` span per model call, one `execute_tool` span per tool call) carrying token, cache, cost and error attributes, exports it to an OTel-native backend (Langfuse, Arize Phoenix, Braintrust, LangSmith), and captures message content only on opt-in. The headline KPI is prompt-cache hit rate, tracked with cost per successful task, tool error rate and p50/p95 wall-clock, because agent input outnumbers output about 100:1 and a cached read costs 0.1× base input on most Claude models (0.05× on Opus/Sonnet 5.5, 0.025× on Fable/Mythos 5.1). Long runs execute as durable workflows (Temporal, whose OpenAI Agents SDK integration went GA on 2026-03-23, or Restate, Inngest, DBOS) or behind an append-only session log decoupled from harness and sandbox (Anthropic Managed Agents, Apr 2026), so a crash resumes from the last event without re-billing completed model calls. Errors are split into retryable ones (429, 5xx, timeouts, dropped streams: about 4–5 retries with jittered exponential backoff) and terminal ones (auth, context overflow after failed compaction, budget or usage limits); gateway fallbacks to another model happen only after retries run out, and every side-effecting tool carries an idempotency key. Deploys shift traffic gradually ("rainbow deployments") so in-flight agents keep their prompt and tool versions. Harness architecture moves latency independently of the model: lazy sandbox provisioning cut p50 time-to-first-token (TTFT) by about 60% and p95 by more than 90%.

### 10.1 Where the field is (Nov 2026) — consensus and recent shifts, with dates

**Consensus**
- **One span model for agent traces.** The OTel GenAI semantic conventions define `invoke_agent` → `chat` (per model call) → `execute_tool`, plus `create_agent`, with token-usage attributes. They are still in *Development* status. Instrumenting against them keeps traces portable across Langfuse, Phoenix, Braintrust and LangSmith. — [OTel GenAI agent spans spec](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/gen-ai-agent-spans) (via search snippet; opentelemetry.io was not fetchable)
- **Tracing is on by default in the vendor SDKs.** The OpenAI Agents SDK traces every run server-side by default. Claude Code exports OTel metrics and events behind `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1`. Codex ships an `otel` crate in `codex-rs`. The Claude Code v2.1.317 changelog mentions OTel attributes, and Claude Code ships a built-in `telemetry` mod. — [OpenAI Agents observability](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents/integrations-observability); [Claude Code monitoring](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/monitoring-usage?m=1); [codex-rs tree](https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/main/codex-rs); [Claude Code CHANGELOG](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md); [mods/README.md](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/main/mods/README.md)
- **Prompt-cache hit rate is the top production KPI.** Manus (2025-07-18) calls KV-cache hit rate "the single most important metric for a production-stage AI agent". OpenAI's Codex loop write-up (2026-01-23) treats exact-prefix caching as a design constraint. One Anthropic-focused article reportedly calls cache misses "production incidents" (secondary, unverified). — [Manus](https://manus.im/blog/Context-Engineering-for-AI-Agents-Lessons-from-Building-Manus?hl=en-GB); [OpenAI, Unrolling the Codex agent loop](https://openai.com/index/unrolling-the-codex-agent-loop); [implicator.ai](https://www.implicator.ai/anthropic-says-cache-misses-are-production-incidents-reveals-caching-shaped-claude-code/)
- **Trace structure, not content.** Anthropic's production research agent monitored "agent decision patterns and interaction structures" without reading conversation contents. OTel treats content capture as opt-in. — [Anthropic multi-agent research system, 2025-06-13](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/multi-agent-research-system)
- **Durable, resumable execution is standard for long runs.** Each model call and each tool call is a checkpointed step. Anthropic "built systems that can resume from where the agent was when the errors occurred". — [Anthropic multi-agent research system](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/multi-agent-research-system); [Temporal blog](https://temporal.io/blog/announcing-openai-agents-sdk-integration)
- **Retry taxonomy.** Both labs split errors into retryable transient ones (about 4–5 retries with backoff) and terminal ones (context overflow after failed compaction, auth, credit or usage limits, budget exceeded). — [openai/codex turn.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/core/src/session/turn.rs); [Claude Code /goal docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal)
- **Cost is dominated by input tokens.** That makes a cache-stable prefix the biggest cost lever. Effort/thinking tuning, cheaper subagent models, batch for offline work and compaction tuning come after it.

**Recent shifts (dated)**
- **2025-06-13**: Anthropic's research-system post introduces **rainbow deployments** for agents and reports ~4× chat tokens for agents and ~15× for multi-agent. — [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/multi-agent-research-system)
- **2025-07-30**: Temporal + OpenAI Agents SDK Python integration enters public preview. **2026-03-23**: it goes GA. — [Temporal changelog](https://temporal.io/changelog/open-ai-agents-sdk-integration-pp); [Temporal blog](https://temporal.io/blog/announcing-openai-agents-sdk-integration)
- **Oct 2025**: OpenAI AgentKit adds datasets, trace grading, automated prompt optimization and third-party model support to Evals, alongside RFT for agents. — [OpenAI, Introducing AgentKit](https://openai.com/index/introducing-agentkit/)
- **Jan 2026**: ClickHouse acquires Langfuse. Langfuse stays MIT-licensed and self-hostable. — [MarkTechPost 2026-08-09](https://www.marktechpost.com/2026/08/09/top-llm-observability-and-evaluation-platforms-in-2026-langfuse-langsmith-braintrust-arize-and-more-compared/) (secondary)
- **2026-01-23**: OpenAI's "Unrolling the Codex agent loop" (Michael Bolin) describes the old prompt as an exact prefix of the new one. MCP tool lists and compaction both break that prefix. — [OpenAI](https://openai.com/index/unrolling-the-codex-agent-loop) (secondary summaries)
- **2026-04-08**: Anthropic's "Scaling Managed Agents" splits the system into Session (append-only event log), Harness and Sandbox. Lazy sandbox provisioning cuts p50 TTFT by ~60% and p95 by >90%. — [Anthropic Engineering](https://anthropic.com/engineering/managed-agents)

Separately, the Nov 2026 docs price cache reads at 0.05× base on Opus/Sonnet 5.5 and 0.025× on Fable/Mythos 5.1, against 0.1× elsewhere. — [Claude docs: Prompt caching](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching); [Mid-conversation system messages](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-system-messages)

That is a cost/quality knob, and it changes benchmark scores. — [Claude docs: Extended thinking](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/extended-thinking); [Vellum](https://www.vellum.ai/blog/claude-opus-5-5-benchmarks-explained) (secondary)

### 10.2 By lab

#### Anthropic

**Claude Code telemetry (OTel)** — [Claude Code monitoring docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/monitoring-usage?m=1); [Bindplane guide](https://docs.bindplane.com/how-to-guides/cloud-and-platform-integrations/send-claude-code-telemetry-to-bindplane); [li0nel/claude-otel](https://github.com/li0nel/claude-otel)
- Turn it on with `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1`.
- Exporters are `OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER` and `OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER`. Values are `otlp`, `console` and `prometheus`, and you can set more than one.
- Endpoint and auth go in `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` and `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS`. Headers are read **only at startup**.
- Metrics export every 60,000 ms by default.
- Metrics include `claude_code.cost.usage` and `claude_code.token.usage`. Token usage is labeled by `token.type` = `input` / `output` / `cacheRead` / `cacheCreation`.
- Events go through the logs exporter, for example `claude_code.api_request`.
- Prometheus conversion renames metrics, for example to `claude_code_cost_usage_USD_total`.
- Other event names (`tool_result`, `tool_decision`, `user_prompt`) come from the researcher's background knowledge and were **not verified** this session.

**Claude Code cost and cache surfaces** — [Claude Code: Costs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs); [Claude Code: Prompt caching](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/prompt-caching)
- `/usage` shows a "Prompt cache (main)" line: the share of input served from cache, misses, and warm/cold state. It also makes recommendations such as "Trim ~/code/api/CLAUDE.md · 49k tokens per request".
- Request layering is system prompt + tool definitions → project context (CLAUDE.md, memory, unscoped rules) → conversation.
  - Plan mode and skill loading append messages rather than editing the prefix.
  - A file edit produces an appended `system-reminder` instead of rewriting earlier reads.
  - A CLAUDE.md edit takes effect only after `/clear`, `/compact` or a restart, so that the cache survives.
- These actions bust the cache:
  - switching model (each model has its own cache)
  - changing effort, except on Opus/Sonnet/Haiku 5.5 and Fable 5.1
  - connecting or removing an MCP server
  - denying an entire tool
  - compaction
  - removing batches of old images
- TTL policy:
  - The main conversation gets 1 hour on a subscription within plan usage and 5 minutes on an API key or usage credits.
  - Subagents, compaction, forks and titles get 5 minutes.
  - Subagents start their own cache. Forks inherit the parent's prefix and read its cache.
  - Workflow fan-outs hold every agent except the first for up to 5 seconds so they read the first agent's cached prefix (`CLAUDE_CODE_WORKFLOW_PREFIX_STAGGER_MS`, default 5000). `subagentPromptCacheTtl: 1h` extends the subagent TTL at a higher write cost. — [Claude Code workflows docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows)

**Claude Agent SDK run accounting and budgets** — [agent-loop docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/agent-loop)
- `ResultMessage` carries the final text, `total_cost_usd`, `usage`, `num_turns` and `session_id`.
  - `subtype` is one of `success`, `error_max_turns`, `error_max_budget_usd`, `error_during_execution` (e.g. a cancelled request or a crash) and `error_max_structured_output_retries`.
  - `stop_reason` is `end_turn`, `max_tokens` or `refusal`, and `null` after a crash.
- `max_turns`/`maxTurns` and `max_budget_usd`/`maxBudgetUsd` both default to "No limit". The docs say "Setting a budget is a good default for production agents."
- The budget is checked *after* each model response. Spend "can therefore pass the cap by up to the cost of that one response", plus whatever running subagents spend. Subagent spend counts toward the cap.
  - Once the cap is hit, spawning a subagent fails with `Budget limit reached` and background subagents are stopped (Claude Code v2.1.217+).
- A single-shot `query()` raises after yielding an error result. A streaming-input session "stays alive". A message still queued when max-turns is hit starts a new turn and resets the turn count, but the budget keeps accumulating.
- `ClaudeAgentOptions` includes these ops-relevant fields: `fallback_model`, `effort`, `max_turns`, `max_budget_usd`, `task_budget`, `enable_file_checkpointing`, `session_store`, `fork_session`, `resume` and `include_partial_messages`. — [claude-agent-sdk-python types.py](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python/blob/main/src/claude_agent_sdk/types.py)
  - The `session_store`/`sessionStore` adapter mirrors transcripts to your own backend so stateless hosts can resume them ("dual-write"). The repo has a `session_stores/` example and a `max_budget_usd.py` example.
- Effort levels are `"low"`, `"medium"`, `"high"`, `"xhigh"` and `"max"`. Effort can be set per session or per subagent (`AgentDefinition.effort`). Opus 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 default to `"medium"`; other effort-capable models default to `"high"`. — [Extended thinking docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/extended-thinking)

**Managed Agents (2026-04-08): the decoupled ops architecture** — [Anthropic Engineering: Scaling Managed Agents](https://anthropic.com/engineering/managed-agents)
- There are three swappable interfaces:
  - **Session**: "an append-only event log".
  - **Harness**: "the loop that calls Claude and routes Claude's tool calls".
  - **Sandbox**: the execution environment.
- The API surface:
  - Tools dispatch through `execute(name, input) → string`, and sandboxes come from `provision({resources})`.
  - A crashed harness is replaced via `wake(sessionId)`, and `getSession(id)` resumes "from the last event".
  - `emitEvent(id, event)` persists events. `getEvents()` reads positional slices so the brain can "rewind".
- When a sandbox dies, the harness returns a tool-call error to Claude, "which can choose to retry". The first design kept session, harness and sandbox in one container, so one container failure lost the session. Decoupling made containers disposable ("pets vs. cattle").
- Lazy provisioning creates a container only when a tool call needs one. It cut **p50 TTFT by ~60% and p95 TTFT by >90%**.
- The session log lives outside the context window because compaction, the memory tool and trimming of old tool results or thinking "are irreversible". The harness may transform fetched events before they enter context, for example "to improve the prompt-cache hit rate".

**Multi-agent research system (2025-06-13): production reliability practice** — [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/multi-agent-research-system)
- Minor failures compound in long stateful runs. The system therefore resumes from where the error occurred instead of restarting, using regular checkpoints and retry logic. Agents are *told* when a tool is failing so they can adapt.
- Full production tracing was used to diagnose failures, without monitoring conversation contents.
- **Rainbow deployments**: traffic shifts gradually from the old version to the new one while both run, so agents in flight are not broken.
- Synchronous subagent waits are a bottleneck. The lead waits for each batch, and subagents cannot steer each other. Async execution was future work.
- Cost and quality:
  - Agents use ~4× chat tokens and multi-agent ~15×.
  - An Opus 4 lead with Sonnet 4 subagents beat single-agent Opus 4 by 90.2% on the internal research eval.
  - On BrowseComp, token usage alone explained ~80% of performance variance. Tool-call count and model choice raised that to ~95%.
  - Upgrading to Sonnet 4 gained more than doubling the token budget on Sonnet 3.7.

**Workflows and subagent ops controls (Claude Code)** — [Claude Code workflows docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows); [Agent SDK subagents](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/subagents); [Claude Code subagents](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents)
- **Deterministic replay.** `Date.now()`, `Math.random()` and `new Date()` throw inside workflow scripts, so a relaunch repeats the same `agent()` calls. Completed agents return cached results up to the first agent whose prompt differs; that agent and every later one re-run.
- **Fault handling.**
  - A stalled agent auto-restarts up to 5 times (`stallMs`, `CLAUDE_ASYNC_AGENT_STALL_TIMEOUT_MS`).
  - Inside `parallel`/`pipeline`, a failure leaves `null` and the run continues. A directly awaited failure ends the run.
  - Usage-limit hits pause and auto-resume.
  - `schema` outputs are validated with up to 5 retries (`MAX_STRUCTURED_OUTPUT_RETRIES`).
  - API errors are never delivered as a subagent's result.
- **Cost controls.**
  - A "Large workflow" warning fires above 25 agents or 1.5M projected tokens.
  - Size guideline values are `small` <5, `medium` <10 (default) and `large` <50 agents.
  - The docs advise "Run the workflow on a small slice first."
  - Harness caps are `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH` (default 3) and `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS` (default 20), plus per-agent `maxTurns`, `effort` and `model`, which routes cheap work to smaller models such as `haiku`.
- **`/goal` error policy.** — [/goal docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal)
  - Unrecoverable errors clear the goal: auth failure, exhausted credit, context overflow that auto-compaction couldn't clear, or an unavailable model.
  - Transient errors (overload, dropped connection) retry automatically, then pause after three retries.
  - Rate or usage limits pause the goal, which resumes when the limit resets.
  - While background work runs, the evaluator defers. It checks in after 30 minutes, then backs off to 1 h and then every 2 h, capped at three idle check-ins (`CLAUDE_CODE_GOAL_CHECKIN_MINUTES`).

**Checkpoints.** Claude Code checkpointing is on by default. Checkpoints are saved with the conversation and auto-cleaned after 30 days. `/rewind` (or Esc Esc) restores code and conversation, conversation only, or code only. Checkpoints are "separate from git" and cannot undo remote side effects. The SDK's file checkpointing tracks only Write/Edit/NotebookEdit changes, not Bash side effects. — [Claude Code SDK file checkpointing](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/file-checkpointing); [How Claude Code works](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/how-claude-code-works)

**Observed cost of long runs (useful for budget defaults)**
- RetroForge game maker on Opus 4.5. A solo run took 20 min, cost $9 and produced a broken app. The full planner/generator/evaluator harness took 6 hr and cost $200 (>20× the cost) and produced a playable app. — [Harness design for long-running apps](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/harness-design-long-running-apps)
- Browser DAW on Opus 4.6 took ~3 h 50 m and cost $124.70:
  - planner: 4.7 min / $0.46
  - build round 1: 2 h 7 m / $71.08
  - QA: 8.8 min / $3.24
  - build round 2: 1 h 2 m / $36.89
  - plus two more short rounds
- C compiler (2026-02-05): 16 parallel Opus 4.6 agents ran nearly 2,000 Claude Code sessions over two weeks. The API cost was just under $20,000, for ~2B input and ~140M output tokens. — [Anthropic, Building a C compiler](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/building-c-compiler)
- Anthropic also published "Quantifying infrastructure noise in agentic coding evals" (2026-02-05). Only the title was seen. — [Anthropic Engineering index](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering)

#### OpenAI

**Agents SDK tracing and run controls**
- Tracing is built in and on by default server-side. Each run records model calls, tool calls, handoffs, guardrails and custom spans, viewable in the Traces dashboard.
  - A `withTrace` helper groups several runs into one trace.
  - Trace processors export to Braintrust and other backends.
  - The code lives in `src/agents/tracing/` (spans, traces, processors, provider).
  - Sources: [OpenAI Agents integrations & observability](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents/integrations-observability); [Braintrust Agents SDK integration](https://www.braintrust.dev/docs/integrations/openai-agents-sdk); [src/agents/tracing](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/tree/main/src/agents/tracing)
- The exact tracing span types, the `handoff_input_filter`/`nest_handoff_history` details and Sessions internals were **not verified**, because openai.github.io was blocked.
- The loop internals sit in `run_internal/`: `model_retry.py`, `prompt_cache_key.py`, `session_persistence.py`, `streaming.py`, `tool_execution.py`, `approvals.py`, `guardrails.py`, and so on. — [src/agents/run_internal](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/tree/main/src/agents/run_internal)
- Run controls: [running_agents.md](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/main/docs/running_agents.md)
  - `max_turns` overflow raises `MaxTurnsExceeded`; `max_turns=None` disables the limit.
  - `error_handlers` keys `"max_turns"`, `"model_refusal"` and `"invalid_final_output"` can return fallback outputs instead of raising.
  - `tool_not_found_behavior` raises `ModelBehaviorError` by default and can be set to `"return_error_to_model"`.
  - `ToolExecutionConfig.max_function_tool_concurrency` caps concurrent function tools. `ModelSettings.timeout` and `ToolTimeoutError` handle timeouts.
  - `reasoning_item_id_policy` is `"preserve"` by default; `"omit"` mitigates Responses API 400s caused by a reasoning item missing its required following item.
- Resume and persistence: input can be a `RunState` when resuming a paused run. Sessions are `SQLiteSession`, `OpenAIConversationsSession`, or Redis. `OpenAIResponsesCompactionSession` triggers `responses.compact` when stored history grows. — [openai-agents-python](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python)

**Temporal integration (GA 2026-03-23)** — [Temporal blog](https://temporal.io/blog/announcing-openai-agents-sdk-integration); [Temporal changelog](https://temporal.io/changelog/open-ai-agents-sdk-integration-pp); [Temporal cookbook](https://docs.temporal.io/ai/cookbook/openai-agents-sdk-python); [demos repo](https://github.com/temporal-community/openai-agents-demos)
- Agents run inside a Temporal Workflow, and **every model invocation runs as an Activity**.
- You enable it with `OpenAIAgentsPlugin` on the client. `activity_as_tool` exposes Activities as durable tools.
- Traces still flow to OpenAI tracing.
- The Python version was in public preview from 2025-07-30 and went GA on 2026-03-23. A TypeScript version also exists.
- Demos cover hello world, a tools workflow, research, and multi-agent interactive research.

**Trace grading** — [OpenAI Trace grading guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/trace-grading); [OpenAI agent-evals guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agent-evals)
- Trace grading assigns structured scores or labels to an end-to-end trace (decisions, tool calls, reasoning). The dashboard flow is Logs > Traces → pick a workflow → create a grader → run.
- **Trace evals** reuse graded traces across many examples for benchmarking and regression.
- The guidance is to start with trace grading while debugging and move to dataset graders once behavior stabilizes: "Trace grading is the fastest way to identify workflow-level issues."
- The exact grader types (string_check, text_similarity, score_model, label_model, python, multi) were **not confirmed** this session.

**Codex harness ops (source code, Nov 2026)**
- Retry defaults are `DEFAULT_STREAM_MAX_RETRIES = 5`, `DEFAULT_REQUEST_MAX_RETRIES = 4` and `DEFAULT_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS = 300_000` (a 300 s idle timeout). — [model-provider-info/src/lib.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/model-provider-info/src/lib.rs)
- In `run_sampling_request`, `ContextWindowExceeded`, `UsageLimitReached`, `SessionBudgetExceeded` and `Fatal` return **without retry**. Other stream errors go through `handle_response_stream_error` with backoff. Cancellation surfaces as `CodexErr::TurnAborted`. — [turn.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/core/src/session/turn.rs)
- Codex sends `store: false` and `include: ["reasoning.encrypted_content"]`, so the API is stateless (zero data retention) and the client replays encrypted reasoning itself. `parallel_tool_calls` is passed through. — [core/src/client.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/core/src/client.rs)
- Auto-compaction triggers at `min(model_auto_compact_token_limit, context_window * 9 / 10)`, which is 90% of the window. — [protocol/src/openai_models.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/protocol/src/openai_models.rs)
- Relevant crates and modules: `otel`, `rollout`, `thread-store`, `responses-api-proxy`, and `core/src/responses_retry.rs`. — [codex-rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/main/codex-rs)
- Caching per the Codex loop post (secondary summaries):
  - The old prompt must be an exact prefix of the new one.
  - Dynamic tool lists (MCP) can break the prefix.
  - Compaction rewrites history and so invalidates the cached prefix.
  - Sources: [all-ai.de](https://www.all-ai.de/news/beitrage2026/codex-agent-loop); [danielvaughan Codex caching](https://codex.danielvaughan.com/2026/04/21/codex-cli-prompt-caching-maximise-cache-hits-cost-reduction/)
- Effort changes without breaking the cache: on GPT-6, add a `configuration_update` input item and "keep request-level `reasoning.effort` unchanged to preserve the prompt prefix for caching". Effort values are `low`, `medium` (default), `high`, `xhigh` and `max`. — [codex upgrading-to-gpt-6-astra.md](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/skills/src/assets/samples/openai-docs/references/upgrading-to-gpt-6-astra.md) (bundled docs snapshot; near-primary)
- Rate-limit-aware background work: the Codex memories pipeline runs at session start over **idle** past rollouts (`min_rollout_idle_hours`, ">12h recommended"). It is gated by `min_rate_limit_remaining_percent` and uses DB leases with retry backoff. — [codex config schema](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/core/config.schema.json)

**OpenAI prompt caching** — [OpenAI Prompt caching](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompt-caching) (via search extracts)
- Caching is automatic for prompts ≥1,024 tokens. It gives up to 90% input-cost reduction and up to 80% latency reduction. The `cached_tokens` usage field is always present.
- `prompt_cache_key` routes requests that share a prefix to the same cache. Keep each prefix+key combination under ~15 requests/minute to avoid overflow.
- `prompt_cache_retention` takes `in_memory` or `24h`, at the same price.
  - Extended retention stores KV tensors on GPU-local storage and is not ZDR-eligible.
  - Defaults reportedly vary by org and platform. Azure says `in_memory` for gpt-5.4 and older. — [Azure Foundry](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-ca/Azure/foundry/openai/how-to/prompt-caching)
- `allowed_tools` restricts the callable subset per turn without changing the `tools` list, which keeps the prefix stable (third-party description). — [OpenAI function calling (search summary)](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/function-calling)

#### DeepSeek
- **Context caching.** Disk-based caching launched on 2024-08-02, at $0.014/MTok for cache hits at that time. It is automatic. Usage reports hit and miss token counts separately, and a hit requires the prefix to already be persisted to disk. — [DeepSeek news](https://deepseek.com/en/news/context-caching/); [DeepSeek KV cache guide](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/kv_cache) (via search)
- **Later pricing (secondary).** V4 Flash costs $0.0028/MTok on a hit vs $0.14/MTok on a miss. V4 Pro costs $0.003625 on a hit vs $0.435 on a miss. — [benchlm.ai](https://www.benchlm.ai/deepseek/api-pricing). The cache granularity and the current official price list were **not verified**.
- **Routing compatibility.** An Anthropic-format endpoint (`https://api.deepseek.com/anthropic`) lets Claude Code and other Messages-API harnesses drive DeepSeek via `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`. The `anthropic-beta` and `anthropic-version` headers are ignored. The Chinese docs reportedly map `claude-opus*` → `deepseek-v4-pro`, and `claude-sonnet*`/`claude-haiku*` and unknown names → `deepseek-v4-flash`. A third-party summary says MCP tool-use blocks are unsupported. — [DeepSeek anthropic_api](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/anthropic_api) (search-summarized)
- **Serving-side cost.** DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA) lowers long-context cost at the serving layer. For self-hosted DeepSeek, that makes less aggressive compaction viable (inference in the repo notes).
- No public information in the research notes on DeepSeek observability or tracing tooling.
