**Observability platforms (2026; secondary comparison blogs)** — [MarkTechPost 2026-08-09](https://www.marktechpost.com/2026/08/09/top-llm-observability-and-evaluation-platforms-in-2026-langfuse-langsmith-braintrust-arize-and-more-compared/); [latitude.so](https://latitude.so/blog/best-ai-agent-observability-tools-2026-comparison); [laminar.sh](https://laminar.sh/article/langfuse-alternatives-2026)

| Platform | License / hosting | Distinctive capability | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Langfuse** | MIT; self-hostable | OTel-native | Acquired by ClickHouse, Jan 2026. Anthropic's eval guide names it for self-hosting. |
| **LangSmith** | Proprietary; self-host on enterprise tier only | Online evals on live traffic; automatic trace clustering of failure modes | |
| **Braintrust** | SaaS | Eval-first, CI gates, "Loop" assistant, Topics clustering (beta), `autoevals` | Has an OpenAI Agents SDK trace-processor integration |
| **Arize Phoenix / AX** | Phoenix: ELv2 source-available, free to self-host; AX is the SaaS | OTel-native | |

- Anthropic's eval guide advises: "pick a framework quickly, then invest in high-quality tasks and graders." — [Anthropic, Demystifying evals](https://anthropic.com/engineering/demystifying-evals-for-ai-agents)
- `agentevals-cli` scores existing OTel traces without re-running LLM calls and can delegate grading to the OpenAI Evals API. — [PyPI agentevals-cli](https://pypi.org/project/agentevals-cli/)
- No source in the notes describes "session replay" as a distinct platform feature.

**Durable-execution runtimes**
- **Temporal**: see OpenAI above.
- **Restate**: a lightweight durable runtime with keyed "Virtual Objects" for agent sessions, idempotency keys, and durable calls and timers.
- **Inngest**: event-driven durable steps, queues and flow control with minimal infra. Mastra has an Inngest agent integration. — [Mastra Inngest agent](https://mastra.ai/reference/agents/inngest-agent)
- **DBOS**: durable workflows stored in Postgres, with no separate orchestrator.
- **LangGraph-style checkpointers**: LangChain's `deepagents` (~30.9k stars, `deepagents==0.7.32`) is built on LangGraph for streaming, persistence and checkpointing.
- A 2026 guide recommends idempotency keys derived from `(workflow_id, step_id)` for non-idempotent tool calls.
- Sources (secondary vendor comparisons): [Diagrid, Temporal alternatives 2026](https://www.diagrid.io/infrastructure/10-best-temporal-alternatives-2026); [ZenML Inngest alternatives](https://www.zenml.io/blog/inngest-alternatives); [AppScale durable execution 2026](https://appscale.blog/en/blog/durable-execution-llm-agents-temporal-langgraph-checkpointing-2026). No primary Restate, Inngest or DBOS docs were fetched.

**Durable agent state in open harnesses**
- **OpenHands SDK.** The conversation is "an append-only event log". Condensation is recorded as `Condensation` events ("similar to tombstones in … Cassandra and Kafka"), and a `View` projects the LLM-visible context.
  - The default `LLMSummarizingCondenser` replaces the first half of events with a summary. Its settings are `max_size=240`, `keep_first=2` and an optional `max_tokens`.
  - Condensation is "soft" (resource limit; skippable) or "hard" (explicit, e.g. after a context-window error). Regular condensation is justified explicitly as keeping prompt-cache rebuild costs low.
  - A `StuckDetector` flags repetitive patterns, e.g. 4 repeats × 2 events per cycle.
  - The repo notes call it "the best open reference for durable, replayable agent state". — [condenser/README.md](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/main/openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/context/condenser/README.md); [stuck_detector.py](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/main/openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/conversation/stuck_detector.py)
- **Cline SDK.** The canonical session history is kept at full fidelity. Compaction state lives in a separate `${sessionId}.compaction.json`, which is reused on resume only after validating a hash of the canonical prefix.

**Gateways and routing**
- **LiteLLM Router** semantics: retries, then fallbacks, then cooldowns. Details are in 10.3. — [LiteLLM retries (mirror)](https://www.mintlify.com/BerriAI/litellm/features/retries); [LiteLLM routing (mirror)](https://git.kvant.cloud/phoenix/litellm-mirror/src/commit/f2991203941095109707c47265090bcfb0588965/docs/my-website/docs/routing.md); [orq.ai retries](https://docs.orq.ai/docs/proxy/retries.md)
- LiteLLM and the Vercel AI Gateway both expose `/v1/responses/compact`. — [LiteLLM](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/response_api_compact.md); [Vercel](https://vercel.com/docs/ai-gateway/sdks-and-apis/responses/compaction.md)
- Harbor uses LiteLLM for model access. — [Harbor Terminus-2 docs](https://www.harborframework.com/docs/agents/terminus-2)

**Manus** (2025-07-18) — [Manus blog](https://manus.im/blog/Context-Engineering-for-AI-Agents-Lessons-from-Building-Manus?hl=en-GB)
- Input:output is ~100:1, and a typical task makes ~50 tool calls.
- Cached versus uncached input is ~10× cheaper: $0.30 vs $3/MTok on Claude Sonnet.
- Cache-breakers are timestamps at the start of the system prompt, non-deterministic serialization, and adding or removing tools mid-session. Manus masks logits instead of removing tools.

**Sandboxes (latency and cost)**
- Reported cold starts: E2B ~150 ms (Firecracker microVM, pause/fork/snapshot); Daytona "sub-90ms" by the vendor's figure vs 200–500 ms by a third party; Modal ~100 ms–3 s (gVisor, GPU, 24 h cap). — [Northflank](https://northflank.com/blog/daytona-vs-e2b-ai-code-execution-sandboxes) (secondary/vendor; numbers vary widely)
- The 2026 lab pattern is "one sandbox per rollout" on pooled lightweight CPU sandboxes. Fresh-per-attempt sandboxes hit creation-rate limits at scale. The alternative is recycling: reset one sandbox between runs on the same image. — [HF blog, One sandbox per rollout](https://huggingface.co/blog/sergiopaniego/rl-environments-2026); [fly.io RL sandbox pricing](https://fly.io/learn/rl-sandbox-pricing/); [k8s agent-sandbox RL](https://agent-sandbox.sigs.k8s.io/docs/use-cases/examples/agent-sandbox-rl/)

**Kimi K2.5 "critical steps" latency metric.** Latency is measured as the longest dependent chain, not total steps, so spawning sub-agents helps only if it shortens the critical path. Moonshot reports up to 4.5× less execution time vs a single agent and 80% lower end-to-end runtime in internal evals. — [Kimi K2.5 blog (via search snippet)](https://kimi.com/en/blog/kimi-k2-5) (secondary)

**MCP 2026-07-28 ops-relevant changes** — [MCP changelog](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/blob/main/docs/specification/2026-07-28/changelog.mdx)
- OTel `traceparent`/`tracestate`/`baggage` travel in `_meta` (SEP-414).
- `CacheableResult` carries a required `ttlMs` and a `cacheScope` (`public`/`private`) on list/read results (SEP-2549).
- Servers SHOULD return `tools/list` in deterministic order "to enable client-side caching and improve LLM prompt cache hit rates".
- Logging is deprecated in favor of stderr/OTel (SEP-2577).
- Long-running tools should use the `io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks` extension (poll with `tasks/get`) rather than holding streams open.
- `ToolAnnotations` defaults: `readOnlyHint` false, `destructiveHint` true, `idempotentHint` false, `openWorldHint` true. These are hints, untrusted unless the server is trusted.

### 10.3 Techniques and patterns

**OTel GenAI span tree instrumentation (what to log)**
- **What it is:** each agent run is emitted as a standard span hierarchy so that any OTel backend can render, query and grade it.
- **Mechanics:**
  - The root span has `gen_ai.operation.name` = `invoke_agent`. Its span name is `invoke_agent {gen_ai.agent.name}` when the name is known, else `invoke_agent`.
  - Span kind is CLIENT; INTERNAL is allowed for in-process agents.
  - `create_agent` marks agent creation. `execute_tool` marks tool execution.
  - Each loop step has `chat` and `execute_tool` children under the agent span. Tool spans carry the tool name, call ID, arguments, result and error status.
  - Add custom spans for harness events the spec does not cover: compaction, subagent spawn, approval waits.
  - Attribute names below that are not the spec's (`harness.*`) are recommendations from the notes, not spec names. The spec's exact cache-token attribute names (e.g. `gen_ai.usage.cache_read.input_tokens`) and its current release number are **unverified**.
- **Evidence:** spec via search snippet ([OTel GenAI agent spans](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/gen-ai-agent-spans)); [DEV Community guide, 2026](https://dev.to/gabrielanhaia/opentelemetry-genai-semantic-conventions-your-llm-traces-should-look-like-this-in-2026-3ff6); [Morph agent tracing](https://www.morphllm.com/agent-tracing). Conventions are still "Development". For the version conflict (v1.42.0 move on 2026-06-12 vs v1.41.0), see 10.1.
- **When to use:** always. Instrument against the spec rather than one vendor's SDK so traces stay portable across Langfuse, Phoenix, Braintrust and LangSmith. **When not:** do not pin attribute names to a single release while the spec is in Development. Keep a mapping layer.

```yaml
 # Minimum span schema for the harness (from the research notes' recommended schema)
invoke_agent:                       # root, one per run; span kind CLIENT (INTERNAL if in-process)
  gen_ai.operation.name: invoke_agent
  gen_ai.agent.name / gen_ai.agent.id
  gen_ai.conversation.id
  harness.version                   # harness build
  harness.model / harness.effort    # model and effort/thinking setting
  harness.prompts_tools_sha         # git SHA of system prompt + tool definitions
  harness.termination               # e.g. success / error_max_turns / error_max_budget_usd (SDK ResultMessage.subtype)
  harness.total_cost_usd / harness.num_turns
  children:
    chat:                           # one per model call
      tokens: input, output, cache_read, cache_write   # map to spec usage attrs (names unverified)
      ttft_ms, latency_ms
      stop_reason, request_id
      retry_count
      fallback_from                 # set when a gateway fallback served this call (expected cache rebuild)
      cost_usd
    execute_tool:                   # one per tool call
      tool.name, tool.call_id
      args_hash                     # hash, not raw args, unless content capture is opted in
      result_tokens, truncated       # result size in tokens; truncated flag
      error_class
      duration_ms
      idempotency_key
      sandbox_id
    custom:                         # harness-specific
      compaction                    # tokens before/after, expected cache rebuild
      subagent_spawn                # link child invoke_agent to parent tool call
      approval_wait                 # human/classifier decision latency
```

**Structure-only production tracing (content opt-in)**
- **What it is:** trace the shape of agent behavior (which tools ran, in what order, with what errors and timings) without storing user content by default.
- **Mechanics:**
  - Content capture is off by default and enabled per environment or tenant, or redacted. OTel treats message content as opt-in.
  - Hash arguments rather than storing them.
  - Anthropic monitored "agent decision patterns and interaction structures" without reading conversations.
- **Evidence:** this let Anthropic diagnose production research-agent failures while preserving privacy. — [Anthropic, 2025-06-13](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/multi-agent-research-system)
- **When to use:** any multi-tenant or regulated product. **When not:** offline eval runs and internal dogfooding, where full transcripts are needed for weekly transcript reading and grader QA.

**Cache-hit rate as a first-class KPI, with expected vs unexpected misses**
- **What it is:** treat prompt-cache hit rate as the top cost and latency metric.
- **Mechanics:**
  - Compute hit rate = cacheRead / total input. On Anthropic, total input = `cache_read_input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens + input_tokens`, and `input_tokens` counts only tokens after the last breakpoint. On OpenAI, read `cached_tokens`. On DeepSeek, read the separate hit/miss counts. In Claude Code telemetry, use the `token.type` = `cacheRead`/`cacheCreation` labels.
  - Log cache-write tokens and "expected rebuilds" (compaction, tool-result clearing, model or effort switch) separately from unexpected misses. Treat unexpected misses as regressions.
- **Evidence:** Manus calls it "the single most important metric". Average input:output is ~100:1, and cached input is ~10× cheaper ($0.30 vs $3/MTok on Sonnet). — [Manus](https://manus.im/blog/Context-Engineering-for-AI-Agents-Lessons-from-Building-Manus?hl=en-GB). Claude Code's `/usage` exposes the "Prompt cache (main)" share and misses. — [Claude Code: Costs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs). The notes found no independent measurement of real-world agent cache-hit rates across providers.
- **When to use:** always. Target >80–90% cache-read share of input tokens (an inference in the notes). **When not:** prompts below the minimum cacheable length (512–4,096 tokens on Anthropic depending on model; ≥1,024 on OpenAI), which silently never cache.

**Derived ops dashboards**
- **What it is:** a fixed set of derived metrics computed from spans.
- **Mechanics:**
  - cache hit rate (cacheRead / total input)
  - cost per *successful* task, not per run
  - tool error rate by tool
  - turns per task
  - p50/p95 wall-clock
  - compaction frequency
  - pass rate from online trace graders
  - Optional: a "critical steps" metric (the longest dependent chain) to judge whether a fan-out reduced latency.
- **Evidence:** this is the dashboard set recommended in the notes. Anthropic's eval YAML tracks turns, tool calls, tokens and latency, and Anthropic's tool evals collect accuracy, tool and task runtime, number of tool calls, token consumption and tool errors. — [Demystifying evals](https://anthropic.com/engineering/demystifying-evals-for-ai-agents); [Writing tools for agents](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/writing-tools-for-agents). Kimi's "critical steps" metric — [Kimi K2.5 (secondary)](https://kimi.com/en/blog/kimi-k2-5).
- **When to use:** from the first production deploy.

**Online trace grading and failure clustering (Tier 4 evals)**
- **What it is:** run graders on sampled production traces and cluster the failures.
- **Mechanics:**
  - OpenAI: Logs > Traces → pick a workflow → create a grader → run. Then promote graded traces into "trace evals".
  - LangSmith offers online evals on live traffic and automatic failure-mode clustering. Braintrust has Topics clustering (beta).
  - `agentevals-cli` grades existing OTel traces offline without re-running LLM calls.
- **Evidence:** "Trace grading is the fastest way to identify workflow-level issues." — [OpenAI agent-evals guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agent-evals)
- **When to use:** once production traffic exists. Move to dataset graders once behavior stabilizes. **When not:** as a replacement for deterministic outcome graders in CI.

**Durable execution: workflow plus activities**
- **What it is:** each agent session is a durable workflow keyed by session id. Every LLM call and every side-effecting tool call is an activity whose result is persisted, so replay never re-bills or re-executes completed steps.
- **Mechanics (Temporal + OpenAI Agents SDK):**
  - Register `OpenAIAgentsPlugin` on the Temporal client. The agent then runs inside a Workflow, and each model invocation becomes an Activity.
  - Wrap side-effecting tools with `activity_as_tool` so they get Temporal retries and durability.
  - Human approvals become durable signals and timers.
  - Traces still flow to OpenAI tracing.
- **Alternatives:** Restate (keyed Virtual Objects per session, idempotency keys, durable calls and timers), Inngest (event-driven durable steps, queues, flow control; Mastra integration), DBOS (Postgres-stored workflows, no orchestrator), LangGraph checkpointers.
- **Evidence:** Temporal GA 2026-03-23 ([Temporal](https://temporal.io/blog/announcing-openai-agents-sdk-integration)). Anthropic: errors compound in long stateful runs, so the system resumes from the failure point ([Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/multi-agent-research-system)).
- **When to use:** runs that last minutes to hours, involve human approvals, or perform side effects. **When not:** short single-turn requests, where a plain retry is cheaper than a workflow engine.

```python
 # Schematic only: names from the notes (OpenAIAgentsPlugin, activity_as_tool);
 # exact Temporal signatures were not verified in the research notes.
 #
 # client = TemporalClient(..., plugins=[OpenAIAgentsPlugin()])   # every model call -> Activity
 #
 # @workflow  (key = session_id)
 # def agent_session(session_id, task):
 #     agent = Agent(tools=[activity_as_tool(write_file), activity_as_tool(open_pr),
 #                          read_only_search])             # read-only tools: retry-safe
 #     approval = await workflow.wait_for_signal("approve")  # durable HITL
 #     return await Runner.run(agent, task)                   # replay never re-bills completed calls
```

**Append-only session log, decoupled from the context window**
- **What it is:** keep a durable, append-only event log that is the source of truth. The context window is a projection of it.
- **Mechanics:**
  - Managed Agents: `emitEvent(id, event)`, `getEvents()` for positional slices, `wake(sessionId)` + `getSession(id)` to resume "from the last event". A dead sandbox comes back to the model as a tool error.
  - OpenHands: `Condensation` tombstone events plus a `View` projection.
  - Cline: a full-fidelity canonical transcript plus a hash-validated `${sessionId}.compaction.json`.
  - Claude Code: JSONL under `~/.claude/projects/`, with `--continue`/`--resume`/`--fork-session`.
- **Evidence:** p50 TTFT −~60%, p95 −>90% from lazy provisioning once the pieces were decoupled. A container failure no longer loses the session. — [Managed Agents](https://anthropic.com/engineering/managed-agents)
- **When to use:** always. This is what makes crash-resume, rewind, fork and non-destructive compaction possible. **When not:** n/a. Even simple harnesses should persist the log.

**Deterministic replay for orchestration scripts**
- **What it is:** orchestration code that is a pure function of its inputs, so a relaunch replays and returns cached results.
- **Mechanics:** ban non-determinism (`Date.now()`, `Math.random()` and `new Date()` throw in Claude Code workflow scripts). Cache each `agent()` result keyed by its prompt. On relaunch, return cached results until the first agent whose prompt differs, then re-run that agent and everything after it.
- **Evidence:** Claude Code workflows. — [docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows). The multi-agent notes add "idempotent agent calls keyed by prompt hash for replay" as a recommendation.
- **When to use:** any fan-out or pipeline of agent calls. **When not:** steps that legitimately need fresh time or randomness. Inject those as recorded inputs.

**Checkpoint / resume and rewind**
- **What it is:** snapshot files and conversation so the run can resume or rewind.
- **Mechanics:**
  - Claude Code checkpoints are on by default, kept 30 days, and restored with `/rewind` or Esc Esc (code+conversation, conversation only, or code only).
  - The SDK has `enable_file_checkpointing`, `resume` and `fork_session`, plus `session_store` dual-write to your backend.
  - OpenAI Agents SDK resumes from `RunState`.
- **Evidence:** SDK file checkpointing tracks only Write/Edit/NotebookEdit, **not Bash side effects**. Pair it with git-stash or worktree snapshots. — [file checkpointing](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/file-checkpointing)
- **When to use:** local and interactive agents. **When not:** as a guarantee for remote side effects. Checkpoints cannot undo those, so use idempotency keys and compensations instead.

**Idempotency keys for side-effecting tools**
- **What it is:** a deterministic key per tool invocation so that retries and replays do not duplicate side effects.
- **Mechanics:**
  - Derive the key from `(workflow_id, step_id)` or `hash(session_id, step_idx, tool_call_id)`.
  - Mark read-only tools retry-safe. Do not trust MCP `idempotentHint` (default false) from untrusted servers.
  - Log the key on the `execute_tool` span.
  - For Agent RFT-style backends, a unique rollout ID attached to each tool call plays the same correlating role.
- **Evidence:** a 2026 durable-execution guide ([AppScale](https://appscale.blog/en/blog/durable-execution-llm-agents-temporal-langgraph-checkpointing-2026), secondary). Restate ships idempotency keys natively (secondary). Anthropic's PTC guidance: "prefer idempotent, parallel-safe tools". — [Anthropic advanced tool use](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/advanced-tool-use)
- **When to use:** every non-idempotent tool (writes, payments, messages, PR creation, deploys). **When not:** pure reads.

```python
import hashlib, json

def idempotency_key(session_id: str, step_idx: int, tool_call_id: str) -> str:
    # Stable across retries/replays of the same step; differs across steps.
    return hashlib.sha256(f"{session_id}:{step_idx}:{tool_call_id}".encode()).hexdigest()

def execute_side_effecting_tool(store, session_id, step_idx, call):
    key = idempotency_key(session_id, step_idx, call.id)
    prior = store.get(key)                 # durable store (workflow history / Postgres / KV)
    if prior is not None:
        return prior                        # replay: return the recorded result, no re-execution
    result = call.tool.run(call.args, idempotency_key=key)  # pass key to downstream APIs that accept one
    store.put(key, result)
    return result
```

**Retry taxonomy with jittered exponential backoff**
- **What it is:** retry only transient errors, with bounded attempts. Fail fast on terminal errors.
- **Mechanics:**
  - **Retryable:** 429/RateLimitError, 5xx, timeouts, dropped or idle streams.
  - **Terminal:** auth and validation errors, `ContextWindowExceeded` (after compaction failed), `UsageLimitReached`, `SessionBudgetExceeded`, `Fatal`, exhausted credit.
  - Backoff with jitter of ~0–2 s, 0–4 s, 0–8 s, honoring `retry_after`.
  - Codex defaults are 5 stream retries, 4 request retries and a 300 s stream idle timeout.
  - Claude Code `/goal` retries transient errors, pauses after three retries, and pauses then auto-resumes on rate or usage limits.
  - Every retry counts against rate limits and adds latency. Record `retry_count` on the `chat` span.
- **Evidence:** [codex model-provider-info](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/model-provider-info/src/lib.rs); [turn.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/core/src/session/turn.rs); [LiteLLM retries](https://www.mintlify.com/BerriAI/litellm/features/retries); [/goal](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal)
- **When to use:** every model call and every network tool. **When not:** never retry non-idempotent tools without an idempotency key.

```python
import random, time

RETRYABLE = {429, 500, 502, 503, 504, "timeout", "stream_idle", "connection_reset"}
TERMINAL  = {"auth", "validation", "context_window_exceeded", "usage_limit_reached",
             "session_budget_exceeded", "fatal"}

def call_with_retry(send, max_retries=4):          # Codex: 4 request / 5 stream retries
    for attempt in range(max_retries + 1):
        try:
            return send()
        except ProviderError as e:
            if e.kind in TERMINAL or attempt == max_retries:
                raise
            if e.kind not in RETRYABLE:
                raise
            cap = 2 ** (attempt + 1)                # ~0-2s, 0-4s, 0-8s ...
            delay = e.retry_after if e.retry_after else random.uniform(0, cap)
            time.sleep(delay)
```

**Retry-then-fallback model routing via a gateway**
- **What it is:** a router tries the same deployment first and falls back to another model group only after retries are exhausted.
- **Mechanics (LiteLLM Router semantics):**
  - Retries hit the same deployment first, e.g. `num_retries=3`, then a fallback to a cheaper model.
  - Context-window-exceeded errors fall back to a **larger-context** model group.
  - A deployment goes into cooldown after N failures per minute.
  - The Claude Agent SDK exposes `fallback_model` natively.
  - The DeepSeek Anthropic-compatible endpoint with model-name aliasing gives a cheap cross-provider fallback for Messages-API harnesses: point `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` at `https://api.deepseek.com/anthropic`.
- **Evidence:** [LiteLLM routing](https://git.kvant.cloud/phoenix/litellm-mirror/src/commit/f2991203941095109707c47265090bcfb0588965/docs/my-website/docs/routing.md); [orq.ai](https://docs.orq.ai/docs/proxy/retries.md); [claude-agent-sdk types.py](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python/blob/main/src/claude_agent_sdk/types.py)
- **When to use:** availability incidents, 429 storms, context-overflow escape hatches. **When not:** mid-session in a cache-heavy agent unless forced. Each model has its own cache, so a fallback mid-session pays a full cache write. Tool and edit formats may also not match the fallback model's training (see §11).

**Rate-limit management for agent fleets**
- **What it is:** shape concurrency and background work around provider limits.
- **Mechanics:**
  - Honor `retry_after` and use per-deployment cooldowns.
  - Pause and auto-resume on usage limits (`/goal`, workflows).
  - Gate background jobs on remaining quota (Codex memories `min_rate_limit_remaining_percent`).
  - Cap fan-out (`CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS` default 20, depth 3).
  - On OpenAI, keep each `prompt_cache_key`+prefix under ~15 RPM so cache routing does not overflow.
- **Evidence:** cited above. The notes found **no quantitative data** on rate-limit tiers or recommended concurrency limits for agent fleets.
- **When to use:** any multi-agent or multi-tenant deployment.

**Three-layer budget enforcement**
- **What it is:** hard caps on turns, money or tokens, and wall-clock time.
- **Mechanics:**
  - Per-run turns: `max_turns`.
  - Cumulative dollars or tokens: `max_budget_usd`, Codex thread-goal token budgets. These are checked *after* each response, so leave headroom of one response plus subagent spend.
  - Wall-clock and idle timeouts for streams (Codex 300 s idle).
  - Map terminations to explicit result subtypes (`error_max_turns`, `error_max_budget_usd`).
- **Evidence:** [agent-loop docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/agent-loop); [codex ext/goal](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/ext/goal/templates/goals/budget_limit.md)
- **When to use:** always in production ("Setting a budget is a good default for production agents").

**Prompt caching as the main cost lever (Anthropic mechanics)**
- **What it is:** a stable prefix (`tools` → `system` → `messages`) with explicit or automatic cache breakpoints.
- **Mechanics:**
  - A single top-level `cache_control` (automatic mode) moves the breakpoint to the last cacheable block each turn. Alternatively, use up to 4 explicit breakpoints; the automatic one uses one slot.
  - Reads walk back at most 20 blocks. A run of consecutive tool_use/tool_result blocks counts as one position. A turn that adds 20 or more blocks between writes misses unless you add a second breakpoint.
  - The default TTL is 5 minutes, refreshed free on each hit, and measured from the start of the request. A 4-minute streamed response leaves ~1 minute for the follow-up.
  - A cache entry becomes available only once the first response starts, so parallel fan-out should wait for it.
  - Classic mistake: putting a breakpoint on a block that contains a timestamp means a write on every request and never a read.
  - Recommended breakpoints: end of tools, end of system/project context, the moving automatic breakpoint, and an extra mid-history breakpoint for large parallel fan-outs.
- **Evidence (prices):**
  - Reads cost 0.1× base input, 5-minute writes 1.25× and 1-hour writes 2×.
  - Reads cost 0.05× on Opus/Sonnet 5.5 and 0.025× on Fable/Mythos 5.1.
  - Multipliers stack with batch, long-context and data-residency modifiers.
  - Example: Opus 4.5 at $5/MTok base, $6.25 for 5-minute writes and $10 for 1-hour writes.
  - The 1-hour TTL is not available on every model or platform.
  - Sources: [Claude docs: Prompt caching](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching); [Vertex AI Claude caching](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/partner-models/claude/prompt-caching)
- **When to use:** cache tool definitions from day one; the 25% write markup pays back on the second hit. **When not:** the 1-hour TTL on short, bursty sessions, where the 2× write never amortizes.

**Cache-preserving dynamic context**
- **What it is:** add per-turn dynamic data (time, budgets, reminders, tool changes) without editing the prefix.
- **Mechanics:**
  - **Mid-conversation system messages:** append `{"role":"system"}` to `messages`. No beta header is needed on supported 5.x models.
  - **Turn-scoped system messages:** beta `mid-conversation-system-clear-at-2026-08-21` with `clear_at: "next_user_message"`. The message renders until the next user or tool_result message and then costs 0 tokens. Resend cleared messages verbatim.
  - **Inline tool changes:** beta `inline-tools-2026-09-15` with `tool_addition`/`tool_removal`. Keep at least one non-deferred tool in `tools`, or the first by-value definition costs a full miss.
  - **Deferred tools:** `defer_loading: true` plus tool search. A discovered tool is appended as a `tool_reference` inline, and a deferred tool cannot carry `cache_control`.
  - **OpenAI:** `allowed_tools` restricts tools per turn without editing `tools`. `configuration_update` changes effort mid-conversation.
  - **Self-hosted:** Manus-style logit masking with namespaced tool prefixes (`browser_*`, `shell_*`).
- **Evidence:** [Mid-conversation system messages](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-system-messages); [Manus](https://manus.im/blog/Context-Engineering-for-AI-Agents-Lessons-from-Building-Manus?hl=en-GB)
- **When to use:** any per-turn reminder or tool gating. **When not:** never put timestamps or environment state in the system prompt.

**Effort and thinking tuning per task class**
- **What it is:** set reasoning effort per session, per subagent or per task class as a cost/quality knob.
- **Mechanics:**
  - Anthropic effort levels are low/medium/high/xhigh/max. Opus 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 default to medium.
  - OpenAI GPT-6 levels are low/medium (default)/high/xhigh/max.
  - Treat effort, thinking mode and budget as part of the cache key. Changing `budget_tokens` or the thinking mode invalidates the cache; the docs show a full re-creation of a 1,370-token cache after a budget change.
  - Change effort in-band (`configuration_update`) or per subagent, not per request.
- **Evidence:** [Extended thinking docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/extended-thinking); [codex GPT-6 guide](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/skills/src/assets/samples/openai-docs/references/upgrading-to-gpt-6-astra.md). Opus 5.5's Terminal-Bench 4.0 self-report used xhigh effort (66.4%, reported); see the evals section.
- **When to use:** per task class, chosen by eval. **When not:** flipping effort per request inside one cached conversation.

**Model cascades and tiering**
- **What it is:** a strong model for planning or leading, cheaper models for subagents, search and summarize steps, and side tasks.
- **Mechanics:**
  - An Opus lead with Sonnet subagents.
  - Route cheap work to `haiku` via per-agent `model`.
  - Cognition reportedly uses a frontier lead with a cheaper executor (secondary).
  - Route side tasks such as compaction to subagents or forks that share the prefix. Anthropic's server compaction cannot use a cheaper model.
- **Evidence:** Opus 4 lead + Sonnet 4 subagents scored +90.2% over single-agent Opus 4 ([Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/multi-agent-research-system)). [Cognition (snippet)](https://ai.engineer/orgs/cognition).
- **When to use:** high-volume parallel subtasks. **When not:** switching the *main* conversation's model mid-session, which breaks the cache.

**Batch API for offline work**
- **What it is:** submit evals, backfills and offline grading through provider batch endpoints.
- **Mechanics:** batch multipliers stack with cache multipliers on Anthropic, per the docs.
- **Evidence:** the 50% batch discount is commonly cited but **not verified** in the notes, and neither is how it stacks with caching on Anthropic or OpenAI.
- **When to use:** nightly eval suites, trace re-grading, data synthesis. **When not:** interactive sessions.

**Fan-out cache sharing**
- **What it is:** sibling agents with identical model, effort, tools, schema and cwd share one cached prefix.
- **Mechanics:** hold siblings until the first response begins (`CLAUDE_CODE_WORKFLOW_PREFIX_STAGGER_MS`, 5000 ms). Vary only the task message. Use forks, which inherit the parent cache, rather than fresh subagents when context sharing is wanted.
- **Evidence:** [Claude Code workflows](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows); [Claude Code prompt caching](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/prompt-caching)
- **When to use:** any parallel fan-out.

**Latency optimizations**
- **What it is:** architectural latency cuts that are independent of the model.
- **Mechanics:**
  1. Lazy sandbox provisioning: create the container only when a tool call needs it.
  2. Pre-warmed or pooled sandboxes. Cold starts range from ~90 ms to 3 s by vendor.
  3. Streaming (`include_partial_messages` / `StreamEvent` deltas in the Claude SDK).
  4. Parallel tool calls. Read-only tools (`Read`, `Glob`, `Grep`, MCP tools marked read-only) run concurrently. State-modifying tools (`Edit`, `Write`, `Bash`) run sequentially. Custom tools are sequential unless `readOnlyHint` is set.
  5. Async subagents, since synchronous waits were a bottleneck at Anthropic.
  6. A cache-stable prefix. OpenAI caching cuts latency by up to 80%.
  7. Measure "critical steps" to verify that a fan-out shortened the critical path.
- **Evidence:** p50 TTFT −~60% and p95 −>90% from lazy provisioning ([Managed Agents](https://anthropic.com/engineering/managed-agents)). OpenAI agent RFT reports models learned to issue more parallel calls ([InfoQ](https://www.infoq.com/presentations/rft-openai-model/)). The notes found **no credible source** on speculative execution of tool calls or LLM responses in production harnesses.
- **When to use:** always. Lazy provisioning matters most for chat-like sessions where many turns never touch a tool.

**Rainbow deployments and versioned workflows**
- **What it is:** run old and new harness versions side by side and shift traffic gradually, so agents already running finish on the version they started with.
- **Mechanics:**
  - Version workflows, prompts and tool sets.
  - New sessions go to the new version and in-flight sessions stay pinned.
  - Never mutate a running workflow's prompt or tool set.
  - Record the harness version and the prompts/tools SHA on the root span so regressions can be attributed.
- **Evidence:** [Anthropic, 2025-06-13](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/multi-agent-research-system)
- **When to use:** any deploy of a harness that hosts long-running agents.

**Tell the agent about failures**
- **What it is:** return tool and sandbox failures to the model as tool results instead of crashing the run.
- **Mechanics:**
  - Managed Agents returns a dead sandbox as a tool-call error that Claude "can choose to retry".
  - Denied tool calls come back "as the tool result".
  - OpenAI's `tool_not_found_behavior="return_error_to_model"`.
  - Anthropic agents are *told* when a tool is failing.
- **Evidence:** [Managed Agents](https://anthropic.com/engineering/managed-agents); [agent-loop docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/agent-loop); [Anthropic research system](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/multi-agent-research-system)
- **When to use:** recoverable tool-level errors. **When not:** API or auth errors, which must not be delivered as a subagent's result.

**Compaction cost-awareness**
- **What it is:** compaction trades the cached prefix for context headroom, so schedule it deliberately.
- **Mechanics:**
  - Compact at about 90% of the window (Codex default) or at natural task breaks.
  - Put `cache_control` on the compaction block, plus a separate breakpoint at the end of the system prompt so only the summary is re-written.
  - Prefer `/rewind` (truncate to an already cached prefix) when abandoning a path.
  - Clear stale tool results with `clear_at_least` large enough to amortize the cache write.
  - A mid-session `/compact` reuses the warm prefix and costs "a fraction of what the context size suggests". After the TTL expires it reprocesses uncached. With the 1-hour TTL, Claude Code can idle-compact (`idleCompaction`).
  - **Billing trap:** compaction adds a sampling iteration that top-level `usage.input_tokens`/`output_tokens` exclude. Sum true cost over `usage.iterations`.
  - Use `pause_after_compaction` plus a compaction counter to enforce a total token budget across a long task. Managed Agents always compacts and emits an `agent.thread_context_compacted` event.
  - Context-editing responses carry `context_management.applied_edits` with `cleared_input_tokens`. Log these as expected rebuilds. `clear_tool_uses_20250919` triggers by default at 100,000 input tokens and keeps the last 3 tool use/result pairs.
- **Evidence:** [Claude docs: Context editing](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/context-editing); [Claude docs: threshold compaction](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/compaction-threshold); [Claude Code prompt caching](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/prompt-caching)
- **When to use:** long sessions. Log each compaction as an expected cache rebuild.
