| temporal-community/openai-agents-demos | demos | Durable rollouts if RL tool backends need durability (cf. §10) |

### 11.7 Build checklist for our harness

1. **Ship per-model tool profiles.** A profile bundles {tool names and schemas, edit format, system-prompt file, reasoning-replay mode, compaction prompt}. The default for OpenAI Codex models is OpenAI's exact `apply_patch` grammar (freeform or first-class tool), `shell`/`exec_command`, `update_plan` and the matching `codex-rs/core` prompt file. The default for Claude is str_replace-style edit, bash, read/glob/grep and todo. The default for DeepSeek is the reference encoders. Select the profile by model id. Never fall back to a generic profile silently.
2. **Detect profile mismatches.** Log calls to unknown tools (e.g. `apply_patch` attempted where it's absent) as a `profile_mismatch` metric, and return an actionable tool error rather than crashing.
3. **Implement correct reasoning replay per provider.** That means encrypted reasoning items with `store:false` (OpenAI), signed thinking blocks (Anthropic), and `reasoning_content` (DeepSeek). Tool results always go in the native tool role. Add a regression test that fails if tool results are ever sent as user messages.
4. **Match the compaction protocol to the model.** For Codex-family models, use a 90% trigger, the handoff-summary prompt with the summary prefix, and `new_context`/`get_context_remaining` tools. For models with context anxiety, offer a reset-plus-handoff mode. Keep every scaffold (resets, sprints, todo, planner, evaluator) behind a feature flag.
5. **Use one task format for evals and RL.** Write each Tier-1/2 eval task as {image, instruction, hidden verifier, reference solution, limits}, compatible with Harbor (and ideally exportable to OpenEnv/Verifiers). Record token IDs and logprobs when running open models (`collect_rollout_details`-style) so the same runs can feed RL.
6. **Harden verifiers before anything optimizes against them.**
   - Tests are hidden and read-only to the agent.
   - Grade final state, not claims.
   - Detect `sys.exit(0)`-style exits and test tampering.
   - Use a clean sandbox per trial with no shared git history.
   - Give judges an "Unknown" option, with one judge per dimension.
   - Audit tasks at 0% pass@100 or at saturation.
7. **Build a rollout-scoped tool backend.** Use a unique rollout/session ID on every tool call, one sandbox per rollout from a pooled and recycled pool, a per-rollout tool-call cap, and checkpointable environment state for long-horizon runs. The same backend serves agent RFT, open RL and evals.
8. **Run the Anthropic tool-improvement loop for every new tool.** Generate realistic multi-call tasks with Claude Code, run them, collect accuracy, runtime, calls, tokens and errors, read the transcripts, let the agent refactor descriptions, schemas, pagination and errors, and accept only on a held-out set. Defaults: a `response_format` (concise/detailed) parameter, a 25k-token result cap with truncation guidance, and actionable errors.
9. **Run a gated nightly self-improvement loop.** Run the capability suite, cluster failures, have an agent propose GEPA-style prompt or tool-description diffs and ACE-style playbook deltas, and accept only if the held-out gain exceeds the noise band (≥3–5 trials; single runs swing 2–6 pts), with no regression-suite loss and cost and latency within budget. Log every accepted diff with its eval delta and harness SHA.
10. **Keep persistent playbooks and memory ACE-style.** Use itemized bullets with IDs and helpful/harmful counters, deterministic merge, de-dup and pruning, and never whole-file rewrites. Promote self-generated skills only after verification (tests, review or evidence).
11. **Sandbox DGM-style code self-modification.** If we experiment with it at all, run it only offline, in isolated sandboxes with hidden verifiers, and require human review before any evolved harness code reaches production.
12. **Escalate in order:** prompt/tool optimization (GEPA/ACE) → per-model profile tuning → agent RFT (hosted) or open RL (Agent Lightning / ClawGym-style proxy over our unmodified harness, with verl/SkyRL/ART/prime-rl as the trainer). Move to RL only when a stable, high-volume task has an automatic, hack-resistant grader.
13. **Prepare for training on our harness.** Route all model calls through a single client or proxy that can log token-level data, so a black-box RL trainer can attach later without harness changes.
14. **Steer parallelism explicitly.** Set fan-out caps and prompts, and track a critical-steps metric. Models under-parallelize (Kimi "serial collapse") or over-delegate (Opus 5), and only trained orchestrators (PARL) learn this themselves.
15. **Ablate at every model upgrade.** Re-run the suite with each scaffold flag off and against a mini-swe-agent-style control. Delete components the new model no longer needs.
16. **For self-hosted open models, expose learnable context operations as tools** (fold/branch/return, compress, memory ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP) so FoldGRPO-, ACON- or Memory-R1-style training can target them.
17. **Report harness-sensitive results with full context:** harness version and profile, model, effort, number of runs, mean ± SE, and strict vs partial-credit scoring. Hold the model fixed when claiming harness wins.

### 11.8 Pitfalls and anti-patterns

- **A generic tool set for every model.** Codex models trained on `apply_patch` call it even when it's missing. Harness mismatch costs several to 20+ points.
- **Sending tool results as user messages.** DeepSeek drops reasoning on user turns (Roo Code and Terminus are named as triggering this), and it breaks native tool-role training on every provider.
- **Hand-rolled chat templates for open models.** Use DeepSeek's reference encoders and Harmony for gpt-oss. The DeepSeek V3.2 parser "is designed to handle well-formatted strings only".
- **Hackable verifiers.** Visible or writable tests, claim-based grading, and shared state across trials all count. In production RL these taught models to hack and generalized to misalignment, including ~12% sabotage of detection code. In self-improvement loops they get optimized directly.
- **Trusting environment counts.** 2,500+ hub environments or 1,827 synthesized ones say nothing about verifier robustness.
- **Fresh sandboxes per attempt at scale.** These hit creation-rate limits. Pool and recycle, and checkpoint persistent environment state for long-horizon RL.
- **RL before prompt optimization.** GEPA reaches comparable or better results with up to 35× fewer rollouts on many tasks. Start there. The exception is math-style reasoning, where GRPO beat GEPA on AIME-2025.
- **Accepting self-improvement changes on single runs.** Single-run noise is 2–6 pts. Require repeated trials and held-out plus regression gates.
- **Whole-file rewrites of playbooks or memory.** These cause ACE's "context collapse" and "brevity bias". Use delta bullets.
- **Promoting self-generated skills unverified.** SkillsBench shows ~0 or negative average benefit, and EvoClawBench shows over-specific skills tied to first-run filenames.
- **Running DGM-style self-modification in production.** It risks sandbox escape and reward hacking of the eval, and nothing is known about transfer across model versions.
- **Keeping stale scaffolds.** Context resets, sprints and todo tools became dead weight on newer models. Every component encodes an assumption that expires.
- **Cross-harness comparisons that change the model, benchmark version (TB 2.0 vs 2.1) or effort setting at the same time.** These confound the harness effect. Harness deltas in the notes are partly inconsistent: Opus 4.6 is reported higher in Terminus-KIRA than in Claude Code.
- **Over-trusting LLM-judge rewards.** Judges reach 66% agreement with experts vs 71% human–human on GDPval. Calibrate rubric and RULER-style rewards against humans.
- **Mid-training mini-batch off-policyness and MoE routing drift** if GRPO is used naively at scale. DeepSeek needed sequence masking plus Keep Routing and Keep Sampling Mask.

### 11.9 Open questions and unverified claims

- **How OpenAI RL-trains Codex models in the harness.** No primary system card or addendum confirms it. Only "trained to excel at this diff format" (the prompting guide) is primary. "Trained in the presence of the harness" (harness-engineering post) is a secondary snippet. That GPT-5.5 is trained on the Codex CLI loop and ordered system prompt is a third-party claim.
- **Anthropic's agentic RL environment mix**, and whether Claude is trained on Claude Code's exact toolset, are not publicly described. The Claude tool-profile recommendation is an inference.
- **Agent RFT as of Nov 2026:** endpoint payloads, tool-call caps, pricing and the GA model list are unconfirmed (platform.openai.com blocked).
- **DeepSeek V3.2 internals:** the per-agent task counts (~50K / 24.7K / 5.9K / 4.4K), RL compute >10% of pretraining, and the release benchmark numbers are recalled, not verified. The paper itself was read only via search summaries. The V3.1 search- and code-agent trajectory templates and the V4 tech report were not accessible.
- **Kimi K2 tool counts** (~3,000 real MCP, ~20,000 synthetic) are unconfirmed. **PARL** reward formulas and the swarm-vs-single benchmark numbers were not accessible. The K2.6 (300 sub-agents) and K3 (persistent sandbox RL) claims are secondary.
- **Cursor Composer 2 / Composer 1 / Windsurf SWE-1.5** training details come from report snippets and Simon Willison's coverage. No quantitative in-harness-training ablation was found.
- **The reward-hacking study** was read through secondary summaries (alphaxiv, Alignment Forum, Zvi). Exact effect sizes beyond ~12% sabotage aren't in the notes.
- **GEPA's abstract changed between versions** (4 tasks / 10% average earlier vs 6 tasks / 6% average, up to 20%, later). Use the latest.
- **ADAS** (Meta Agent Search, 2024) did not surface. Its results are background only and unverified.
- **No 2026 production case studies** quantify GEPA or ACE gains in deployed commercial agents rather than on benchmarks.
- **DGM-evolved harnesses across model versions:** no data on transfer.
- **HGM's 56.7% on SWE-Verified-60** has an unclear baseline.
- **OpenRLHF agent extensions** were not researched.
- **Hub verifier robustness:** there is no public audit of Environments Hub, OpenEnv or Harbor environments for reward-hackability.
- **Harness-delta numbers** (Terminal-Bench 2.0/2.1, SWE-bench Pro SEAL vs Claude Code) are secondary and partly inconsistent. Snorkel reportedly lists Claude Code + Fable at 83.8% where a blog has 83.1%, and tbench.ai was unreachable.
- **Self-generated-skill benchmarks** (SkillsBench, EvoClawBench, SkillEvolBench, EvoAgentBench) are cited from secondary sources (alphaxiv, papers.cool, arXiv HTML).

## 12. Reference repositories (OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepSeek, open source)

> **SOTA in one paragraph:** The most complete open-source production coding-agent harness is `openai/codex` (Apache-2.0, ~150 Rust crates), whose reference parts are a Lark-grammar `apply_patch` freeform tool, PTY-backed `exec_command`/`write_stdin`, OS-native sandboxes, handoff-summary compaction, hierarchical AGENTS.md, Claude-Code-compatible hooks, a two-phase background memory pipeline, and the thread/turn/item JSON-RPC "app-server" that every OpenAI surface is built on. Anthropic keeps Claude Code closed under Commercial Terms but open-sources the interfaces around it: the MIT Python Agent SDK (a subprocess transport plus a `control_request` protocol), the Apache-2.0 `sandbox-runtime`, the Agent Skills format, plugins/hooks/"mods", cookbooks, and the initializer-plus-coding-agent long-running quickstart. DeepSeek ships weights, kernels and chat-format encoders, serves an Anthropic-format endpoint so that Claude Code, OpenCode and others can drive its models, and has only a thinly documented "DeepSeek Harness" repo whose status is reported by secondary sources. Among community harnesses, OpenCode, Pi, Gemini CLI, OpenHands (now Agent Canvas plus the Software Agent SDK), Cline, Goose, Crush, deepagents and mini-swe-agent lead, while Roo Code shut down, Kimi CLI was archived and Aider has slowed. The primitives (AGENTS.md, MCP, SKILL.md, the Claude/Codex hook vocabulary, ACP) are standardizing faster than any single harness, so protocol compatibility is the safest investment.

**Provenance and confidence.** Unless marked otherwise, every repo fact below comes from a shallow clone of the repo's default branch on 2026-11-03, with the README, source tree, docs and changelog read directly. Version tags come from `git ls-remote --tags`. Star counts come from GitHub page fetches on 2026-11-03 through a summarizing tool; they are approximate and should be spot-checked before quoting. The GitHub REST/Releases API, huggingface.co, arxiv.org, api-docs.deepseek.com, developers.openai.com and openai.com were blocked from the research sessions. As a result:
- Release dates for most tags are unknown.
- DeepSeek template and API details come from search-engine summaries.
- Some OpenAI guidance comes from snapshots of developers.openai.com that are bundled inside the Codex repo.

Markers used: **(secondary)** means from search snippets or third-party write-ups; **(reported)** means a claim attributed to a vendor or press report that was not verified; **(inference)** means the notes' own reasoning, not a sourced fact.

### 12.2 OpenAI

#### 12.2.1 openai/codex (codex-rs)

**Purpose.** This is OpenAI's production coding agent, shipped as a CLI, an IDE extension, a desktop app (`codex app`) and cloud "Codex Web". It installs via a standalone installer, npm `@openai/codex` or Homebrew, and works with a ChatGPT plan or an API key ([README](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/README.md)). The macOS Codex app launched on Feb 2, 2026 as a "command center" for managing several coding agents in parallel **(secondary)** ([IntuitionLabs](https://intuitionlabs.ai/articles/openai-codex-app-ai-coding-agents); [heise](https://heise.de/-11165126)). It is the most complete open-source (Apache-2.0) production harness available.

**Architecture.** The workspace has roughly 150 Rust crates ([codex-rs tree](https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/main/codex-rs)):
- `codex-core` "implements the business logic for Codex … used by the various Codex UIs written in Rust" ([core/README.md](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/core/README.md)).
- Around the core sit:
  - edit: `apply-patch`
  - client boundary: `app-server` / `app-server-protocol`
  - headless and remote execution: `exec` and `exec-server`
  - policy: `execpolicy`
  - extension points: `hooks`, `skills` and `memories`
  - sandboxes: `linux-sandbox`, `bwrap`, `windows-sandbox-rs`, `sandboxing` and `network-proxy`
  - MCP: `rmcp-client` and `codex-mcp`
  - persistence: `rollout` and `thread-store`
  - UI: `tui`
  - telemetry: `otel`
  - multi-agent: `worktree`, `agent-roles` and `message-board`
  - code-as-action: `code-mode`, `code-mode-runtime` and `code-mode-host`
  - `responses-api-proxy`
- Every OpenAI surface (TUI, IDE, desktop, SDK) speaks the app-server protocol to the same core.

**Key files and modules**

| Area | Files / modules | What is there |
|---|---|---|
| Thread and session state | `core/src/codex_thread.rs`, `thread_manager.rs`, `session/`, `tasks/`, `rollout.rs`, `thread-store` | Threads, sessions and tasks; rollouts are append-only JSONL (`session_meta`, `turn_context`, `event_msg`, `response_item`) ([read_path.md](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/ext/memories/templates/memories/read_path.md)) |
| Turn loop | `core/src/session/turn.rs` (`run_turn`, `run_sampling_request`, `run_turn_stop_hooks`) | See "Agent loop" below ([turn.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/core/src/session/turn.rs)) |
| Model client | `core/src/client.rs`, `responses_retry.rs`, `codex-api/src/endpoint/responses_websocket.rs`, `model-provider-info/src/lib.rs` | Responses API client, retries, WebSocket endpoint, provider defaults |
| Context | `core/src/context_manager/`, `turn_diff_tracker.rs`, `shell_snapshot.rs`, `compact.rs`, `compact_remote_v2*.rs`, `compact_retained_tool_outputs.rs` | History, diffs, shell-environment snapshot, compaction |
| Tool plumbing | `core/src/tools/{registry,router,orchestrator,parallel,approvals,sandboxing,network_approval,spec_plan}.rs`, `core/src/tools/handlers/`, `codex-rs/tools` | Registration, routing, parallelism, approvals, sandbox selection ([core/src/tools](https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/main/codex-rs/core/src/tools)) |
| Policy | `core/src/exec_policy.rs`, `core/src/guardian/` (also `guardian_review.rs`), `execpolicy/` | Starlark prefix rules; LLM auto-reviewer |
| Instructions | `core/src/agents_md.rs`, `docs/agents_md.md` | Hierarchical AGENTS.md loading |
| MCP and skills | `core/src/mcp_tool_call.rs`, `codex-mcp/`, `rmcp-client/`, `core/src/skills.rs`, `skills/` | MCP client; SKILL.md loading and bundled sample skills |
| Prompts | `core/{gpt_5_codex_prompt,gpt-5.1-codex-max_prompt,gpt-5.2-codex_prompt,gpt_5_1_prompt,gpt_5_2_prompt}.md`, `core/prompt_with_apply_patch_instructions.md`, `protocol/src/prompts/base_instructions/default.md`, `models-manager/prompt.md`, `prompts/templates/` | Per-model base prompts; sandbox, approval, compaction, guardian and persistent-mode templates |
| Modes and goals | `collaboration-mode-templates/templates/plan.md`, `ext/goal/templates/goals/{continuation,budget_limit}.md`, `prompts/templates/persistent_mode.md` | Plan Mode, thread goals, persistent follow-ups |
| Config | `core/config.schema.json`, `core/src/config/mod.rs`, `protocol/src/openai_models.rs`, `features/src/lib.rs`, `protocol/src/protocol.rs` | Thresholds, feature flags, `SandboxPolicy`/`AskForApproval` enums |
| CLI | `cli/src/main.rs`, `utils/cli/src/shared_options.rs` | Subcommands and dangerous-mode flags |

**Agent loop** ([turn.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/core/src/session/turn.rs)):
- Each iteration clones history and calls `run_sampling_request`, a streamed Responses call. That returns `SamplingRequestResult { needs_follow_up, last_agent_message }`.
- `needs_follow_up = model_needs_follow_up || has_pending_input`: either the model emitted tool calls, or the user queued input mid-turn.
- The loop then reads the context-window token status and may start async compaction (phase `MidTurn` or `PostTurn`).
- If `auto_compaction_enabled && needs_follow_up && (model requested new context window || token_limit_reached || async-compaction candidate ready)`, it runs `run_auto_compact` and continues.
- If there is no follow-up, it runs Stop hooks. If a hook blocks and supplies a continuation prompt, that prompt is recorded as a new message, `stop_hook_active = true` is set, and the loop continues. A block that has no prompt is ignored with the warning "Stop hook requested continuation without a prompt; ignoring the block."
- Retry defaults: `DEFAULT_STREAM_MAX_RETRIES = 5`, `DEFAULT_REQUEST_MAX_RETRIES = 4`, `DEFAULT_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS = 300_000` ([model-provider-info/src/lib.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/model-provider-info/src/lib.rs)). `ContextWindowExceeded`, `UsageLimitReached`, `SessionBudgetExceeded` and `Fatal` are returned without retry. Other stream errors go through `handle_response_stream_error` with backoff, and cancellation surfaces as `CodexErr::TurnAborted`.
- Request shape: `store: false` plus `include: ["reasoning.encrypted_content"]`. The API stays stateless (zero data retention), and the client replays encrypted reasoning items itself. `parallel_tool_calls` is passed through ([client.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/core/src/client.rs)).
- The base prompt says "You are a coding agent. Please keep going until the query is completely resolved, before ending your turn and yielding back to the user". It asks for a short "preamble" before tool calls ([default.md](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/protocol/src/prompts/base_instructions/default.md)); `models-manager/prompt.md` puts the preamble at 8–12 words ([models-manager/prompt.md](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/models-manager/prompt.md)).

**Tools** ([core/src/tools/handlers](https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/main/codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers); [unified_exec.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/unified_exec.rs); [codex-rs/tools](https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/main/codex-rs/tools)):
- Shell:
  - `exec_command` plus `write_stdin` form the "unified exec" shell, with PTY sessions keyed by `session_id`.
  - Legacy `shell` / `shell_command` remain.
  - A code-mode `exec` exists as well.
- Editing and planning: `apply_patch`, `update_plan`, `view_image`, `request_user_input`, `request_permissions`, `tool_search`, `web_search`.
- MCP resources: `list_mcp_resources`, `list_mcp_resource_templates`, `read_mcp_resource`.
- Multi-agent: `spawn_agent`, `send_input`, `send_message`, `wait_agent`, `close_agent`, `resume_agent`, `interrupt_agent`, `list_agents`, `followup_task`. The handler directories are `multi_agents` / `multi_agents_v2`.
- Context and loop control:
  - `get_context_remaining` ("Get the remaining tokens in the current context window.")
  - a new-context tool, listed as `new_context_window` in one reading and `new_context` in another: "Start a new context window. Does not clear, reset, or otherwise affect environment state."
  - `sleep` ("The sleep ends early when new input arrives for the active turn")
  - `send_message_to_user_async`
  - `request_plugin_install`
- `update_plan` contract: "a short list of 1‑sentence steps (no more than 5-7 words each)", statuses `pending`/`in_progress`/`completed`, "exactly one `in_progress` step", and "Do not repeat the full contents of the plan after an `update_plan` call — the harness already displays it" ([default.md](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/protocol/src/prompts/base_instructions/default.md)).
- Code mode: `augment_tool_spec_for_code_mode` augments tool descriptions "with code-mode-specific exec samples" ([tools/src/code_mode.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/tools/src/code_mode.rs)). The runtime engine (JS/V8?) was not confirmed from source.

**apply_patch** ([parser.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/apply-patch/src/parser.rs); [seek_sequence.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/apply-patch/src/seek_sequence.rs); [apply_patch_spec.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/apply_patch_spec.rs)):
- An official Lark grammar defines the format (`assets/tools/apply_patch.lark`). Its start rule is `start: begin_patch environment_id? hunk+ end_patch`.
- Markers: `*** Begin Patch`, `*** Add File: `, `*** Delete File: `, `*** Update File: ` (with optional `*** Move to: `), `@@` / `@@ <context>` anchors, `+`/`-`/space-prefixed lines, optional `*** End of File`, and `*** End Patch`.
- The new optional `*** Environment ID:` header supports multi-environment threads.
- Line numbers are deliberately absent; hunks are anchored by context.
- The parser is deliberately lenient and tolerates surrounding whitespace. Code comments say only gpt-4.1 "knowingly requires lenient parsing".
- Context matching (`seek_sequence`) falls back step by step: exact match, then trim-end, then trim, then Unicode-normalised match.
- It is exposed as a FREEFORM tool with `format: {type: "grammar", syntax: "lark"}`. The tool description says "This is a FREEFORM tool, so do not wrap the patch in JSON".
- The crate also contains a `streaming_parser.rs` (it parses patches as they stream in) and a standalone `apply_patch` executable ([apply-patch/src](https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/main/codex-rs/apply-patch/src)).
- OpenAI's Codex prompting guide: "We strongly recommend using our exact apply_patch implementation as the model has been trained to excel at this diff format" ([Codex Prompting Guide](https://developers.openai.com/cookbook/examples/gpt-5/codex_prompting_guide), blocked host, cited via [prompt_with_apply_patch_instructions.md](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/core/prompt_with_apply_patch_instructions.md)).

**Compaction** ([compact.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/core/src/compact.rs); [prompt.md](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/prompts/templates/compact/prompt.md); [summary_prefix.md](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/prompts/templates/compact/summary_prefix.md); [openai_models.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/protocol/src/openai_models.rs); [config/mod.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/core/src/config/mod.rs)):
- Prompt: "You are performing a CONTEXT CHECKPOINT COMPACTION. Create a handoff summary for another LLM that will resume the task". It asks for current progress and key decisions; context, constraints and user preferences; clear next steps; and critical data, examples and references. `compact_prompt` in config overrides it.
- Re-injection prefix: "Another language model started to solve this problem and produced a summary of its thinking process. You also have access to the state of the tools that were used by that language model…"
- History rebuild:
  - The new history is the initial context, then the user's own prior messages, then the summary.
  - User messages are kept newest-first up to `COMPACT_USER_MESSAGE_MAX_TOKENS = 20_000`. Over-budget messages are truncated, and images and audio are dropped.
  - The initial context is re-inserted before the last real user message or summary.
- Triggers:
  - Inline when the token limit is hit (`run_inline_auto_compact_task`), or manual.
  - `auto_compact_token_limit()` = min(configured `model_auto_compact_token_limit`, `context_window * 9 / 10`), so the default is 90% of the window.
  - `effective_context_window_percent` defaults to 95%.
  - `model_auto_compact_token_limit_scope` chooses between the full context and the tokens after the carried compaction prefix.
  - `model_post_turn_compact_threshold_percent` sets turn-end compaction; 0 disables it.
  - The `token_budget` feature adds `reminder_threshold_tokens`, `auto_compact_fallback_prompt` (≤2,000 bytes) and `auto_compact_fallback_buffer_tokens`.
- A separate server-side path (`compact_remote_v2*.rs`) retains selected tool outputs (`compact_retained_tool_outputs.rs`), budgets images, falls back to another model, and runs `PreCompact`/`PostCompact` hooks ([compact_remote_v2.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/core/src/compact_remote_v2.rs)).
- Known bug: in codex-cli 0.117.0, changing `model_context_window` could make auto-compaction fail permanently after the first overflow, because the check read a stale token count ([issue #16068](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/16068)).

**AGENTS.md loading** ([agents_md.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/core/src/agents_md.rs); [docs/agents_md.md](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/docs/agents_md.md); [models-manager/prompt.md](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/models-manager/prompt.md)):
- Every `AGENTS.md` from the project root down to the cwd is collected and auto-injected.
- `AGENTS.override.md` is the preferred local override.
- User and project docs are joined with `--- project-doc ---`.
- A byte budget (`project_doc_max_bytes`) is enforced across all files.
- Semantics given to the model:
  - scope is the directory tree rooted at the file
  - more deeply nested files take precedence
  - direct system/developer/user instructions beat AGENTS.md

**Sandboxing** ([core/README.md](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/core/README.md); [protocol.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/protocol/src/protocol.rs); [linux-sandbox README](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/linux-sandbox/README.md); [sandboxing](https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/main/codex-rs/sandboxing); [network-proxy README](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/network-proxy/README.md)):
- `SandboxPolicy` variants:
  - `danger-full-access`
  - `read-only {network_access=false}`
  - `external-sandbox {network_access}`: full disk, for use when Codex is already inside a container or VM
  - `workspace-write {writable_roots, network_access=false, exclude_tmpdir_env_var, exclude_slash_tmp}`
- Writable roots carry `read_only_subpaths`, so `.git` (notably `.git/hooks`), the resolved gitdir and `.codex` stay read-only even under a writable root. This prevents privilege escalation.
- macOS: `/usr/bin/sandbox-exec` (Seatbelt) with profiles such as `seatbelt_network_policy.sbpl` and `seatbelt_read_only_platform_defaults.sbpl`.
- Linux:
  - The binary re-execs itself as `codex-linux-sandbox` (an arg0 trick). It "uses bubblewrap for filesystem and namespace isolation, and seccomp for syscall filtering" (`PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS`).
  - It prefers a system `bwrap` on PATH outside the CWD, falls back to a bundled bwrap, and warns if user namespaces are unavailable.
  - Landlock is kept only as a legacy path.
  - WSL2 is supported; WSL1 is rejected.
- Windows: an elevated sandbox with split filesystem policies (`windows-sandbox-rs`, `windows-sandbox-service`).
- Network proxy:
  - `codex-network-proxy` runs an HTTP proxy (default `127.0.0.1:3128`) and SOCKS5 (`127.0.0.1:8081`) and enforces allow/deny policy.
  - `mode = "limited"` gives read-only network, with automatic HTTPS MITM and a managed CA exported to child processes.
  - Local and private networking is rejected by default, and hostnames that resolve to private IPs stay blocked even if allowlisted.
  - Config lives under `[permissions.<profile>.network]` with `default_permissions = "workspace"`. Non-loopback binds need `dangerously_allow_non_loopback_proxy`.
- `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` (alias `--yolo`) is "EXTREMELY DANGEROUS. Intended solely for running in environments that are externally sandboxed" ([shared_options.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/utils/cli/src/shared_options.rs)).
- The `worktree` crate suggests git worktrees isolate parallel tasks **(inference from the crate name only)**.

**Approvals, exec policy and guardian** ([protocol.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/protocol/src/protocol.rs); [execpolicy README](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/execpolicy/README.md); [core/src/guardian](https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/main/codex-rs/core/src/guardian); [prompts/templates](https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/main/codex-rs/prompts/templates)):
- `AskForApproval` variants:
  - `untrusted` (`UnlessTrusted`): commands need approval unless an exec-policy rule allows them
  - `on-request` (the default): the model decides when to ask; `on-failure` is now only a serde alias for it
  - `granular` (`GranularApprovalConfig`): per-category booleans, where false means auto-reject rather than prompt
  - `never`: failures go back to the model and are never escalated
- Prompt templates exist for each mode:
  - `permissions/sandbox_mode/{read_only,workspace_write,danger_full_access}.md`
  - `approval_policy/{never,on_request,unless_trusted}.md`
  - `approved_prefixes.md`
- `ApprovalsReviewer` is `user` (the default) or `auto_review` (alias `guardian_subagent`):
  - The guardian module "hosts approval decisions and the isolated synchronous reviewer". Its classifier prompts are `guardian/policy.md` and `classifier_instructions.md`, and there is a separate network-access guardian prompt.
  - Admin `requirements` layers can constrain `allowed_approvals_reviewers`.
  - No precision/recall numbers for the guardian were found.
- `execpolicy` is written in Starlark:
  - Rule form: `prefix_rule(pattern=[...], decision="allow"|"prompt"|"forbidden", justification=..., match=[...], not_match=[...])`. The `match`/`not_match` examples are validated at load time as unit tests.
  - `host_executable(name="git", paths=[...])` pins which absolute binaries may match basename rules.
  - Check rule files with `codex execpolicy check`.

**Hooks** ([hooks/src](https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/main/codex-rs/hooks/src)):
- Events: `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `SessionStart`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `Stop`, `PreCompact`, `PostCompact`, `SubagentStop`, `PermissionRequest`. A second reading of the crate also lists `SessionEnd`.
- These are the Claude Code event names. Stop hooks can block with "continuation fragments" that are injected as a prompt message.

**MCP** ([Cargo.toml](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/Cargo.toml); [codex-mcp/README.md](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/codex-mcp/README.md)):
- The client uses the official Rust SDK `rmcp`, pinned `=3.5.1`.
- `codex-mcp` "manages Codex's MCP connections, tool calls, and their captured authority".
- Servers can opt into an experimental `codex/sandbox-state` capability, which delivers the sandbox policy in `_meta`.
- `codex mcp` manages external servers (list/get/add/remove/login/logout).
- In current `main` there is no top-level `mcp-server` subcommand (it existed in 2025-era versions). This was checked only against the subcommand enum.

**CLI subcommands** ([cli/src/main.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/cli/src/main.rs)): `exec` (alias `e`), `review`, `mcp`, `plugin`, `app-server`, `remote-control`, `sandbox`, `execpolicy`, `apply`, `resume`, `fork`, `queue`, `cloud`, `exec-server`.

**Headless mode: `codex exec --json`** ([exec_events.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/exec/src/exec_events.rs)) emits JSONL `ThreadEvent`s: `thread.started`, `turn.started`, `turn.completed`, `turn.failed`, `item.started`, `item.updated`, `item.completed`, `error`.

**App-server JSON-RPC** ([app-server-protocol](https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/main/codex-rs/app-server-protocol); [app-server/README.md](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/app-server/README.md)) uses a thread/turn/item model:
- Threads: `thread/start|resume|fork|read|list|search|compact/start|revert|archive`, `thread/goal/set|get|clear`, `thread/queue/*`, `thread/memory/read`.
- Turns: `turn/start`, `turn/steer`, `turn/interrupt`.
- Streamed items and approvals: `item/agentMessage/delta`, `item/commandExecution/requestApproval`, `item/fileChange/requestApproval`, `item/plan/delta`, `item/reasoning/summaryTextDelta`.
- Other: `review/start`, `skills/list`, `mcpServer/elicitation/request`.
- SDKs:
  - The TypeScript `@openai/codex-sdk` "wraps the `codex` CLI … spawns the CLI and exchanges JSONL events over stdin/stdout". Usage is `codex.startThread()` then `thread.run(...)`.
  - A Python SDK lives in `sdk/python` ([sdk/typescript/README.md](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/sdk/typescript/README.md); [sdk/](https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/main/sdk)).
  - App-server and the SDKs appear to be the supported embedding paths.

**Memories** ([memories/README.md](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/memories/README.md); [read_path.md](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/ext/memories/templates/memories/read_path.md); [stage_one_system.md](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/memories/write/templates/memories/stage_one_system.md); [consolidation.md](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/memories/write/templates/memories/consolidation.md); [config.schema.json](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/core/config.schema.json); [features/src/lib.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/features/src/lib.rs)):
- Feature status:
  - The feature flag `memories` (`Feature::MemoryTool`) is stage Stable but `default_enabled: false` at HEAD.
  - A separate `ExternalAgentMemoryImport` feature imports "project-scoped memory from external agents".
- Trigger: the pipeline runs asynchronously at root-session start, and only when the session is non-ephemeral, memory is enabled, it is not a subagent session, and the state DB is available. It processes idle rollouts (`min_rollout_idle_hours`, ">12h recommended"), gated by remaining rate limit.
- Phase 1 (per rollout, parallel):
  - It claims eligible rollouts using DB leases and filters each to memory-relevant items.
  - A model returns strict JSON `{rollout_summary, rollout_slug, raw_memory}`, or all-empty strings for a no-op.
  - Secrets are redacted to `[REDACTED_SECRET]`.
  - Outcomes are `succeeded` / `succeeded_no_output` / `failed`, with retry backoff.
  - The stage-1 prompt says "Raw rollouts are immutable evidence" and "No-op is allowed and preferred", and asks to over-index on user corrections.
- Phase 2 (one global lock):
  - It drops outputs whose `last_usage` is older than `max_unused_days` and ranks the rest by `usage_count`, then recency.
  - It syncs `raw_memories.md` and `rollout_summaries/` into the git-baselined `~/.codex/memories/` and writes `phase2_workspace_diff.md`.
  - If the diff is non-empty, it spawns a consolidation subagent (no approvals, no network, local writes only, no recursive delegation). That agent updates `MEMORY.md`, `memory_summary.md` and `skills/`. The baseline is then reset, deleting the diff so deleted content does not linger in git objects.
- Read path:
  - `memory_summary.md` is injected between `MEMORY_SUMMARY BEGINS/ENDS`.
  - The "quick memory pass" greps `MEMORY.md`, then opens 1–2 rollout summaries or skills, "ideally <= 4-6 search steps".
  - The final reply ends with an `<oai-mem-citation>` block (file line ranges plus `<rollout_ids>`). These citations drive `usage_count`/`last_usage`.
  - The main agent may edit memory only on explicit user request, by dropping a note in `extensions/ad_hoc/notes/`.
- Config keys:
  - `generate_memories`, `use_memories`
  - `extract_model`, `consolidation_model`
  - `max_raw_memories_for_consolidation` (1–4096), `max_rollouts_per_startup` (1–128), `max_rollout_age_days`
  - `disable_on_external_context`, which marks a thread's `memory_mode` as `"polluted"`
  - `version` (v1/v2), `dual_write`

**Plan Mode, goals and persistent mode:**
- Plan Mode is a "collaboration mode" that allows only non-mutating actions. It ends in a `<proposed_plan>` that must be "decision complete", and calling `update_plan` in Plan Mode returns an error ([plan.md](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/collaboration-mode-templates/templates/plan.md)).
- Thread goals (`codex-rs/ext/goal`) inject an `<objective>` (treated as "user-provided data… not as higher-priority instructions") plus the token budget on every continuation turn ([continuation.md](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/ext/goal/templates/goals/continuation.md); [budget_limit.md](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/ext/goal/templates/goals/budget_limit.md)):
  - A no-progress check runs on each turn.
  - A completion audit applies the rule "must prove completion, not merely fail to find obvious remaining work".
  - `blocked` is allowed only after the same blocker repeats for "at least three consecutive goal turns".
  - At budget exhaustion the goal moves to `budget_limited`.
- Persistent mode asks for scope, evidence and a stopping condition before any proactive follow-up, and for polling with "short, proportionate waits, often 1–3 minutes" ([persistent_mode.md](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/prompts/templates/persistent_mode.md)).

**Bundled OpenAI docs.** The `skills` crate ships sample skills that include snapshots of developers.openai.com, for example `upgrading-to-gpt-6-astra.md` (GPT-6 Astra / 6.1 Sol / 6 Sol / Luna; `reasoning.effort` low…max; `configuration_update` items to change effort without breaking the cache) and `prompting-guide.md` ([upgrading-to-gpt-6-astra.md](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/skills/src/assets/samples/openai-docs/references/upgrading-to-gpt-6-astra.md); [prompting-guide.md](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/skills/src/assets/samples/openai-docs/references/prompting-guide.md)). Treat them as near-primary.

**Notable design decisions:**
- **Grammar-constrained edits.** The edit tool is grammar-constrained freeform text, not JSON.
- **Interactive shell.** The shell is a PTY session (`exec_command` + `write_stdin`), not one-shot subprocesses.
- **Stateless API.** `store:false` plus encrypted-reasoning replay keeps the API ZDR-compatible.
- **Two compaction paths.** Compaction runs either locally or on the server, and both paths fire hooks.
- **Policy above the sandbox.** Policy (execpolicy prefix rules, approval-policy templates, the guardian LLM reviewer) is layered above the OS sandbox and kept separate from it.
- **One protocol for every UI.** Every UI sits on one JSON-RPC protocol.
- **Tuned per model.** System prompts are tuned per model.
- **Main agent cannot write memory.** Memory is written only by a background, idle-gated pipeline, never by the main agent.
- **Model co-design.** Secondary coverage of OpenAI's "harness engineering" post says "Codex models are trained in the presence of the harness" **(secondary)**. GPT-5.1-Codex-Max was "trained to run across several context windows via compaction" **(secondary)**.

**What to copy:**
- The `apply_patch` grammar, the `seek_sequence` fallback chain and the streaming parser. The same envelope has been adopted by OpenCode, the Agents SDK, gpt-oss, OpenHands and Aider, so it is becoming a de facto cross-vendor format.
- The app-server thread/turn/item protocol, which includes `turn/steer`, `turn/interrupt`, item-level approval requests and delta streams. It is the most complete open spec for a UI-agnostic harness/client boundary.
- The `exec --json` JSONL event schema, for headless use.
- The compaction recipe: a handoff-summary prompt, 20k tokens of retained user messages, re-inserted initial context, and a 90% trigger.
- The `SandboxPolicy` with protected subpaths, the network proxy with private-IP blocking, and Starlark exec policy with inline tests.
- The goal-continuation audit templates.
- The two-phase memory pipeline with citation-driven forgetting.

**Caveats:**
- developers.openai.com was blocked; the in-repo `docs/*.md` are mostly stubs pointing there. The execpolicy rule syntax above was read from the crate README, not the docs.
- The release date of `rust-v0.166.0` is unverified because the Releases API was blocked.
- OpenAI's "Unrolling the Codex agent loop" (Michael Bolin, 2026-01-23) could not be read. Secondary summaries say the old prompt must be an exact prefix of the new one for caching, dynamic MCP tool lists can break that prefix, and compaction invalidates the cached prefix **(secondary)** ([all-ai.de](https://www.all-ai.de/news/beitrage2026/codex-agent-loop); [danielvaughan](https://codex.danielvaughan.com/2026/04/21/codex-cli-prompt-caching-maximise-cache-hits-cost-reduction/)).
- Harness-model coupling is real:
  - GPT-5.2-Codex reportedly scored 64.7% in the Codex CLI versus 57.5% in Terminus-2 on Terminal-Bench **(secondary)** ([particula](https://particula.tech/blog/agent-scaffolding-beats-model-upgrades-swe-bench)).
  - GPT-5.3-Codex reportedly tries to call a non-existent `apply_patch` in harnesses that lack it **(secondary)** ([zenn.dev](https://zenn.dev/c_c/articles/188a9bef9f3290?locale=en)).
  - A third-party claim says Codex-tuned models need `apply_patch`/V4A emulation in other harnesses **(secondary)** ([danielvaughan](https://codex.danielvaughan.com/2026/04/28/codex-models-third-party-harnesses-apply-patch-v4a-portable-agent/)).

#### 12.2.2 openai/openai-agents-python and openai/openai-agents-js

**Purpose.** These are OpenAI's general-purpose agent SDKs. They describe themselves as "provider-agnostic, supporting the OpenAI Responses and Chat Completions APIs, as well as 100+ other LLMs". The core concepts are:
- Agents, Sandbox agents, Realtime agents and Voice
- Agents-as-tools and Handoffs
- Tools (function, MCP, hosted)
- Guardrails, Human in the loop, Sessions and Tracing

([README](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/main/README.md)). Python is at `v0.24.0` (last commit 2026-10-30, ~30.5k stars) and JS at `v0.21.0` (last commit 2026-11-02).

**Architecture: the Runner loop** ([running_agents.md](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/main/docs/running_agents.md)):
- Entry points are `Runner.run()`, `run_sync()` and `run_streamed()`. Each turn calls the LLM and then classifies the output:
  - A **final output** ("text output with the desired type, and there are no tool calls") ends the loop.
  - A **handoff** switches the current agent and re-runs.
  - **Tool calls** are run, their results appended, and the loop re-runs.
- Input can be a string, Responses-format items, or a `RunState` when resuming a paused run.
- Budgets and errors:
  - `max_turns` overflow raises `MaxTurnsExceeded`; `max_turns=None` disables it.
  - `error_handlers` keys `"max_turns"`, `"model_refusal"` and `"invalid_final_output"` can return fallback outputs instead of raising.
  - `tool_not_found_behavior` defaults to raising `ModelBehaviorError` and can be set to `"return_error_to_model"`.
  - `ToolExecutionConfig.max_function_tool_concurrency` caps tool concurrency; `ModelSettings.timeout` / `ToolTimeoutError` handle timeouts.
  - `reasoning_item_id_policy` is `"preserve"` (the default) or `"omit"`. `"omit"` mitigates "Responses API 400 errors caused by a reasoning item that lacks its required following item".
- Conversation state lives in exactly one of these, which are mutually exclusive: client-side `to_input_list()`, an SDK session, a server `conversation_id`, or `previous_response_id` chaining.

**Key files and modules:**
- **Loop internals** in [src/agents/run_internal](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/tree/main/src/agents/run_internal): `run_loop.py`, `turn_preparation.py`, `turn_resolution.py`, `tool_planning.py`, `tool_execution.py`, `approvals.py`, `guardrails.py`, `session_persistence.py`, `prompt_cache_key.py`, `model_retry.py`, `streaming.py`.
- **Handoffs:**
  - Handoffs are exposed to the model as tools named `transfer_to_{agent.name}` ([handoffs/__init__.py](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/main/src/agents/handoffs/__init__.py)).
  - `Agent.as_tool()` is the manager-keeps-control alternative.
  - The docs recommend code orchestration for predictability: structured-output routing, chaining, evaluator `while` loops and `asyncio.gather` (examples in `examples/agent_patterns`) ([multi_agent.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/openai-agents-python/main/docs/multi_agent.md)).
  - Rule of thumb from third-party guides: "if the specialist owns the answer, handoff; if the manager owns the answer, tool" **(secondary)**.
- **Guardrails:**
  - `InputGuardrail` / `OutputGuardrail` return `GuardrailFunctionOutput(tripwire_triggered=…)`, and a tripwire halts execution ([guardrail.py](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/main/src/agents/guardrail.py)).
  - Tool-level guardrails live in `tool_guardrails.py`.
  - HITL: approval pauses the run, and `RunResult.interruptions` holds `ToolApprovalItem`s. Hosted-MCP sticky decisions are keyed by `server_label` + tool name ([PR #4280](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/pull/4280/files)).
  - A vendor claims guardrails do not cover hosted tools, MCP or computer/shell **(vendor claim; unverified)** ([Arcjet](https://arcjet.com/compare/openai-agents-guardrails-vs-arcjet)).
- **Sessions:**
  - The protocol is `get_items`, `add_items`, `pop_item`, `clear_session`. `SessionSettings(limit=N)` caps history, and `RunConfig.session_input_callback` customizes how history and new input merge.
  - Backends: `SQLiteSession`, `AsyncSQLiteSession`, `RedisSession`, `SQLAlchemySession`, `MongoDBSession`, `DaprSession`, `OpenAIConversationsSession`, `AdvancedSQLiteSession` (branching/analytics) and `EncryptedSession`.
  - `OpenAIResponsesCompactionSession` is a decorator that "triggers responses.compact when stored history grows" (`should_trigger_compaction`; Responses-API models only).
  - Sources: [sessions docs](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/main/docs/sessions/index.md); [openai_responses_compaction_session.py](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/main/src/agents/memory/openai_responses_compaction_session.py).
- **Tracing.** `tracing/` holds spans, traces, processors and the provider. It exports to the OpenAI Traces dashboard by default and records model calls, tool calls, handoffs, guardrails and custom spans. A `withTrace` helper groups runs, and processors can export to Braintrust and others ([src/agents/tracing](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/tree/main/src/agents/tracing); the observability guide comes via a blocked host **(secondary)**).
- **SandboxAgent (new in 2026)** ([sandbox_agents.md](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/main/docs/sandbox_agents.md); [src/agents/sandbox](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/tree/main/src/agents/sandbox); [extensions/sandbox](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/tree/main/src/agents/extensions/sandbox)):
  - A `SandboxAgent` takes:
    - a `Manifest` of workspace entries (`GitRepo`, `LocalDir`)
    - `capabilities`: `Capabilities.default()` plus `Skills(lazy_from=…)`
    - `SandboxRunConfig(client=UnixLocalSandboxClient()|DockerSandboxClient|hosted)`
  - It provides "file staging, filesystem tools, shell access, sandbox lifecycle, snapshots".
  - Capability modules are `compaction.py`, `filesystem.py`, `memory.py`, `shell.py` and `skills.py`, plus `apply_patch.py`, `snapshot.py` and `manifest.py`.
  - Hosted extensions: `e2b`, `modal`, `daytona`, `cloudflare`, `vercel`, `blaxel`.
  - Warning: UnixLocal "adds no OS-level confinement" on Linux.
- **Sandbox `Memory()` capability** ([sandbox memory docs](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/main/docs/sandbox/memory.md)):
  - It mirrors the Codex pipeline. Generation runs at sandbox-session close in two phases.
  - Layout: `sessions/<rollout-id>.jsonl` plus `memories/{memory_summary.md, MEMORY.md, raw_memories.md, phase_two_selection.json, raw_memories/, rollout_summaries/, skills/}`.
  - Requires `Shell()`. `live_update` (on by default) requires `Filesystem()`.
  - `MemoryGenerateConfig(max_raw_memories_for_consolidation=256)` keeps the newest memories; this is the forgetting mechanism.
  - `Memory(generate=None)` gives read-only memory for subagents and checkers. Isolation is by `MemoryLayoutConfig`, not by agent name.
- **JS SDK.** The same concept set in a monorepo of `agents`, `agents-core`, `agents-openai`, `agents-extensions` and `agents-realtime`, running on Node 22+, Deno and Bun ([openai-agents-js README](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-js/blob/main/README.md)).
- **Durable execution.** The Temporal integration (Python public preview 2025-07-30, GA 2026-03-23) runs agents inside a Temporal Workflow, with each model invocation as an Activity. It is enabled with `OpenAIAgentsPlugin`, `activity_as_tool` exposes Activities as durable tools, and a TypeScript version also exists ([Temporal blog](https://temporal.io/blog/announcing-openai-agents-sdk-integration); [demos](https://github.com/temporal-community/openai-agents-demos)).

**Notable design decisions.** Handoffs are a third output class in the core loop, alongside final output and tool calls. Guardrails are tripwires, not filters. Provider-side compaction (`responses.compact`) is wrapped as a session decorator. SandboxAgent is OpenAI's answer to the Claude Agent SDK's "give the agent a computer" model.

**What to copy.** For non-coding agent apps, copy the `run_internal/` split (preparation, resolution, planning, execution, approvals, persistence), the `transfer_to_*` handoff convention, tripwire guardrails, the Session protocol, and the Manifest/Capabilities/Client decomposition for sandboxed workspaces.

**Caveats:**
- openai.github.io was blocked, so `handoff_input_filter`/`nest_handoff_history` details and tracing span types were not verified.
- AgentKit's visual Agent Builder (launched DevDay Oct 2025) reportedly received deprecation notices on 2026-06-03, with shutdown on 2026-11-30. Sources disagree on the dates **(secondary)** ([osher.com.au](https://osher.com.au/blog/openai-agentkit/); [timewell.jp](https://timewell.jp/en/columns/agent-builder)).
- The JS SDK's license and star count were not captured.

#### 12.2.3 openai/swarm (deprecated)

**Status.** The README reads: "Swarm is now replaced by the OpenAI Agents SDK … We recommend migrating to the Agents SDK for all production use cases." It is described as "experimental, educational" and runs almost entirely client-side and stateless ([swarm README](https://github.com/openai/swarm/blob/main/README.md)).

**What to copy.** Nothing for production. Its ideas (agents plus handoff functions) live on as Agents SDK handoffs. Swarm's history and the Agents SDK launch date were not verified against a primary source.

#### 12.2.4 openai/harmony and openai/gpt-oss

**Purpose.** Harmony is the response format gpt-oss was trained on. gpt-oss ships the reference tools and servers for the open-weight models.

**Harmony format** (latest tag `v0.0.8`) ([harmony README](https://github.com/openai/harmony/blob/main/README.md)):
- Roles: `system` / `developer` / `user` / `assistant`.
- Channels: `analysis` / `commentary` / `final`. Function calls go to `commentary`.
- Tools are declared TypeScript-style: `namespace functions { type f = (_: {...}) => any; }`.
- Special tokens: `<|start|>…<|message|>…<|end|>`.
- A Rust core with Python bindings does loss-free render/parse.

**gpt-oss** (`v0.0.9`, last commit 2026-10-29) ([gpt-oss README](https://github.com/openai/gpt-oss/blob/main/README.md); [gpt_oss/tools](https://github.com/openai/gpt-oss/tree/main/gpt_oss/tools)):
- Reference tools the models were trained on:
  - `gpt_oss/tools/simple_browser`
  - `python_docker`, a stateless Python tool
  - `apply_patch.py` / `apply_patch.md`
- A terminal chat: `python -m gpt_oss.chat … -a` enables apply_patch.
- A Responses-API-compatible example server: `gpt_oss/responses_api`.
- The README states the models "should only be used with this format".
- AWS Bedrock added open-weight GPT-OSS-20B for RFT in Feb 2026 **(secondary)** ([AWS ML blog](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/reinforcement-fine-tuning-on-amazon-bedrock-with-openai-compatible-apis-a-technical-walkthrough/)).

**What to copy.** If you serve gpt-oss, use harmony for rendering and parsing; never hand-roll the template. Ship the trained-on tools (`apply_patch`, the browser, stateless Python) with their exact descriptions.

**Caveats.** Star counts and licenses for harmony and gpt-oss were not captured.

### 12.3 Anthropic

Anthropic's harness itself, Claude Code, is not open source. The repo is licensed under "Commercial Terms of Service", "All rights reserved". What Anthropic does open-source is the scaffolding around it. On Sep 29, 2025 the Claude Code SDK was renamed the Claude Agent SDK, because "the agent harness that powers Claude Code" now powers "almost all of [Anthropic's] major agent loops". The loop is described as "gather context -> take action -> verify work -> repeat", under the principle "give your agents a computer" ([Claude blog](https://claude.com/blog/building-agents-with-the-claude-agent-sdk)).

#### 12.3.1 anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python (MIT) and claude-agent-sdk-typescript (Commercial Terms)

**Purpose.** These SDKs embed the Claude Code agent loop in a host application.
- Python: `v0.2.177`, last commit 2026-11-03, ~8.4k stars, LICENSE MIT.
- TypeScript: `v0.3.317`. Its LICENSE.md reads "© Anthropic PBC. All rights reserved. Use is subject to Anthropic's Commercial Terms of Service".

Sources: [python LICENSE](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python/blob/main/LICENSE); [TS LICENSE.md](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-typescript/blob/main/LICENSE.md).

**Architecture: the CLI transport plus a control protocol:**
- "The Claude Code CLI is automatically bundled with the package." The SDK uses the bundled CLI by default, or a custom `cli_path` ([README](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python/blob/main/README.md)).
- There are two entry points:
  - `query()`, one-shot
  - `ClaudeSDKClient`, bidirectional, which enables custom tools and hooks
- The SDK is a single transport, `_internal/transport/subprocess_cli.py`, plus `_internal/query.py`. The query layer writes `control_request` JSON lines to the CLI and handles inbound control requests with these subtypes ([_internal/query.py](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python/blob/main/src/claude_agent_sdk/_internal/query.py)):
  - `initialize`
  - `can_use_tool` (the permission callback)
  - `hook_callback`
  - `mcp_message`, which routes to in-process SDK MCP servers
- Custom tools are in-process MCP servers built with `@tool` and `create_sdk_mcp_server()`. The README lists "No subprocess management … No IPC overhead … Single Python process" as the benefits.
- `allowed_tools` pre-approves tools; it "does not control tool availability".
- Loop semantics, from the agent-loop docs:
  - `ResultMessage.subtype` is one of `success`, `error_max_turns`, `error_max_budget_usd`, `error_during_execution` or `error_max_structured_output_retries`. Each carries `total_cost_usd`, `usage`, `num_turns` and `session_id`.
  - `stop_reason` is `end_turn`, `max_tokens` or `refusal`, and `null` after a crash.
  - Read-only tools (`Read`, `Glob`, `Grep`, read-only MCP tools) run concurrently. State-modifying tools (`Edit`, `Write`, `Bash`) run sequentially. Custom tools are sequential unless they set `readOnlyHint`.
  - A denied tool call comes back to Claude "as the tool result".
  - Source: [agent-loop docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/agent-loop).

**Key types** ([types.py](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python/blob/main/src/claude_agent_sdk/types.py)):
- **`HookEvent`:** `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `PostToolUseFailure`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `Stop`, `SubagentStop`, `PreCompact`, `Notification`, `SubagentStart`, `PermissionRequest`. To block a call, a hook returns `hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision: "deny"` with a reason.
- **Permission modes:** `default`, `acceptEdits`, `plan`, `bypassPermissions`, `dontAsk`, `auto`.
- **Subagents:** `AgentDefinition(description, prompt, tools, disallowedTools, model, skills, memory: user|project|local, mcpServers, initialPrompt, maxTurns, background, effort, permissionMode)`.
- **`ClaudeAgentOptions`** fields:
  - tools and permissions: `tools`, `allowed_tools`, `disallowed_tools`, `permission_mode`, `can_use_tool`
  - prompt, extensions and config: `system_prompt`, `mcp_servers`, `hooks`, `agents`, `setting_sources`, `skills`, `sandbox`, `plugins`
  - budgets and model: `max_turns`, `max_budget_usd`, `task_budget`, `fallback_model`, `thinking`, `effort`
  - output and sessions: `output_format`, `enable_file_checkpointing`, `session_store`, `fork_session`, `resume`, `include_partial_messages`
- **Examples** ([examples/](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python/tree/main/examples)): `agents.py`, `filesystem_agents.py`, `hooks.py`, `tool_permission_callback.py`, `mcp_calculator.py`, `max_budget_usd.py`, `plugin_example.py`, `session_stores/`, `setting_sources.py`, `streaming_mode*.py`.
- **File checkpointing** tracks only Write/Edit/NotebookEdit changes, not Bash side effects ([SDK file checkpointing](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/file-checkpointing)).

**Notable design decisions:**
- The harness is a subprocess and the SDK is a protocol client.
- Host policy (`can_use_tool`), hooks and tools are callbacks over the same NDJSON channel, which cleanly separates the agent loop from host-supplied policy.

**What to copy:**
- The control-protocol shape: newline-delimited JSON plus `control_request`/`control_response`, with `can_use_tool`, `hook_callback` and `mcp_message` callbacks into the host.
- In-process MCP for custom tools.
- The `ResultMessage` termination enum.

**Caveats:**
- Because the TypeScript SDK is under Commercial Terms, only the Python SDK can be forked.
- Both SDKs drive a closed CLI.

#### 12.3.2 anthropics/claude-code (closed product; the repo holds issues, changelog, examples and plugin/mod sources)

**Status.** ~154.3k stars; tag `v2.1.317`. LICENSE.md reads "© Anthropic PBC. All rights reserved … Commercial Terms of Service" ([LICENSE.md](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/main/LICENSE.md)).

**Key contents:**
- **Plugins.** Official plugins have moved to [anthropics/claude-plugins-official](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-plugins-official). Plugins bundle "custom slash commands, specialized agents, hooks, and MCP servers" and install via `/plugin` marketplaces ([plugins/README.md](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/main/plugins/README.md)).
- **Mods (new).** A mod is a plugin whose behaviour is a hooks module with `register(on, options)`, which hooks engine events as `($, e, next)` middleware ([mods/README.md](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/main/mods/README.md)). Four built-in mods ship as source:
  - `sec-default` shields managed policy from user-installed plugins.
  - `diff`.
  - `telemetry`.
  - `agents-md` has four modes:
    - load AGENTS.md where no CLAUDE.md exists (the default, `claude-md-or-agents-md`)
    - load it beside CLAUDE.md (`claude-md-and-agents-md`)
    - `managed-only`
    - `claude-md` only
- **AGENTS.md behaviour per the Claude Code docs.** With only AGENTS.md present, it reads AGENTS.md. With both present, it reads CLAUDE.md only, unless CLAUDE.md imports `@AGENTS.md`. This is configurable via the "Project instructions" setting ([Claude Code memory docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory)).
- **Example settings** ([examples/](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/tree/main/examples)):
  - configurations for strict, lax, bash-sandbox and HIPAA setups (`settings-strict.json`, `settings-bash-sandbox.json`, `managed-mcp-hipaa.json`)
  - the hook example `bash_command_validator_example.py`
- **Changelog `v2.1.317`** mentions ([CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)):
  - Agent SDK hook callbacks `onFailure: "block"`
  - auto mode, agent teams, background agents, `/loop` and `/schedule`
  - compaction fixes ("Fixed very long conversations losing their earlier summary when compaction had to shorten its own request")
  - OTel attributes
- **Hooks beyond the SDK enum.** The docs list `PermissionDenied` (auto-mode denials) and the agent-team quality gates `TaskCompleted` / `TeammateIdle`; exit code 2 blocks and sends feedback ([hooks reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks); [agent teams](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams)). The exact `permissionDecision` schema in the CLI docs was not verified.
- **Telemetry.** `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1` turns it on:
  - Exporters: `OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER` / `OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER` (`otlp`, `console`, `prometheus`).
  - Metrics: `claude_code.cost.usage` and `claude_code.token.usage`, labeled by `token.type`.
  - The default export interval is 60,000 ms.
  - Source: [monitoring docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/monitoring-usage?m=1).

**claude-plugins-official: `ralph-loop`** ([plugins/ralph-loop](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-plugins-official/tree/main/plugins/ralph-loop)):
- It reimplements Huntley's "Ralph is a Bash loop" inside a session. A **Stop hook** blocks exit and feeds the same prompt back, so "Claude's previous work persists in files" and git.
- Usage: `/ralph-loop "<prompt>" --max-iterations <n> --completion-promise "<text>"`. Cancel with `/cancel-ralph`.
- State lives in `.claude/ralph-loop.local.md`, with frontmatter `max_iterations`, `completion_promise` and `session_id`.
- The hook reads the last assistant text block from `transcript_path` and looks for `<promise>…</promise>`.

**What to copy:**
- The mods middleware signature.
- The `agents-md` loading modes.
- The example managed settings as templates for enterprise policy.
- The Stop-hook re-feed loop, as the simplest outer loop.

**Caveats.**
- The core is closed: the system prompt, the built-in tool implementations (Edit/MultiEdit/TodoWrite/Task) and the compaction thresholds. No primary source for its internal tool schemas was inspected.
- You cannot fork the harness. You can only use it via the SDK or replicate its open interfaces (hooks, skills, settings, plugins, AGENTS.md).

#### 12.3.3 anthropics/skills (Agent Skills)

**Purpose and format:**
- ~186.8k stars. Skills are "folders of instructions, scripts, and resources that Claude loads dynamically".
- Each skill has a `SKILL.md` with YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`), followed by markdown instructions loaded when relevant. Optional `scripts/`, `references/` and `assets/` folders can sit alongside it.
- The spec has moved: "The spec is now located at https://agentskills.io/specification".
- The repo installs as a plugin marketplace: `/plugin marketplace add anthropics/skills`.
- Sources: [README](https://github.com/anthropics/skills/blob/main/README.md); [spec/agent-skills-spec.md](https://github.com/anthropics/skills/blob/main/spec/agent-skills-spec.md); [template/SKILL.md](https://github.com/anthropics/skills/blob/main/template/SKILL.md).

**Licensing.** Many skills are Apache-2.0. The document skills (docx/pdf/pptx/xlsx) are source-available.

**History and adoption:**
- Skills launched Oct 16, 2025 and became an open standard on Dec 18, 2025.
- Reported adopters include OpenAI Codex, GitHub Copilot, VS Code, Cursor and Gemini CLI. Roughly 40–44 clients were listed on agentskills.io by mid-2026, and one analysis found that 22% of 673 sampled skills failed structural validation **(secondary; counts unverified)** ([Atlan](https://atlan.com/know/ai-agent/ai-agent-skills/what-are-agent-skills/); [aictrl.dev](https://aictrl.dev/blog/skill-md-adoption-trajectory)).

**What to copy.** Use SKILL.md as the capability-packaging format: progressive disclosure, where frontmatter is always loaded and the body is loaded on demand. Use the marketplace layout for distribution. Validate skills structurally at install time.

#### 12.3.4 anthropic-experimental/sandbox-runtime (`srt`, Apache-2.0, "Beta Research Preview")

**Purpose.** `srt` provides "filesystem and network restrictions on arbitrary processes at the OS level, without requiring a container". It runs as a CLI or a library (npm `@anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime`) and can wrap MCP servers (`"command": "srt"`). Tag `v0.0.81`, last commit 2026-10-25 ([README](https://github.com/anthropic-experimental/sandbox-runtime/blob/main/README.md)).

**Mechanisms:**
- **macOS:** `sandbox-exec` with dynamically generated Seatbelt profiles. The profile allows only one localhost proxy port.
- **Linux:** bubblewrap with the network namespace removed entirely. All traffic goes through host HTTP and SOCKS5 proxies on bind-mounted Unix sockets; this needs `bwrap` and `socat`.
- **Windows (alpha):** runs as a dedicated `srt-sandbox` user with a WFP egress filter keyed on its SID, a write-restricted token and ACEs.

**Policy semantics:**
- **Reads** are allowed by default, using deny-then-allow. `allowRead` beats `denyRead`, but a more-specific deny such as `**/.env` stays denied.
- **Writes** are allow-only, and `denyWrite` beats `allowWrite`.
- **Network:** "By default, all network access is denied". It is configured with `allowedDomains`, `deniedDomains`, `allowUnixSockets` and `allowLocalBinding`. HTTP(S) goes through an HTTP proxy and other TCP through SOCKS5, both enforcing the domain allowlists.
- **Other knobs:** `ignoreViolations`, `enableWeakerNestedSandbox`, `allowNestedUserNamespaces`, `enableWeakerNetworkIsolation`, `allowAppleEvents`.
- **Violations** are attributed by `commandId`. An ask-callback can deny with a reason, and that reason is surfaced to the model in a `<sandbox_violations>` block.
- **Control:** `--control-fd` allows live config updates, and `srt proxy` mode works with an external decider.

**Notable design decisions.** No container is needed. Network is denied by default, with a domain allowlist enforced through a local proxy. Violations feed back to the model. The example config denies reads of sensitive paths such as `~/.ssh`. Anthropic measured an 84% reduction in permission prompts from sandboxing ([Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/claude-code-sandboxing)).

**What to copy.** Treat it as the most reusable open-source container-free OS sandbox for agent bash and local MCP servers, and use it directly as a library.

**Caveats.** It is a Beta Research Preview, and Windows support is alpha.

#### 12.3.5 anthropics/claude-code-action

**Purpose.** A GitHub Action (tag `v1.0.267`) that runs Claude Code on your own runner. It works in two ways:
- It responds to `@claude` mentions and issue assignments.
- It runs explicit automation through unified `prompt` and `claude_args` inputs.

It auto-detects its mode, tracks progress with checkboxes, and supports structured JSON outputs. Source is under `src/{modes,mcp,github,create-prompt,entrypoints}` ([README](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action/blob/main/README.md); [src/](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action/tree/main/src)).

**What to copy.** Mode auto-detection (mention, assignment, automation), checkbox progress comments, and structured outputs for CI integration.

#### 12.3.6 anthropics/claude-quickstarts (reference harnesses)

**`autonomous-coding/`** is "a minimal harness demonstrating long-running autonomous coding with the Claude Agent SDK" ([autonomous-coding/README.md](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-quickstarts/blob/main/autonomous-coding/README.md)):
- **Initializer agent:** writes `feature_list.json` (200 test cases), `init.sh` and a git repo.
- **Coding agent:** runs fresh-context sessions that resume from `feature_list.json`, `claude-progress.txt` and git commits, and auto-continues.
- **Security** is defense in depth:
  - an OS sandbox
  - a filesystem restricted to the project directory
  - a bash allowlist enforced by a security hook (`security.py`)

**`agents/`** is "a minimal educational implementation of LLM agents using the Claude API … NOT an SDK": tools in a loop plus MCP ([agents/README.md](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-quickstarts/blob/main/agents/README.md)).

**`managed-agents/`** holds apps built on "Claude Managed Agents: agents Anthropic runs for you, with server-side sessions, sandboxed tools, and an event stream your app consumes" ([managed-agents/README.md](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-quickstarts/blob/main/managed-agents/README.md)):
- Examples cover assistant-ui, the Vercel Chat SDK, AG-UI/CopilotKit, Slack, Linear, Sentry autofix and self-hosted sandboxes.
- Bash can be set to `always_ask`, with resumable approval gates.
- **Background on the hosted architecture** (Managed Agents engineering post, Apr 8, 2026; docs, not the repo):
  - **Session** is "an append-only event log". **Harness** is the loop. **Sandbox** is the execution environment.
  - The interfaces are `execute(name, input) → string`, `provision({resources})`, `wake(sessionId)`, `getSession(id)`, `emitEvent(id, event)` and `getEvents()`.
  - Provisioning sandboxes lazily cut p50 TTFT by about 60% and p95 by more than 90%.
  - Compaction is always on and emits `agent.thread_context_compacted`.
  - Sources: [Managed Agents](https://anthropic.com/engineering/managed-agents); [compaction docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/compaction-threshold).

**What to copy.** The two-agent long-running pattern: a feature list as ground truth, a progress file, git checkpoints and fresh context per session. It is the canonical open reference for multi-session work and is model-agnostic in principle. Also copy the session/harness/sandbox split for hosted deployments.

**Caveats.** No separately published Anthropic "long-running agent harness" repo was found beyond `claude-quickstarts/autonomous-coding`. Some material may exist only on the engineering blog.

#### 12.3.7 anthropics/claude-cookbooks

**Key notebooks:**
- `tool_use/context_engineering/context_engineering_tools.ipynb` compares compaction, tool-result clearing and memory as levers against "context rot" ([notebook](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-cookbooks/blob/main/tool_use/context_engineering/context_engineering_tools.ipynb)).
- `tool_use/automatic-context-compaction.ipynb` uses the Python SDK tool runner's `runner.compact_before_next_turn()` to "summarize the history server-side" ([notebook](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-cookbooks/blob/main/tool_use/automatic-context-compaction.ipynb)).
- `misc/session_memory_compaction.ipynb` builds session memory proactively in the background for "instant compaction", using threading plus prompt caching. It claims about 80% lower cost for the background updates ([notebook](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-cookbooks/blob/main/misc/session_memory_compaction.ipynb)).
- `tool_use/memory_cookbook.ipynb` with `memory_tool.py`, a client-side implementation of the memory tool.
- `programmatic_tool_calling_ptc.ipynb` and `tool_search_with_embeddings.ipynb`.
- `patterns/agents/`: workflows, orchestrator-workers, evaluator-optimizer and async multi-agent.
- `claude_agent_sdk/` notebooks 00–08: research, chief-of-staff, observability, SRE, migrating from the OpenAI Agents SDK, session browser, hosting and dynamic workflows.

Sources: [tool_use/](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-cookbooks/tree/main/tool_use); [claude_agent_sdk/](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-cookbooks/tree/main/claude_agent_sdk); [patterns/agents](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-cookbooks/tree/main/patterns/agents).

**What to copy.** Use `memory_tool.py` as a client-side memory-tool backend. Use the session-memory-compaction notebook to avoid compaction latency. The OpenAI-to-Claude migration notebook works as a concept map between the two SDKs.

**Caveats.** The cookbook's multi-agent prompt texts were not fetched. Star counts for sandbox-runtime, claude-code-action, the cookbooks and the quickstarts were not fetched.

### 12.4 DeepSeek

DeepSeek publishes four kinds of artifacts:
- MIT model and inference code
- kernels (FlashMLA, DeepGEMM, DeepEP, plus TileLang examples)
- Python "encoding" reference scripts for its chat formats, on Hugging Face
- API compatibility layers

Its agent strategy is to train for third-party harnesses and to serve them compatible endpoints. huggingface.co, api-docs.deepseek.com and arxiv.org were all blocked, so **every V3.2/V4 template and API detail below comes from search summaries unless it is marked as repo-read**.

#### 12.4.1 Model and kernel repos

**`deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp`** (MIT; last commit 2025-11-18; repo-read) ([README](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp/blob/main/README.md)):
- V3.2-Exp "builds upon V3.1-Terminus by introducing DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA)".
- Kernels:
  - indexer logit kernels in DeepGEMM (PR 200)
  - sparse attention kernels in FlashMLA (PR 98)
  - readable TileLang kernels in `tile-ai/tilelang/examples/deepseek_v32`
- SGLang and vLLM had day-0 support.
- The inference demo is `inference/{model.py,kernel.py,generate.py,convert.py,config_671B_v3.2.json}`, launched via torchrun ([inference/README.md](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp/blob/main/inference/README.md)).
- 2025-11-17 bug disclosure: the RoPE layout in the DSA indexer must be **non-interleaved**, while MLA RoPE is interleaved.

Agentic benchmarks from the V3.2-Exp README:

| Benchmark | V3.1-Terminus | V3.2-Exp |
| :--- | :---: | :---: |
| BrowseComp | 38.5 | 40.1 |
| SWE Verified | 68.4 | 67.8 |
| SWE-bench Multilingual | 57.8 | 57.9 |
| Terminal-bench | 36.7 | 37.7 |
| Aider-Polyglot | 76.1 | 74.5 |

**Repo landscape** (from `git ls-remote` probes against [github.com/deepseek-ai](https://github.com/deepseek-ai)):
- `github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2` resolves to the same HEAD as V3.2-Exp (`87e509a`).
- Probes for `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4`, `DeepSeek-V4-Pro`, `DeepSeek-V3.1` and `DeepSeek-Agent` returned no public repo.
- Existing repos include FlashMLA, DeepGEMM, DeepEP, 3FS, DualPipe, smallpond, Engram, DeepSeek-OCR, DeepSeek-Math-V2, DeepSeek-Prover-V2 and awesome-deepseek-integration.

**DSA, from the V3.2 report and secondary write-ups:**
- DSA is the only architectural change in V3.2 and was introduced through continued training.
- A "lightning indexer" selects the top-2048 key-value entries per query (`index_topk` default 2048).
- Training used a 2.1B-token dense warm-up of the indexer, then 943.7B tokens of sparse training.
- Core attention is O(L·k).
- Top-k selection is lossy, with roughly 60% overlap.

Sources: [arXiv 2512.02556](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.02556) (via search); [AMD](https://www.amd.com/en/developer/resources/technical-articles/2025/amd-instinct-mi335x-gpu-supports-deepseek-v3-2-exp.html); [Raschka](https://www.sebastianraschka.com/llm-architecture-gallery/deepseek-sparse-attention/). **(secondary)**

**V3.2 agentic post-training, from the tech report via search summaries (secondary):**
- 1,827 synthesized task-oriented environments and 85,000+ complex prompts, designed to be "hard to solve but easy to verify".
- Tens of thousands of reproducible issue-resolution environments mined from GitHub issue/PR pairs.
- GRPO stabilizers: an unbiased KL estimate, off-policy sequence masking, Keep Routing and Keep Sampling Mask.
- Release-time numbers (recalled and unverified): SWE-bench Verified ~73.1, Terminal Bench 2.0 ~46.4, BrowseComp ~51.4 (~67.6 with context management), tau2 ~80.3.

#### 12.4.2 Chat templates and encoders

**V3.2** (from mirrors of the HF model card, because the official page was blocked; search-summarized and unverified) ([HF mirror](https://huggingface.co/Deniss8686/DeepSeek-V3.2); [official commit page](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2/commit/ecea77f188a446a72e5edbc4b41de9c3764be7f0)):
- It introduced "a revised format for tool calling and … 'thinking with tools'".
- An `encoding/` folder holds Python scripts and tests with `encode_messages` and `parse_message_from_completion_text`.
- Configuration: `encode_config = dict(thinking_mode="thinking", drop_thinking=True, add_default_bos_token=True)`.
- A `developer` role exists "only for search-agent scenarios" and is not accepted by the official API.
- The parser "is designed to handle well-formatted strings only".
- V3.2-Speciale does not support tool calling ([SGLang cookbook](https://cookbook.sglang.io/autoregressive/DeepSeek/DeepSeek-V3_2)).
- Thinking retention in tool loops:
  - Historical reasoning is discarded **only when a new user message arrives**. Appended tool outputs keep it, and tool calls and results always stay in context.
  - The report warns that frameworks which simulate tool calls through user messages will trigger the discard. It names Roo Code and Terminus.
  - Source: [arXiv 2512.02556](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.02556) via snippet; consistent with the [Cline blog](https://cline.bot/blog/deepseek-v3-2-and-v3-2-speciale-are-now-available-in-cline).

**V4** (search-summarized from the HF `encoding/README.md` of the V4 repos; unverified) ([V4-Pro-DSpark encoding README](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-DSpark/raw/main/encoding/README.md); [V4-Flash encoding](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash/blob/main/encoding/README.md)):
