- Thinking mode emits reasoning before tool calls or answers. Chat mode closes the thinking block immediately.
- `drop_thinking` defaults to True but is **automatically disabled when tools are defined**, so tool-calling conversations keep the full reasoning.
- Tool calls use a DSML `tool_calls` block with named invoke/parameter elements. `string="false"` marks JSON-typed parameters.
- Tool results are wrapped in `tool_result` tags inside user messages.
- Three reasoning-effort levels are set as text prefixes.
- The reference file is `encoding_dsv4.py`.

#### 12.4.3 API compatibility

**Anthropic-format endpoint** (from search summaries of the blocked official page) ([anthropic_api](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/anthropic_api); [zh-cn](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/zh-cn/guides/anthropic_api); [developersdigest](https://www.developersdigest.tech/reference/api-compatibility/deepseek); [aiengineerguide](https://aiengineerguide.com/til/deepseek-llm-in-claude-code/)):
- The base URL is `https://api.deepseek.com/anthropic`. It is used with Claude Code via `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` plus `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`; community guides also use `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`.
- `anthropic-beta` and `anthropic-version` headers are ignored.
- Model mapping, reportedly from the Chinese docs:
  - `claude-opus*` maps to `deepseek-v4-pro`.
  - `claude-sonnet*`, `claude-haiku*` and unknown names map to `deepseek-v4-flash`.
- A third-party summary says MCP tool-use blocks are unsupported **(secondary)**.
- The DeepSeek API also reportedly exposes a Responses-API-compatible endpoint ([DeepSeek docs](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/anthropic_api/)) **(secondary)**.

**Thinking mode with tools** ([Thinking Mode guide](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/thinking_mode/), via search; [vLLM recipe](https://docs.vllm.ai/projects/recipes/en/latest/DeepSeek/DeepSeek-V3_2.html)):
- Thinking is enabled with `extra_body={"thinking": {"type": "enabled"}}`. Reasoning comes back in `reasoning_content`.
- In tool loops, the assistant's `reasoning_content` must be passed back with `content` and `tool_calls`, or the API returns 400 **(secondary)**. Without `tools`, it does not need to be passed back and is ignored if sent.
- With no tool calls, the official API returns `None` (vLLM returns `[]`).
- V3.2 (Dec 1, 2025) was "our first model to integrate thinking directly into tool-use" ([news251201](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/news/news251201)).
- Conflict: Vercel AI Gateway says the "V3.2 Thinking" variant does not support tool use ([Vercel](https://vercel.com/ai-gateway/models/deepseek-v3.2-thinking)).
- One extract references `deepseek-flash` with `extra_body={"thinking":{"type":"enabled"}}`, which suggests a post-V3.2 model ID (unverified).

**Strict function calling (Beta)** ([Tool Calls guide](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/tool_calls/); [V3.1 release](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/news/news250821/)):
- Enabled with `base_url="https://api.deepseek.com/beta"` and `strict: true` on every function, in both thinking and non-thinking modes. It was introduced with V3.1 (Aug 2025).
- All properties must be `required`, with `additionalProperties: false`.
- Supported:
  - string `pattern` and the formats email, hostname, ipv4, ipv6 and uuid
  - number `minimum`, `maximum` and `multipleOf`
  - `$ref` / `$def`
- Not supported: string `minLength`/`maxLength`, and array `minItems`/`maxItems`.

**Context caching:**
- Disk-based caching is automatic. It launched Aug 2, 2024 at $0.014/MTok for hits ([DeepSeek news](https://deepseek.com/en/news/context-caching/)).
- Later V4 pricing **(secondary)**: Flash $0.0028/MTok on a hit vs $0.14 on a miss; Pro $0.003625 vs $0.435 ([benchlm.ai](https://www.benchlm.ai/deepseek/api-pricing)).

#### 12.4.4 V4 status (secondary sources only)

- **Launch:** an open-weight preview on 2026-04-24, with MIT weights and 1M context for both models:
  - V4-Pro: reportedly ~1.6T total / 49B active
  - V4-Flash: ~284B / 13B active
- **Conflicts:** sources disagree on parameter counts, on pricing, and on SWE-bench Verified (80.6 "vendor-reported" vs ~91.2) ([letsdatascience](https://letsdatascience.com/news/deepseek-v4-preview-adds-open-weight-1m-context-models-4a8f21c6); [framia](https://framia.converge.ai/page/en-US/news/deepseek-v4-announcement-april-2026); [mindstudio](https://www.mindstudio.ai/blog/deepseek-v4-open-source-frontier-model-review); [framia coding](https://framia.converge.ai/page/en-US/news/deepseek-v4-coding)).
- **Harness support:** V4 reportedly shipped "with documented support for Claude Code, OpenClaw, OpenCode, and CodeBuddy", integrated by swapping the base URL. DeepSeek reportedly runs V4-Pro as its internal coding agent ([handyai](https://handyai.substack.com/p/model-drop-deepseek-v4); [atlascloud](https://www.atlascloud.ai/blog/deepseek-v4-preview-launch)).
- **Leaderboard:** "DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813" ranked second on the Vals.ai SWE-bench Verified page (96.40%) on the mini-SWE-agent bash-only harness as of 2026-09-01 **(secondary; the page is marked archived)** ([Vals.ai](https://www.vals.ai/benchmarks/swebench)).

#### 12.4.5 deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness (conflicting evidence)

- **Repo (read directly):** the repo exists, but its README is tiny and only points agents to `AGENTS.md`. No memory section was found ([deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)).
- **Reported release:**
  - Secondary sources describe "DeepSeek Harness" as an open-source (MIT) agent runtime, reported as v0.1 around 2026-08-13; one source gives a public debut on 2026-07-31.
  - Persistent memory is said to be planned rather than shipped.
  - Sources: [Gigazine](https://gigazine.net/gsc_news/en/20260814-deepseek-harness-v0-1/); [teamorouter](https://teamorouter.com/blogs/deepseek-harness-agent-framework).
- **Third-party plugins:**
  - Mem0 offers `search_memory`/`add_memory` **(secondary)**.
  - AgentScope ReMe needs DSH ≥0.1.2-rc.1 **(secondary)**.
  - MemOS ("MemOS Connects with DeepSeek Harness", 2026-08-17) has a local plugin, according to the MemOS README (repo-read) ([MemOS](https://github.com/MemTensor/MemOS)).
- **Conflict:** the harness-repo survey found "no evidence of a DeepSeek-authored agent framework or harness release in 2025–2026", based on name probes such as `DeepSeek-Agent`. The memory survey did find this repo. Treat DeepSeek Harness as **existing but immature and largely unverified**. Its architecture, loop and license were not read from source.

**What to copy from DeepSeek:**
- **Configurable base URL plus model-alias mapping.** A harness written against the Anthropic Messages API (or honouring `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`) can run DeepSeek V3.2/V4 with no code changes. This is the cheapest way to make a harness model-agnostic.
- **Reference encoders for self-hosted weights.** Do not hand-roll chat templates. Use `encoding_dsv32.py` / `encoding_dsv4.py` and the vLLM/SGLang parsers built on them.
- **Model-specific reasoning retention.** Keep reasoning across tool calls and drop it at a new user turn. Return tool results in the native tool role, never as user messages.
- **Per-provider schema compilers.** DeepSeek's strict-mode subset differs from OpenAI's, so each provider needs its own schema compiler or linter.
- **DSA and compaction.** DSA is a serving-layer concern. Cheaper long contexts make less aggressive compaction viable for self-hosted DeepSeek **(inference)**.

**Caveats:**
- The exact DSML token syntax, the V3.1 "search agent"/"code agent" trajectory templates, the V3.2 report's synthesis numbers, the V4 tech report and the current API compatibility table were all **unverified**.
- DeepSeek's "Engram" repo (a conditional-memory model architecture) was not researched.

### 12.5 Other open-source harnesses

By late 2026 the field has consolidated:
- **Leaders by usage and activity:** OpenCode, Pi, Gemini CLI, OpenHands, Cline, Goose, Qwen Code, Crush, deepagents, and mini-swe-agent (the research baseline).
- **Restructured:** OpenHands, Letta and Kimi.
- **Dead or slowing:** Roo Code shut down; Aider has had no release since ~Aug 2025; SWE-agent is in maintenance.
- **Not open source:** Amp.

**Group A — Active.**

#### 12.5.1 OpenCode (sst/opencode → anomalyco/opencode; MIT; TypeScript/Bun)
- **Purpose:** an open coding agent with TUI, desktop, server and SDK packages. ~224.1k stars (as displayed on the page fetch). The README badges point to `anomalyco/opencode`. `@opencode/core` is at 2.2.5 (tags `v2.2.x`).
- **Architecture:** a TypeScript/Bun monorepo built on Effect plus drizzle/SQLite. Packages are `core`, `server`, `tui`, `desktop`, `sdk`, `plugin`, `codemode` and `protocol` ([README](https://github.com/sst/opencode/blob/dev/README.md); [packages/core/package.json](https://github.com/sst/opencode/blob/dev/packages/core/package.json)).
- **Key files:**
  - The `patch` tool uses the Codex envelope verbatim (`*** Begin Patch … *** Add File / Update File / Delete File / Move to … *** End Patch`) ([patch.txt](https://github.com/sst/opencode/blob/dev/packages/core/src/tool/patch.txt)).
  - Tools include `todowrite`.
  - Core modules include `session/compaction.ts`, `session/subagent-job.ts`, `instruction-discovery.ts`, `permission.ts`, `snapshot.ts`, `worktree.ts`, `persistent-pty.ts` and `lsp` handling ([packages/core/src](https://github.com/sst/opencode/tree/dev/packages/core/src)).
  - The instruction file is AGENTS.md.
- **Design decisions:**
  - There are two built-in primary agents, switched with Tab. `build` has full access. `plan` is read-only: it denies edits and asks before bash.
  - A `general` subagent is invoked as `@general`.
  - The shell is a persistent PTY.
- **Copy:** cross-vendor reuse of the Codex `apply_patch` envelope; Tab-switched build/plan agents as a permission profile rather than a separate mode; a snapshot/worktree module set.
- **Caveats:** the exact date of the org move from sst to anomalyco was not confirmed. DeepSeek V4 reportedly documents OpenCode support **(secondary)**.

#### 12.5.2 Gemini CLI (google-gemini/gemini-cli; Apache-2.0; TypeScript)
- **Purpose:** Google's terminal agent. ~108.7k stars. Releases are stable `v0.66.0`, `v0.67.0-preview.0`, and nightlies. Packages are `cli`, `core`, `sdk`, `a2a-server`, `vscode-ide-companion` and `devtools` ([repo](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli); [packages/](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/tree/main/packages)).
- **Tools** ([core/src/tools](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/tree/main/packages/core/src/tools)):
  - files: `read-file`, `read-many-files`, `write-file`, `edit` (`old_string`/`new_string`, [edit.ts](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/main/packages/core/src/tools/edit.ts))
  - search and listing: `glob`, `grep`/`ripGrep`, `ls`
  - shell: `shell` plus `shellBackgroundTools`
  - web: `web-fetch`, `web-search`
  - memory: `memoryTool` (`GEMINI.md` is the default context filename and is configurable; [memoryTool.ts](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/main/packages/core/src/tools/memoryTool.ts))
  - planning and tracking: `write-todos`, `trackerTools`, `enter-plan-mode`/`exit-plan-mode`
  - other: `activate-skill`, `ask-user`, `complete-task`, MCP resource tools
- **Hook events** use their own vocabulary: `BeforeTool`, `AfterTool`, `BeforeAgent`, `AfterAgent`, `BeforeModel`, `AfterModel`, `BeforeToolSelection`, `PreCompress`, `SessionStart`, `SessionEnd`, `Notification` ([hooks/types.ts](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/main/packages/core/src/hooks/types.ts)).
- **Policy and agents** ([policy/policies](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/tree/main/packages/core/src/policy/policies); [core/src/agents](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/tree/main/packages/core/src/agents)):
  - a TOML policy engine with `policies/{read-only,write,plan,yolo,sandbox-default,non-interactive,agents,conseca}.toml`
  - built-in subagents `codebase-investigator`, `generalist-agent` and `cli-help-agent`
  - remote agents over A2A (`a2a-client-manager.ts`)
- **Context management** ([chatCompressionService.ts](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/main/packages/core/src/context/chatCompressionService.ts); [context/](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/tree/main/packages/core/src/context)):
  - `DEFAULT_COMPRESSION_TOKEN_THRESHOLD = 0.5` (compress at 50% of the window)
  - `COMPRESSION_PRESERVE_THRESHOLD = 0.3` (keep the latest 30%)
  - `toolOutputMaskingService` and `toolDistillationService`
  - a context pipeline with processors
- **Copy:**
  - the TOML policy engine with named profiles (plan, read-only, yolo, non-interactive)
  - model-level hooks (`BeforeModel`/`AfterModel`/`BeforeToolSelection`), which Claude Code and Codex lack
  - tool-output masking and distillation
  - A2A remote subagents
- **Caveats:**
  - The hook names are incompatible with the Claude/Codex vocabulary.
  - It compresses early (50%), unlike Codex's 90%.

#### 12.5.3 Qwen Code (QwenLM/qwen-code; Apache-2.0; TypeScript)
- **Purpose and lineage:** ~28.9k stars; `v0.26.6`. "Originally based on Google Gemini CLI v0.8.2 … Starting from Qwen Code v0.1, we stopped syncing with upstream" ([README](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/main/README.md)).
- **Design:**
  - Multi-protocol: OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini and Qwen APIs.
  - Markets "Auto-Memory, Auto-Skills, SubAgents, Agent Teams, and MCP".
  - Instruction files: QWEN.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and GEMINI.md ([packages/core/src](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/tree/main/packages/core/src)).
- **Copy:** read every vendor's instruction-file name, and support a multi-protocol provider layer.
- **Caveats:** its divergences from Gemini CLI were not inspected in depth.

#### 12.5.4 Pi (badlogic/pi-mono → earendil-works/pi; MIT; TypeScript)
- **Purpose:** ~119.6k stars. Described as an "AI agent toolkit: unified LLM API, agent loop, TUI, coding agent CLI". Pi is "a minimal, extensible agent harness … ships with powerful defaults but skips features like sub-agents and plan mode" ([coding-agent README](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/blob/main/packages/coding-agent/README.md); [earendil-works/pi](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi)).
- **Architecture:**
  - It is extended through extensions, skills, prompt templates and packages.
  - It runs interactively, in print/JSON mode, over RPC, or through a TS SDK.
- **Key file:** [tools/index.ts](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/blob/main/packages/coding-agent/src/core/tools/index.ts):
  - The default coding toolset is exactly four tools: `read`, `bash`, `edit`, `write`.
  - The read-only set is `read`, `grep`, `find`, `ls`.
  - Instruction files are AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md.
- **Ecosystem:** OpenHands Agent Canvas lists Pi as a supported ACP agent, and Kimi Code uses `pi-tui`.
- **Copy:** its high adoption is strong evidence that a 4-tool core plus extensibility is competitive. Plan mode and subagents can be add-ons rather than core.
- **Caveats:** no release tag was captured. The repo-move details are known only from README links.

#### 12.5.5 Cline (cline/cline; Apache-2.0; TypeScript)
- **Purpose:** ~71.2k stars; `v4.1.26`. Cline now ships as:
  - a CLI (headless for CI)
  - a desktop app
  - VS Code and JetBrains extensions
  - an SDK

  ([README](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/main/README.md))
- **SDK layering** ([sdk/ARCHITECTURE.md](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/main/sdk/ARCHITECTURE.md)): `@cline/shared` → `@cline/llms` → `@cline/agents` → `@cline/core` → host apps.
  - `@cline/agents` is the "stateless runtime loop": iteration, tool orchestration, events and hooks.
  - `@cline/core` adds sessions, persistence, compaction policy and RPC.
- **Compaction design:**
  - The canonical session history is kept at full fidelity.
  - Compaction state lives in a separate `${sessionId}.compaction.json`, reused on resume only after a hash of the canonical prefix is validated.
  - Automatic compaction requires a known context window: "unknown custom-model limits do not trigger compaction".
- **Instruction files:** AGENTS.md and `.clinerules`. It has an extension/hook system.
- **Copy:** the "stateless loop package vs stateful core" layering, and a canonical transcript with separately persisted, hash-validated compaction state. Together these are the best pattern for resumable compaction that never loses the original transcript.
- **Caveats:** custom models with unknown windows never auto-compact.

#### 12.5.6 Goose (block/goose → aaif-goose/goose; Apache-2.0; Rust)
- **Purpose:** ~56.2k stars. Stable `v1.57.0`, with v2.0 release candidates in progress. "A general-purpose AI agent" (desktop, CLI and API) with:
  - "15+ providers"
  - ACP providers that let it use "Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini subscriptions"
  - "70+ extensions via MCP"
- **Governance:** it "is part of the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) at the Linux Foundation". It was a founding AAIF project on Dec 9, 2025, alongside MCP and AGENTS.md.
- **Crates:** `goose-agent`, `goose-context-management`, `goose-mcp`, `goose-providers`, `goose-sdk`, `goose-acp-macros` ([README](https://github.com/block/goose/blob/main/README.md); [crates/](https://github.com/block/goose/tree/main/crates); [aaif-goose/goose](https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose)).
- **Instruction files:** AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and `.goosehints`.
- **Copy:** ACP both as a provider (driving other agents' subscriptions) and as a server; a dedicated context-management crate.
- **Caveats:** the internals of `goose-context-management` were not inspected.

#### 12.5.7 Crush (charmbracelet/crush; FSL-1.1; Go)
- **Purpose:** ~28.9k stars; `v0.99.0`. It is built on `charm.land/fantasy` (an agent/LLM library) and `catwalk` (a model catalog). Features:
  - "LSP-Enhanced"
  - "switch LLMs mid-session while preserving context"
  - MCP over http/stdio/sse

  ([README](https://github.com/charmbracelet/crush/blob/main/README.md); [go.mod](https://github.com/charmbracelet/crush/blob/main/go.mod); [LICENSE](https://github.com/charmbracelet/crush/blob/main/LICENSE.md))
- **Tools** ([internal/agent/tools](https://github.com/charmbracelet/crush/tree/main/internal/agent/tools)):
  - shell and files: `bash`, `edit`, `multiedit`, `glob`, `grep`, `ls`
  - network: `fetch`, `download`
  - feedback and jobs: `diagnostics`, `job_output`/`job_kill`, `question`
  - LSP: `lsp_definition`, `lsp_rename`, `lsp_replace_symbol`, `lsp_symbols`, `lsp_call_hierarchy`
  - Tool descriptions are `.md`/`.md.tpl` templates kept next to the Go code.
- **Skills and instruction files:** skills live in `internal/skills`. Instruction files are AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, CRUSH.md and GEMINI.md.
- **Copy:** LSP-as-tools (rename, definition, diagnostics) for refactor-heavy work; tool descriptions as templates kept beside the code.
- **Caveats:** FSL-1.1 is source-available, not OSI-approved, so check the terms before forking.

#### 12.5.8 LangChain deepagents (langchain-ai/deepagents; MIT; Python, plus deepagents.js)
- **Purpose:** ~30.9k stars; `deepagents==0.7.32`. "The batteries-included agent harness", built on LangGraph (streaming, persistence, checkpointing). It includes:
  - sub-agents with isolated context
  - a pluggable filesystem backend
  - summarization and offloading of tool outputs to disk
  - shell, persistent memory, HITL, skills and MCP
  - a terminal coding agent, "Deep Agents Code"

  ([README](https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/blob/main/README.md))
- **Key files:**
  - Middleware in [middleware/](https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/tree/main/libs/deepagents/deepagents/middleware):
    - context: `summarization.py`, `_blob_offload.py`, `_message_eviction.py`, `_overflow_clip.py`, `_prompt_caching.py`
    - agents and capabilities: `subagents.py`, `async_subagents.py`, `skills.py`, `memory.py`
    - control: `permissions.py`, `patch_tool_calls.py`
  - Backends in [backends/](https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/tree/main/libs/deepagents/deepagents/backends): `filesystem`, `local_shell`, `sandbox`, `state`, `store`, `composite`.
  - The libs include `acp`.
- **Evidence (secondary):** LangChain reports that the Deep Agents coding agent went from 52.8% to 66.5% on Terminal-Bench 2.0 with the same GPT-5.2-Codex, through harness changes only. The changes included time-budget warnings and loop-detection middleware that tracks per-file edit counts ([explainx.ai](https://www.explainx.ai/blog/agent-harness-engineering-terminal-bench-langchain-2026)). An earlier run had the Deep Agents CLI with Sonnet 4.5 at a 42.65% mean ([LangChain blog](https://www.blog.langchain.com/evaluating-deepagents-cli-on-terminal-bench-2-0), snippet).
- **Copy:** context management as composable middleware (summarization, offload-to-filesystem, eviction, overflow clipping, cache-control). It is the best Python reference for this pattern.
- **Caveats:** the LangChain blog was blocked, so the benchmark numbers are secondary.

#### 12.5.9 mini-swe-agent (SWE-agent/mini-swe-agent; MIT; Python)
- **Purpose:** ~9.0k stars; `v2.4.6`. The minimal research baseline, which powers the SWE-bench "bash only" leaderboard.
- **Design claims** ([README](https://github.com/SWE-agent/mini-swe-agent/blob/main/README.md); [agents/default.py](https://github.com/SWE-agent/mini-swe-agent/blob/main/src/minisweagent/agents/default.py); [environments/local.py](https://github.com/SWE-agent/mini-swe-agent/blob/main/src/minisweagent/environments/local.py)):
  - "Just some 100 lines of python for the agent class". `agents/default.py` is 190 lines including config.
  - "Does not have any tools other than bash — it doesn't even need to use the tool-calling interface".
  - "completely linear history … no difference between the trajectory and the messages".
  - Actions run via "`subprocess.run` — every action is completely independent (as opposed to keeping a stateful shell session)". Sandboxing is therefore just a matter of swapping in `docker exec`.
  - Environments are `local.py`, `docker.py` and `singularity.py`.
  - The README argues that special tools and interfaces are "not needed at all to build a useful agent".
- **Results:**
  - "Scores >74% on the SWE-bench verified benchmark" (the July 2025 version scored 65%). PyPI attributes the 74% to Gemini 3 Pro ([PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/mini-swe-agent/)).
  - Reported users include Meta, NVIDIA, Essential AI, IBM, Nebius, Anyscale, Princeton and Stanford.
  - The SWE-bench project now treats mini-SWE-agent runs as regular Verified submissions, with "Bash Only" as a filter ([swebench.com](https://www.swebench.com/verified.html)).
  - On 2026-09-01, Vals.ai listed Claude Opus 5 + mini-SWE-agent first at 97.00%, DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813 at 96.40% and GPT-5.6 Sol at 96.20% **(secondary; the page is marked archived)**.
- **Copy:** build your harness so it can be ablated down to this; it is the control condition for evals. It also shows the stateless-subprocess shell model at its simplest.
- **Caveats:** the SWE-bench numbers are the repo's own claims or aggregator data, not independently verified.

#### 12.5.10 smolagents (huggingface/smolagents; Apache-2.0; Python)
- **Purpose:** `v1.26.0`; last commit 2026-10-06. "The logic for agents fits in ~1,000 lines".
- **Design:**
  - `CodeAgent` "writes its actions in code" (Python snippets), alongside a standard `ToolCallingAgent`.
  - Sandboxes are E2B, Blaxel and Modal, plus Docker and WASM options.
  - Warning: "`LocalPythonExecutor` is not a security sandbox" ([README](https://github.com/huggingface/smolagents/blob/main/README.md)).
- **Copy:** code-as-action as an alternative action space. Codex `code-mode` and OpenCode `codemode` pursue the same idea.
- **Caveats:** its 2026 status in multi-agent use ("managed agents") was not researched, and its star count was not fetched.

**Group B — Pivoted or restructured.**

#### 12.5.11 OpenHands → Agent Canvas + Software Agent SDK (OpenHands org, formerly All-Hands-AI; MIT)
- **Agent Canvas** (`OpenHands/OpenHands`, ~92.5k stars, `v1.34.0`):
  - It is now "Agent Canvas: the self-hosted developer control center for coding agents and automations".
  - It runs "OpenHands, Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Pi, OpenCode, or any ACP-compatible agent across local, remote, and cloud backends" ([README](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/blob/main/README.md)).
- **Software Agent SDK** (`OpenHands/software-agent-sdk`, `v1.59.0`):
  - It offers Python, TypeScript and REST APIs.
  - Packages: `openhands-sdk`, `openhands-tools`, `openhands-workspace`, `openhands-agent-server`.
  - It is "the engine behind the OpenHands CLI and OpenHands Cloud", and runs locally or in Docker/Kubernetes workspaces via the Agent Server.
  - The README badge claims SWEBench 77.6; the tech report is arXiv 2511.03690 ([SDK README](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/main/README.md)).
- **SDK modules** ([openhands/sdk](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/tree/main/openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk)):
  - `agent`
  - `context` (condenser, view, memory)
  - `conversation` (event_store, stuck_detector, goal)
  - `event`, `critic`
  - `security` (LLM analyzer, shell AST parser, confirmation policy, defense_in_depth)
  - `hooks`, `skills`, `subagent`, `mcp`, `plugin`, `marketplace`, `workspace`
- **Tools** ([openhands-tools](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/tree/main/openhands-tools/openhands/tools)):
  - shell and files: `terminal`, `file_editor` (str_replace style), `apply_patch`, `glob`, `grep`, `planning_file_editor`
  - browsing: `browser_use`
  - planning and delegation: `task_tracker`, `delegate`, `task`, `child_conversation`
  - consultation: `ask_oracle`, `tom_consult`
- **Event-stream and condenser design** ([condenser/README.md](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/main/openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/context/condenser/README.md); [llm_summarizing_condenser.py](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/main/openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/context/condenser/llm_summarizing_condenser.py)):
  - The conversation is "an append-only event log".
  - Condensation is recorded as `Condensation` events ("similar to tombstones in … Cassandra and Kafka"), and a `View` applies them to produce the LLM-visible context.
  - The default `LLMSummarizingCondenser` replaces "the first half of all events with a single summary event", with `max_size=240` events, `keep_first=2` and an optional `max_tokens`.
  - "Soft" condensation happens at a resource limit and can be skipped if it would break message-structure invariants. "Hard" condensation is explicitly requested, for example after a context-window error.
  - The stated rationale: regular condensation keeps prompt-cache rebuild costs low.
- **StuckDetector:** scans recent events for repetitive patterns, for example 4 repeats × 2 events per cycle ([stuck_detector.py](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/main/openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/conversation/stuck_detector.py)).
- **Copy:** the best open reference for durable, replayable agent state. That means the append-only event log, tombstone condensation events with a `View` projection, halving condensation with `keep_first`, the soft/hard distinction, the stuck detector, the layered security analyzer, and the control-center-over-ACP model.
- **Caveats:** the SWE-bench 77.6 figure is a self-reported README claim, and the tech report was not fetched (arXiv was blocked).

#### 12.5.12 Letta (MemGPT) → Letta Code (Apache-2.0)
- **Status:** `letta-ai/letta` now says "The current source code lives in letta-ai/letta-code". The server's last tag is `0.16.8`, and the V1 API server has been retired to an `archive` branch ([letta README](https://github.com/letta-ai/letta/blob/main/README.md)).
- **Letta Code** (`@letta-ai/letta-code`) is "a stateful agent harness" ([letta-code README](https://github.com/letta-ai/letta-code/blob/main/README.md)). It has:
  - memory blocks
  - system-prompt learning
  - MemFS ("All context (including memory blocks) is tracked via git")
  - skills (`~/.letta`, `.agents/skills`)
  - subagents (general-purpose, forked, recall)
  - hooks, permissions, crons/heartbeats
  - channels (Slack, Telegram, Discord)
- **Memory design** ([letta_local_memfs.md](https://github.com/letta-ai/letta-code/blob/main/src/agent/prompts/letta_local_memfs.md)):
  - Memory blocks and external memory are projected to `$MEMORY_DIR`. The agent manages them with bash and file tools and inspects their evolution via `git log`, and they can sync to a GitHub repo via `/memory-repository set`.
  - Changes take effect only after commit, on the next prompt recompile, never mid-turn.
  - Blocks use `[[path]]` wiki-links between memory, skills and files.
  - Rules: "Never store secrets" (secrets live as `$SECRET_NAME` in a harness secret store) and "Keep blocks lean".
  - Recall memory is immutable and searchable (`/search`).
  - `/sleeptime` configures periodic "dreaming"; `/dream` and `/reflect` are manual.
  - AgentFile (`.af`) export/import is deprecated and removed.
- **Reflection subagent** ([reflection-v2.md](https://github.com/letta-ai/letta-code/blob/main/src/agent/subagents/builtin/reflection-v2.md)):
  - It runs in the background between turns, with Bash and Edit tools.
  - Priorities in order: mistakes and corrections, preferences, new facts, contradictions, then reusable procedures turned into skills.
  - It makes at most one skill change per run and commits with typed messages, such as `fix|feat|chore(reflection): …`. If nothing is worth persisting, it does not commit.
- **Copy:** git-tracked memory (MemFS), self-editing memory blocks and commit-gated memory activation. These are the reference for persistent, learning agents and go beyond per-session compaction.
- **Caveats:** docs.letta.com was unreachable, so MemFS details come from source prompts. The sleep-time-compute blog details are **(secondary)**.

#### 12.5.13 Kimi CLI → Kimi Code CLI (Moonshot)
- **Status:** `MoonshotAI/kimi-cli` (Python) reads "This project has been archived and is no longer maintained … replaced by Kimi Code CLI" ([kimi-cli README](https://github.com/MoonshotAI/kimi-cli/blob/main/README.md)).
- **`MoonshotAI/kimi-code`:** TypeScript, MIT, last commit 2026-11-03 ([kimi-code README](https://github.com/MoonshotAI/kimi-code/blob/main/README.md); [packages/](https://github.com/MoonshotAI/kimi-code/tree/main/packages)).
  - Packages: `agent-core-v2`, `acp-server`, `kap-server`, `node-sdk`, `session-import`, `transcript`, `tree-sitter-bash`, `pi-tui`.
  - Built-in `coder`/`explore`/`plan` subagents.
  - Lifecycle hooks and a plugin marketplace with trust levels.
  - `kimi acp` for Zed and JetBrains.
  - The instruction file is AGENTS.md.
- **Copy:** an ACP server as a first-class package, plugin trust levels, and `session-import` (importing other harnesses' sessions).
- **Caveats:** the `agent-core-v2` loop was not inspected, and the star count was not fetched. Moonshot's Kimi K2.5 Agent Swarm (a trained orchestrator with up to 100 sub-agents) is a model/product feature, not part of this repo **(secondary)**.

#### 12.5.14 Amp (Sourcegraph → Amp Inc.; proprietary)
- **Status:** closed source. It was spun out of Sourcegraph in Dec 2025, and a rebuilt CLI ("Neo") began rolling out in May 2026 **(secondary)** ([tessl](https://tessl.io/blog/sourcegraph-spins-out-ai-coding-agent-amp-as-a-standalone-company/); [latent.space](https://latent.space/wiki/amp-code/); [amplifying.ai](https://amplifying.ai/coding-agents/amp)).

**Group C — Shut down or slowing.**

#### 12.5.15 Roo Code (RooCodeInc/Roo-Code; Apache-2.0) — shut down
- **Timeline:**
  - The last commit, "Remove roocode.com web app", is dated 2026-05-15. The last tag is `v3.54.0` ([repo](https://github.com/RooCodeInc/Roo-Code)).
  - The sunset was announced around 2026-04-20/21. The extension, Cloud and Router ended on 2026-05-15.
- **Aftermath:** the team pivoted to "Roomote". Third-party sources point users to Cline or the community fork "Zoo Code" ([distillintelligence](https://www.distillintelligence.com/news/roomote); [kilo.ai](https://kilo.ai/compare/roo-code-shutdown-roomote); [thenewstack](https://thenewstack.io/roo-code-cloud-ides-ai-coding/)).
- **Lesson:** the DeepSeek V3.2 report named Roo Code as a framework that simulates tool calls through user messages, which breaks reasoning retention **(secondary)**.

#### 12.5.16 Aider (Aider-AI/aider; Apache-2.0; Python) — slowing
- **Status:** ~49.9k stars. The latest tag is `v0.86.2`, and the v0.86.0 analytics timestamps date to Aug 2025. Main has unreleased changes; the last commit, on 2026-05-22, added Claude 4.5–4.7, GPT-5.x and Gemini 3 aliases ([HISTORY.md](https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider/blob/main/HISTORY.md)). The changelog also added "DeepSeek Reasoner model and updated DeepSeek model metadata with costs and prompt caching".
- **Repo map** ([repomap.py](https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider/blob/main/aider/repomap.py)):
  - `aider/repomap.py` uses tree-sitter tag queries (`aider/queries/tree-sitter-language-pack`).
  - It ranks symbols within a token budget: `map_tokens=1024` by default, scaled up when no files are in the chat.
- **Edit formats** ([edit-formats doc](https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider/blob/main/aider/website/docs/more/edit-formats.md); [aider/coders](https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider/tree/main/aider/coders)):
  - `whole`, `diff` (SEARCH/REPLACE blocks), `diff-fenced`, `udiff`
  - `editor-diff`/`editor-whole`, used by the architect/editor two-model split
  - `patch_coder.py`, an apply_patch-style coder
  - None of these use tool calling.
- **Copy:** the tree-sitter repo map, and the empirical per-model edit-format matrix. Both remain the reference for matching edit formats to models and for supporting weak models.
- **Caveats:**
  - There has been no tagged release in more than a year.
  - Aider's leaderboard data was not extracted.
  - The Darwin Gödel Machine reportedly self-improved a harness past "hand-built Aider" on Polyglot (14.2% → 30.7%) **(secondary)**.

#### 12.5.17 SWE-agent (SWE-agent/SWE-agent; MIT; Python) — maintenance
- **Status:** `v1.1.0`; last commit 2026-07-16. The README says "Most of our current development effort is on mini-swe-agent … Our general recommendation is to use mini-SWE-agent instead of SWE-agent going forward" ([README](https://github.com/SWE-agent/SWE-agent/blob/main/README.md)).
- **ACI tool bundles** in `tools/` ([tools/](https://github.com/SWE-agent/SWE-agent/tree/main/tools)): `windowed`, `windowed_edit_linting`, `windowed_edit_replace`, `windowed_edit_rewrite`, `edit_anthropic`, `search`, `filemap`, `submit`, `review_on_submit_m`, `diff_state`, `web_browser`.
- **Copy:** the ACI lesson to avoid line counting, through context-anchored or string-replace edits. `edit_anthropic` is the str_replace-style bundle.
- **Caveats:** superseded. The ACI papers were not fetched.


### 12.6 Convergence and divergence

#### What has converged

| Primitive | Converged form | Harnesses (evidence) | Outliers / notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Small core toolset | Shell + read/edit/write + grep/glob | Codex, Gemini CLI, Crush, OpenCode, OpenHands, Pi (exactly `read`/`bash`/`edit`/`write`), Claude Code (SDK-visible `Read`/`Glob`/`Grep`/`Edit`/`Write`/`Bash`) | mini-swe-agent uses bash only |
| Todo / plan tool | A checklist tool, often with a separate read-only plan mode | Codex `update_plan` + Plan Mode, OpenCode `todowrite` + `plan` agent, Gemini CLI `write-todos` + `enter-plan-mode`/`exit-plan-mode`, OpenHands `task_tracker`, Claude `TodoWrite`/`TaskCreate`/`TaskUpdate` + `plan` permission mode | Pi omits plan mode by design. Anthropic now turns todo tools **off by default on its newest models** ("newer models track multi-step work without a written todo list") |
| Subagents with isolated context | Spawn/wait/close tools or declarative agent definitions | Codex `spawn_agent`/`wait_agent`/…, Claude `AgentDefinition`, Gemini CLI built-ins + A2A, OpenCode `@general`, Kimi Code `coder`/`explore`/`plan`, deepagents `subagents.py`/`async_subagents.py`, OpenHands `delegate`/`task`/`child_conversation`, Letta Code forked/recall subagents | Pi omits them by design |
| Instruction file | AGENTS.md, hierarchical, stewarded by the Linux Foundation AAIF since Dec 9, 2025 (donated by OpenAI; used in ~40,000 open-source projects per one report) | See the instruction-file table below | Gemini CLI defaults to GEMINI.md |
| Tool-extension bus | MCP | Universal: Codex (`rmcp`), Claude SDK (in-process SDK servers), Goose ("70+ extensions"), Crush (http/stdio/sse), Gemini, OpenHands, deepagents, Kimi Code | MCP joined AAIF Dec 9, 2025 |
| Capability packaging | Agent Skills `SKILL.md` folders (agentskills.io) | Claude, Codex (`skills` crate, `skills/list` RPC), Agents SDK `Skills(lazy_from=…)`, Gemini `activate-skill`, deepagents `skills.py`, Letta Code `.agents/skills`, Pi, OpenHands `skills/`, Crush `internal/skills`, Qwen "Auto-Skills" | 22% of sampled skills fail validation **(secondary)** |
| Compaction | LLM summary of older history | Every surveyed harness; see the compaction table below | Retention and placement diverge |
| Hook vocabulary | `PreToolUse`/`PostToolUse`/`UserPromptSubmit`/`Stop`/`SubagentStop`/`PreCompact`/`PermissionRequest` with a `permissionDecision` output | Claude Agent SDK and Codex hooks crate; hooks also exist in Kimi Code, Letta Code, OpenHands SDK `hooks/` and Cline | Gemini CLI uses `BeforeTool`/`AfterTool`/… |
| Sandbox + policy | OS-level sandbox (Seatbelt / bubblewrap) plus an approval policy layered on top | Codex, `srt`/Claude Code; policy layers: Codex execpolicy + guardian, Gemini TOML policies, Claude permission modes, OpenHands security analyzers | Container/hosted alternatives below |
| Headless + SDK | A JSON-streaming headless mode plus an SDK | Codex `exec --json` + TS/Python SDKs, Claude stream-JSON SDKs, Pi print/JSON/RPC/TS SDK, Cline headless CLI + SDK, Gemini `sdk` package, OpenCode `sdk`, Kimi `node-sdk`, OpenHands REST/Python/TS | — |
| Plugin marketplaces | Bundles of commands, agents, hooks and MCP servers | Claude `/plugin` (claude-plugins-official, `anthropics/skills`), Codex `plugin` subcommand + `request_plugin_install`, Kimi Code (trust levels), OpenHands SDK `plugin`/`marketplace`, OpenCode `plugin` package | — |
| Background memory consolidation | A separate agent rewrites file/git memory between sessions | Codex memories (Phase 2), Agents SDK sandbox `Memory()`, Letta Code reflection subagent | Claude Code writes memory inline instead |

**Instruction-file names found in source:**

| Harness | Instruction files |
|---|---|
| Codex | AGENTS.md (root→cwd), `AGENTS.override.md` |
| Claude Code | CLAUDE.md; AGENTS.md via the `agents-md` mod (default `claude-md-or-agents-md`) or an `@AGENTS.md` import |
| OpenCode | AGENTS.md |
| Kimi Code | AGENTS.md |
| Pi | AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md |
| Cline | AGENTS.md, `.clinerules` |
| Goose | AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, `.goosehints` |
| Crush | AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, CRUSH.md, GEMINI.md |
| Qwen Code | AGENTS.md, QWEN.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md |
| Gemini CLI | GEMINI.md (default, configurable) |
| DeepSeek Harness | README points agents to AGENTS.md |

Sources: [opencode core](https://github.com/sst/opencode/tree/dev/packages/core/src); [kimi-code packages](https://github.com/MoonshotAI/kimi-code/tree/main/packages); [pi coding-agent](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/tree/main/packages/coding-agent/src); [cline sdk](https://github.com/cline/cline/tree/main/sdk/packages); [goose crates](https://github.com/block/goose/tree/main/crates); [crush internal](https://github.com/charmbracelet/crush/tree/main/internal); [qwen-code core](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/tree/main/packages/core/src); [gemini memoryTool.ts](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/main/packages/core/src/tools/memoryTool.ts); [agents.md AboutSection](https://github.com/agentsmd/agents.md/blob/main/components/AboutSection.tsx).

**Hook vocabularies:**

| Event family | Claude Agent SDK `HookEvent` | Claude Code docs (extra) | Codex hooks crate | Gemini CLI |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tool | `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `PostToolUseFailure` | `PermissionDenied` | `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse` | `BeforeTool`, `AfterTool`, `BeforeToolSelection` |
| Permission | `PermissionRequest` | — | `PermissionRequest` | (TOML policy engine instead) |
| Prompt / agent | `UserPromptSubmit`, `Stop` | — | `UserPromptSubmit`, `Stop` | `BeforeAgent`, `AfterAgent` |
| Model call | — | — | — | `BeforeModel`, `AfterModel` |
| Subagents / teams | `SubagentStart`, `SubagentStop` | `TaskCompleted`, `TeammateIdle` | `SubagentStop` | — |
| Compaction | `PreCompact` | — | `PreCompact`, `PostCompact` | `PreCompress` |
| Session | — | — | `SessionStart` (and `SessionEnd` in one reading) | `SessionStart`, `SessionEnd` |
| Other | `Notification` | — | — | `Notification` |

**Compaction recipes (converged on LLM summary; they diverge on trigger, retention and placement):**

| Harness | Trigger | Retention / recipe | Where | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Codex | 90% of window (`min(config, window*9/10)`); also mid-turn/post-turn async; manual | Handoff-summary prompt + ≤20k tokens of prior user messages, newest first; re-insert initial context; remote-v2 path retains selected tool outputs | Local, or server-side (remote v2) | [compact.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/core/src/compact.rs) |
| Gemini CLI | 50% of window | Keep the latest 30%, plus tool-output masking/distillation | Client | [chatCompressionService.ts](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/main/packages/core/src/context/chatCompressionService.ts) |
| OpenHands SDK | `max_size=240` events (soft), or explicit/context-error (hard) | Summarize the first half of events, `keep_first=2`, recorded as tombstone `Condensation` events projected by a `View` | Client, on an append-only log | [condenser README](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/main/openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/context/condenser/README.md) |
| Cline SDK | Known context window only | Canonical transcript untouched; projection in a hash-validated `${sessionId}.compaction.json` | Client sidecar | [ARCHITECTURE.md](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/main/sdk/ARCHITECTURE.md) |
| deepagents | Middleware | Summarization + filesystem blob offload + eviction + overflow clip | Client middleware | [middleware](https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/tree/main/libs/deepagents/deepagents/middleware) |
| OpenAI Agents SDK | `should_trigger_compaction` | Provider-side `responses.compact` | Provider | [compaction session](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/main/src/agents/memory/openai_responses_compaction_session.py) |
| Anthropic SDK tool runner | `compact_before_next_turn()` | Server-side summarization | Provider | [cookbook](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-cookbooks/blob/main/tool_use/automatic-context-compaction.ipynb) |
| Claude Managed Agents | Always on | Emits `agent.thread_context_compacted`; the durable session log stays outside context | Hosted | [compaction docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/compaction-threshold) |

#### Where they diverge

| Axis | Options | Who | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Edit format** | `apply_patch` envelope (context-anchored, no line numbers) | Codex (Lark grammar, freeform), OpenCode `patch`, Agents SDK sandbox `apply_patch.py`, gpt-oss `apply_patch`, OpenHands `apply_patch`, Aider `patch_coder.py` | Best for OpenAI models, which are trained on it |
| | `str_replace` / `old_string`→`new_string` | Gemini CLI `edit`, Crush `edit`/`multiedit`, Pi `edit`, SWE-agent `edit_anthropic`, OpenHands `file_editor`, Claude `Edit`/`str_replace` | Best for Claude-style models **(inference)** |
| | SEARCH/REPLACE, udiff, whole-file in plain text (no tool calling) | Aider | Chosen per model from a matrix |
| | bash-only (sed/heredoc) | mini-swe-agent | Baseline |
| | Code-as-action | smolagents `CodeAgent`; Codex `code-mode`; OpenCode `codemode` | — |
| **Shell model** | Stateful PTY sessions | Codex `exec_command` + `write_stdin`; OpenCode `persistent-pty` | Interactive processes survive between calls |
| | Background-job tools | Crush `job_output`/`job_kill`; Gemini `shellBackgroundTools` | — |
| | Stateless `subprocess.run` per action | mini-swe-agent ("a big deal" for sandboxing and scaling) | Swap in `docker exec` for isolation |
| | Hosted shell | OpenAI Responses `shell` tool: no interactive TTY, no sudo; containers reusable across calls **(secondary)** | — |
| **Embedding / client protocol** | JSON-RPC thread/turn/item | Codex app-server (+ `exec --json` JSONL) | Has steer/interrupt and item-level approvals |
| | NDJSON stream + `control_request`/`control_response` | Claude Agent SDKs | Host callbacks: `can_use_tool`, `hook_callback`, `mcp_message` |
| | ACP (Agent Client Protocol) | Kimi Code (`acp-server`, `kimi acp`), Goose (ACP providers, `goose-acp-macros`), deepagents (`libs/acp`), Pi; OpenHands Agent Canvas as the client that runs any of them | Zed and JetBrains integration |
| | A2A | Gemini CLI (`a2a-server`, `a2a-client-manager.ts`) | Remote agents |
| | MCP | Universal for tools, not for embedding the agent | Codex dropped its top-level `mcp-server` subcommand |
| **Compaction location** | Client-side | Codex local, Gemini, OpenHands, Cline, deepagents, Claude Code | — |
| | Provider-side | OpenAI `responses.compact` (Agents SDK session, Codex remote v2), Anthropic server-side compaction (tool runner), Managed Agents | Compaction rewrites history and invalidates cached prefixes **(secondary)** |
| **Language / runtime** | Rust | Codex, Goose | — |
| | TypeScript | OpenCode (Bun), Gemini CLI, Qwen Code, Cline, Kimi Code, Pi, Letta Code, Claude Code (closed) | — |
| | Python | OpenHands SDK, SWE-agent / mini, Aider, smolagents, deepagents, OpenAI Agents SDK, Claude Agent SDK (a wrapper) | — |
| | Go | Crush | — |
| **Client vs hosted** | Local client harness | All of the above | — |
| | Hosted counterparts | Codex Web/Cloud tasks, OpenHands Cloud, Claude Managed Agents | Session, harness and sandbox are decoupled in Managed Agents |
| | Hosted sandboxes for client harnesses | Agents SDK clients (Docker, E2B, Modal, Daytona, Cloudflare, Vercel, Blaxel), OpenHands Agent Server (Docker/K8s), smolagents (E2B/Blaxel/Modal), mini-swe-agent (docker/singularity) | — |
| **Memory write path** | Inline by the main agent | Claude Code auto memory, Anthropic memory tool | — |
| | Background two-phase pipeline only | Codex, Agents SDK | The main agent writes only ad-hoc notes on user request |
| | Reflection subagent + git commits | Letta Code | — |
| **Plan mode** | Separate mode or agent | Codex Plan Mode, OpenCode `plan`, Gemini plan mode, Claude `plan` permission mode | — |
| | None | Pi | — |

**(Inference)** The primitives are standardizing faster than the harnesses. Two notable 2025-era harnesses died or were replaced within a year (Roo Code, Kimi CLI), while AGENTS.md, MCP, Skills and ACP spread across almost all of them. Building on protocol compatibility is lower-risk than coupling tightly to any one harness.

### 12.7 Build checklist: what to copy from where

1. **Core loop.**
   - Rust: `codex-rs/core/src/session/turn.rs` (`run_turn` / `run_sampling_request` / Stop-hook continuation).
   - TypeScript: Pi `packages/coding-agent` or Cline `@cline/agents` (stateless loop).
   - Python: OpenHands Software Agent SDK (event-sourced).
   - Ablation baseline: mini-swe-agent `src/minisweagent/agents/default.py`.
2. **Termination and budgets.** Claude SDK `ResultMessage.subtype` enum plus `max_turns`/`max_budget_usd`/`task_budget`. Agents SDK `max_turns` + `error_handlers`. Codex retry constants in `model-provider-info/src/lib.rs`.
3. **Model client and reasoning replay.**
   - Codex `core/src/client.rs`: `store:false` + `include: ["reasoning.encrypted_content"]`.
   - Agents SDK `reasoning_item_id_policy`.
   - DeepSeek: return `reasoning_content` with `tool_calls`.
   - Anthropic: return thinking blocks unmodified with their signatures.
4. **Edit tool.**
   - `codex-rs/apply-patch/src/{parser.rs,seek_sequence.rs,streaming_parser.rs}`, `assets/tools/apply_patch.lark` and `core/src/tools/handlers/apply_patch_spec.rs`. Expose it as a freeform grammar tool.
   - Add a `str_replace` tool, modeled on Gemini `packages/core/src/tools/edit.ts`, Pi `src/core/tools` or OpenHands `file_editor`.
   - Select the format per model, as in Aider's `aider/website/docs/more/edit-formats.md`.
5. **Shell tool.** Use Codex `core/src/tools/handlers/unified_exec.rs` (PTY `exec_command` + `write_stdin`) as the default. Keep mini-swe-agent's `environments/{local,docker,singularity}.py` stateless mode for evals and scale-out.
6. **Read and search tools.** Pi `src/core/tools/index.ts` (the four-tool core and read-only set) and Gemini `packages/core/src/tools` (`read-many-files`, `ripGrep`, `glob`).
7. **Plan/todo and plan mode.** The `update_plan` contract in Codex `protocol/src/prompts/base_instructions/default.md`. Plan Mode in `collaboration-mode-templates/templates/plan.md` (where `update_plan` errors). The OpenCode `plan` agent permission profile.
8. **Subagents.** Codex `core/src/tools/handlers/multi_agents_v2`. Claude `AgentDefinition` in `claude_agent_sdk/types.py`. deepagents `middleware/subagents.py` / `async_subagents.py`. Gemini `core/src/agents` (A2A remote agents).
9. **Compaction.**
   - Codex `core/src/compact.rs`, `prompts/templates/compact/{prompt,summary_prefix}.md` and the thresholds in `protocol/src/openai_models.rs`.
   - Gemini `context/chatCompressionService.ts` + `toolOutputMaskingService`.
   - OpenHands `context/condenser/llm_summarizing_condenser.py`.
   - The Cline `${sessionId}.compaction.json` sidecar.
   - Anthropic `misc/session_memory_compaction.ipynb` for background pre-compaction.
10. **Durable state.** OpenHands `conversation/event_store` + `context/view`. Codex `rollout.rs` JSONL rollouts. The Managed Agents session/harness/sandbox split.
11. **Loop and stuck detection.** OpenHands `conversation/stuck_detector.py`. Codex goal no-progress check (`ext/goal/templates/goals/continuation.md`). deepagents-style per-file edit-count middleware **(secondary)**.
12. **Outer goal loop and long-running work.**
    - Codex `ext/goal/templates/goals/{continuation,budget_limit}.md` and `prompts/templates/persistent_mode.md`.
    - `claude-plugins-official/plugins/ralph-loop`.
    - `claude-quickstarts/autonomous-coding`: `feature_list.json`, `claude-progress.txt`, git, `security.py`.
13. **Instruction files.**
    - Codex `core/src/agents_md.rs`: root→cwd, `AGENTS.override.md`, `project_doc_max_bytes`.
    - The Claude Code `mods/agents-md` modes.
    - Also read CLAUDE.md / GEMINI.md / QWEN.md / CRUSH.md / `.goosehints`, as Qwen Code and Crush do.
14. **Skills.** `anthropics/skills` (`spec/agent-skills-spec.md`, `template/SKILL.md`) and agentskills.io. Codex `codex-rs/skills` + `skills/list`. Agents SDK `Skills(lazy_from=…)`.
15. **MCP client.** `rmcp` (pinned `=3.5.1` in Codex) via `codex-mcp` / `rmcp-client`. The `codex/sandbox-state` capability idea. Claude SDK in-process servers (`create_sdk_mcp_server`). Wrap local servers in `srt`.
16. **Hooks.**
    - Event names and `permissionDecision` from `claude_agent_sdk/types.py`.
    - The Codex `hooks/src` implementation, including Stop-hook continuation fragments.
    - Gemini-style `BeforeModel`/`AfterModel`/`BeforeToolSelection` as extras.
    - Claude Code `mods/` `register(on, options)` middleware for in-process extensions.
17. **OS sandbox.**
    - `anthropic-experimental/sandbox-runtime` as a library.
    - Or Codex `linux-sandbox` (bwrap + seccomp), `sandboxing` (Seatbelt `.sbpl`) and `windows-sandbox-rs`.
    - The `SandboxPolicy` + `read_only_subpaths` model in `protocol/src/protocol.rs`.
18. **Network egress.** Codex `network-proxy` (HTTP 3128 / SOCKS5 8081, limited mode, private-IP blocking) or the `srt` HTTP+SOCKS5 proxies with `allowedDomains`. Feed violations to the model as `srt` does with `<sandbox_violations>`.
19. **Container or hosted sandbox.** Agents SDK `src/agents/sandbox` (`manifest.py`, `snapshot.py`) + `extensions/sandbox/{e2b,modal,daytona,cloudflare,vercel,blaxel}`. OpenHands `openhands-agent-server` / `openhands-workspace`.
20. **Approval and policy.**
    - Codex `execpolicy` (Starlark `prefix_rule` with `match`/`not_match` tests, `host_executable`).
    - The `AskForApproval` variants and the `core/src/guardian` auto-reviewer.
    - Gemini `policy/policies/*.toml` profiles.
    - Claude permission modes.
    - The OpenHands `security` analyzer (shell AST parser, LLM analyzer).
21. **Headless mode.** The Codex `exec/src/exec_events.rs` `ThreadEvent` JSONL schema.
22. **Client protocol.** Codex `app-server-protocol` (thread/turn/item, `turn/steer`, `turn/interrupt`, `item/*/requestApproval`). Also ship an ACP server, as Kimi Code `acp-server`, Goose and deepagents `libs/acp` do, so that Zed, JetBrains and OpenHands Agent Canvas can drive the harness.
23. **SDK embedding.** Claude SDK `_internal/transport/subprocess_cli.py` + `_internal/query.py` (control protocol). Codex `sdk/typescript` (spawns the CLI, JSONL over stdio) and `sdk/python`.
24. **Memory.**
    - Codex `codex-rs/memories` + `ext/memories/templates/memories/read_path.md` + `memories/write/templates/memories/{stage_one_system,consolidation}.md`, or Agents SDK `docs/sandbox/memory.md`.
    - Letta Code `src/agent/prompts/letta_local_memfs.md` + `subagents/builtin/reflection-v2.md`.
    - Cookbook `memory_tool.py` for an inline memory tool.
25. **Repo map.** Aider `aider/repomap.py` (tree-sitter tags, `map_tokens=1024`).
26. **LSP tools.** Crush `internal/agent/tools` (`lsp_definition`, `lsp_rename`, `lsp_replace_symbol`, `lsp_symbols`, `lsp_call_hierarchy`, `diagnostics`).
27. **Model-agnostic providers.** A configurable base URL + model-alias mapping (the DeepSeek `https://api.deepseek.com/anthropic` pattern). Qwen Code's multi-protocol layer. `goose-providers`. Crush `catwalk`.
28. **Open-weight chat formats.** `openai/harmony` for gpt-oss. DeepSeek `encoding_dsv32.py` / `encoding_dsv4.py`. Never hand-roll templates.
29. **Tracing and telemetry.** Agents SDK `src/agents/tracing`. The Codex `otel` crate. The Claude Code OTel metric names. Instrument against the OTel GenAI `invoke_agent` → `chat` → `execute_tool` span tree.
30. **Durable execution.** Temporal's `OpenAIAgentsPlugin` / `activity_as_tool` integration for the Agents SDK.
31. **CI integration.** `anthropics/claude-code-action` (`src/modes`, mention, assignment and automation modes, structured outputs).
32. **Plugins and distribution.** The `claude-plugins-official` layout, the `anthropics/skills` marketplace, and Kimi Code plugin trust levels.
33. **Code mode (optional).** Codex `code-mode`, `code-mode-runtime`, `code-mode-host` and `tools/src/code_mode.rs`. smolagents `CodeAgent`, with a real sandbox, never `LocalPythonExecutor`.
34. **Eval control condition.** Run mini-swe-agent (bash-only) on the same model next to your harness. Per the notes' synthesis, harness-only changes move agentic scores by roughly 3–14 points with the model held fixed (LangChain 52.8 → 66.5 on Terminal-Bench 2.0; Codex CLI vs Terminus-2 64.7 vs 57.5; both **(secondary)**).

### 12.8 Pitfalls (licensing, deprecated repos, moved repos)

**Licensing**
- **Claude Code and `claude-agent-sdk-typescript`** are under Anthropic Commercial Terms ("All rights reserved"). Neither can be forked or vendored.
  - `claude-agent-sdk-python` is MIT, but it spawns a bundled, closed CLI. Your product therefore depends on proprietary code even though the wrapper is open.
- **Crush is FSL-1.1** (Functional Source License). It is source-available, not OSI-approved, so check the terms before forking or reusing its code.
- **anthropics/skills** mixes licenses. Many skills are Apache-2.0, but the document skills (docx/pdf/pptx/xlsx) are only source-available.
- **Amp** is proprietary and closed.
- **Licenses not captured in the notes**: openai-agents-js, swarm, harmony, gpt-oss, claude-code-action, claude-quickstarts, claude-cookbooks, claude-plugins-official and kimi-cli. The license of deepseek-harness (MIT) and of the DeepSeek V4 weights (MIT) is known only from secondary sources. Check each LICENSE file before vendoring.
- Apache-2.0 / MIT safe bets for forking:
  - Codex, sandbox-runtime, Gemini CLI, Qwen Code, Goose, Cline
  - OpenCode, Pi, OpenHands, deepagents, mini-swe-agent, SWE-agent
  - Aider, smolagents, Letta / Letta Code, Kimi Code
  - the OpenAI Agents SDK (Python), the Claude Agent SDK (Python) and the DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp code

**Deprecated, archived or shut down**

| Repo / feature | Status | Use instead |
|---|---|---|
| openai/swarm | Deprecated: "replaced by the OpenAI Agents SDK" | openai-agents-python/js |
| OpenAI AgentKit Agent Builder (visual canvas) | Deprecation notices reportedly 2026-06-03, shutdown 2026-11-30 **(secondary; dates conflict)** | Code-first Agents SDK |
| MoonshotAI/kimi-cli | Archived, "no longer maintained" | MoonshotAI/kimi-code |
| RooCodeInc/Roo-Code | Shut down 2026-05-15 (extension, Cloud and Router); team pivoted to "Roomote" | Cline, or the community fork "Zoo Code" **(secondary)** |
| SWE-agent/SWE-agent | Maintenance; authors recommend mini-swe-agent | SWE-agent/mini-swe-agent |
| Aider-AI/aider | No tagged release since `v0.86.x` (~Aug 2025); main still gets commits (last 2026-05-22) | Pin to main, or treat as reference only |
| letta-ai/letta (V1 API server) | Retired to an `archive` branch; last tag `0.16.8` | letta-ai/letta-code |
| Letta AgentFile (`.af`) export/import | Deprecated and removed | MemFS git sync |
| Codex top-level `mcp-server` subcommand | Absent from current `cli/src/main.rs` (it existed in 2025-era versions) | `app-server` JSON-RPC or the SDKs |
| Codex Landlock sandbox | Legacy only; bubblewrap + seccomp is the Linux default | bwrap path |
| Codex `on-failure` approval policy | Now just a serde alias for `on-request` | `on-request` / `granular` |
| Codex on WSL1 | Unsupported/rejected | WSL2 |

**Moved or renamed repos**

| Old | New | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `sst/opencode` | `anomalyco/opencode` | README badges point to the new org; move date unconfirmed |
| `block/goose` | `aaif-goose/goose` | Moved into the Linux Foundation AAIF |
| `badlogic/pi-mono` | `earendil-works/pi` | Known from README links only |
| `All-Hands-AI/OpenHands` | `OpenHands/OpenHands` (+ `OpenHands/software-agent-sdk`) | Main repo is now Agent Canvas |
| `letta-ai/letta` | `letta-ai/letta-code` | "The current source code lives in letta-ai/letta-code" |
| `anthropics/claude-code/plugins` | `anthropics/claude-plugins-official` | Official plugins moved |

| Claude Code SDK | Claude Agent SDK | Renamed Sep 29, 2025 |
| `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2` | Same HEAD as `DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp` (`87e509a`) | No separate V3.2 or V4 GitHub repo; V4 lives on HF |

**Behavioural pitfalls found in the repos**
- **Harness–model coupling.**
  - Codex-family models are trained on `apply_patch` and the Codex loop. OpenAI says to use "our exact apply_patch implementation". GPT-5.3-Codex reportedly calls a non-existent `apply_patch` in harnesses that lack it **(secondary)**.
  - gpt-oss "should only be used with" the harmony format.
  - DeepSeek drops reasoning when tool results arrive as user messages; the V3.2 report names Roo Code and Terminus. In thinking-mode tool loops, omitting `reasoning_content` reportedly returns a 400 **(secondary)**.
- **"Sandboxes" that are not sandboxes.**
  - The Agents SDK `UnixLocalSandboxClient` "adds no OS-level confinement" on Linux.
  - smolagents' "`LocalPythonExecutor` is not a security sandbox".
  - `srt` is a "Beta Research Preview", and its Windows support is alpha.
  - Codex `--yolo` is "Intended solely for running in environments that are externally sandboxed".
- **Compaction edge cases.**
  - Cline never auto-compacts models whose context window is unknown.
  - In codex-cli 0.117.0, changing `model_context_window` could permanently break auto-compaction ([#16068](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/16068)).
  - Claude Code stops auto-compacting after a few attempts if a single huge output refills the context ("instead of looping").
  - Compaction and dynamic MCP tool lists invalidate cached prompt prefixes **(secondary)**.
- **Hook-name incompatibility.** Gemini CLI hooks (`BeforeTool` …) do not match the Claude/Codex names. A cross-harness hook layer needs a mapping table (see 12.6).
- **DeepSeek API surprises (secondary).**
  - The Anthropic-format endpoint ignores `anthropic-beta` and `anthropic-version` headers, so beta features silently do nothing **(inference)**.
  - MCP tool-use blocks are reportedly unsupported.
  - Unknown model names silently map to `deepseek-v4-flash`.
  - The V3.2 parser "is designed to handle well-formatted strings only".
  - V3.2-Speciale has no tool calling.
  - The `developer` role is not accepted by the official API.
- **DSA inference bug.** The DSA indexer RoPE must be non-interleaved while MLA RoPE is interleaved. This was disclosed 2025-11-17 for the inference demo.
- **Feature defaults.** Codex `memories` is Stable but `default_enabled: false`, so you must opt in. Agents SDK sandbox memory persists only if the `memories/` directory is preserved (same live sandbox or a persisted snapshot).
- **Self-reported numbers.** SWE-bench figures in READMEs are each repo's own claim and were not independently verified: OpenHands 77.6, mini-swe-agent "above 74%", and the DeepSeek V3.2-Exp table. Aggregator leaderboards (Vals.ai) are archived or secondary.
- **Star counts** come from a summarizing page fetch and are approximate. For example, OpenCode's ~224.1k is "as displayed". Spot-check before quoting.

### 12.9 Open questions and unverified claims

**OpenAI**
- The default auto-compaction thresholds are known from source (90% of the window, a 95% effective window). The developers.openai.com Codex pages were blocked, though, so the documented defaults, the execpolicy docs and the per-environment internet-access settings for Codex cloud were not cross-checked.
- The release date of `rust-v0.166.0` is unknown because the Releases API was blocked.
- The full text of "Unrolling the Codex agent loop" (2026-01-23) is unread; its caching claims are **(secondary)**.
- The code-mode runtime engine (JS/V8?) is unconfirmed. No public numbers exist for OpenAI `tool_search` or Codex code-mode.
- No precision/recall numbers exist for the Codex `auto_review` guardian.
- No primary OpenAI source (system card or addendum) confirms how Codex models were RL-trained in the Codex harness. The prompting guide's "trained to excel at this diff format" is the only primary statement.
- The `new_context` vs `new_context_window` tool name differs between two readings of the handler directory, and the presence of the `SessionEnd` hook in the Codex crate also differs between readings.
- Agents SDK: the `handoff_input_filter` / `nest_handoff_history` semantics and the tracing span types were not verified, because openai.github.io was blocked.
- The Agent Builder deprecation and shutdown dates conflict across sources.
- Star counts for agents-js, harmony and gpt-oss, and licenses for several OpenAI repos, are missing.

**Anthropic**
- Claude Code's core (system prompt, Edit/MultiEdit/TodoWrite/Task schemas, compaction thresholds) is closed, and no primary schema source was inspected. The exact `permissionDecision` schema in the CLI hook docs was also not verified.
- It is unknown whether a long-running harness repo exists beyond `claude-quickstarts/autonomous-coding`; some material may exist only on the engineering blog.
- Agent Skills adoption counts (40–44 clients, 22% failing validation) are **(secondary)**. The agentskills.io spec text was not fetched.
- Star counts for sandbox-runtime, claude-code-action, the cookbooks and the quickstarts were not fetched.

**DeepSeek**
- None of these could be checked against primary sources: the DSML token syntax, the V3.1 search-agent and code-agent trajectory templates, the V3.2 report's agentic-synthesis numbers, the V4 tech report, V4 parameter counts and pricing, and the current Anthropic-compatibility table and model-alias mapping.
- The V4 SWE-bench Verified figure conflicts: 80.6 "vendor-reported" vs ~91.2.
- DeepSeek Harness is unclear. Is it a real, maintained harness, and what are its loop and tools? Its repo was found, but only a tiny README was read; v0.1, MIT and the memory plans are **(secondary)**. One survey's name probes missed it.
- Current API model IDs (`deepseek-flash` vs `deepseek-v4-flash`) and any server-side context-management features are unverified.
- Vercel AI Gateway says "V3.2 Thinking" has no tool use, which conflicts with DeepSeek's statement that thinking and tools are integrated.

**Other harnesses**
- The OpenHands tech report (arXiv 2511.03690) and the SWE-agent/ACI papers were not read. The 77.6 and "above 74%" numbers are self-reported.
- Not inspected: Goose `goose-context-management` internals, Qwen Code's divergences from Gemini CLI, and the Kimi Code `agent-core-v2` loop.
- The OpenCode org-move date and the Pi repo-move details are unconfirmed.
- Star counts for Kimi Code, Letta Code, smolagents and SWE-agent were not fetched, and no release tag was captured for Pi.
- The LangChain Terminal-Bench gains (52.8 → 66.5) and the Codex-vs-Terminus-2 gap (64.7 vs 57.5) are **(secondary)**.
- The 2026 status of smolagents' managed agents, LangGraph, CrewAI and DSPy was not researched.

**Cross-cutting**
- No head-to-head benchmark comparing edit formats (apply_patch vs str_replace vs SEARCH/REPLACE) across 2026 models was found. Aider's leaderboard is the closest, but it was not extracted.
- ACP spec details (agentclientprotocol.com) were not fetched, so ACP's method set and how it compares with the Codex app-server protocol are open.
- The AGENTS.md nested-file precedence rule ("closest file wins") is implemented by Codex (deeper files win), but it was not verified in the AGENTS.md spec itself.

## Appendix: known conflicts between sources

These are places where the research notes disagree with each other, or where primary and secondary sources disagree. Each section repeats the conflict in its `N.9` subsection. Confirm these against primary sources before you depend on them.

| Topic | Conflict | Where discussed |
|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek harness repo | The memory notes cite an official `deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness` repo. The repository survey found no harness written by DeepSeek. Treat the repo as unverified. | §1.2, §4.2, §12.4, §12.9 |
| Memory tool beta header | Primary Claude docs say `memory_20250818` needs no beta header. A third-party source says `context-management-2025-06-27`. | §4.9, §5.9 |
| Programmatic tool calling version | `code_execution_20250825`, from the Nov 2025 Anthropic post, versus `code_execution_20260120` in the current docs. | §3.9, §5.9 |
| Codex compaction defaults | The research notes give two values for the default compaction limit: 64k and about 200k. The logic itself is the same: trigger at min(configured limit, 90% of the context window). | §2.9, §3.9 |
| Tool search threshold | Guidance on when to switch on tool search varies: from about 10 tools, from about 20, or once selection degrades at 30–50 tools. | §3.9, §5.9 |
| A2A v1.0 release date | The exact release date is unconfirmed. | §5.9, §8.1 |
| Default effort on Opus 5.5 | The architecture notes cite Claude docs for a "medium" default. The evals notes mark it secondary. | §9.9, §10.9 |
| SWE-bench Pro scores | About 59–61% on Scale's standardized harness versus about 90% reported by vendors. Some secondary sources say about 30% of public tasks are broken. | §9.4, §9.9 |
| Terminal-Bench 2.1 leader / DeepSeek V4 | Two values for the Terminal-Bench 2.1 lead score (83.1 vs 83.8). Two values for a DeepSeek V4 score (80.6 vs 91.2). | §9.4, §9.9 |
| Memory benchmarks | The LoCoMo question count differs across sources. SkillsBench figures differ between the arXiv and NeurIPS versions. | §4.9 |
| Context-rot study | Two figures (about 300 vs about 100 tokens) are attributed to the Chroma study. | §3.9 |
| LLM-judge design | Anthropic's 2025 advice favored a single judge call. Its 2026 eval guide favors one judge per dimension. | §9.3, §9.9 |
| DeepSeek thinking mode with tools | Third-party SDK docs (Vercel) and DeepSeek's own docs disagree on whether tool calls are supported in thinking mode. | §5.9 |
| Codex context tools | The notes name the Codex fresh-context tool both `new_context` and `new_context_window`. | §2.9, §3.9, §5.9 |
| Codex hook events | It is unclear whether the Codex hook vocabulary includes `SessionEnd`, beyond the names it shares with Claude Code. | §1.9, §12.6 |
| Claude Code auto mode as default | The date and version from which auto mode became the starting mode for interactive Claude Code differ across the notes. | §1.9, §7.1 |
